Combined Synopsis/Solicitation 
 
1 
 
Description: 
This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in 
accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested 
and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. 
 
Solicitation number 70CTD026R00000007 is issued as a streamlined request for proposal (RFP) 
for licenses for the Inmate Identification and Recognition System (I.R.I.S.™ ) and the Mobile Offender 
Recognition & Information (MORIS™ ) for Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO).  
 
PSC: 5865 - Electronic Countermeasures, Counter-Countermeasures and Quick Reaction Capability  
NAICS: 541519- Other Computer Related Services 
 
This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and 
clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically 
at www.acquisition.gov. 
 
A list of line-item number(s) and items, quantities, and units of measure (including option(s), if 
applicable):

brand name descriptions (see 12.102): 
ICE requires the contractor to provide the licenses identified in the section above. Exhibit A: Statement of 
Objectives provides additional details about the requirement. 
 
Date(s) and place(s) of delivery and acceptance and f.o.b. point (see part 47): 
The contractor shall deliver the license access instructions and license keys no later than 20 calendar days 
from date of award to Program Manager, Patrick Lewis at Patrick.Lewis@ice.dhs.gov.   
 
A list of solicitation provisions that apply to the acquisition (see 12.205(a)): 

Combined Synopsis/Solicitation 
 
2 
 
All applicable solicitation provisions are contained in Attachment D – Terms and Conditions. 
 
A list of contract clauses that apply to the acquisition (see 12.205(b)): 
All applicable contract clauses are contained in Attachment D – Terms and Conditions. 
 
The date, time, and place for receipt of offer and point of contact: 
Proposals shall be submitted electronically to ice-ero-procurements@ice.dhs.gov no later than May 12, 
2026 at 9:00AM Eastern Time.          
 
Any other additional information required by 5.101(c): 
 
Proposal Submission Requirements 
There is no page limit for the proposal. All documents must be submitted in Microsoft Word, Microsoft 
Excel or Adobe PDF compatible formats. Text shall be single-spaced, on 8½” x 11” paper (except as 
specifically noted), with margins not-less-than one inch. Pages shall be numbered consecutively. 
Contractors may use 11” x 17” sized fold-out pages for tables, charts, graphs, or pictures that cannot be 
legibly presented on 8½” x 11” paper. Each 11” x 17” page applies as two pages to the overall page count. 
Print must be of a minimum 11-point font size. 
Bi2 shall submit a proposal which contains the following documents: 
1. Cover Letter – The contractor shall prepare a cover letter which includes the following 
information: 
 
• RFP Number & Title 
• Name and address of Contractor 
• Name, telephone number & e-mail address of main point-of-contact 
• Name of your contract administration office 
• Date of submission 
• Name, title and signature of authorized representative 
• Company Unique Identifier Number and CAGE Code 
• The validity period of the proposal (at least through 05/20/2026) 
• All assumptions (if any) 
a. All assumptions (especially technical and pricing) to the RFP must be 
identified in this cover letter. Assumptions identified in other areas of the 
RFP will not be considered. 
 
2. Performance Work Statement (PWS) - The contractor shall prepare a PWS to address how 
the company will address all aspects of the requirement identified in Attachment B: Statement 
of Objectives. The PWS shall include the following sections: Background, Scope, 
Performance Requirements, Performance Standards, Deliverables and Delivery Schedule, 
Government Furnished Equipment, Place of Performance and Period of Performance. 
• PWS Addendum - The contractor shall incorporate Attachment C: PWS Addendum 
into the PWS with no changes. (The addendum contains Government-required 
language that must be included in the resulting PWS and contract.) 
 
3. Terms and Conditions – The contractor shall complete the fill-ins for all provisions 
referenced in this attachment. 
 
4. Draft Security Plan – The contractor shall provide a draft security plan in response to 
Attachment E: Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) which explains how they will protect 
ICE data and work towards FedRAMP certification.  

Combined Synopsis/Solicitation 
 
3 
 
 
5. End User License Agreement (EULA) – The contractor shall provide a copy of the EULA 
for the IRIS and MORIS licenses. The EULA shall be consistent with Federal procurement 
law as well as Federal, Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and ICE regulation, policy 
and guides and otherwise in the best interest of the Government. Licensing agreements shall 
be provided as .pdf attachments. No links or references will be considered. Any terms in the 
EULA that conflict with federal law are given no effect.  
 
6. Pricing Summary and Narrative: The contractor shall complete Attachment F: Pricing 
Template to provide a pricing summary and a narrative detailing a breakdown of the pricing. 
The contractor shall also provide any supporting documentation (such as established catalog 
prices/market prices and sales to nongovernmental and governmental entities) to explain how 
the pricing is fair and reasonable. Acceptable forms of supporting documentation include 
contracts or receipts for showing pricing paid by other customers. Supporting pricing data 
must include appropriate dates on the prices at which the same or similar items have been 
sold previously to ensure they are adequate for evaluating the reasonableness.  
 
Evaluation Process 
ICE intends to evaluate BI2’s proposal to ensure the following: 
• The proposed PWS demonstrates the contractor’s ability to successfully perform the requirements 
of this contract; 
• The Draft Security Plan complies with RTM and explains how they will protect ICE data and work 
towards FedRAMP certification. 
• The proposed price is accurate, complete and reasonable. 
 
Basis for Award 
The Government intends to award a single Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Contract (with a 12-month period of 
performance) to Bi2 provided the proposal is determined to be technically acceptable and the proposed 
price is determined to be fair and reasonable. No award will be made if the proposal is not acceptable or if 
the price is not fair and reasonable. Bi2 is strongly encouraged to submit its best technical and price 
proposal. ICE reserves the right to contact Bi2 to obtain additional information regarding the proposal. 
ICE reserves the right to negotiate any aspect of proposal (price or non-price factors) if it is determined to 
be in the best interest of the Government.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) 
 
 
 
 
 
U.S. Department of Homeland Security 
Immigration and Customs Enforcement  
Office of Chief Information Officer  
 
Inmate Recognition and Identification System (IRIS) and   
Mobile Offender Recognition & Identification System 
(MORIS) – Bi2 Technologies, LLC 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
May 2026 
 
  


IRIS & MORIS Access – Bi2 Technologies, LLC 
Page 2 of 5 
 
1. Purpose:  
 
This requirement is for services to provide ICE with immediate access to over 5.025 
million booking records across the United States through the nation's only secure, 
encrypted, real-time national criminal justice data sharing network. This network is based 
on advanced iris biometric technology, enabling rapid authentication of subject identities. 
The implementation of this solution supports Presidential Proclamation 108 “Declaring 
an Emergency at the Southern Border of the United States” and Executive Orders (EO) 
14159, “Protecting the American People Against Invasion,” and 14165, “Securing Our 
Borders,” by enhancing ICE's capability to quickly and accurately identify individuals 
encountered during ICE operations. 
 
2.  Background: 
 
Bi2 Technologies has developed and maintains the only national, web-based iris 
biometric network and database. No other organization, public or private, has developed 
or implemented a comparable capability. This award will grant ICE immediate access to 
over 5 million booking records for over 1.5 million unique individuals enrolled by more 
than 247 agencies. By leveraging advanced iris biometric technology, this solution will 
enable the positive identification of individuals within seconds, significantly enhancing 
ICE's operational efficiency and accuracy. 
 
3.  Scope: 
 
Bi2's Inmate Recognition and Identification System (IRIS) is the  nation's only secure, 
encrypted, real-time national criminal justice data sharing network, based on Iris Biometric 
technology. MORIS works in conjunction with Bi2 ’s IRIS . MORIS allows law 
enforcement to authenticate an individual’s identity and immediately have access to any 
information and data previously entered into the IRIS national database. 
 
4.  Performance Objectives: 
 
ICE will utilize Bi2 Technologies' solution and data analytics to access over five million 
booking records across the United States in multiple jurisdictions. ICE will access the 
Inmate Identification & Recognition System (IRIS) and the Mobile Offender Recognition 
& Identification System (MORIS).

12-month period to the IRIS and MORIS solutions, to include:   
 
• The Contractor shall supply 1,570 IRIS biometric devices to ICE for deployment 
at designated locations nationwide within 30 days of the award. Additionally, the

throughout the duration of the award. 
• The Contractor shall support identification/verification against any images 
produced from ISO 19794-6 and ISO 29794-6 compliant devices. 
• The Contractor shall provide ICE with immediate 24/7/365 electronic access to 
the IRIS database records on agnostic platforms, including Microsoft, Apple, and 
Android, for both fixed and mobile devices. This access shall be available for an 
unlimited number of users and support an unlimited number of queries and/or

• The Contractor shall ensure complete identity and booking records are provided

Request for Information (RFI) 
TO: All Interested Parties 
FROM: 72d Air Base Wing Communications Directorate (SC) 
Air Force Materiel Command 
Tinker AFB, OK 73145 
SUBJECT: Request For Information (RFI) for Application, Database & Server Support 
Services (ADBSSS) 
RFI Number: RFI-ADBSSS-2026-01 
Date of Issuance: 11 May 2026 
1. Introduction and Purpose 
PLEASE NOTE: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP). This is a Request for 
Information (RFI) issued solely for information and market research planning 
purposes, as deﬁned in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.201(e). Companies 
should not submit proposal-style documents or that level of detail in response to 
this RFI.  
 
The 72d Air Base Wing Communications Directorate (SC) at Tinker Air Force Base 
(TAFB) is seeking to identify sources capable of providing comprehensive 
Application, Database, and Server Support Services. The primary goal is to acquire 
non-personal services for base-wide application development and sustainment; 
database administration; ﬁle, print, and application server administration; and 
quality assurance.  All services will be provided on site at Tinker AFB, OK. 
 
The purpose of this RFI is to gain industry insight into current market capabilities 
and innovative approaches for providing Information Technology (IT) services to 
TAFB. The information gathered will be used to reﬁne the Government's acquisition 
strategy in terms of cost, schedule, and performance. 
 
2. Program Background and Description of Requirements  
The 72d Air Base Wing Communications Directorate (SC) provides critical 
Information Technology (IT) services to TAFB. This requirement is for a contractor to 
provide the necessary resources to design, develop, sustain, and enhance new and 
existing IT capabilities for a wide range of software applications and tools. The 
scope in) and managing systems hosted in various environments, including on-
premises data centers and cloud platforms (e.g., Cloud One, Microsoft Azure, AWS, 

DISA STRATUS), and requires the ability to handle a signiﬁcant volume of trouble 
tickets and service requests. 
 
The overall scope of work includes, but is not limited to, the following service areas: 
 
a. Program and Project Management: Overseeing all contract activities, 
managing multiple simultaneous IT projects, and ensuring requirements are 
met on schedule and within budget. 
b. Software and Application Development & Sustainment: Developing, 
maintaining, and sustaining a variety of web, client, and database 
applications using technologies such as .NET Framework/Core, C#, Oracle, 
and MS SQL Server. This includes support for the Contract Repair 
Management System (CRMS). 
c. Database Administration (DBA): Installing, monitoring, and maintaining 
Oracle and MS SQL Server databases, including performance tuning, 
security hardening (STIGs), and high-availability architecture. 
d. Server Administration (SA): Managing and maintaining a large-scale server 
environment (Windows, Linux, Solaris) across physical and virtualized 
platforms (VMware). This includes patching, backup/recovery, and 
vulnerability management using tools (ACAS).   
e. Storage and Backup Administration (EMC2): Providing specialized expert 
Server Administrators with current certiﬁcations for EMC2 platforms. 
Personnel must be trained to an adequate level to obtain AFNET SCCM Level 
3 rights. Duties include providing optimized conﬁgurations, implementing 
processes/procedures, and maintaining expert-level knowledge of Dell EMC 
storage platforms, backup and recovery products, and monitoring/reporting 
solutions to keep the Data Center running at peak levels. 
f. Cybersecurity Support: Providing Information System Security Manager 
(ISSM) support, managing Risk Management Framework (RMF) packages in 
eMASS to maintain Authority to Operate (ATO), and ensuring all deliverables 
comply with DoD and Air Force cybersecurity policies. 
g. Application Quality Assurance (QA): Providing dedicated QA support across 
multiple concurrent hardware/software initiatives. Responsibilities include 
comprehensive test planning; developing and executing test cases via tools 
like Team Foundation Server (TFS); managing strict User Acceptance Testing 
(UAT) documentation and deﬁciency thresholds; performing 
daily/weekly/maintenance system validations (including non-core hours); 
loading/testing electronic Technical Orders (TOs); supporting continuous 

process improvement (e.g., Art of the Possible); and assisting in providing 
documentation to obtain Authority to Operate (ATO). 
h. Conﬁguration Management (CM): Executing test plans, validating application 
functionality, managing the change control process, and maintaining all 
lifecycle documentation.   
i. Business Intelligence (BI): Providing administration and report development 
using BI tools, QLIK and IBM Cognos. 
 
3. Speciﬁc Government Questions Interested parties are requested to provide 
responses to the following questions. Please be clear and concise. 
 
a. Corporate Experience & Capability: 
i. Describe your company's experience in providing capabilities like the 
broad scope of requirements outlined in this RFI (e.g., enterprise-level 
application development, database/server administration, and 
cybersecurity for a DoD client). Please provide speciﬁc examples of 
past projects, including contract value and duration. 
ii. Describe your company’s approach to managing a large and diverse IT 
services contract, including your methodology for program 
management, quality control, and continuous process improvement. 
b. Technical Approach & Solutions: 
i. Describe your technical approach to modernizing legacy applications 
and migrating systems to a cloud environment (e.g., AWS, Azure, DISA 
STRATUS) while ensuring operational availability and security. 
ii. Describe your processes for vulnerability management, including how 
you would use tools like ACAS to review scan results, prioritize 
vulnerabilities, and apply patches (e.g., TCNOs, STIGs) across a large 
server environment within the required timelines. 
iii. The government seeks support for a wide array of technologies (e.g., 
Oracle, MS SQL, VMware, .NET, Cognos). How would you ensure your 
workforce possesses and maintains the required expertise and 
certiﬁcations (e.g., DoD 8140/8570, Microsoft, VMware) to support 
this diverse environment? 
iv. Describe any technical risks or problem areas you anticipate for this 
requirement and your proposed mitigation strategies. 
c. Business Information & Set-Asides: 

i. The Government anticipates utilizing the GSA 8(a) STARS III GWAC. 
Please conﬁrm if your company is an active contract holder on this 
vehicle and provide your GSA STARS III Contract Number. 
ii. State your company's size (Large or Small Business) under the 
anticipated NAICS code 541512 (Computer Systems Design 
Services), with a size standard of $34 million. Please include any 
socio-economic statuses (e.g., 8(a), Woman-Owned, HUBZone, 
Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business).   
iii. Describe what percentage of the work would be performed in-house 
versus subcontracted. If you are a large business, what are your 
projected small business utilization percentages in key areas of the 
PWS? 
iv. If this effort were to be set aside for small businesses, describe your 
approach to complying with FAR 52.219-14, "Limitations on 
Subcontracting. " 
 
4. Response Instructions 
a. Submission Deadline: Responses are requested no later than 4:00 PM CDT 
on 12 June 2026. 
b. Format: Please limit your response to 20 single-sided pages, using a 
minimum of 10-point font. Responses should be submitted in Microsoft 
Word or Adobe PDF format. Marketing materials are not desired. 
c. Proprietary Information: Do not include proprietary, classiﬁed, or export-
controlled information in your response. The Government reserves the right 
to use the information provided to inform its acquisition strategy. All 
information submitted will be treated as informational and will not be 
returned. 
d. Point of Contact (POC): Submit responses and any questions concerning this 
RFI via email to the Contracting, Gerald Mosley/Simon Montolvo, 
at gerald.mosley.1@us.af.mil / simon.montalvo@us.af.mil. Please include 
the RFI number in the subject line. 
 
5. Disclaimers 
This is an RFI issued for information and planning purposes only and does not 
constitute a solicitation or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. This 
request for information does not commit the Government to contract for any supply 
or service whatsoever. 
 

The Government is not seeking proposals and will not accept unsolicited proposals. 
Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or 
administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with 
responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party’s expense. 
 
Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future Request for 
Proposal (RFP), if any is issued. The information provided in this RFI is subject to 
change and is not binding on the Government.

Request for Information/Sources Sought Notice for 

NIST ANDOVER DDC System Maintenance

Notice ID: OFPM/TEAM SS26-15	

Contract Opportunity Type

Sources Sought

Response Date: 01:00 PM EST, 05/15/2026

NAICS Code

541519-Other Computer Related Services

BACKGROUND

This is a notice to request information from industry to help the U.S. Department of Commerce, National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) determine the availability and capability of small businesses and other than small businesses to provide labor, supervision, tools, material, and equipment for preventative maintenance and emergency services for the Continuum and I/NET building automation systems specified at the NIST Gaithersburg, MD campus. 

This notice is strictly to request information for market research purposes to help NIST determine the appropriate acquisition strategy for this requirement. This notice shall not be construed as a solicitation, an obligation, or commitment by the NIST.

OVERVIEW

See attached draft Statement of Work (SOW).

ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE

This is a 1-year Base Period contract with four (4) 1-year Option Periods. Approximate schedule is as follows:

Base Year –  8/1/2026 – 7/31/2027

Opt.1 Year – 8/1/2027 – 7/31/2028

Opt.2 Year – 8/1/2028 – 7/31/2029

Opt.3 Year – 8/1/2029 – 7/31/2030

Opt.4 Year – 8/1/2030 – 7/31/2031

INFORMATION REQUESTED FROM INDUSTRY SOURCES:

NIST invites industry sources to review this notice carefully and to familiarize themselves with the draft SOW. Thereafter, by the closing date of this notice, NIST encourages those sources to submit responses to brandon.butler@nist.gov. Do not include proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information in response to this notice. 

Responses should be submitted to contain the following, in Microsoft Word format or in .pdf format, use 12-point font, with a page limitation of ten pages (excluding cover page and excluding standard commercial pricing information):

Cover page, including:

Sources Sought Notice number, title, and date of issuance

Unique Entity ID

Company name

Company address

Company website address

Company point of contact and their phone number and email address

Validation of company size status under NAICS: 54519- Other Computer 
Related Services. See table of business size standards at Table of size standards | U.S. Small Business Administration for more information. 

Indicate whether your company has an active registration for procurement purposes in sam.gov.

Provide any suggestions for NIST to consider for the draft SOW, with the goal of  improving the draft SOW in a way that makes it clearer and as competitive as possible.

STATEMENT OF WORK/PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT

Title: ANDOVER DDC System Maintenance

 

I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION 

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is a 576-acer facility consisting of thirty-six (36) mixed use (mainly office and research laboratory) buildings. There are currently four (4) proprietary building automation systems used to control various mechanical equipment that maintain the required environmental conditions on campus. The Andover system (Continuum and I/NE) pertains to this statement of work.

II. PURPOSE

Contractor is to provide all labor, supervision, tools, material, and equipment to provide preventative maintenance and emergency services for the Continuum and I/NET building automation systems specified. Contractor shall maintain systems to ensure systems are in proper operating order.

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

Maintenance service shall be provided twice a month, and the place of performance shall be at NIST, Gaithersburg Campus. Maintenance service shall be performed during normal business hours (7am – 5 pm Monday through Thursday, excluding Federal Holidays).

PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 

This is a 1-year Base Period contract with four (4) 1-year Option Periods.

Base Year – 8/1/2026 – 7/31/2027

Opt.1 Year – 8/1/2027 – 7/31/2028

Opt.2 Year – 8/1/2028 – 7/31/2029

Opt.3 Year – 8/1/2029 – 7/31/2030

Opt.4 Year – 8/1/2030 – 7/31/2031

Task 2 –   Graphics Revisions

The contractor shall maintain all graphics at each of the applicable workstations.

Task 3 – Programing Diagnostics

The contractor shall perform diagnostics of programs and make recommendations for change/correction to meet original control performance requirements. After consulting with NIST COR the contractor shall make changes to programming to achieve the performance requirement.

Task 4 – Field Panel Diagnostics 

The contractor shall perform diagnostics of all field panels. The contractor shall evaluate and tune critical control loops to maintain peak efficiency of equipment as the building mechanical systems performance changes over time. NIST DDC personnel shall work with the Contactor to identify the critical control loops on each system.

Task 6 – Consultation

The Contractor shall consult with NIST DDC personnel to identify and resolve problems with hardware and/or software in the applicable automation system. Any changes required to hardware will be the reasonability of NIST. Changes required to software to resolve issues shall be the reasonability of the contractor.

Pre-Solicitation Notice IAW RFO 5.101(c) 
Integrated Tactical Warning/Attack Assessment (ITW/AA) IV 
 
(1) Point of contact. The Contracting Officer is Angela LeRoy, email: angela.leroy@us.af.mil, 
telephone: (402) 232-5956 and Contract Specialist is Amanda Smith, email: 
amanda.smith.70@us.af.mil, telephone: (402) 232-0590 at 55th Contracting Squadron, 106 
Peacekeeper Lane, Ste 2N3, Offutt AFB NE 68113. 
(2) Codes for services or supplies. NAICS: 541512, PSC: R425.  
(3) Description. 
(i) 55 CONS/PKT, Offutt AFB, NE intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price five year, six month sole 
source contract to Delta Solutions & Strategies, LLC under authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as 
implemented by RFO 6.103-1(c)(2), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or 
services will satisfy agency requirements.  The contractor shall provide ITW/AA services, 
including software updates to the proprietary Missile Warning Threat Suite (MWTS) software; 
generate dynamic ITW/AA simulations for the Joint Chiefs of Staff, United States Strategic 
Command (USSTRATCOM), United States Indo-Pacific Command (USINDOPACOM), Defense 
Information Systems Agency (DISA), North American Aerospace Defense Command – United 
States Northern Command (NORAD-USNORTHCOM) and other forward users; provide 
NORAD-USNORTHCOM with Correlation Center Emulator (CCE) and MWTS software 
engineering, software and simulation enhancement and Command and Control (C2) system 
virtualization and integration support; develop and support an interface between Missile 
Defense Agency’s (MDA’s) Training Support System (TSS), Integrated Command and Control 
System (IC2S) strategic missile warning capability, Combatant Commanders Integrated 
Command and Control System (CCIC2S) and Global Command and Control System (GCCS); 
develop, maintain and support software utilized in the production of simulations for processing in 
Nuclear Planning and Execution System (NPES) which support automated, realistic, dynamic, 
scalable message generation with near real-time system injection; provide configuration 
management scheme for the generation and maintenance of scenarios and define applicable 
quality control methods for Joint Staff and USSTRATCOM/J7 scenarios; integrate the output of 
the Graphic User Interface (GUI) with the MWTS, the Protocol Data Unit (PDU) Converter, the 
Global Sensor Integration on Networks (GSIN) and the GCCS; provide formal configuration 
management, testing and validation/verification of product development and integration; and 
provide monthly status reports.  

(ii) This pre-solicitation notice satisfies the requirement in RFO 5.101. A quote will be solicited 
directly from Delta Solutions, LLC. The anticipated award date is 13 July 2026.  
(iii) The requirement is not subject to the World Trade Organization Government Procurement 
Agreement (WTO GPA) and/or a Free Trade Agreement (FTA).   
(iv) The product does not require any technical data not already provided. 
(v) This is not a construction requirement.  
(vi) This is a sole source requirement IAW RFO 6.103-1(c)(2), as Delta Solutions is the only 
vendor that possesses the requisite capabilities to successfully fulfill the requirement. This 
determination is primarily based on the fact that the MWTS source code, a critical component of 
the requirement, is the exclusive proprietary intellectual property of Delta Solutions. Currently, 
there is no other known service provider capable of performing the requirement, and engaging 
any other source would introduce unacceptable risks to the mission. 
(vii) No product or service qualification requirement for this effort.

GENERAL INFORMATION

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY.  This is not a solicitation for bids, proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations.  The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of all qualified sources to perform a potential requirement.  The responses received from interested contractors will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method.

The intended contract is a firm-fixed price.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 20, is conducting market research to identify potential sources which can provide the following in support of the VA Puget Sound Healthcare System (VAPSHCS), Seattle, Washington.

VAPSHCS has a need for a base plus four (4) option year contract for a web-based on-call and physician scheduling software brand name or equal to AMION FOR ENTERPRISES+ (see requirement information).

Vendor shall be an OEM, authorized dealer, authorized distributor, or authorized reseller for the proposed equipment/system, verified by an authorization letter or other documents from the OEM. All software licensing, warranty and service associated with the equipment/system shall be in accordance with the OEM terms and conditions.

For set-asides: Please indicate in your response whether they can comply with VAAR 852.219-75, VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting and/or FAR 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting (e.g., will not pay more than 50 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities) should a set-aside be considered.

Full text of clauses can be found here: 

852.219-75, VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting: https://www.va.gov/oal/library/vaar/vaar852.asp#85221975 

FAR 52.219-14: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-52#FAR_52_219_14 

Potential candidates having the capabilities necessary to provide the stated services at a fair and reasonable price are invited to respond to this Sources Sought Notice via e-mail to Jennifer Robles at jennifer.robles1@va.gov  no later than May 26, 2026, 1PM, Mountain Time. No telephone inquiries will be accepted. 

RESPONSES SHOULD INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING INFORMATION:  Company name, address, SAM UEI, and business size; point of contact name, phone number, and e-mail address; whether supplies/services are presently offered on a current GSA Federal Supply Schedule contract, NASA SEWP, or any other Federal contract.  If offering a system with similar physical characteristics, please include business size of manufacturer for Non-Manufacturer Rule (NMR) determination. NAICS Code 541519, 150 employees, is applicable to determine business size standard. Any questions or concerns may also be directed via email to Jennifer Robles at jennifer.robles1@va.gov.

SCOPE

4.1. The Contractor shall provide, transport, install (network application), and configure all listed equipment. All products must meet all salient characteristics defined in this section. 

4.2. All equipment and installation must meet manufacturers and VA specifications. 

4.3. Contractor shall furnish all supplies, equipment, facilities and services required for delivery and installation. 

4.4. Contractor is responsible for any missing parts and components not included in order to carry out installation. 

5. SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS 

5.1. Web-based on-call and physician scheduling software brand name or equal to AMION FOR ENTERPRISES+ software for group practices, residents, hospitalists, and other medical providers for call, clinic, rotation, and shift schedules, as listed below: 

Specifications/Salient Characteristics: 

At least 45 annual subscription software licenses

Unlimited user accounts provided to access/view schedule for all Amion or equivalent  account types

Enterprise or equivalent accounts to have unlimited number of scheduling groups.  Typically allocated to different departments within a health care facility and allow each  department to customize staff and schedules build per their specific workflow.

There are currently ~50 active groups in VA Puget Sound Amion.

Non-enterprise Amion or equivalent accounts require an individual license to be purchased for each scheduling group.

Host schedules on contractor's web server 

Assist in immediate recovery of facility's schedules in the event of server crashes 

24/7/365 internet availability of schedules 

24/7/365 telephone support for crashes and schedule-level outages 

One business-day support for technical problems affecting individual providers 

5.2 Installation (Network Application) 

Assist site administrator/facility point of contact with the software configurations per facility's      preferences. Install all equipment to manufacturer's specifications maintaining federal and local safety standards 

5.3 Training 

Provide eight live, remote, two-hour minimum training sessions for facility's provider schedulers to provide instruction on creating and maintaining service section schedules; incorporating in the facility wide master schedule; receiving and posting trade requests; creating schedule templates/patterns; configuring auto-scheduler feature; and basic troubleshooting. 

Provide four live, remote, one-hour minimum training sessions for provider Super users to instruct on accessing, viewing, and navigating schedules on computers and mobile devices; submitting trades; navigating and paging on-call providers from schedules. 

Provide one in-depth technical training configuration session for site administrator/COR and alternate to instruct on creating schedule templates, patterns, business rules, and other site configurations. 

Provide more advanced troubleshooting instruction upon request. 

Training must be completed within 30 days after receipt of award. 

5.4. DELIVERY/INSTALLATION 

5.4.1. DELIVERY 

5.4.1.1. Contractor shall deliver all equipment to VAPSHCS, 1600 S. Columbia Way, Seattle, WA 98108

6.3. Deliver specified items only when the site is ready for installation work to proceed. 

6.4. Store products in dry condition inside enclosed facilities. 

6.5. Any government requested delayed delivery up to 90 days after initial delivery date shall be at no additional cost to the Government.

7.1.1. Binders - Quantity (2) each for items 5.1-5.4.1.1

7.2. Deliver compilation of all manufacturer recommended maintenance schedule and operation materials packaged in binder(s) to COR upon completion of installation. 

8. MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT SERVICES REQUIREMENTS

8.1. The AMION FOR ENTERPRISES or Equivalent software must permit maintenance professionals the ability to perform diagnostics, troubleshooting, and maintenance as required. 

8.2. The vendor must have preventive maintenance service to meet at minimum The Joint Commission standards. 

8.3. Licensing Software updates 

8.3.1. The Contractor shall provide, for the duration of the warranty period, all computer software, access keys or codes, or external devices required for the operation, calibration, or repair of the equipment purchased. Any such items not listed on the price proposal and required for maintenance of the system shall be taken as included with the purchase of the system. 

8.3.2. Any minor upgrades or changes to the maintenance software, hardware, or access keys or codes shall be provided at no charge to the medical center during the time the equipment is operational at this facility. 

8.3.3. All application software licenses are included in the purchase of the equipment and shall not require a renewal charge for the period of time the equipment is in use in the facility. 

8.4. Support Services 

8.4.1. The Contractor shall provide support services for a period of one year and option of additional four years. Contractor shall provide list of support services provided including phone service support. 

8.4.2. Contractor shall furnish all management equipment inclusive of parts, material, travel and labor required to support and maintain in good working condition, the AMION FOR ENTERPRISES software or equivalent. 

8.4.3. All materials and services provided shall be according to the OEM specifications and guidelines. Contractor shall repair any inadequate or improper repairs performed at a time convenient to the VA at no additional expense to the VA. 

8.4.4. Contractor must have the capability to provide remote support via VPN access. VA will provide authorized personnel limited access for remote connectivity to the system. 

9. TRAINING:

9.1. Contractor shall provide On-site training of the equipment to the Clinical Users. Scheduling of operator training shall be coordinated with the VAPSHCS point of contact after installation is complete. 

9.2. Contractor shall provide On-site training of the equipment to the Technical Users. Scheduling of technical training shall be coordinated with the VAPSHCS point of contact after installation is complete. 

9.3. The contractor shall provide a training program to the Biomedical Engineering technicians and in-house clinical personnel. If the training program is offsite, the contractor shall also provide lodging and airfare. 

9.4. Technical training must provide Biomedical Engineering with the tools and knowledge to fully operate and maintain the system.

Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
 
OMNISSA HORIZON SOFTWARE SUPPORT 
 
KEESLER AIR FORCE BASE (AFB), MISSISSIPPI 
 
9 April 2026 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Prepared By 
 
81st Communications Squadron 
510 H. Street 
Keesler AFB, MS   39532 
 

Provide independent assessment, analysis, consultation and support of the Omnissa Horizon 
software components used in the current Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) at Keesler Air 
Force Base (AFB), Mississippi (MS). 
 
The VDI environment hardware consists of a four-node Dell/EMC VxRail cluster and 60 Dell 
Optiplex 3000 thin clients.  The VDI environment utilizes Broadcom’s vSphere Client, vCenter 
Server Appliance (VCSA); Omnissa’s  Horizon 8,  Dynamic Environment Manager, Apps 
V olume Manager; and Microsoft’s FSLogix software applications.  PC-over-IP (PCoIP) protocol 
is used for network communication between thin clients and internal system components via a 10 
GB network backbone. The VDI directly supports Keesler AFB’s Emergency Operations Center 
(EOC) in Buildings 4213 and 4330. 
The Contractor shall provide remote assistance and telephone support to meet the requirements 
as stated in this SOO.  The Contractor shall provide analysis, assessment and consultation with 
limited down time or scheduled down time to minimize interruption of EOC activities. The 
contractor shall achieve the following objectives: 
• Provide 50 hours of Ad Hoc support.  Hours can be used for operational support requests 
and proactive project work.  Unused hours shall be rolled over to subsequent annual 
renewal agreements. 
 
• Provide an initial independent technical assessment of the current VDI architecture. The 
objective is to receive expert analysis and forward-looking recommendations that support 
modernization efforts, enhance security posture, and ensure long-term sustainment. 
 
• Implement the use of the Omnissa Blast Extreme protocol to replace the currently used 
PCoIP protocol which reaches end of support in 2028. 
 
• Provide technical support, and remote assistance to resolve degradation of service, and 
implement improvements to sustain the VDI’s operational health and performance. 
 
• Perform follow-up technical assessment and optimization review to ensure the VDI meets 
the evolving operational needs and mission goals of the Keesler AFB Emergency 
Operations Center (EOC) and other key stakeholders as needed.

GENERAL INFORMATION

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

This Source Sought notice is issued for market information and planning for future acquisition in accordance with (IAW) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.201(e). Responses to sources sought notice 36C26226Q0752 will improve the understanding of the Government’s requirement and industry capabilities. It will enhance the Government s ability to obtain quality equipment and allow for potential offerors to judge whether or how they can satisfy the Government s requirement. This is not a solicitation announcement. Responses to this notice cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Information received shall be safeguarded adequately from unauthorized disclosure. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office 22 (NCO 22) is seeking sources that can provide RADFORMATION SOFTWARE SUBSCRIPTION IAW Request for Information (RFI) 36C26226Q0752, and Salient Characteristics. Reference attached RFI 36C26226Q0752 and Salient Characteristics for more details. Inquiries shall be submitted via email to Anna.Cevallos@va.gov. Please Reference RFI 36C26226Q0752 in subject email.

The purpose of this notice is to gain knowledge of potential qualified sources and their size classification relative to North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 541511, size standard $34 million dollars. If the Government’s pending market research establishes reasonable expectation that two or more Veteran owned businesses certified on vetbiz.gov can fulfill the requirement, the Government will set aside the acquisition for Veteran owned businesses. If the Government establishes reasonable expectation that two or more small business concerns can fulfill the requirement, the Government will set aside the acquisition for small business concerns. A determination by the Government to compete this action based on this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office 22 (NCO 22) is seeking sources that can provide RADFORMATION subscription (B +4 OY) for Long Beach VA Healthcare System. The salient characteristics are intended to be descriptive, not restrictive and to indicate the quality that will be satisfactory. It is the responsibility of the interested source to demonstrate to the Government that they can provide the sought-out brand name or equal product. “Equal” products will be evaluated based on information furnished by the interested source or reasonably available to the Government. 1.0  BACKGROUND 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), North Texas Healthcare System Pharmacy 
Service strives to provide high quality, effective, and efficient Information Technology 
(IT) services to those responsible for providing care to the Veterans at the point-of-care 
as well as throughout all the points of the Veterans’ health care in an effective, timely 
and compassionate manner.  VA depends on Information Management/Information 
Technology (IM/IT) systems to meet mission goals. 
 
The Contractor shall provide access and support for a Pharmacy Staff Scheduling  
 software platform for the Dallas VA Medical Center; 4500 S Lancaster Rd, Dallas, TX 
75216 This includes 24/7 access (excluding scheduled downtimes), software hosting, 
updates, and technical support. The platform supports staff scheduling and competency 
assessment for 125 users. 
 
Platform software service 
 Platform Availability: Continuous access to the platform with uptime monitoring 
and reliability measures. 
 Business Hours Support: Unlimited technical support during business hours 
with documented response times. 
 Emergency Support Response: After-hours emergency support with 
documented response and resolution timelines. 
 Training Sessions: Onboarding and refresher training for client administrators; 
training materials provided. 
 Online Help Center Access: 24/7 access to updated documentation, FAQs, 
tutorials, and self-service resources. 
 Account Management Reports: Regular updates from a dedicated account 
manager, including usage insights and recommendations. 
 Monthly Progress Report: Submitted by the 10th business day; including 
performance metrics and service summaries. 
 Platform Uptime Report: Detailed report of outages, root causes, and corrective 
actions. 
 Support Ticket Summary: Monthly summary of ticket volume, types, 
response/resolution times, and trends. 
 Training Completion Log: Record of training sessions, dates, topics, and 
participant roles.

GENERAL INFORMATION

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

PYXIS EQUIPMENT

NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLICIT BRAND NAME- PYXIS MEDSTATION & REFRIGERATOR 

Requirement: BRAND NAME ONLY

The proposed procurement is for products which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one brand name under the authority of FAR 6.302-1 -- Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1). The North American Industry Classification System code (NAICS) for this requirement is 541519. All responsible sources that feel they should be considered qualified to provide the above-mentioned products may submit a response to this notice (by the response due date shown above) to janice.jones@va.gov.  

The information provided shall include detailed (and relevant) documentation to allow the government to perform adequate market research and make a proper determination. A determination by the government not to compete this proposed requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct an unrestricted open-market procurement.  

The BD Pyxis ES system is a proprietary platform, and no other manufacturer’s products are technically compatible with the existing VA Pyxis ecosystems. Key justifications include:

System Integration & Compatibility: Only Pyxis ES equipment integrates natively with current Pyxis servers, access controls, software, audit logs, and existing profiles. No alternative ADC refrigerator or cabinet can interoperate with the Pyxis ES environment without compromising chain of custody controls. 

Mandatory Patient Safety Requirements: BD Pyxis systems provide automated transaction logging, controlled access, and security features required for high-alert medication management, protecting both patients and staff. 

VHA Directive 1195 Compliance: The OR requires an automated dispensing cabinet (ADC) for high alert medications. The existing refrigerator is not automated or secure and cannot be made compliant. Only the Pyxis ES ADC refrigerator meets mandatory VHA 1195 requirements. 

Established Workflows & Training: Clinical workflows—nursing, pharmacy, anesthesia—are built around Pyxis ES user access rules, override procedures, discrepancy reporting, and emergency protocols. Replacing with a different system would require significant retraining and introduce patient safety risk. 

Medication Security Infrastructure: Facility approved Pyxis devices across the medical center. Only Pyxis ES equipment can operate as a secure extension of this existing network. 

OEM Exclusivity: BD/CareFusion is the sole manufacturer of Pyxis equipment and the only qualified provider of installation and maintenance. A letter dated 03/04/2026 confirms BD/CareFusion as the exclusive source. 

Thus, only BD Pyxis ES equipment satisfies the clinical, operational, safety, and regulatory requirements.

Statement of Work (Revised) 
AFLCMC/ES VTC and A/V System Maintenance 
 
1.0 Purpose 
The purpose of this Statement of Work (SOW) is to secure a contractor to perform 
comprehensive maintenance and support for the Video Teleconferencing (VTC) and 
Audio/Visual (A/V) system located in building 1624, conference room 203, at 5 Eglin Street, 
Hanscom AFB, MA 01731. The contractor shall ensure the system remains fully functional 
through proactive maintenance, timely hardware replacement, on-call support, and user 
training. 
2.0 Scope of Work 
• Provide maintenance for a full audio visual and URL solution for one independent 
conference room that is capable of both classiﬁed and unclassiﬁed video 
teleconferencing (VTC) connectivity.  
• Classiﬁed and unclassiﬁed VTC utilizes a single CODEC, automated periods 
processing hardware, and has NIPR/SIPR Teams capabilities.  
• Replacement parts to the VTC AV system shall comply with the established Defense 
Information Systems Agency (DISA) policy, Video Services Policy Security Technical 
Implementation Guide (STIG).  
• The system will maintain GVS comparability and remain on the Defense Information 
Systems Agency (DISA) Approved Products List (APL) and be Joint Interoperability 
Test Command (JITC) approved.  
• Video Teleconference equipment must be searched as both terms; VTC and Uniﬁed 
Capabilities Conferencing Systems (UCCS) in the following DISA APL: 
https://aplits.disa.mil/processAPList.action.  
The contractor's responsibilities include: 
• Evaluating all existing A/V equipment against current security and compliance 
standards. 
• Replacing or upgrading components as required to meet the speciﬁcations outlined 
in this SOW. 
• Installing, integrating, programming, and testing all new equipment. 
• Providing comprehensive documentation and user training. 

• Delivering ongoing preventative maintenance and on-call support services. 
3.0 Technical Requirements 
3.1. System Security and Compliance 
Governing Standards: Cybersecurity requirements will be governed by the DISA Risk 
Management Executive (RME) Vendor Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIG) 
program. Interoperability requirements will be identiﬁed by the Uniﬁed Capabilities 
Requirements (UCR)-CORE document.  
(Please note: DISA APL has been sunset, so it is no longer the standard. Moving forward, 
cybersecurity requirements will transition to the DISA RME Vendor Security Technical 
Implementation Guides (STIG) program, while interoperability requirements will be 
identiﬁed by the Uniﬁed Capabilities Requirements (UCR)-CORE document and enforced 
through contractual provisions.) 
• Prohibited Technology: The system is non-radio. No components shall be enabled 
for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or any other wireless communication method. 
• Secure/Non-Secure Status: The existing secure/non-secure marquee indicators, 
both inside and outside the room, shall remain operational. 
• UPS Replacement: The rack UPS needs to be replaced to meet AF compliance. 
Smart Online UPS required to include Double Conversion feature, Utilizing current 
wall sockets and voltages in room 203.   
3.2. Hardware and Equipment Upgrades 
• Cameras: There are currently two cameras. A CISCO Precision 60 PTZ for SIPR & a 
recent QSC NC-20-60 PTZ for NIPR via Fiber.  
• The CISCO camera may need to be replaced with High deﬁnition PTZ camera 
that has two ports. One for SIPR GVS and one for adding SIPR TEAMS laptop 
app. Recommend QSC NC-20-60 so, matches current NIPR camera in looks, 
speciﬁcations and functionality.  
• Will consider alternate compatible business class PTZ camera’s that 
speciﬁcations are equivalent or better. 
• CODEC: The VTC CODEC for the classiﬁed and unclassiﬁed system shall be 
replaced with a modern, compliant equivalent that supports IP-based connections 
and unclassiﬁed Voice over IP (VoIP) audioconferencing. 

• All replacements must be a DISA approved product and compatible with the 
existing system. VTC unit can connect via Internet Protocol (IP) 
• In addition, it has the ability for Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) 
connections for unclassiﬁed audioconferencing. The audioconferencing is 
programmed to be disabled for classiﬁed conferences. 
• Operator Display Upgrade:  
Note: Operator desk currently has one GFE furnished 32in ViewSonic computer 
display as that is the largest ﬁt for console.  It shall be replaced with two monitors of 
desktop standard viewing size or larger. 
• Upgrade operator area display hardware & program conﬁguration so, any 
display output can be shown on any room display independently and 
simultaneously.  
• Ability to see Main desktop display presentations or communication apps 
and extended display separately simultaneously on front screens, that will 
mirror operator desk monitors.  
• The ability for operators to work on local desktop displays will not be seen by 
attendees so the operator can research questions or check emails.  
 
• Credenza: If current AV cabinet cannot properly be reconﬁgured to house all 
required equipment and ensure that the temperature does not exceed the device's 
maximum MFR operating temperature limits then, the contractor’s proposal will 
provide estimate for a new locking credenza on casters with built in racks.  After 
Award of contract, the credenza design, material and color must be pre-approved by 
the Government ES POC prior to purchase. Shall have proper AC voltages and surge 
protection available where UPS is not utilized. Use existing AV racks for audio-visual 
equipment that can be locked in a rack system. 
 
3.3. Control System and User Interface 
• Touch Panels: 
• If touch panel replacement is required for compatibility, new screens no 
smaller than 10 inches shall be installed. The existing design, coloring, and 
icon style of the touch panel interface shall not be changed without 
Government consent (21.5 in at Operator desk & 10.1in at conference table.)  

• The ES logo on the touch panels must be updated, and the time display must 
be set to Eastern Standard Time. This feature should be user-friendly for 
future modiﬁcations. 
• SIPR Teams Integration: The newly introduced SIPR Teams audio/video signal data 
will come from DoD SIPR laptop connected at operator console and shall be wired 
and programmed into AV rack/touch panel system.  
• May require adding a (3rd Freeport SCC unit to current periods processing 
system.) 
• Camera Control: The control system must allow the SVTC camera to be turned 
on/off and have its presets utilized without interrupting active service. 
• White Noise System: One white noise system with a minimum of two white noise 
speakers mounted on the outside of each door, wired safely in/thru wall with the 
ability to turn on and off from inside the room. The volume level to the white noise is 
adjustable from inside the room, if able to automate into AV system. No Bluetooth, 
wireless, or Wi-Fi system/speaker exist or are allowed. 
3.4. Cabling and Installation 
• The contractor shall provide all cables, connectors, power strips, power supplies, 
and miscellaneous materials required for a complete installation. All wiring at the 
A/V desk must be professionally managed and bundled. 
4.0 Contractor Deliverables 
• System Documentation: The contractor shall produce and develop supporting 
documentation, diagrams, and artifacts for all system modiﬁcations and 
replacements. 
• Source Code: Uncompiled CRESTRON source code shall be delivered in a DISC to 
the Government. (It should be uncompiled so that it can be edited in the future if 
you ever need to get the system updated with new components or add a capability 
like secure VTC etc.) 
• Diagrams: Signal ﬂow diagrams (for Audio, Video, and Control) and wiring 
schematics shall be provided in both PDF and large-format prints. All equipment 
and wiring must be clearly labeled. (Signal ﬂow diagrams should include separate 
sheets for 1) AUDIO 2) VIDEO 3) CONTROL Coding (raw code). Wiring Schematics- 
Label equipment and wiring. 

• Equipment Disposal: The contractor is responsible for the removal and disposal of 
all broken, unserviceable, or replaced components.  
• Purchase and Install: All new equipment included as needed after receiving 
approval from the Government representative. The government will need to be 
informed if any equipment is backordered or will not arrive on time for installation. 
• Training: The contractor shall provide training and orientation for at least two 
Government individuals on the use of all new equipment and system functionalities. 
5.0 Service and Support Requirements 
• Service Calls: A one-hour remote response time is required for all service calls, 
Monday-Friday, 0800-1800 ET. 
• On-site Support: If requested, the contractor must provide on-site support for 
troubleshooting and maintenance within one business day. It is expected that the 
assigned technician will be local to meet this requirement. Additionally, the 
technician will ensure installation, integration, programming and testing of the new 
equipment is up to customer standards. 
• Preventative Maintenance: The contractor shall perform preventative maintenance 
twice annually on a mutually agreed upon schedule. 
• Service Hours: The estimated yearly service commitment is 16 hours. 
6.0 Period of Performance and Warranty 
• Period of Performance: The contract will consist of one (1) base year plus four (4) 
one-year option periods, commencing promptly after the contract is awarded, with 
no break in service between periods. 
• System Warranty: If replacement equipment or hardware is required, the contractor 
shall provide a one-year warranty on all equipment and systems installed, effective 
from the date of installation. This warranty applies to the base year and all exercised 
option years. 
  

Appendix A: Current Equipment Inventory 
The following is a non-exhaustive list of equipment currently installed in the VTC/AV system. 
The contractor is responsible for maintaining or replacing this equipment to meet the 
requirements of this SOW. Equipment is not required to be brand name, but must be equal 
in quality, function, compatibility with the overarching system, and meet the security 
standards set out in Section 2.0.

Statement of Work (SOW) 
Sole Source License and Maintenance – Careware Nurse Self-Scheduling and Productivity 
System 
 
1. Purpose 
The purpose of this acquisition is to provide continued licensing, maintenance, and support for 
the Careware Nurse Self-Scheduling and Productivity System currently deployed within the NIH 
Clinical Center Nursing Department.  This system improves efficiency in generating monthly 
staff schedules and provides critical data to support budgetary planning and staffing decisions.  
This is a sole source requirement to ensure uninterrupted system availability and operational 
continuity  
 
2. Background 
The National Institutes of Health (NIH), within the U.S. Department of Health and Human 
Services (HHS), operates the Clinical Center (CC) in Bethesda, Maryland—the nation’s largest 
hospital dedicated to clinical research. 
The Clinical Center Nursing Department includes approximately 701 FTEs, 3-day hospitals, over 
19 outpatient clinics, and approximately 14 inpatient units supporting continuous (24/7/365) 
clinical operations.  The primary mission of the Nursing Department is to support clinical 
research by delivering compassionate, evidence-based nursing care to a diverse population of 
patients and their families, while ensuring safe, high quality patient care.   
The Careware system is currently used to: 
• Develop and manage nursing staff schedules  
• Support workload balancing and staffing level optimization  
• Supporting adequate staffing levels and skill mix  
• Reducing risks associated with understaffing or staff fatigue  
• Enhance overall patient care quality.   
• Provide data for staffing, budgeting, and operational decision-making  
• Enhance operational effectiveness, improve outcomes and reduce waste.  
The system is fully integrated into current nursing workflows and operations. 
 
3. Objective 

The objective of this requirement is to maintain full operational capability of the existing 
Careware system through continued licensing, maintenance, and technical support without 
interruption. 
 
4. Scope of Work 
The Contractor (Care Systems) shall provide all necessary licenses, maintenance, and support 
services required to sustain the existing Careware Nurse Self-Scheduling and Productivity 
System. 
The Contractor shall: 
• Provide nurse self-scheduling and productivity system that functions as a single, 
integrated solution.  
• Ensure the system remains fully operational, is reliable and continues to meet existing 
performance requirements.  
• Provide software updates, patches, and bug fixes as released  
• Provide all required software licenses for continued system use  
• Provide technical support, including troubleshooting and issue resolution  
• Maintain compatibility with the current NIH Clinical Center environment  
No system reconfiguration, redesign, or new implementation is required under this effort. 
 
5. Sole Source Justification (Operational Context) 
The Clinical Center Nursing Department operates in a fast-paced and highly complex clinical 
environment, where efficient workforce management is critical to ensuring safe, high-quality 
patient care.  The need for a comprehensive scheduling and productivity system is essential to 
effectively manage nursing staff, optimize workloads, and maintain appropriate staffing levels 
across patient care units.  This type of system also provides productivity data the informs budget 
planning and contributes to cost-effective decision making.   
Care Systems is the original developer and sole provider of the Careware system. As the system 
is fully implemented and integrated into daily nursing operations, continuation with the current 
vendor eliminates the need for additional installation, data migration, transition or training costs.   
It also ensures support for critical staff functions as well as reduced operational costs associated 
with staff retraining or potential disruption to patient care services. Continued support by the 
original vendor is required to: 
• Ensure uninterrupted access to proprietary software and licensing  
• Maintain system integrity and data continuity  
• Avoid unacceptable risk to clinical operations caused by system disruption  

• Prevent additional costs and delays associated with transitioning to an alternate vendor 
during ongoing operations  
No other vendor can provide the required proprietary licenses, maintenance, and support services 
for the existing system. 
 
6. Contract Type and Period of Performance 
• Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP)  
• Period of Performance: July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027  
 
7. Hours of Operation 
The NIH Clinical Center operates 24 hours per day, 365 days per year. 
The Contractor shall provide maintenance and support services on a 24/7/365 basis, including all 
Federal holidays. 
The ten Federal holidays currently observed are: 
• New Year’s Day  
• Martin Luther King, Jr. Day  
• Washington’s Birthday (Presidents Day)  
• Memorial Day  
• Juneteenth National Independence Day  
• Independence Day  
• Labor Day  
• Columbus Day  
• Veterans Day  
• Thanksgiving Day  
• Christmas Day  
This also includes any additional day declared a Federal holiday by the President of the United 
States. 
 
 
8. Place of Performance 
Primary place of performance: 

NIH Clinical Center 
9000 Rockville Pike 
Building 10 
Bethesda, MD 20892 
Services may be performed remotely as appropriate. 
 
9. Security Requirements 
All Contractor personnel must obtain and maintain an NIH Contractor Badge, including 
completion of background investigations and required annual training. 
The Contractor shall: 
• Safeguard all Government systems, data, and property  
• Comply with NIH security and access control policies  
• Ensure proper control of any Government-issued credentials or access devices  
 
10. Government Oversight 
The Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) will provide technical oversight and monitor 
Contractor performance. 
COR: 
Teresa McDivitt 
NIH Clinical Center Nursing Department 
The Government may conduct periodic performance reviews at no additional cost. 
 
11. Data Rights 
All data generated, maintained, or processed under this contract remains the property of the 
Government. 
The Contractor shall not use, disclose, or distribute Government data without prior written 
approval from the Contracting Officer. 
 
12. Organizational Conflict of Interest 

The Contractor shall comply with FAR Subpart 9.5 and disclose any actual or potential 
Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI). Mitigation plans must be submitted for Government 
approval.

National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)

Distributed Antenna System (DAS) Service Agreement

INTRODUCTION

The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases' (NIAID) Operations and Engineering Branch (OEB) of the Office of Cyber Infrastructure and Computational Biology (OCICB) manages and develops the technology infrastructure that supports Intramural research, Extramural investments and Administrative management, providing services for 4000+ end users in more than 20 locations throughout the United States.

This is a commercial services contract to provide a year of maintenance for the DAS at the Integrated Research Facility (IRF) at Fort Detrick in Frederick Maryland.

BACKGROUND

The IRF biomedical research facility has a Neutral Host In-Building Wideband Cellular DAS that provides building wide cellular and VHF radio signal coverage.  The system was upgraded in 2024 with new DAS infrastructure to bring the technology up to current standards and provide expansion capabilities.

The system enhances emergency communications for staff and NIH Police by supporting both commercial cellular networks and public safety communications.  The system also minimizes coverage gaps in critical areas like stairwells and the buffer corridor outside the BSL4 laboratories that might delay emergency response times and potentially endangering lives.

SCOPE

The scope of this effort includes maintenance of the DAS to provide technical services to regularly access, evaluate, report and restore the DAS in the event of a system failure.

A summary of the key activities include:

Maintain onsite spare parts

Support services

Response times

REQUIREMENTS

Maintain onsite spare parts.  These spare parts shall be utilized by the contractor to restore system to operational status.  The contractor will repair or replace defective parts and add them back to the onsite parts kit.  NIAID will stock the spare parts initially and then it is the contractor’s responsibility to fix or replace parts that are used.  See Appendix A – Bill of Materials for list of required onsite spare parts.

Support Services.  Provide maintenance and support for DAS.  This includes software upgrades and modifications as specified by the manufacturer; telephone, email and internet technical support; support staff training on the daily operation and troubleshooting of system; and integration services for automated monitoring of system faults.  Please see Appendix A for equipment associated with DAS system.

Response Times.  Times are as follows:

Equipment will be maintained at industry standards/manufacturer specifications.

Contractor shall be responsible for all labor and materials necessary to maintain the DAS.

Quarterly Preventative Maintenance Visits are required.

PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: The period of performance shall be for one (1) Base Year of 12 months and three (3) 12-month option years.  The Period of Performance reads as follows:

Base Year

Option Year 1

Option Year 2

Option Year 3

CONTRACTING OFFICER REPRESENTATIVE (COR):

The (COR) will be identified by separate letter.  The COR is responsible for: (1) monitoring the Contractor's technical progress, including the surveillance and assessment of performance and recommending to the Contracting Officer changes in requirements; (2) interpreting the statement of work and any other technical performance requirements; (3) performing technical evaluation as required; (4) performing technical inspections and acceptances required by this contract; and (5) assisting in the resolution of technical problems encountered during performance.

The Contracting Officer is the only person with authority to act as agent of the Government under this contract.  Only the Contracting Officer has authority to: (1) direct or negotiate any changes in the statement of work; (2) modify or extend the period of performance; (3) change the delivery schedule; (4) authorize reimbursement to the Contractor for any costs incurred during the performance of this contract; (5) otherwise change any terms and conditions of this contract; or (6) sign written licensing agreements.  Any signed agreement shall be incorporated by reference in the contract.  The Government may unilaterally change its COR designation.

HOURS OF OPERATION

The contractor is responsible for conducting business, between the hours of 7:30AM – 4:00PM Monday through Friday except Federal holidays or when the Government facility is closed due to local or national emergencies, administrative closings, or other Government directed facility closings.

NOTE:  The IRF operates 24 hours a day seven days a week when experiments are running.

New Year’s Day	Labor Day

Martin Luther King Jr.’s Birthday	Columbus Day

President’s Day	Veteran’s Day

Memorial Day	Thanksgiving Day

Juneteen	Independence Day

Christmas Day

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

These services will be provided at the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) Integrated Research Facility (IRF) at Fort Detrick in Frederick, Maryland.

GOVERNMENT QUALITY ASSURANCE AND MONITORING OF WORK

All work under this contract shall be monitored by the COR, who will act as the primary representative of the Government.  Final inspection and acceptance of all work performed, reports and other deliverables will be performed by the COR.  In the absence of the COR, an alternate Point of Contact (POC) will be designated, and the Contracting Officer will provide final inspection and acceptance.

EVALUATION CRITERIA

NIAID will evaluate all quotes to determine the best value to the government.  NIAID will make a Best Value Determination based on the capability of each offeror’s quote to meet the brand name technical specifications, past performance, providing the proposed products/service in a timely manner, and reasonable price.  Technical specifications include: the BOM specifications.  The Government’s objective is to obtain the highest technical quality considered necessary to achieve the project objectives, with a realistic and reasonable cost.  Technical and past performance non-price factors are considered equal and are more important than price.  In the event quotes are evaluated as technically equal in quality, price or cost will become a major consideration in selecting the successful Offeror.

SECURITY REQUIREMENTS

The Government will require Tier 2- Public Trust level investigations for performance of this project.  The offeror must submit the required forms, complete the online eQIP submission and have a favorably adjudicated SAC (fingerprints) before beginning work on the task order (NIH will not allow contract employees without some level of investigation in any of its facilities).  The offeror must obtain these background investigation submissions by using the NIH eQIP system.  If these requirements cannot be met with the offeror, the offer will be disqualified.

Offeror personnel are required to have background investigations for suitability to work on the IRF campus, and must pass a background check by the U.S. Army in order to access the IRF facility which is located on a secure U.S. Army military base, Fort Detrick, MD. Requirements for non-U.S. citizens are: Non-US citizens must complete the IRF foreign national (FN) visitor information request form 10 business days prior to the visit.  The non-US citizens must bring a current passport, green card, or other approved identification.  These visitors must be escorted by an NIH badge holder starting at the Nallin visitor center and then for the duration of the visit.

All necessary facility and/or staff background investigation submissions must be complete prior to start of work on the task order.

This Sources Sought Notice is for planning purposes only and shall not be considered as an

the Government to acquire any products or services described herein.  Your response to this

contract vehicle that will provide contractor support for Naval Information Warfighting 
Development Center (NIWDC) in support of the Electronic Warfare Database (EWD).  This is an

to support Naval Information Warfighting Development Center (NIWDC) Electronic Warfare 
Database (EWD) professional, technical, and administrative support.

SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE 
 
INTRODUCTION 
 
This Sources Sought Notice is for planning purposes only and shall not be considered as an 
Invitation for Bid, Request for Quotation, Request for Proposal or as an obligation on the part of 
the Government to acquire any products or services described herein.  Your response to this 
sources sought will be treated as information only.  No entitlement to payment of direct or 
indirect costs or charges to the government's use of such information.  This request does not 
constitute a solicitation for proposals or the authority to enter into negotiations to award a 
contract.  No funds have been authorized, appropriated or received by the Government for this 
Sources Sought Notice.  The information provided by contractors may be used by the Navy in 
developing its acquisition strategy, Performance Work Statement (PWS) and/or Performance 
Specifications. 
 
Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive 
information contained in their response.  The Government does not intend to award a contract on 
the basis of this Sources Sought notice or to otherwise pay for the information submitted in 
response to this Sources Sought notice. 
 
BACKGROUND 
 
Naval Supply Systems Command (NA VSUP) Fleet Logistics Center (FLC) Norfolk is seeking 
information on qualified and experienced sources for planning purposes in an effort to derive a 
contract vehicle that will provide contractor support for Naval Information Warfighting 
Development Center (NIWDC) in support of the Electronic Warfare Database (EWD).  This is an 
ongoing requirement where NIWDC has utilized contractor support at respective Command 
locations to perform professional, technical, and administrative support for the cybersecurity 
operations within the current Amazon Web Services (AWS) Information Level 6 (IL6) certified 
environment comprised of two Elastic Cloud Compute instances and one integrated cloud-based 
Development Operations (DEVOPS) environment.  Anticipated requirements for the 
continuation of this requirement can be found in the draft Performance Work Statement included 
within the Sources Sought. 
 
The Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) Fleet Logistics Center (FLC) Norfolk is 
issuing this Sources Sought as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having 
an interest in and the resources to support the requirement for a non-personal services contract 
to support Naval Information Warfighting Development Center (NIWDC) Electronic Warfare 
Database (EWD) professional, technical, and administrative support. 
 
ELIGIBILITY 
 
The purpose of this sources sought notice is to identify authorized and verified sources of 
services for an anticipated Firm Fixed-Price services contract under NAICS code 541512 
Computer Systems Design Services with a Small Business Size Standard of $34.0 (millions of 

dollars). The Product Service Code is DB02 IT and telecom - compute support services, non-hpc 
(labor).  The proposed contract vehicle will provide all the required supplies and support 
services.  Small Businesses are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly 
identify their business size in their capabilities statement. 
 
A draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) which entails tasks, personnel qualifications, and 
deliverables are attached for review (Attachment 1). 
 
Reponses to this Sources Sought Notice shall reference the Opportunity Name “NIWDC-EWD 
Support” and shall include the following information in this format: 
 
1. Company name, address point of contact name, phone number, and email address.  
 
2. Contractor, Government Entity (CAGE) Code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). 
 
3. Size of Business - Large Business, Small Business, 8(a), HubZone, Woman-Owned Small Business, 
Economically Disadvantaged Woman-Owned Small Business, and/or Service Disabled Veteran-
Owned Small Business. 
 
4.  Capability Statement displaying the contractor’s experience and ability to provide the 
minimum requirements of the PWS to include past performance information.  If past 
performance information is used, please include only relevant information on the 
same/similar work within the last five (5) years. 
 
5. Include any other supporting documentation to include your Seaport-NxG and or GSA 
contract number and contracting experience under Seaport-NxG or GSA task orders 
awarded, task order number, award date, dollar value, period of performance/lead time for 
delivery, sub or prime, and brief description for each contract referenced. 
 
6. Proof/Verification that contractor possesses a current TS/SCI Facilities clearance. 
 
7.  Provide any questions, comments, feedback, regarding the NAICS, draft PWS, or any other 
associated information.  
 
8.  Provide any current government wide contract with GSA or Seaport. 
 
Standard company brochures will not be reviewed. Submissions are not to exceed five (5) pages 
in length in Times New Roman font of not less than 12-point font.  
 
The Government is still determining the acquisition strategy and if this acquisition will be a 
small business set-aside, then FAR clause 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, applies.  
Note that if there is sufficient demonstrated interest and capability among small businesses, a 
key factor in determining if an acquisition will be a small business set-aside is that two or more 
potential small business prime contractors must be capable of performing at least 50% of the 
effort, as defined in FAR clause 52.219-14.  If it is determined that a small business set-aside is 
appropriate and your company anticipates submitting a proposal as the prime contractor for a 

small business set-aside, please provide specific details and rationale as to how compliance with 
FAR clause 52.219-14 would be achieved, including specific details regarding teaming 
arrangements, and if subcontracts are to be used, provide anticipated percentage of the effort to 
be subcontracted and whether small or large business subcontractors will be used.  Teaming 
and/or subcontracting arrangements should be clearly delineated and previous experience in 
teaming must be provided. 
 
This is not a solicitation announcement for proposals and no contract will be awarded from this 
announcement.  This sources sought notice is not to be construed in any way as a commitment 
by the Government, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response. 
 
The deadline for responses to this request is no later than 11 AM, EST 7 May 2026.  
All responses under this Sources Sought Notice shall be emailed to Justin Hall
