NATO UNCLASSIFIED  
PP.A2(07.25)   NATO UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
 
 
NCIA Request for Information (RFI) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 GOVERNANCE, RISK, AND COMPLIANCE TOOL 
RFI-07119-GRC 
 
 
 
 


 NATO UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
  
NATO UNCLASSIFIED Page 2 
 
 
 
NCIA/ACQ/2026/07119 
Thursday, 07 May 2026 
 
NCIA Request for Information (RFI) 
 
To: Industry Partners 
 
  
1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) is conducting market 
research to identify qualified vendors and gather input on potential solutions to support the 
upcoming acquisition for  a Commercial -Off-The-Shelf (COTS) Governance, Risk, and 
Compliance (GRC) tool. To that end, we are issuing the attached Request for Information 
(RFI) 07119 to solicit feedback from capable and interested industry partners. 
 
2. This RFI is issued for planning purposes only and is not a request for bids . It is part of 
NCIA’s effort to ensure it has a clear understanding of the marketplace, available 
capabilities, and potential acquisition strategies. 
 
3. We value your insight and invite you to: 
a. Share relevant corporate capabilities and experience; 
b. Review and comment on our draft requirements (Annexes A and B) with a view in 
providing recommendations for improving performance outcomes,  competition, 
and efficiency; and identify ing any risks or concerns that should be considered 
during planning. 
 
4. Submission instructions and additional details can be found in the enclosure to this RFI. 
 
5. Only companies from a NATO member country can participate in or respond to this RFI 
(https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/nato_countries.htm). 
 
6. Should you have any questions or need clarification, please contact Esteban DIAZ at 
Esteban.Diaz@ncia.nato.int. 
 
7. We thank you in advance for your time and input, and we look forward to engaging with 
you as we shape this potential acquisition.

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION  
 
A. Introduction 
 
1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NC IA) is conducting market 
research to identify potential sources and gather information regarding industry 
capabilities to suppor t a Commercial -Off-The-Shelf (COTS) solution to meet the 
requirements provided in this document for a Governance, Risk and Compliance tool. 
This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for informational purposes and does 
not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or invitation 
for bid.  
 
B. Purpose 
 
1. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain input from industry to help inform the NCIA’s 
acquisition planning. Responses to this RFI will assist in refining requirements, 
identifying capabilities, and shaping the strategy for any future solicitation. 
 
C. Background 
 
1. NCIA is seeking an automated solution to synchronize the risk management and 
regulatory compliance processes that is adaptable based on the definition of security 
requirements coming from the NATO Policies and Directives. This includes providing 
the unified view of the enterprise IT related risks with flexible risk calculation, data 
visualization reporting, and dashboard capabilities.    
2. The NCIA provide, maintain and defend the NATO enterprise -wide information 
technology infrastructure to enable Allies to consult together and, when required, stand 
together in the face of attack. The environment in which we operate is evolving and 
the growing number of services across the enterprise requires more centralized 
solutions to aggregate all required data. The NCIA is looking for a system to efficiently 
and effectively calculate, manage, and track risk mitigations and compliance status, 
considering compliance challenges and risk-based assessment decisions. This must 
be done expeditiously before vulnerabilities can be exploited by an adversary. 
3. The sought GRC tool should enable smooth transition from a “static” approach to a 
dynamic “real-time” model, Everything as a code (EaC) and RegOps methodology. 
RegOps (Regulatory Operations) is a philosophy and methodology that applies 
DevOps principles – like automation, continuous integration, and collaboration – to 
the field of regulatory compliance.  
 
D. Submission Instructions 
 
1. Interested parties are invited to respond in accordance with the instructions below: 
 
a. Submit responses via the email address in section H no later than 12:00 hours 
Central European Time (CET) on 29 May 2026. 
 
b. Responses should be submitted in PDF or Word format and must not exceed 15 
pages, including: 
i. Responses to Annex A  
 
excluding: 
i. Cover page

c. Use the following subject line for submission 
i. “Response to RFI [RFI-07119-GRC] – [Company Name]” 
 
d. All responses should address the items listed in Annex A – Requested Information. 
 
 
E. Industry Engagement 
 
1. Industry day is not foreseen during this initial stage, however technical discussions via 
one-on-one virtual sessions may take place following the submission of responses, 
with the purpose of clarifying or further augmenting those responses where required. 
 
 
F. Disclaimer 
 
1. This RFI is for planning and informational purposes only and shall not be construed as 
a solicitation or obligation on the part of the NCIA. The NCIA does not intend to award 
a contract based on responses to this RFI. Respondents are solely responsible for all 
costs incurred in responding to this RFI.  The NCIA will consider and analyse all 
information received from this RFI and may use these findings to develop a future 
solicitation. The NCIA will consider all responses as confidential commercial 
information and will protect it as such. 
 
2. NCIA reserves the right, at any time, to cancel this informal market survey, partially or 
in its entirety. No legal liability on the part of NCIA for payment of any sort shall arise 
and in no event will a cause of action lie with any prospective participant for the 
recovery of any costs incurred in connection with the preparation of documentation or 
participation in response hereto. All effort initiated or undertaken by prospective 
informal market survey participants shall be done considering and accepting this fact.

THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ANNOUNCEMENT 
ONLY .  
 
REQUESTS FOR SOLICITATION WILL NOT RECEIVE A RESPONSE. 
 
This Sources Sought is in support of Market Research being conducted by the Alabama 
Army National Guard, and is issued for information and planning purposes only. This is 
not a Request for Proposal (or solicitation) or an indication that a contractual 
commitment will exist for this requirement. The Government does not intend to award a 
contract on the basis of this market research. 
 
The Alabama National Guard is requesting information, pursuant to FAR PART 10, to 
identify potential sources to procure Black Ohm SIGMA-X / Alpha GPS Physio Tracker 
Package listed below: 
 
• 10 each - BLK-7000556ALP-5Y/ Alpha Tracker & 5yrs Service 
• 1 each - BLK-ALPHA-CHG Charging Case/ Black Ohm Alpha Charging Case: 
Includes Alpha Charging Case with 25 tracker capacity  
• 190 each - BLK-703002SIG-X Personnel and Asset GPS Tracker with Global 
Commercial and Private Cellular connectivity, and field replaceable, hot 
swappable batteries.  
• 1 each - BLK-7000556MS-5Y Monitoring Laptop: Includes Ruggedized Laptop  
 
Estimated Delivery Date: 31 July 2026  
 
The proposed North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) Code is 518210, 
Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related 
Services, which has a corresponding Size Standard of – $40.0M.  
 
The Government is interested in all small businesses. The Government requests that 
interested parties respond to this notice if applicable and identify your business status 
to the identified NAICS code. 
 
Additionally, please provide any anticipated teaming arrangements, along with a 
description of similar products offered to the Government and to commercial 
customers for the past three years.  Any responses involving teaming agreements 
should delineate between the work that will be accomplished by the prime, and the 
work accomplished by the teaming partners. 
 
1. Responses should include the following information: 
a. Company Name and Address 
b. Cage Code 
c. UEI Number 
d. Company business size by NAICS code 
e. Small Business Type (s), if applicable 
f. Point of Contact for questions and/or clarification 

g. Telephone Number, fax number, and email address 
h. Web Page URL 
i. Teaming Partners (if applicable) 
 
If you are an interested party who can provide some, but not all of the requested 
services/supplies, please explain the limiting factors (e.g., Global Commercial and 
Private Cellular connectivity, etc.). 
Responses must be submitted via email to amelia.p.davis.civ@army.miland 
stephen.shanks.1@us.af.mil . 
Responses are due no later than: May 19, 2025 @ 12pm CDT. 
Note: No facsimile responses will be honored. 
 
Provide any recommendations and/or concerns.

NAICS: 541511 – Custom Computer Programming Services
Size Standard: $34.0M

4. Description

The Department of Veterans Affairs, VISN 12, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 12, intends to issue a sole-source purchase order to Stoelting Co., the exclusive authorized U.S. distributor of the Ugo Basile G.A.I.T. (Gait Analysis and Imaging Tool) system. This acquisition is for a commercial, integrated gait-analysis platform required by the William S. Middleton Memorial VA Medical Center, Madison, WI, for execution of a MERIT-funded traumatic brain injury (TBI) research project.

The G.A.I.T. system provides simultaneous ventral and lateral high-resolution imaging, automated AI-driven gait detection, and artifact correction essential for post-TBI locomotion analysis in mice. Market research confirms that no other vendor can meet the required technical specifications, and no verified VOSB/SDVOSB or U.S. manufacturer provides an equivalent product. As the system qualifies as an IT commercial product, the IT exception to the Buy American statute applies.

5. Sole Source Justification

Stoelting Co. is the only authorized U.S. distributor of the Ugo Basile G.A.I.T. system. No alternative system offers the required dual-view imaging and AI-based artifact correction capabilities necessary for accurate motor-function evaluation in TBI mouse models. Other available systems rely on single-view imaging or threshold-based detection and cannot meet research requirements. The VA Rule of Two cannot be met, as no VOSB/SDVOSB sources provide or distribute this product. Additionally, the Nonmanufacturer Rule cannot be satisfied for a set-aside. Therefore, an unrestricted, sole-source award is required.

The 42d Contracting Squadron, on behalf of the 23rd Flying Training Squadron at Cairns AAF, Fort Rucker, AL, is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing a complete, turnkey audio-visual (AV) system upgrade for Baker Auditorium and expanding AV capabilities into the adjacent Heritage Room.

The Government requires a contractor to engineer, de-install the existing outdated equipment, furnish, install, and integrate a modern, non-proprietary AV solution. The new system must provide multi-zone audio/video management, secure briefing isolation capabilities, and user-friendly control for both local presentations and Unified Communications (UC) events (e.g., MS Teams). The full scope of work, including all required performance capabilities and extensive system documentation requirements, is detailed in the attached draft Statement of Requirements (SOR).

NOTES OF IMPORTANCE:

A solicitation does not exist for this requirement. This is only a sources sought synopsis, so please do not submit proposals. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on this sources sought.

If the Government decides to pursue a solicitation, portions of your responses to this sources sought may be incorporated into the final solicitation. Respondents are discouraged from submitting any information deemed competition-sensitive or proprietary.

Respondents will not be reimbursed for any costs incurred in responding to this sources sought. Information submitted will not be returned to the respective respondents.

Oral submissions of information will not be considered in response to this sources sought.

To assist the Government in developing a potential acquisition strategy, please provide the following information:

1. GENERAL INFORMATION:

Company name, address, point of contact, voice and fax telephone numbers and email address. 

Type of business, (i.e., small, small disadvantaged, woman-owned, Hub Zone, serviced-disabled veteran-owned small business, large business, etc.), under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 541519 which contains a size standard of 150 EMP., CAGE Code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI).

Under which NAICS code does your company usually provide the requirements described above. Please provide rationale for your answer if different from NAICS 541519.

Please describe any customary commercial contract terms or conditions that you feel would make any resulting contract more effective if applicable.

2. CAPABILITIES: The Government is seeking qualified, experienced sources interested in meeting the requirements of the attached draft SOR. Please address the following regarding your capabilities in meeting the requirements detailed in the attached draft SOR:

Is your company capable of meeting this requirement in accordance with the attached draft SOR? If so, please provide your company’s capability statement.

3. RESPONSES: Interested vendors must e-mail responses to this sources sought to the points of contact identified below. The due date and time for responses to this sources sought is at 12:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on 13 May 2026.

1st Lt John Putnam (Contract Specialist) @john.putnam.8@us.af.mil (334)953-8083

Statement of Requirements
Audio Visual System Upgrade and Expansion for Baker Auditorium
23rd Flying Training Squadron, Cairns AAF, Ft Rucker, Alabama

PURPOSE. 

The purpose of this requirement is to upgrade and refresh the audio-visual (AV) system in Building 30137 Auditorium (Baker Auditorium) and expand AV capabilities into the adjacent Heritage Room (Hover Hole). Baker Auditorium is essential to squadron daily operations and is used for special events as well (training days, assignment release celebrations, retirement ceremonies, All calls, etc.) Baker Auditorium does not have the seating capacity for the entire squadron, therefore the Heritage Room is used for overflow seating and needs systems to share audio and video with that space as well. The project will replace outdated, proprietary equipment with a modern, non-proprietary system that does not require certified technicians for future upgrades or maintenance, ensuring seamless integration, secure multi-zone management, Unified Communications (UC) capabilities, and user-friendly control for presentations, briefings, and events. 

2.0   APPLICABLE PUBLICATIONS AND REGULATIONS. 

All work shall comply with the most recent versions of the following industry and federal standards:


2.1 National Electrical Code (NEC) / NFPA 70.

2.2 Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) applicable to telecommunications and interior electrical systems.


2.3 Standard commercial AV installation best practices (AVIXA/INFOCOMM standards).

3.0   DESCRIPTION OF ITEMS.
The following items are required for performance under this contract:

3.0.1 'Or Equal' Substitutions: Where a brand name is specified followed by 'or equal', the proposed substitute must meet or exceed the technical specifications of the named product. Furthermore, the substitute must offer native, seamless integration with the primary control system (e.g., Q-SYS) via established plugins or open APIs, without requiring complex middleware or custom programming that increases long-term maintenance costs.

3.1   Baker Auditorium AV System Upgrade

3.1.1 De-Installation: Remove the existing Crestron touch screen controller, in-ceiling speakers, amplifier, input selector, projector, and 12ft electric projector screen. All removed equipment shall be neatly palletized or staged in a location designated by the Government POC within Building 30137.

3.1.2 Projector: One (1) short-throw laser projector, brand name “or equal” to Epson or Optoma, with a minimum of 4K resolution and 5,000+ lumens.

3.1.3 Projector Screen: One (1) new 12ft wide electric projector screen with motorized up/down functionality, compatible with the new projector.

3.1.4 Audio System:

3.1.4.1 Non-proprietary, high-quality in-ceiling speakers (e.g., JBL, Yamaha, or equal).

3.1.4.2 New amplifier compatible with the speaker system.

3.1.4.3 Two (2) in-ceiling microphones (flush-mount or hanging) installed near the stage for speaking area coverage.

3.1.4.4 Wireless Microphones: One (1) professional dual-channel wireless microphone system (brand name "or equal" to Shure QLX-D or Sennheiser EW-DX). The system shall include a rack-mounted dual receiver and two (2) handheld wireless microphones. Must include a compatible networked charging station and rechargeable batteries.

3.1.5 Speaker Prompt TV: One (1) flat-screen TV (appropriately sized for the wall, ~55”-65”) mounted on the back wall for speaker prompts.

3.1.6 PTZ Camera:  One (1) Pan-Tilt-Zoom (PTZ) camera with AI-powered presenter auto-tracking (brand name “or equal” to BirdDog P240, AVer TR333V2, or Panasonic AW-UE series). Minimum specifications: 

3.1.6.1 1080p resolution (4K preferred).
3.1.6.2 Minimum 20x optical zoom. 
3.1.6.3 Built-in AI auto-tracking (no lanyards required).
3.1.6.4 HDMI and IP/NDI streaming outputs.
3.1.6.5 Software or physical privacy mode.

3.1.7 Control System: One (1) professional AV-over-IP control processor (brand name "or equal" to QSC Q-SYS Core Nano) and one (1) dedicated, PoE-powered touch screen controller. The system must be capable of managing independent audio/video zones, input selection, and secure isolation logic. The system must allow Baker Auditorium to securely isolate its AV feeds from the Heritage Room and other outputs during classified or private briefings, including any cameras installed.

3.1.8 Inputs: System must incorporate Government-furnished equipment: wireless microphone receiver, DVD/Blu-ray player, Apple TV, standalone PC, and a secondary PC/laptop input (HDMI).

3.1.9 Unified Communications (UC) & Streaming Integration: The system must include USB AV bridging capabilities.

3.1.9.1 Primary Host PC: Provide a USB connection at the primary presentation location that delivers the room's mixed audio (microphones) and selected video feed (PTZ camera or presentation) to a host laptop for use with software codecs (e.g., MS Teams).

3.1.9.2 Secondary Streaming PC: Provide a secondary, independent output (USB or HDMI with capture card) to allow a second PC to receive the room's AV feed for social media streaming or recording.

3.1.9.3 VTC Readiness: The system architecture must be capable of integrating a future dedicated hardware VTC codec (e.g., Cisco, Poly) without requiring total system redesign.

3.1.10 Equipment Rack: Utilize the existing equipment rack. If the existing rack is not feasible, the offeror shall note this in their response. See optional add-on 3.3.5 for a new rack.

3.2 Heritage Room (Hover Hole) AV Expansion

3.2.1 Video & Audio Feed: Provide a reliable AV-over-IP or HDBaseT network solution to route the Baker Auditorium presentation and PTZ camera feed (video and audio) to the two existing TVs in the Heritage Room. 

3.2.2 Soundbars: Incorporate the two (2) existing soundbars and subwoofers, one for each TV, with local volume and mute control.

3.2.3 Secure Isolation / Local Control: The system must allow the Heritage Room to be isolated from its AV input/feeds from the Auditorium during classified or private briefings. Must include local input selection to incorporate an existing Apple TV device and a secondary PC/laptop input (HDMI or similar). Must include ability to output to other audio devices such as in-ceiling speakers or sound systems that may be installed in the future.

3.3 Optional Add-ons (Offeror to Provide Itemized Pricing)

3.3.1 Fixed Camera: Installation of a fixed camera for a wide view of the audience.

3.3.2 Heritage Room 4.1 Sound System: A 4.1 channel sound system with an independent receiver, Bluetooth, four satellite speakers, and one subwoofer, capable of independent operation as well as incorporation as an output from the Heritage Room controller.

3.3.3 Microphone Array Upgrade: Provide an itemized pricing option to upgrade the baseline in-ceiling microphones (listed in 2.1.4.3) to one (1) networked ceiling microphone array (brand name "or equal" to Shure MXA920 or Sennheiser TeamConnect Ceiling 2) with dynamic beamforming to provide seamless stage and audience coverage.

3.3.4 Video Windowing Processor: Provide an itemized pricing option for a seamless presentation switcher capable of compositing two video feeds together (Picture-in-Picture or Side-by-Side) before sending them to the projector, Teams host PC, and Streaming PC.

3.3.5 New Equipment Rack: Provide itemized pricing for one (1) new, taller equipment rack sufficient to house all required components.

4.0   DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS:

4.1 The project location is an auditorium and adjacent room. The building is a single story. The offeror is responsible for assessing site conditions, including access via doorways or any potential delivery obstacles.

4.2 All equipment shall be delivered to the place of performance:
Cairns Army Airfield
Building 30137 Auditorium and Heritage Room
Ft Rucker, Alabama 36362

5.0   INSTALLATION REQUIREMENTS:
The contractor shall design, procure, install, and integrate a fully functional AV system. This includes the de-installation of specified existing equipment. 

5.1 Facility Integrity and Safety:

5.1.1 Fire-Stopping: Any penetration in walls and ceilings made by the contractor must be appropriately fire-stopped to maintain the building's fire rating.

5.1.2 Damage Restoration: All damage to walls, floors, ceilings, or existing furnishings caused by the contractor must be repaired and restored to its original condition at no additional cost to the Government.

5.1.3 Electrical Safety: The contractor must utilize Ground Fault Circuit Interrupters (GFCI) for all portable power tools used during installation.

5.2 Cabling Standards: All new network cabling installed for AV-over-IP, HDBaseT, or control signal distribution must be, at a minimum, Shielded CAT6A (Category 6A STP) to support future bandwidth requirements. All cables must be plenum-rated where required by facility fire codes, dressed neatly using hook-and-loop fasteners (no zip ties), and clearly labeled at both ends. Any significant electrical work (e.g., installing new outlets) must be performed by a licensed electrician.

6.0   TRAINING REQUIREMENTS:
The contractor shall provide a minimum of two (2) hours of on-site training for Squadron personnel covering system operation, UC/Teams integration, independent room routing, secure isolation procedures, and basic troubleshooting.

7.0   SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION AND HANDOVER:
Upon completion of the installation and prior to final government acceptance, the contractor shall provide a comprehensive "System Hand-Off Package" to ensure continuity of operations.

7.1 The contractor shall provide this package in two formats:

a. One (1) physical binder to be kept with the equipment rack.

b. One (1) digital copy provided on a USB flash drive or CD/DVD.

7.2 The System Hand-Off Package must include, at a minimum, the following:

7.2.1 Uncompiled Source Code / Design Files: The native, editable project configuration file(s) for the AV control system and audio digital signal processor (e.g., the .qsys file). The government shall retain full ownership of these files without any proprietary lockouts.

7.2.2 System Credentials: A comprehensive list of all administrator usernames, passwords, and IP addresses for every networked component in the system (Control Core, Network Switches, PTZ Cameras, etc.).

7.2.3 As-Built Diagrams: Accurate, as-built line drawings showing all physical audio, video, and control wiring, as well as the logical network topology.

7.2.4 Equipment Inventory: A complete list of all installed equipment, including make, model, serial numbers, and MAC addresses.

7.2.5 Quick Start Guide: A customized, easy-to-understand instruction sheet for end-users on how to operate the system for daily use and secure briefings. Provide two (2) total, one (1) for Baker Auditorium and one (1) for the Heritage Room.

8.0   STANDARD WARRANTY:

8.1 Prior to project acceptance, the contractor shall provide the customer with all manufacturer warranties as needed for any component incorporated into this project such as equipment manuals, literature, CDs and DVDs and other documentation on all equipment and software.

Specifications and Salient Characteristics for Dell OEM Installation, Configuration, and Deployment Services

The VA Augusta Research Department purchased a Dell server and storage system that was designed and built by Dell to work only when Dell completes the installation and setup. Because the equipment is proprietary and engineered as a complete package, the system cannot be installed or configured by anyone other than Dell’s own certified technicians. These services must bring the newly purchased equipment online so researchers can use it for secure data work inside the VA network.

To meet the VA’s needs, Dell must physically install the server and storage equipment in the designated research server rooms, connect all components properly, verify that everything powers on and communicates correctly, and ensure the system is ready for configuration. Once installed, Dell must set the equipment up according to the specifications they designed, which includes preparing the storage system, loading the necessary software, updating it to the right versions, and making sure the server and storage communicate together as intended. These steps require Dell‑specific tools, knowledge, and access that only OEM technicians have.

The services must be completed onsite at the VA Augusta Health Care System in the Research Server Room (2C121) and the Communications Closet (5B). When the work is finished, the system must be fully usable, stable, and ready for researchers to begin working with data. Dell must also confirm everything is set up correctly before leaving and provide documentation that the installation and setup are complete.

These characteristics are essential because the VA must receive a system that is properly installed, configured, and ready to use without risking damage, malfunction, security issues, or loss of warranty. Only Dell can provide these services, and the VA requires the work to be completed directly by the manufacturer to ensure the equipment performs exactly as intended and meets all VA operational and security requirements.

PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), VHA, VISN 8 has a requirement for brand name Cleo Streem software licenses, installation, application maintenance and technical support. 

The required Cleo Streem solution provides secure network fax capabilities and electronic faxing to automate workflow utilizing secure faxing, secure file transfer, communications and messaging capabilities. As a standard solution at many VA facilities, the Cleo Streem solution can be seamlessly integrated with multifunctional devices as an alternative to analog faxing. This feature eliminates the need for analog phone lines and modems in the multifunctional devices. The Cleo Streem solution provides the ability to securely fax documents directly to and from the desktop, eliminating the need for excess usage of paper and consumables.

The Contractor shall provide technical support, project management services and training services to enable the solution contained. The Local VA Office of Information and Technology (OIT) will request two virtual servers configured with Windows Server 2019 or 2022 operating systems and will provide remote access to virtual servers and technical assistance as needed to Contractor personnel, who will perform the installation and testing of the solution remotely. OIT will also ensure that the required data feed from VA is sent securely to the Contractor’s servers. The virtual servers will be managed by the VA, and standard server maintenance (such as operating system patching, backups, and related tasks) will be performed by VA personnel.  The vendor will be responsible for supporting the application, in coordination with the Community Care application administrators. 

The Contractor will provide the following Software Maintenance:

Coverage: 24x7

Type of Support: Telephone, Email, Online & Updates

NOTICE OF THE FEDERAL ACCESSIBILITY LAW AFFECTING ALL INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) PROCUREMENTS (SECTION 508)

On January 18, 2017, the Access Board issued a final rule that updated accessibility requirements covered by Section 508 and refreshed guidelines for telecommunications equipment subject to Section 255 of the Communications Act.  The final rule went into effect on January 18, 2018.  The revisions and updates to the Section 508-based standards and Section 255-based guidelines are intended to ensure that information and communication technology (ICT) covered by the respective statutes is accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities.

SECTION 508 – INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) STANDARDS

The Section 508 standards established by the Access Board are incorporated into, and made part of all VA orders, solicitations and purchase orders developed to procure ICT.  These standards are found in their entirety at: Revised 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines (access-board.gov).  A single PDF file version of the Revised Section 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines will be supplied upon request, or can be obtained from the Access Board website.  Federal agencies must comply with the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended. 

The Contractor shall comply with “508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements” for all electronic ICT and content delivered under this contract. Specifically, as appropriate for the technology and its functionality, the Contractor shall comply with the technical standards marked here: 

	E205 Electronic Content – (Accessibility Standard -WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA Guidelines)

	E204 Functional Performance Criteria

	E206 Hardware Requirements

	E207 Software Requirements

	E208 Support Documentation and Services Requirements

COMPATABILITY WITH ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY

The standards do not require installation of specific accessibility-related software or attachment of an assistive technology device. Section 508 requires that ICT be compatible with such software and devices so that ICT can be accessible to and usable by individuals using assistive technology, including but not limited to screen readers, screen magnifiers, and speech recognition software.

ACCEPTANCE AND ACCEPTANCE TESTING

Deliverables resulting from this solicitation will be accepted based in part on satisfaction of the Section 508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements standards identified above.

The Government reserves the right to test for Section 508 Compliance before delivery.  The Contractor shall be able to demonstrate Section 508 Compliance upon delivery.

GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

VA TECHNICAL REFERENCE MODEL

The Contractor shall comply with the VA OIT Technical Reference Model (VA TRM). Compliance with the VA TRM is achieved by using only technologies and standards that are listed as approved for use in the VA TRM.  The Contractor shall provide all necessary information requested by VA to ensure TRM approval is obtained prior to use on VA’s network.

ZERO TRUST – VA CRITICAL SECURITY CONTROLS

VA has established minimum mandatory security requirements and requires that any network connected software system or service must meet the VA Critical Security Controls as outlined in the VA Memorandum, “VA Security Controls”, https://www.voa.va.gov/DocumentView.aspx?DocumentID=5010.  VA Critical Security Controls identify the minimum mandatory requirements that must be implemented across all VA enterprise infrastructure, cloud computing environments, information systems, networks, and specialized devices (medical devices/systems, special-purpose systems, and research scientific computing devices) that process, store, and/or transmit VA data.  Effective July 1, 2025, the Contractor shall implement these VA Critical Security Controls, within any network connected software system or service prior to being authorized for use in the VA.  This functional requirement is not negotiable, and Plan of Action & Milestones (POAM) will not be accepted in the event these controls cannot be implemented for new systems.  Critical Security Controls are intended to increase VA’s security posture and provide security and privacy risk visibility into the VA network and is not a new requirement.  The Contractor’s failure to maintain these VA Critical Controls after implementation will result in VA discontinuing the use of the system.

SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER (SSN) REDUCTION 

The Contractor solution shall support the Social Security Number (SSN) Fraud Prevention Act (FPA) of 2017 which prohibits the inclusion of SSNs on any document sent by mail.  The Contractor support shall also be performed in accordance with Section 240 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act (CAA) 2018, enacted March 23, 2018, which mandates VA to discontinue using SSNs to identify individuals in all VA information systems as the Primary Identifier.  The Contractor shall ensure that any new IT solution discontinues the use of SSN as the Primary Identifier to replace the SSN with the Integrated Control Number (ICN) in all VA information systems for all individuals.  The Contractor shall ensure that all Contractor delivered applications and systems integrate with the VA Master Person Index (MPI) for identity traits to include the use of the ICN as the Primary Identifier. The Contractor solution may only use a Social Security Number to identify an individual in an information system if and only if the use of such number is required to obtain information VA requires from an information system that is not under the jurisdiction of VA.

INTERNET PROTOCOL VERSION 6 (IPV6)

The Contractor solution shall support IPv6-Only based upon the memo issued by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) on November 19, 2020 (https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/M-21-07.pdf). Which defines IPv6-only as the state of an operational system or service when IPv4 protocol functions (addressing, packet forwarding) are not in use. The NIST USGv6 profile defines technical requirements for a product to be capable of operating in IPv6-Only environments.  IPv6-Only technology, in accordance with the USGv6 Program (https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/usgv6-program/usgv6-revision-1), NIST Special Publication (SP) 500-267B Revision 1 “USGv6 Profile” (https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.500-267Br1), and NIST SP 800-119 “Guidelines for the Secure Deployment of IPv6” (https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-119), compliance shall be included in all IT infrastructures, application designs, application development, operational systems and sub-systems, and their integration.  In addition to the above requirements, all devices, applications, and systems shall support all applicable functionality on native IPv6-Only as well as dual stack (IPv6 / IPv4) connectivity without additional memory or other resources being provided by the Government, so that they can function in a mixed environment.  All public/external facing servers and services (e.g., web, email, DNS, ISP services, etc.) shall support native IPv6-Only and dual stack (IPv6 / IPv4) users and all internal infrastructure and applications shall support using native IPv6-Only and dual stack (IPv6 / IPv4) for all functionality and operations.

SOFTWARE AND LICENSING REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall be responsible for the provision of all software licenses and any associated licensing maintenance required for any development, delivery, integration, operation, and/or maintenance associated with its proposed application(s), software products, software solution, and/or system including, but not limited to, any and all application(s), software and/or software products that comprise, are a part of, or integrate with the Contractor’s proposed application(s), software products, software solution, and/or system for the life of any resulting contract.

TRUSTED INTERNET CONNECTION (TIC)

The Contractor solution shall meet the requirements outlined in Office of Management and Budget Memorandum M-19-26, “Update to the Trusted Internet Connections (TIC) Initiative“ (https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/M-19-26.pdf), VA Directive 6513 “Secure External Connections”, and shall comply with the TIC 3.0 Core Guidance Documents, including all Volumes and TIC Use Cases, found at the Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) (https://www.cisa.gov/publication/tic-30-core-guidance-documents.)

GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE REQUIREMENTS

If Artificial Intelligence (AI) is part of the Contractor system/solution, the Contractor shall be in compliance with E.O. 13960 and 14319, OMB Memorandums M-25-21, M-25-22, and M-26-04, and VA Directive and Handbook 6500 to support VA in trustworthy, secure, responsible, accountable, Truth Seeking, and Ideologically Neutral AI innovation.

No web-based, publicly available generative AI service has been approved for use with VA-sensitive data including, but not limited to OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Microsoft’s Copilot, Google’s Gemini, and Anthropic’s Claude.  No PII, protected health information (PHI), or VA-sensitive data should be entered into these unapproved services.  The entire definition of VA Sensitive Data can be found at 38 U.S.C. § 5727 (23).  The Contractor shall protect VA Sensitive data from unauthorized disclosure or use, and from being used to train or improve the functionality of the vendor's commercial offerings without express permission from VA.

The Contractor shall deliver the services, technical data, configurations, models, weights, documentation or other information, including source code, developed during contract performance.  The Contractor, in collaboration with VA, must evaluate the output of any AI tool for accuracy prior to using the output in VA efforts.  All data, including models, weights, algorithms, and outputs generated using either Government-furnished data or data first developed under this contract shall be the property of the Government with unlimited rights as defined by FAR 52.227-14.  The Contractor shall also deliver any custom-developed code developed with AI methodologies in accordance with the SHARE IT Act, if applicable.  VA shall also retain unlimited rights to any improvements to that data, including the continued design, development, testing, and operation of AI systems and/or systems utilizing AI.

The Contractor shall ensure that all AI Systems, including Large Language Models (LLM), whether standalone LLMs or integrated into broader software platforms,  procured under this effort and/or used in performance of this contract complies with the Unbiased AI Principles as defined in Executive Order 14319 and OMB Memorandum M-26-04, e.g. Truth Seeking and Ideologically Neutral, as applicable to the intended use of the system.

Statement of work – Sports Streaming Services 
 
Background 
 
The purchase of a sports streaming service for varsity sports statistics and online viewing services as 
required by NFHS.  
Objectives 
 
The objective of this service is to have digital records of all varsity sport activities and to be able to 
accurately track sports statistics, in compliance with NFHS.  
 
Scope 
 
The scope of this project is to obtain access to online streaming services to track varsity games. 
 
Tasks 
 
The task will be to deliver a compatible streaming service similar to the ones used in our region, 
southwest 1-A, to stream and record all varsity games.

BIE – St. Stephens Indian School

The RFI references approximately 700,000 cores for the virtualization environment. For VDI and EUC licensing purposes, can you provide an estimated number of end users or concurrent sessions we should use for the Cost ROM?  That would likely be easiest for an apples to apples evaluation perspective.  Alternatively, we’ll plan to do a % of cores assumption.

Response: At this time, we do not have a precise count of end users across all participating programs and agencies.

To facilitate an apples-to-apples evaluation across all vendor responses, we request that you provide Cost ROM estimates for the following scenarios:

Maximum case: All 700,000 subscriptions allocated to VDI/EUC end users.

Sample cases: 10%, 25%, and 50% of the 700,000 subscriptions allocated to VDI/EUC end users, with the remainder allocated to server virtualization.

If you believe another percentage is more realistic based on your experience or industry standards, you may include that scenario as well. Please clearly state your assumptions and methodology.

If you need to make further assumptions (such as concurrency rates or user profiles), please describe them in your response.

RFI Virtualization Enterprise Software Solutions (Final)
For: Virtualization Enterprise Software Solutions for the Department of War (DoW)
RFI Number: 842674441
Issuing Agency: Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA)
Date of Issuance: April 24, 2026
Response Due Date: 15 Days Post-Release

1.0 INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE

The Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA), on behalf of the Department of War (DoW), is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to conduct market research. The purpose of this RFI is to identify qualified sources capable of providing a standardized, enterprise-scalable virtualization software solution, to include all associated software sustainment, upgrades, and technical support services under an enterprise-wide agreement within the next 12 months.

The objective is to establish a centralized, efficient, and cost-effective procurement vehicle. The Government intends to establish a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) with a five-year ordering period (one-year base period and four one-year options) to procure products and services for the DoW, including 4th Estate Agencies, Combatant Commands (COCOMs), and Military Departments (MILDEPs), against the GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) Information Technology category.

This is an RFI only. This is not a solicitation or Request for Quote (RFQ) and does not commit the Government to award a contract. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI are solely at the interested party's expense.

2.0 BACKGROUND AND CURRENT VIRTUALIZATION ENVIRONMENT

The Department of War (DoW) is committed to leveraging advanced technologies to enhance the security and effectiveness of its IT operations. DISA is collaborating with DoW components to create an enterprise-wide solution for procuring commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) virtualization software. This initiative aims to consolidate numerous existing contracts and streamline vendor management for critical Virtualization products supporting server virtualization, cybersecurity, endpoint protection, and network management across the DoW's IT infrastructure.

The DoW’s virtualization environment is a critical component of its global IT infrastructure, providing enterprise compute capabilities supporting approximately 700,000 cores. This environment is characterized by its significant scale, geographic diversity, and complex security requirements, with resources deployed across CONUS and OCONUS locations. These include DoW data centers, enterprise computing facilities, and tactical/forward-deployed environments, spanning multiple security domains and classification levels.

All solutions must align with DoW enterprise architecture, cybersecurity (e.g., STIGs, Impact Levels), and lifecycle sustainment requirements. The platform primarily supports the following use cases:

Mission Application Hosting: Serving as the foundation for critical warfighting and business systems.

Development & Testing: Providing sandboxed environments for developing and testing new capabilities.

End-User Computing (EUC): Supporting Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) and other virtualized user-facing services.

3.0 SCOPE OF REQUIREMENTS

The Government requires a comprehensive virtualization portfolio to support an estimated 700,000 subscriptions. The proposed solution must be structured to accommodate diverse client needs through offerings like tiered bundles, individual licenses, and hybrid models. A comprehensive migration plan with a detailed timeline is mandatory. This plan must detail the strategy for transitioning from the current VMware framework to the proposed solution with minimal disruption to mission-critical operations.

The plan must also explicitly describe how Artificial Intelligence (AI) will be leveraged to drive automation, reduce administrative overhead, and simplify the deployment, management, and security of the platform. Furthermore, all proposed capabilities must be designed to integrate with DoW regulations and frameworks, and must minimally address the following core areas:

3.1. Core Platform Capabilities

Virtualization: Provide a solution that supports both full virtualization and paravirtualization to consolidate applications and establish cloud or VDI environments. It must include live VM migration, storage migration, and seamless import/export functionality, including cross-migration, all managed from a unified administration plane.

Disaster Recovery & Backup: Deliver robust business continuity through VM-centric snapshots, clones, and replication. The solution must support enterprise-grade backup and recovery via modern APIs (e.g., VSS) and allow for granular recovery (file/folder, full VM, disk-level) across data centers.

Application & Data Virtualization: Provide capabilities to decouple applications from the underlying OS (application virtualization) and to abstract and integrate disparate data sources without requiring data movement (data virtualization).

Remote & Automated Management: Enable remote management and monitoring of all infrastructure, including direct remote console access. A comprehensive REST API for programmatic automation and third-party integration is mandatory.

3.2. Management, Analytics, and Security

Cybersecurity: Deliver advanced threat detection and incident response. This must include Secure Boot, shielded VMs, and native micro-segmentation for application-centric security policies. The system must use AI-driven insights for self-healing security configurations to maintain compliance.

Asset Management: Provide a centralized dashboard to discover, track, monitor, and manage all physical and virtual IT assets. Crucially, this tool must operate across the DoW's globally distributed and logically partitioned network boundaries, providing a unified view of real-time asset utilization. 

Network Management & Security: Offer solutions for network monitoring, management, and security, including capabilities for SD-WAN, web/email security, and virtual networking.

Logging, Analytics, and Reporting:

Log Management: Ingest syslog and custom logs from all platform components (hypervisors, hosts) and retain them for at least one year.

Analytics & Search: Provide real-time search and analytics to correlate events across all layers (hosts, clusters, VMs, applications, storage).

Performance & Capacity: Offer real-time and historical analytics (CPU, memory, storage, network) with one-year data retention. The platform must provide forecasting, capacity planning, and "what-if" modeling for workload placement.

Alerting & Notifications: Support threshold-based and dynamic anomaly detection alerts, with routing to multiple platforms via email, webhooks, and REST API integrations.

3.3. Security, Compliance, and Workforce Enablement

Security and Compliance:

DoW Impact Level: Products must meet a minimum of DoW Impact Level 5 (IL5) certification, with a clearly defined roadmap to achieve IL6.

Authentication: The solution must support two-factor authentication via SAML 2.0 or OIDC to ensure integration with the DoW Enterprise Identity, Credential, and Access Management (E-ICAM) solution.

Training and Continuous Learning:

Foundational Awareness: Introductory training for all technical staff to build a baseline understanding of the new platform's architecture, terminology, and core concepts.

Deep Technical Training: An intensive, hands-on curriculum for senior engineers and the core migration team covering platform administration, advanced networking, security configuration, and migration-specific tooling.

Operational Enablement: Role-based training for day-to-day operations teams focused on new Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), common administrative tasks, and basic troubleshooting.

Continuous Learning: A strategy for ongoing education, including hands-on labs, to keep staff skills current on new features, performance optimization, and advanced security practices.

3.4. Operational Use Cases
The following use cases represent critical operational scenarios that the proposed virtualization solution must support. Vendors must address the specific technical challenges and provide detailed responses to the requirements outlined in each scenario.

Use Case 1: Hypervisor-Native Hybrid Cloud and Workload Mobility

Operational Scenario: During a large-scale joint training exercise, a wargaming simulation application exhausts the compute resources of the local Department of War (DoW) cluster and requires immediate expansion into a commercial cloud.

Technical Challenge: The virtualization platform must seamlessly extend its software-defined data center (SDDC) to a DoD-approved Impact Level 5 (IL5) commercial cloud. This must be accomplished without application refactoring by leveraging bare-metal cloud instances to maintain a single, unified management plane.

Required Vendor Response:

Detail the platform's ability to deploy its native hypervisor stack onto bare-metal IL5 cloud infrastructure, creating a single, stretched logical cluster.

Explain the storage replication protocols and memory-state synchronization algorithms that enable live virtual machine (VM) and container migration across the WAN.

Describe how the software-defined networking (SDN) controller uses overlay protocols (e.g., GENEVE, VXLAN) at the hypervisor kernel level to stretch Layer 2 networks to the cloud provider.

Use Case 2: Zero Trust Architecture with Hypervisor-Level Micro-Segmentation

Operational Scenario: A hyper-converged DoW environment hosts hundreds of transient VMs and containers, mixing workloads that process Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) with unclassified tasks on the same physical servers.

Technical Challenge: Security boundaries must be enforced at the VM level. The virtualization software must natively block unauthorized East-West traffic at the virtual network interface before it reaches the physical network, using hypervisor-level controls.

Required Vendor Response:

Describe the platform's distributed firewall (DFW) architecture and how it operates within the hypervisor kernel, independent of the guest operating system.

Detail how the platform uses Guest Introspection APIs to enable agentless anti-malware scans and file integrity monitoring for CUI workloads.

Explain the cryptographic mechanisms built into the software-defined storage (SDS) and SDN layers that provide native encryption for data-at-rest and data-in-transit.

Use Case 3: High-Fidelity Secure Virtual Desktops with GPU Virtualization

Operational Scenario: Geographically dispersed intelligence analysts require real-time, interactive access to 3D geospatial rendering applications (e.g., ArcGIS) and CUI databases from thin clients.

Technical Challenge: The virtualization platform must deliver a high-performance graphical experience comparable to a local workstation while ensuring all compute, memory, and data remain physically secured within the IL5 data center.

Required Vendor Response:

Outline the Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) connection broker architecture and how its display protocol (e.g., Blast Extreme, PCoIP, HDX) dynamically adapts encoding based on real-time network conditions.

Detail the platform's ability to abstract physical GPUs into virtual GPU (vGPU) profiles and algorithmically schedule frame buffer allocation to individual desktop VMs.

Explain how the connection broker enforces DoD CAC/PIV cryptographic authentication and applies granular policy restrictions (e.g., blocking USB drives, clipboard access, and local printing) to prevent data exfiltration.

4.0 INFORMATION REQUESTED

Interested parties are requested to provide a response that addresses the following areas:

4.1. Company Information

Company Name, Address, and Website.

Point of Contact (Name, Title, Email, and Phone Number).

CAGE Code and Unique Entity ID (UEI).

4.2. Capability Statement

A detailed response addressing your company’s capabilities for all requirements outlined in Section 3.0. This should include specific responses to the following areas:

ROI and Value: Describe how your solution provides a clear return on investment (ROI) and long-term value, covering Total Cost of Ownership (TCO), quantifiable ROI metrics, cost effectiveness, enterprise scalability, and strategic modernization value.

Migration Strategy: Outline a phased migration framework (discovery, pilot, full-scale) from legacy virtualization, addressing DoW's scale and decentralized network. Include plans for risk mitigation, business continuity, and rollback.

Technology & Commercial Outlook: Provide a 3-5 year technology outlook for virtualization, detailing your product roadmap alignment with trends like sovereign clouds and AI/ML. Describe alternative and predictable consumption pricing models.

Security & Supply Chain: Detail your corporate security posture, compliance framework (e.g., IL5), and Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC) practices.

Global Technical Support: Present a detailed technical support framework for a globally distributed organization, including a sample SLA matrix. Confirm U.S. citizen support and the availability of cleared personnel.

Program Management: Describe your program management approach, account team structure, and governance model. Provide a sample Executive Dashboard or QBR template.

Training & Adoption: Outline your continuous adoption plan for establishing a Center of Excellence (CoE) and ensuring long-term user proficiency.

CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 1 
Statement of Objectives (SOO) —  Part D Transaction 
Facilitator 
Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
Part D Transaction Facilitator 
 
1. Background 
 
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) administers the Medicare Part D 
prescription drug benefit program. A critical component of Part D administration is the 
coordination of benefits (COB) between Medicare Part D plans and other payers, including non-
Part D plans providing prescription drug coverage. CMS requires a Part D transaction facilitation 
contractor to support the accurate tracking of True Out-of-Pocket (TrOOP) costs, facilitate 
eligibility queries, and ensure secure and compliant exchange of protected health information 
(PHI) in accordance with Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and 
applicable federal regulations. 
 
CMS seeks a contractor to provide transaction facilitation services that support the Medicare 
Part D COB program. The contractor shall bring innovative, efficient, and compliant solutions to 
meet the objectives described herein. 
 
2. Scope 
 
This Statement of Objectives (SOO) describes the high-level outcomes and objectives CMS 
seeks to achieve through this acquisition. Offerors are required to submit, as part of their 
technical proposal, a Performance Work Statement (PWS) and a Quality Assurance 
Surveillance Plan (QASP) that describe how they will meet these objectives and how 
performance will be measured and monitored. 
 
The appendices referenced herein (Appendices A through I) define technical specifications, 
data formats, matching criteria, and transaction standards that shall remain unchanged and 
must be incorporated into the offeror's proposed PWS. 
 
 

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 2 
 
Referenced Appendices (unchanged and incorporated by reference): 
 
• Appendix A – HHS Contractor Non-Disclosure Agreement 
• Appendix B – Baseline Deliverables 
• Appendix C – Medicare Part D Eligibility Index  
• Appendix D – Medicare Part D Eligibility Verification Transactions (E1), Financial 
Information Reporting Transactions (FIR), Supplemental Payment Information Transactions 
(Nx), and Hospice Nx. 
• Appendix E – Transaction Payer Sheets 
• Appendix F – FIR Mass Retrigger Dates 
• Appendix G – Real-time Nx Process 
• Appendix H – E1 Matching Logic 
• Appendix I – BIN/PCN Routing Supplemental Transaction 
 
3. Contract Type 
 
This is a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract with a Time-and-Materials (T&M) Order-level 
materials (OLMs) Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) for each period. 
 
4. Offeror Submission Requirements 
 
In response to this SOO, offerors shall submit the following as part of their technical proposal: 
 
1. Performance Work Statement (PWS): A detailed PWS describing the offeror's approach to 
achieving each objective stated in Section 5 of this SOO. The PWS shall describe the 
specific tasks, methods, processes, staffing, tools, and technologies the offeror will employ. 
The PWS must incorporate all technical requirements contained in Appendices A through I. 
2. Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP): A QASP that identifies measurable 
performance standards, Acceptable Quality Levels (AQLs), surveillance methods, and 
remedies for each performance objective in the PWS. The QASP shall align to the 
performance objectives and framework described in Section 6 of this SOO. 
 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 3 
 
5. Performance Objectives 
 
Objective 1: Part D Transaction Facilitation 
 
CMS seeks accurate, timely, and compliant processing of Part D Coordination of Benefits 
(COB) related transactions between Medicare Part D plans and other payers. The  tasks listed 
below require require a 24/7 real-time, on-line switching network and connectivity with 
pharmacies, other pharmacy switches, Part D plan sponsors, and other payers, providers, and 
other entities as designated by CMS  
The Contractor shall: 
• Maintain the Medicare Part D Eligibility Index (Appendix C) provided by CMS; 
• Use the Medicare Part D Eligibility Index (Appendix C) to accept and respond to 
pharmacy-initiated or from CMS approved entities eligibility queries; 
• Build a database of primary Part D and supplemental payer BIN/PCNs; 
•  Accept from pharmacies, payers and other switches Part D related transactions and 
route these transactions to the appropriate entity; 
• Identify and accept supplemental claims transactions from pharmacies, payers and 
switches, and create and route transactions reporting supplemental claims data to the 
Part D plans; 
• Create and route automated TrOOP balance transfer transactions to Part D plans and 
accept responses to these transactions. 
• Create and route coordination of benefits, other coverage enrollment information and 
other data as defined by CMS. 
• Utilize existing commercial IT system(s) to support this objective. 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 4 
 
Objective 2: HIPAA-Compliant Business Associate Agreement (BAA) Execution 
 
CMS seeks full compliance with the HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Parts 160 and 164) in the 
exchange of Protected Health Information (PHI) between the Part D Transaction Facilitator and 
Medicare Part D plan sponsors. The contractor shall achieve outcomes including, but not limited 
to: 
 
• Execution of a signed BAA with each Medicare Part D prescription drug plan sponsor prior 
to the exchange of TrOOP information. 
• Maintenance of BAA execution rates such that no more than 10% of plan sponsors require 
amendment to the standard language agreement; the Contracting Officer's Representative 
(COR)/Project Officer (PO) shall be notified if this threshold is exceeded. 
• Timely notification to CMS of any plan sponsor that has not executed a BAA by December 
31 of each year. 
• Execution of BAAs with newly identified Part D sponsors prior to the beginning of each new 
Part D contract year, based on a list provided by CMS no later than October 1. 
• Publication of the CMS-provided standard language BAA on the contractor's website for 
plan sponsor access. 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 5 
 
Objective 3: Pharmacy Eligibility Query (E1) Support 
 
CMS seeks reliable, accurate, and secure responses to pharmacy eligibility queries to support 
beneficiary access to Part D benefits at the point of sale. The contractor shall achieve outcomes 
including, but not limited to: 
 
• Provision of timely and accurate responses to E1 eligibility queries using the current 
National Council for Prescription Drug Programs (NCPDP) standard E1 transaction, per 
specifications in Appendix D and Appendix E. 
• Use of all official (non-audited off) records in the "Part D Contract Data" field of the Medicare 
Eligibility Index to determine historical, current, and future coverage, including contract 
information, coverage dates, and 4Rx data. 
• Application of minimum matching criteria as defined in Appendix H.Compliance with CMS 
security and privacy standards for all E1 query responses. 
• Maintenance and ongoing support of the E1 environment, including requirements analysis, 
design, development, quality assurance (QA), and project management. 
• Implementation and management of pharmacy exclusion tables as directed by CMS. 
• Publication of E1 specifications, RxBIN/PCN information, and matching criteria as defined in 
Appendices E, H, and I on the contractor’s website. 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 6 
 
Objective 4: Disaster Recovery (DR) and System Architecture Compliance 
 
CMS seeks a resilient, modern, and compliant system architecture that meets federal continuity 
of operations and security requirements. The contractor shall achieve outcomes including, but 
not limited to: 
 
• Design and re-architecture of the current DR environment to comply with applicable CMS 
and federal guidelines. 
• Maintenance of system availability, integrity, and confidentiality at a Moderate risk level in 
accordance with FIPS 199 and NIST SP 800-60. 
• Alignment with the CMS Technical Reference Architecture (TRA), which will be provided 
upon request. 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 7 
 
Objective 5: Information Security and Privacy Compliance 
 
CMS seeks full compliance with all applicable federal information security and privacy 
requirements. The contractor shall achieve outcomes including, but not limited to: 
 
• Protection of government information and systems in accordance with the HHS Information 
Security and Privacy Policy (IS2P) and CMS Information Systems Security and Privacy 
Policy (IS2P2). 
• Safeguarding of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) at a Moderate confidentiality impact 
level per OMB Circular A-130. 
• Handling of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) in accordance with Executive Order 
13556 and NIST SP 800-171 Rev 3. 
• Immediate notification (within one (1) hour) to CMS of any new or unanticipated threats, 
hazards, or safeguard failures. 
• Destruction of information and data in accordance with NIST SP 800-88 Rev 1 when no 
longer needed. 
• Compliance with the Privacy Act and applicable FAR clauses. 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 8 
 
Objective 6: Program and Technical Management 
 
CMS seeks transparent, accurate, and timely project management and reporting to support 
CMS oversight. The contractor shall achieve outcomes including, but not limited to: 
 
• Development and maintenance of a Project Management Plan (PMP) when requested by 
the COR. 
• Provision and maintenance of a baseline integrated project schedule using the current CMS 
version of Microsoft Project, or an alternative format acceptable to the COR. 
• Active participation in joint management reviews with CMS (Bi-weekly or as needed), 
attended by persons with authority to make cost and schedule decisions. 
• Active participation in MA & Part D system workgroups and meetings as directed by CMS, 
including preparation of materials, agendas, meeting minutes, and presentations upon 
request. 
• Participation in status conference calls as directed by the COR. 
• Preparation and submission of Monthly Status Reports as requested by the COR, including 
the CMS Financial Status Report Spreadsheet. 
• Preparation and submission of meeting minutes documenting meeting date(s), participants, 
purpose, decisions reached, and action items (including responsible party and due date). 
• Preparation and submission of meeting agendas for meetings where the contractor is the 
primary presenter, including meeting date, purpose, intended audience, and specific agenda 
items. 
• Submission of all proposed key personnel substitutions or additions in writing to CMS at 
least thirty (30) days prior to the proposed substitution, including a detailed explanation and 
complete resume; all substitutions must have qualifications equal to or greater than the 
person being replaced. 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 9 
 
Objective 7: Transition-In Support (Optional) 
 
CMS seeks a seamless transition of duties, responsibilities, activities, and functions from the 
incumbent contractor. The contractor shall achieve outcomes including, but not limited to: 
 
• Collaboration with the previous contractor to ensure an orderly and seamless transition over 
approximately 3 months (or as otherwise specified by CMS). 
• Transfer of all tools, data, documentation, and institutional knowledge necessary to maintain 
continuity of operations. 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 10 
 
Objective 8: Section 508 Compliance 
 
CMS seeks full compliance with Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act for all Information and 
Communication Technology (ICT) developed or delivered under this contract, in accordance 
with E205 Electronic Content requirements. 
 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 11 
 
6. QASP Framework 
 
Offerors shall propose a QASP that addresses, at a minimum, the performance objectives, 
standards, AQLs, surveillance methods, and remedies described in this section. The 
Government will use the offeror's proposed QASP as the basis for performance monitoring 
throughout the contract. CMS reserves the right to modify the QASP by mutual agreement 
during the period of performance. 
 
The QASP shall include, at a minimum, the following elements for each performance standard: 
 
• Performance Objective — The outcome or result to be achieved. 
• Performance Standard — The measurable threshold defining acceptable performance. 
• Acceptable Quality Level (AQL) —  The minimum level of performance the Government 
will accept before initiating remedies. 
• Surveillance Method —  How CMS will monitor and verify contractor performance. 
• Remedy —  The action CMS will take if performance falls below the AQL. 
The table below provides the minimum QASP framework that offerors must address. Offerors 
are encouraged to propose additional performance standards that demonstrate their 
commitment to quality and innovation.

NCIA Request for Information (RFI) 
 
To: Industry Partners 
 
  
1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) is conducting market 
research to identify qualified vendors and gather input on potential solutions to support the 
upcoming acquisition for IT Service Management Solution for Asset and Configuration 
Management Database. To that end, we are issuing the attached Request for Information 
(RFI) MS-424363-ITSM to solicit feedback from capable and interested industry partners. 
 
2. This RFI is issued for planning purposes only and is not a request for bids . It is part of 
NCIA’s effort to ensure it has a clear understanding of the marketplace, available 
capabilities, and potential acquisition strategies. 
 
3. We value your insight and invite you to: 
a. Share relevant corporate capabilities and experience; 
b. Review and comment on our draft requirements (Annexes A and B) with a view in 
providing recommendations for improving performance outcomes,  competition, 
and efficiency; and identify ing any risks or concerns that should be considered 
during planning. 
 
4. Submission instructions and additional details can be found in the enclosure to this RFI. 
 
5. Only companies from a NATO member country can participate in or respond to this RFI 
(https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/nato_countries.htm). 
 
6. Should you have any questions or need clarification, please contact Estefania Nunez at 
Estefania.Nunez@ncia.nato.int. 
 
7. We thank you in advance for your time and input, and we look forward to engaging with 
you as we shape this potential acquisition.

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION  
 
A. Introduction 
 
1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NC IA) is conducting market 
research to identify potential sources and gather information regarding industry 
capabilities to provide an integrated ITSM and Asset and Configuration Management 
solution for the management of Deployable CIS (DCIS) services and assets in support 
of NCISG . This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for informational 
purposes and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for 
Quotation (RFQ), or invitation for bid.  
 
B. Purpose 
 
1. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain input from industry to help inform the NCIA’s 
acquisition planning. Responses to this RFI will assist in refining requirements, 
identifying capabilities, and shaping the strategy for any future solicitation. 
 
C. Background 
 
1. NCIA NIMSC L&A BU manages a portfolio of Deployable CIS services across four 
operational domains (Deployable Nodes, Connectivity & SATCOM, Anchor & 
Infrastructure, and Service & Support), supporting NCISG across 25 units in 14 
nations. The portfolio spans over 5000 individual assets requiring lifecycle 
management across two classification domains: NATO Restricted (NR) and NATO 
Secret (NS). 
 
Asset tracking is currently performed using an interim Configuration Management 
System (iCMS). NCIA requires a strategic, purpose-built ITSM and Asset Management 
solution to replace this interim capability and provide full lifecycle visibility, integrating 
with existing enterprise systems: Oracle EBA (financial management, NR network) and 
BMC Remedy (incident and change management, NS network). 
 
The solution must be operational within 12 months of contract award, including full 
migration of existing data, completion of physical inventory, and delivery of all 
documentation. 
 
 
D. Submission Instructions 
 
1. Interested parties are invited to respond in accordance with the instructions below: 
 
a. Submit responses via the email address in section H no later than 12:00 hours 
Central European Time (CET) on 02 June 2026. 
 
b. Responses should be submitted in PDF or Word format and must not exceed 15 
pages, including: 
i. Responses to Annex A and comments on Annex B 
 
excluding: 
i. Cover page 
ii. Company brochures or product literature (if included) 

 
 
 
  
 Page 6 
 
 
iii. Attachments such as past performance references 
 
c. Use the following subject line for submission 
i. “Response to RFI [RFI Number] – [Company Name]” 
 
d. All responses should address the items listed in Annex A
 – Requested Information. 
 
e. Respondents are also encouraged to review and comment on the draft requirements 
in Annex B
 – Draft Statement of Work (SOW)/Performance Work Statement (PWS). 
 
E. Industry Engagement 
 
1.  Not Applicable 
 
 
 
F. Disclaimer 
 
1. This RFI is for planning and informational purposes only and shall not be construed as 
a solicitation or obligation on the part of the NCIA. The NCIA does not intend to award 
a contract based on responses to this RFI. Respondents are solely responsible for all 
costs incurred in responding to this RFI.  The NCIA will consider and analyse all 
information received from this RFI and may use these findings to develop a future 
solicitation. The NCIA will consider all responses as confidential commercial 
information and will protect it as such. 
 
2. NCIA reserves the right, at any time, to cancel this informal market survey, partially or 
in its entirety. No legal liability on the part of NCIA for payment of any sort shall arise 
and in no event will a cause of action lie with any prospective participant for the 
recovery of any costs incurred in connection with the preparation of documentation or 
participation in response hereto. All effort initiated or undertaken by prospective 
informal market survey participants shall be done considering and accepting this fact. 
 
G. Use of Information Provided through Responses 
 
1. Confidentiality of Responses 
 
The NCIA may incorporate industry comments and responses, in part or in whole, into a 
future release of a solicitation.  Should respondents include proprietary data in their 
responses that they do not wish to be disclosed to the public for any purpose, or used by 
NCIA (except for internal evaluation purposes), they must: 
 
a. Mark the title page with the following legend:  
 
This document includes data that shall not be disclosed outside NATO and shall not be 
duplicated, used, or disclosed – in whole or in part – for any purpose other than for NCI A 
internal evaluation purposes, unless otherwise expressly authorised by [insert company 
name]. This restriction does not limit the NCI A’s right to use information contained in this 
data without restriction if it is obtained from another source.  The data subject to this 
restriction are contained in sheets [insert numbers or other identification of sheets] 
 
b. Mark each sheet of data it wishes to restrict with the following legend:  
 

 
 
 
  
 Page 7 
 
 
Use or disclosure of data contained on this sheet is subject to the restriction on the title 
page of this document. 
 
H. RFI Point of Contact

Annex A – Requested Information 
 
1. Respondents are encouraged to provide the following information in their response: 
 
a. Company Information 
i. Legal Business Name  
ii. Address 
iii. Website 
iv. Primary Point of Contact 
v. Email address 
 
b. Technical Capability 
i. Confirmation of multi-domain (dual on-premise instance) support —  
one instance for NR, one for NS, each independently deployed. 
Describe the proposed architecture and how classification separation 
is enforced. 
ii. Description of CMDB capabilities including modular and hierarchical 
asset structure: Module → Product → Component, with 
documentation attachable at each level 
iii. Stock and spare parts management capabilities, including: 
consolidated catalogue, threshold alerts, stock tracking per location 
and classification domain, and pre-positioning support 
iv. Physical inventory tools and field mobility support — confirm barcode 
and/or QR code scanning capability for field inventory operations 
v. Documentation management at component level: version control, 
classification-aware access controls, bulk upload, and metadata 
tagging 
vi. PMI and CMI scheduling and tracking: configurable PMI frequency, 
advance notification (minimum 21 calendar days), maintenance task 
libraries, post-maintenance report generation 
vii. Describe your integration approach for Oracle EBA (NR domain): API

bidirectional synchronisation method, and conflict resolution rules 
viii. Describe any existing certified integrations with Oracle E Business 
Suite — provide integration architecture and reference deployments if 
available 
ix. Describe your integration approach for BMC Remedy (NS domain): 
API type, bidirectional status synchronisation for maintenance tickets, 
CMI workflow triggering, and boundary controls ensuring no data 
leaves the NS domain 
x. Describe any existing certified integrations with BMC Remedy —  
provide integration architecture and reference deployments if available

registration. Describe how NATO UIDs are managed across the asset 
lifecycle. 
xii. Confirm support for location hierarchy: Theatre → Country → Site → 
Building → Room → Rack/Position 
xiii. Existing NATO or defence customer references (anonymised if required)

subsidiary directives applicable to the NR and NS classification domains

viii. Confirm encryption of data at rest and in transit using NATO-approved

ix. Confirm that all personnel requiring access to NR or NS systems hold or 
are able to obtain the appropriate NATO security clearance. Describe 
your security clearance management process. 
x. Describe your experience delivering or supporting the formal CIS 
accreditation process for NATO-classified systems. Prior NATO

conforming hardware

Question

RFQ Reference Question Government Response 
1 Section L / Tech 
Spec 5.1 
The solicitation requires GPU availability by May 
15, 2026. Will the Government consider proposals 
where the infrastructure subcontractor can provision 
and deliver all 50 GPUs within 10 business days of 
contract award, assuming award occurs no later than 
May 5, 2026? 
No. The Government will not consider 
proposals that require a 10-business-day 
provisioning period following contract 
award. The requirement remains that all 
50 GPUs must be available by May 15, 
2026, or immediately upon contract 
award if the award occurs after that date. 
2 Section L, V ol I, 
Go/No-Go #3 
The Go/No-Go requirement lists the NVIDIA HGX 
H100 80GB SXM5 as the baseline but accepts 
"equivalent or better" including Blackwell 
B200/GB200. Will the Government confirm that a 
proposal offering NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs as 
the primary solution will receive a "Pass" on the 
Go/No-Go compliance check, given that B200 
represents a superior architecture to the H100? 
Yes, the Government confirms that a 
proposal offering NVIDIA Blackwell
