Description and Scope: The National Institutes of Health – NCI intends to procure the services of a contractor with expertise in software integration and data management/analysis to provide customized Digital Slide Archives (DSA) system in the NCI cloud and re-identify whole slide image data sets.

The NIH/NCI office of the CIO maintains a digital image management and analysis platform based on the indica HALO software that supports researchers, external collaborators and staff with tools, collaborative workspaces, security protocols and data and image capabilities needed to manage, process and analyze a variety of image types. 

CBIIT requires continued access to the Emory University Imaging Software and Services as the current equipment is a custom developed software capability for the NCI on prem and cloud environments.

Frequently, Investigators need to bring in large slide image collections from outside collaborators, many of which contain PII.  In 2023, extensive market research was conducted to identify an approach for bulk di-identification that could be seamlessly integrated into the NCI HALO environment.  It was determined that the open-source Digital Slide Archive software (DSA), developed by Emory University with funding from NCI, could be adapted to provide bulk de-identification capabilities.  A contract was established with Emory to develop custom de-identification workflows and integrate the customized software into NCI’s HALO environment.  Going forward, additional support is needed to optimize existing workflows, add capabilities to support new file types, and maintain the integration of DSA in the NCI HALO environment.   

Extensive market research was conducted prior to NCI’s adoption of DSA software for use in NCI’s digital pathology data management and analysis environment. No suitable alternatives besides DSA were identified that could be integrated seamlessly into NCI’s environment, which is based on the Indica HALO image management platform. Open-source DSA was selected based on performance and interoperability.  As the developer of DSA, Emory is uniquely positioned to provide follow-on support and maintenance for the DSA deployment at NCI. 

This requirement is for a follow-on contract to provide continued support, maintenance and optimization of a custom software system that was developed for the NCI by Emory/Kitware. Initial market research was done to find a suitable de-identification tool for use in NCI’s environment, but none were identified that could integrate with the existing image management platform besides DSA. This request represents an outyear support element not captured in a previous award. There are no small business interests on current GWAC’s capable of competing for this requirement at a scale that can customize for the NCI environment. 

Responsibilities of the Contractor 

• Weekly meetings to provide updates, discussion, and progress projects 

• Availability during normal business hours to address critical issues in data analyses and interpretation as needed 

• Supply all necessary computer infrastructure including statistical programs to analyze data 

The NCI data set contains over 500,000 file objects, so Emory University expects additional optimizations will be needed to improve the efficiency of identifying slide sets. As they run additional cohorts through the pipeline, the team can provide additional support to improve the schema, enhance organization, and/or enhance documentation as needed. The underlying DeID capabilities of the DSA are also constantly improving, and the University researchers will be able to guide the NCI team on upgrades, backups, and similar maintenance tasks.

Deliverables: As described in the SOW, the University will support and enhance the custom DSA instance within the NCI computer ecosystem that allows batch de-identification of whole slide image data sets. This will include updating the DSA server instance and assisting with any required patches.

Duty Station 

The place of performance is Bethesda, MD 20817. This work may also be performed remotely at the discretion of NCI investigators. 

Period of Performance 

Base: May 28, 2026 - May 27, 2027

OY1: May 28,2027 – May 27,2028

OY2: May 28,2028 – May 27,2029

Contract Type: This is a firm fixed-price type order.  

NAICS Code# 541715 - Research and Development in The Physical, Engineering, And Life Sciences OR under NAICS# 541519 with the business size standard is $34.0 million. 

Initial market research conducted by the Lab has shown availability of such services in Commercial market. The Lab has already solicited from different vendors and received one quote- from the incumbent.   OALM/OA will award this requirement under a sole source under the authority of FAR 6.302.  The proposed contract action is for which the Government does intend to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 6.302.  The response close date of the notice for this requirement is in accordance with FAR 5.203(b). This acquisition will be processed under FAR Part 12 – Acquisition for Commercial Items and will be made pursuant to the authority in FAR Part 13.106-1 (b)(1) However, interested parties may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement and submit quotations. This notice is not a request for competitive quotes, but quotes received within the time and date of publication of this " Notice” will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this special notice # HHSN910EmorySoftwareFY26 is solely within the discretion of the Government.

Information received will normally be considered for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a future competitive procurement.

 

HOW TO RESPOND: In order to compete for this project, interested parties must be registered in the Central Contracting Registration/SAM and submit a technical and price quotation by 10:00 am, ET, May 20, 2026. Offerors should submit one copy of the quote to Mohamed FILALI via email. Electronic transmissions to Moe.Filali@nih.gov are preferable but must be timely. It is the responsibility of the Offeror to ensure the proposal is received by the date and time shown above.

The solicitation/contract will include all applicable provisions and clauses in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2019-05.

The provisions of FAR Clause 52.212-1 Instructions to Offerors – Commercial Items; FAR Clause 52.212-2, Evaluation – Commercial Items; FAR Clause 52.212-4, Contract Terms and Conditions – Commercial Items; and FAR 52.212-5, Contract Terms and Conditions Required to Implement Statutes or Executive Orders – Commercial Items – Deviation for Simplified Acquisitions applies to this acquisition. DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE 
BUSINESS AND ENTERPRISE SYSTEMS DIRECTORATE 
MAXWELL AIR FORCE BASE GUNTER ANNEX ALABAMA 
 
29 April 2026 
Department of the Air Force Program Business and Enterprise Systems (BES)  
Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) 
FA8771-26-S-C0001 
1. INTRODUCTION 
1.1. The Department of the Air Force (DAF), Business and Enterprise Systems (BES), invites 
commercial industry to participate in this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). This 
competitive solicitation seeks to acquire innovative, Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) 
IT and business solutions to enhance Air Force capabilities, improve efficiency, and 
reduce costs. The CSO is a streamlined acquisition process intended to reduce 
procurement timelines and is open to all interested parties, including traditional and non-
traditional defense contractors, large and small businesses, and research institutions. 
1.2. This document establishes the general framework for a multi-year process and is 
not a request for proposals. Specific opportunities will be announced through 
individual Calls for Proposals (Calls), which will be published as needed until 2 March 
2030. Each Call will detail the specific technical requirements, evaluation criteria, and 
submission instructions. 
1.3. Awards may take the form of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) based contracts or 
Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) under 10 U.S.C. § 2371b. All awards are subject 
to the availability of funds and successful negotiations. The Government is not obligated 
to make any awards and is not responsible for any costs incurred by an offeror in 
responding to this CSO or any subsequent Call. The terms of this CSO will govern the 
process unless modified by a specific Call. This CSO is established under the authority 
of Section 7227 of the National Defense Authorization Act for FY2023  
2. CSO SPECIFICS 
2.1. Focus Areas - Each Focus Area identifies an area where prospective Contractors can 
bring substantial value to meet the BES mission. Focus Areas are meant to address 
emerging sustainment and operational requirements, and therefore this CSO is not 
limited to the following Focus Areas. Additional Focus Areas may be included via 
amendments to this CSO. The scope of this CSO encompasses the following Focus 
Areas: 
2.1.1. Agile Methodology: Provide a powerful framework for developing and 
implementing IT business solutions that are faster, more flexible, higher quality, and 
more aligned with business needs.  
2.1.2. Integration: Seamless integration with existing IT infrastructure and tools is 
paramount.  

 
 
DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE 
BUSINESS AND ENTERPRISE SYSTEMS DIRECTORATE 
MAXWELL AIR FORCE BASE GUNTER ANNEX ALABAMA 
 
2.1.3. Scalability: The solution must be able to scale to meet the growing needs of the 
Air Force. 
2.1.4. Security: Security features and compliance are critical to protect against cyber 
threats and maintain each program’s Authority to Operate. 
2.1.5. Automation: Automating repetitive IT tasks, such as provisioning servers, 
deploying applications, and managing configurations. 
2.1.6. Reporting and Analytics: Robust reporting and analytics capabilities are essential 
for monitoring performance and identifying areas for improvement. 
2.1.7. Compliance: Ensure that the solutions comply with relevant federal regulations 
and industry standards.  
2.1.8. Support: Vendor support and training are important for successful implementation 
and ongoing maintenance.  
2.1.9. Artificial Intelligence: Required to keep the government at the forefront of the 
technologies available. 
2.1.10. Reduced Cost of Ownership: Maximize DAF ownership and minimize the total 
lifecycle costs of the systems and programs within PEO BES. 
2.2. Calls- This CSO allows for both Closed Calls and/or Open Period Calls which will be 
published via amendments to the CSO. All Calls issued under this CSO will include 
specific instructions which may include but are not limited to submission dates, Area of 
Interest (AoIs), evaluation criteria and proposal instructions to potential offerors. While 
each offeror shall adhere to this CSO, the Calls will contain other information the 
Contractor shall adhere to. Each Call will be announced on the Government Point of 
Entry (GPE), currently SAM.gov, which may result in the award of the FAR contract or 
an OTA under 10 USC 2371b. In order to be awarded a FAR-based contract, you must be 
registered and hold an active status on Sam.gov.  
2.2.1. Closed Calls (One-Step or Two-Step)  
A Closed Call refers to a specific, time-limited solicitation within the broader CSO 
framework where white papers or proposals must be submitted by a predetermined 
date and time.  Over the period of this CSO, Calls may be issued to request white 
papers and/or proposals for specific AoIs. It will be determined on a Call-by-Call 
basis whether the announcement is for one-step (Proposals only) or a two-step 
process (White Papers first, then Proposals by invite-only). The submission for 
white papers and proposals shall be submitted at a specific date and time as set forth 
in each particular Call. White papers and/or proposals will not be reviewed if 
submitted after the stated date and time. No exceptions will be made for late 
proposal submission, including technology issues encountered during submission. 

 
 
DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE 
BUSINESS AND ENTERPRISE SYSTEMS DIRECTORATE 
MAXWELL AIR FORCE BASE GUNTER ANNEX ALABAMA 
 
2.2.1.1. One-Step Calls  
Step 1: Proposal due date and time will be provided in Calls issued 
against this CSO.  
2.2.1.2. Two-Step Calls 
Step 1: White Paper date and time will be provided in Calls issues against 
this CSO.  
Step 2: Proposal due date and time will be provided in Request for 
Proposals (RFPs) sent to offerors that submit White Papers who are 
evaluated in accordance with the criteria stated in each Call.  
2.2.2. Open Calls  
An Open Call refers to a Call that allows for the submission of proposals or 
white papers at any time during a specified period rather than by a single, strict 
deadline. Open Calls will only be issued under a two-step process. After an 
Open Call is published, white papers may be submitted at any time during an 
Open Period for the AoIs detailed in the Call. It is important to note that only 
white papers submitted in response to the specific AoIs detailed in the Call will 
be considered. The Open Call Process will be as follows: 
Step 1: White paper due date and time will be provided in Calls issued under 
this CSO.  
Step 2: Proposal due date and time will be provided in RFPs sent to offerors 
that submit White Papers who are evaluated as selectable in accordance with 
the criteria stated in each Call. 
2.3. Evaluation Factors - Every call issued under this CSO shall, at least, evaluate the 
following. The evaluation criteria will be further detailed and/or expanded upon as 
needed in specific Calls. When proposing, prospective Contractors should consider both 
the criteria stated in this CSO and the corresponding Call that further defines and/or 
expands the evaluation criteria. Solutions will be evaluated on the basis of the merit of 
the proposed concept in addressing the AoI, not against other solution briefs submitted in 
response to the same AoI. The Government reserves the right to alter or change the 
overarching evaluation criteria via amendments to this CSO. Mandatory evaluation 
factors include:  
2.3.1. Technical: The soundness and technical merit of the proposed solution to 
adequately address the Government’s stated AoI need(s) that relate directly to the 
Technology Focus Areas. AND the demonstrated feasibility of the proposed solution 
to address the AoI.  

 
 
DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE 
BUSINESS AND ENTERPRISE SYSTEMS DIRECTORATE 
MAXWELL AIR FORCE BASE GUNTER ANNEX ALABAMA 
 
2.3.2. Importance to Agency Programs/Commercial Innovation: The degree to which the 
proposed concept provides an innovative, unique and/or previously under-utilized 
capability for government application.  
2.3.3. Funds Availability  
2.3.4. Price: Price shall be considered to the extent appropriate, but at a minimum, to 
determine that the price is fair and reasonable. 
2.4. Proposal content and format requirements will be specified at the call level.  
2.5. The Government reserves the right to extend performance to all, some, or none of the 
selected solutions and will be made based on the availability of government funds.  
2.6. Non-Government Advisors and Source Selection Sensitive Information - Non-
government advisors may participate in the evaluation of all submissions and shall have 
signed a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) with the Government. Non-government 
advisors may also serve in administration & assistance support capacities. The 
Government understands that information provided in response to this CSO is presented 
in confidence and may contain trade secrets or commercial or financial information, and 
it agrees to protect such information from unauthorized disclosure to the maximum 
extent permitted or required by Law. The Government will treat all submissions to Calls 
published against this CSO as source selection information. During the evaluation 
process, submissions may be handled by Non-Government advisors for administrative 
purposes and/or technical evaluation(s). All Government support contractors are bound 
by appropriate NDAs. Submissions will not be returned unless otherwise stated in the 
Call.  
2.7. Multiple White Paper/Proposal Submissions - Companies may submit multiple 
submissions in response to any single AoI detailed in each Call if each submission 
represents a separate and distinct concept. However, for each individual submission, 
prospective Contractors may only address one concept per submission unless otherwise 
detailed in the individual Calls.  
2.8. Future Award Opportunity - All solution briefs and/or proposals that are evaluated as 
“technically acceptable" or "selectable" but are not chosen for an initial contract award 
will be retained by the Government in a vendor pool for a period not to exceed 1 year 
from the due date of the solution brief and/or proposal. Should a new requirement arise 
with a similar scope and nature of the original Call, the Government reserves the right to 
issue an RFP to some, all, or none of the submissions within this vendor pool. Awards 
for future requirements may be based on the original evaluation criteria of this CSO, any 
additional criteria specified in the subsequent RFP or call, or on revised criteria better 

 
 
DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE 
BUSINESS AND ENTERPRISE SYSTEMS DIRECTORATE 
MAXWELL AIR FORCE BASE GUNTER ANNEX ALABAMA 
 
suited to the future requirement at the Government’s discretion. This process is 
considered a component of the original competitive procedures.   
3. CONTRACT/AGREEMENT PARTICULARS  
3.1. Fraud and False Statements - Knowingly and willfully making any false, fictitious, or 
fraudulent statements or representations may be a felony under the Federal Criminal 
False Statement Act (18 U.S.C. 1001), punishable by a fine up to $10,000, up to five 
years in prison, or both.  
3.2. As stated in the Introduction Section, Calls issued under this CSO can result in the award 
of either a FAR Contract or an OTA under 10 USC 2371b. This solicitation does not 
accept offers for grants or cooperative agreements. 
3.3. Any Call posted by the Government under this CSO could result in the potential award 
of a follow-on production or solution integration contract or OT.  
3.4. The Government will be the decision authority on whether to pursue a FAR Contract, an 
OTA or no award at all. The Government reserves the right to award some, all, or none 
of the proposals from responses to each Call. The Contracting/Agreements Officer 
reserves the right to negotiate directly with the offeror on the terms and conditions prior 
to execution of the resulting contract/agreement on behalf of the Government. Only a 
Contracting/Agreements Officer has the authority to enter, or modify, a binding 
contract/agreement on behalf of the United States Government. 
3.5. Small Business - FAR-based contracts awarded pursuant to this CSO shall include FAR 
52.219-8, Utilization of Small Business Concerns (Oct 2018). FAR-based contracts 
awarded pursuant to this CSO which meet FAR Subpart 19.7 criteria for small business 
subcontracting plans shall include FAR 52.219-9, Small Business Subcontracting Plan 
(March 2020).Offerors shall address plans to comply with these requirements as part of 
their Proposals if seeking FAR contracts, or if seeking OTs which provide for follow-on 
non-competitive production contracts. Offerors not seeking either instrument in the 
preceding sentence shall clearly state so as part of their Proposal and shall address these 
requirements as part of competition for follow-on production contracts. If any follow-on 
production contracts are required to have small business subcontracting plans and are 
negotiated using FAR Part 15, DFARS 215.304(c) Small Business Participation Plans 
shall be required. Government reserves the right to small business set asides and will be 
stated at the call level.  
3.6. Proprietary Information - Information constituting a trade secret, commercial or financial 
information, confidential personal information, or data affecting national security must 
be clearly marked. It shall be treated in confidence to the extent permitted by law. This 
restriction does not limit the Government’s right to use information contained if it is 

 
 
DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE 
BUSINESS AND ENTERPRISE SYSTEMS DIRECTORATE 
MAXWELL AIR FORCE BASE GUNTER ANNEX ALABAMA 
 
obtained from another source without restriction. The Government assumes no liability 
for disclosure or use of unmarked data and may use or disclose such data for any 
purpose. If a proposer is awarded a contract as a result of or in connection with the 
submission of proprietary data in a proposal, the Government shall have the right to 
duplicate, use, or disclose the data to the extent provided in the resulting 
contract/agreement.  
3.7. Classified Proposals - Classified whitepapers/proposals will not be accepted under this 
CSO unless otherwise stated in the Call. If topics require classified work, the proposing 
firm must have a facility clearance to perform the work.  
3.8. Security - Security Classification will be determined for each Call/Award. If classified 
data is accessed or generated, a facility and storage clearance, at the required 
classification level, will be required and the proposal will discuss appropriate personnel 
and facility clearances.

that require special protection, the submitter should immediately contact the

Background and Scope:

The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is seeking information to assess industry capabilities, emerging approaches, and best practices for replacing our existing website, VA.gov, with a premier, modern, secure, and Veteran-centric digital experience. VA’s goal is to provide a best-in-class online experience to our nation’s Veterans, their families, and other stakeholders thru VA’s central entry point for benefits, healthcare, services, and information. 

The request complements Notice ID: 365357

Exploring Next-Generation Digital Identity, Authentication, and Navigation on VA.gov

VA recognizes that replacing VA.gov is not solely a technical challenge. Meaningful improvements require coordination across experience design, platform architecture, content strategy, governance, analytics, and operating models. As a result, VA must modernize in a way that:

Maintains continuity of service for millions of users.

Integrates with a diverse portfolio of legacy and emerging systems.

Operates within a regulated, highly visible federal environment.

Supports long-term scalability, adaptability, and resilience.

Offers more seamless customer experience.

Through this request, VA seeks information on solutions, technologies, and approaches that can fundamentally improve the digital experience across all benefit portfolios.

VA welcomes responses that include:

Descriptions of relevant ideas, capabilities, and approaches.

Case studies or examples from similar environments.

User journey workflows for identity proofing, sign-in, recovery, and navigation.

Known limitations, risks, and tradeoffs.

Lessons learned from past deployments.

Responses may be informal and narrative; diagrams, visuals, and workflow illustrations are encouraged (attachments such as images or separate diagram files do not count toward the page limit).

Follow-On Engagement:

VA may schedule follow-on discussions to better understand selected responses. Participation does not imply competitive advantage.

No Commitment to Procure:

This request does not obligate VA to pursue a procurement or award a contract.

How VA Intends to Use This Information:

Responses will inform planning, requirements development, and potential pilot efforts without committing VA to any specific action.

Relevant experience with similar challenges.

Responses to the topics and questions in this request.

832674362 
 
The Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) Command, Control, Communications, and 
Computers Enterprise (C4E) Directorate is seeking sources for Audiovisual (AV), Visual 
Information (VI), Video Teleconferencing (VTC), and Videophone Support Services as a single-
award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract vehicle. 
 
CONTRACTING OFFICE ADDRESS:  
DISA/Defense Information Technology Contracting Organization (DITCO)/PS8323

Scott Air Force Base, IL 62225-5406 
 
INTRODUCTION: 
 
This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE to determine the availability and technical capability of 
small businesses (including the following subsets: Small Disadvantaged Businesses, Certified 
8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses, HUBZone Small Businesses and 
Woman-Owned Small Businesses) to provide the required products and/or services.  
 
This AV/VTC Support Services effort requires the AV and VTC services for both the classified 
(Secret/Allied Secret, Joint Worldwide Intelligence Communications System) and unclassified 
networks supporting AV/VTC operations. The support services provided include modernizing, 
operating, and maintaining DISA J6 supported VTC network infrastructure, endpoints, and 
support services. Contracted AV/VTC services also encompass VI support services, primarily 
supporting DISA Headquarters (HQs) operations.  This AV/VTC Support Services effort 
provides direct support to approximately 400 conference rooms and 2,000 single 
desktop/standalone video conference endpoints.  In general, VTC endpoints are in office spaces 
and range from a single desktop/standalone endpoint/codec to complex integrated conference 
rooms.  VTC endpoints are also located on average at 8-10 General Officer’s quarters across the 
National Capital Region (NCR) and Hampton Roads.  This effort services approximately 1,800 
classified endpoints and 700 unclassified endpoints.  DISA J6 conducts, or supports, on average 
70 new AV/VTC installations and lifecycle upgrades per year consisting of single 
desktop/standalone endpoint install or integrated conference room installation.  This effort 
provides dedicated AV/VTC support for multiple Conference Centers including the Pentagon 
Conference Center, Pentagon Auditorium, the DISA HQs Complex Conference Center, and the 
Joint Services Conference Center at Hampton Roads, Virginia. Additionally, the effort operates 
and maintains the Mark Center Conference Center and auditorium with AV capabilities that 
support production and recording functions. 
 
To sustain these support services, DISA J6 C4E requires a single-award Indefinite Delivery 
Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with a ceiling of $130M to provide AV, VI, VTC, and 
videophone support services for DISA, Department of War (DOW) 4th Estate (4E) Agencies,

DOIRFBO260010 – SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE 
DATA ANALYTICS AND SERVICES 
NOTICE: THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION, BUT RATHER A SOURCES SOUGHT 
SYNOPSIS TO DETERMINE POTENTIAL SOURCES FOR INFORMATION AND 
PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY. 
The Bureau of Reclamation is conducting market research to identify qualified contractors 
capable of providing Data Analytics and Services to support the monitoring, assessment, and 
performance analysis of hydroelectric power generation equipment. The information obtained 
through this Sources Sought will help determine the appropriate acquisition strategy, including 
the potential for small business set-asides.
 
NAICS CODE / SIZE STANDARD 
Based on internal documentation for the requirement, the Government has identified the 
following primary NAICS code: 
• NAICS 541512 – Computer Systems Design Services 
Other NAICS codes that may also be relevant to this type of work, depending on firm 
capabilities, include: 
• 541511 – Custom Computer Programming Services 
• 541513 – Computer Facilities Management Services 
• 541519 – Other Computer Related Services 
Respondents should identify which NAICS code(s) best align with their services and state their 
corresponding Small Business Size Standard.
 
NARRATIVE OF WORK REQUIRED 
The Government seeks vendors capable of delivering a comprehensive data analytics 
capability designed to improve the monitoring, reliability, and operational awareness of 
hydroelectric generating units. The work includes providing software, analytical tools, and 
technical assistance to help Reclamation assess and interpret large volumes of operational and 
historical data. 
The anticipated work will include: 
• Supporting analysis of equipment performance and operational conditions 

• Identifying unusual or deteriorating behavior in generating equipment 
• Providing tools to trend, visualize, and assess operational data 
• Offering insights that help inform maintenance decisions 
• Supporting integration or use of existing Government data sources 
• Providing training, technical assistance, and user support 
• Assisting with set-up, configuration, and use of analytics tools 
• Providing recommendations that support reliability and operational improvement 
The objective is to enable the Government to more effectively understand equipment conditions, 
detect emerging issues earlier, and make more informed maintenance decisions.
 
SMALL BUSINESS PARTICIPATION 
All Small Business Sources are encouraged to respond, including: 
• Small Business 
• 8(a) 
• HUBZone 
• Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) 
• Economically Disadvantaged WOSB (EDWOSB) 
• Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) 
• Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises 
 
REQUESTED CAPABILITIES STATEMENTS 
Interested firms shall provide a Capabilities Statement including: 
(a) Business Information 
• Company name and address 
• Point of contact (email and phone) 
• CAGE Code 
• Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) 
• Business size and socioeconomic status 
(b) Relevant Experience 
Provide evidence of experience within the past several years performing similar work, including: 
• Data analytics or data-driven decision-support projects 
• Work involving analysis of operational, industrial, or infrastructure-related data 
• Deployment or support of analytics software or platforms 

• Project details: contract numbers, titles, values, and points of contact 
(c) Technical Capability 
Describe organizational capabilities related to: 
• Data analytics tools or systems your firm provides or supports 
• Ability to help customers analyze, trend, and visualize performance data 
• Experience identifying anomalies or supporting equipment performance assessments 
• Ability to provide training, user support, system configuration, or integration assistance 
(d) Resources 
• Relevant personnel, software, hardware, or tools available 
• Demonstrated ability to support the work described above 
 
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION 
This announcement is for planning and market research purposes only. It does not constitute a 
solicitation or commitment by the Government. No reimbursement will be made for any costs 
associated with responding. 
Respondents must be registered in SAM.gov to be considered for any future solicitation.

May 15, 2026, at 3:00 PM Eastern Standard Time 
 
Submit responses by email to: 
rhonda_ligon@ios.doi.gov 
 
Email Subject Line: 
Request for Information for Data Analytics and Services

The Offeror’s quotation shall be clearly divided into the following distinct volumes: 
 
Volume I – Technical Quotation 
Volume II – Price Quotation  
Volume III – Terms and Conditions 
 
 
Volume I - Technical Quotation: 
 
The Offeror shall submit one (1) copy of their technical quotation, electronically, via E-mail to the 
Contract Specialist identified above. The technical quotation shall address the following:  
 
Technical Capability:  
The offeror shall submit technical approach and capability documentation which may include a 
narrative, charts, graphs, tables, drawings, product / service literature, and as applicable, 
demonstrated authority to provide the necessary items and perform the required services identified 
in the Statement of Work/Specifications document (Attachment 1). The documentation shall 
clearly describe, in sufficient detail, the vendor's authority, proposed items, resources and 
methods to successfully fulfill the requirements including specifications, performance capability 
requirements, delivery schedules, warranties, and all service requirements. The submission shall 
clearly identify each line item above. The submission must demonstrate that the proposed system 
meets or exceeds each minimum requirement described within the attached statement of work 
document by providing a citation between the statement of work paragraph and the relevant 
section of the technical description or product literature.  The offeror must not simply state they 
will meet or exceed the requirement; evidence must be provided. If applicable, evidence that the 
quoter is authorized by the manufacturer to provide the item(s) in the quotation shall be included.  
 
Past Performance: 
The offeror shall submit up to 3 examples of relevant past performance performed within the last 3 
to 5 years. Examples should be of work similar in scope, size and complexity to this requirement.  
The description of each reference described in this section shall not exceed one single-sided page. 
For each of the contracts, the quoter shall provide the following information:  
• Contract number 
• Client’s name and address 
• Total contract value 
• Period of performance 
• Identification of role played by quoter (i.e., Prime Contractor, Subcontractor, etc.) 
• Narrative describing the requirement and its relevance to the current requirement 
• Name of contracting officer or point of contact, telephone number and e-mail address 
 
The quoter is encouraged to focus on prior projects encompassing the same RFQ requirements and 
describe how these requirements were specifically supported by the quoter. The quoter may use 
prior experiences in which they served as a prime contractor or subcontractor; however, past 
performance as a prime contractor may instill higher confidence. 
 
 
 

 
Volume II - Price Quotation: 
 
The offeror shall submit one (1) copy of their entire quotation, electronically, via E-mail to the 
Contract Specialist identified above. The price quotation shall address, at minimum, the following 
information.  
 
a) The solicitation number  
b) The name, phone number, and email address of the quoter's/contractor’s point of contact; 
c) Unique Entity Identifier # for quoter's/contractor’s active SAM.Gov registration. 
d) A firm fixed price for each required line item, including a unit price and total amount where 
applicable, and the aggregate quoted firm fixed price for the requirement. Where the 
Government has identified a line item as requiring a Not to Exceed price, quoters shall comply 
with this. 
e) If applicable, Shipping and Delivery costs must be included in the quotation either as a 
separate line item or contained in the total price of the quote. The quotation shall include a 
total firm fixed price for the requirement that includes all shipping/delivery costs 
f) Any applicable discount terms.  
 
Volume III – Terms and Conditions: 
 
The offeror shall review the provision and clauses attachment and complete any required 
information as record via a separate volume response to this solicitation.   
 
Note: System updates may lag policy updates. The System for Award Management (SAM) may 
continue to require entities to complete representations based on provisions that are not included 
in this solicitation. Contracting officers will rely on representations from offers based on provisions 
in the solicitation. Entities are not required to, nor are they able to, update their entity registration to 
remove these representations in SAM. 
 
Acceptance of Terms and Conditions: 
If the contractor objects to any of the terms and conditions contained in this solicitation, the contractor 
shall state "The terms and conditions in the solicitation are acceptable to be included in the award 
document with the exception, deletion, or addition of the following:" [Contractor shall list exception(s) 
and rationale for the exception(s)]. It is the sole responsibility of the contractor to identify in their 
quotation any exceptions to the terms and conditions of the solicitation. If the contractor does not 
include such a statement, the submission of a quotation in response to this solicitation will be regarded 
as the Contractor's acceptance of the Government's terms and conditions for inclusion into the 
resultant purchase order (PO).  
  
Note: This procurement is not being conducted under the GSA Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) program 
or another Government-Wide Area Contract (GWAC). If a quoter submits a quotation based upon an 
FSS or GWAC contract, the Government will accept the proposed price. However, the terms and 
conditions stated herein will be included in any resultant purchase order, not the terms and conditions 
of the Quoter’s FSS or GWAC contract, and the statement required above shall be included in the 
quotation.    
 

 
 
 
Basis of Award 
 
Evaluation Factors 
  
Award shall be made to the offeror whose quotation offers the best value to the Government price and 
other factors considered. The Government will evaluate quotations based on the following evaluation 
criteria listed in descending order of importance: 1) Technical Capability 2) Technical Key Personnel, 3) 
Past Performance, and 4) Price. All non-price factors, individually and when combined, are more 
important than price.  
  
Technical Capability: The government will evaluate the extent to which the offeror has demonstrated 
the technical capability to successfully perform these services, and demonstrated a feasible technical 
approach to successfully perform and manage the required tasks while ensuring that all deliverable 
schedule requirements are met.  
 
Technical Key Personnel:  
The Government will evaluate the key personnel proposed by the offeror for the extent to which they 
are qualified to efficiently and effectively address the requirements in the Statement of Work. The 
Government will consider the extent to which the proposed key personnel meets or exceeds the 
minimum qualifications identified in the Statement of Work, as well as the qualifications “preference” 
identified in the Statement of Work. Greater consideration will be given to key personnel that exceed 
the specific minimum qualification requirements and/or meet the key personnel preference identified 
in the Statement of Work. 
  
Past Performance: The Government will evaluate the Offeror's past performance information and, if 
appropriate, its proposed subcontractors' past performance to determine its relevance to the current 
requirement and the extent to which it demonstrates that the offeror has successfully completed 
relevant contracts in the past three years.  In assessing the offeror's past performance information, 
NIST will evaluate, as appropriate, successful performance of contract requirements, quality and 
timeliness of delivery of goods and services, cost management, communications between contracting 
parties, proactive management and customer satisfaction. Evaluation of this factor will be based on 
information contained in the technical portion of the quotation and information provided by 
references.  The Government will evaluate past performance information by contacting appropriate 
references, including NIST references, if applicable.  The Government may also consider other 
available information in evaluating the Offeror’s past performance.  The Government will assign a 
neutral rating if the offeror has no relevant past performance information.   
  
NOTE -- If an offeror does not have a history of relevant contract experience, or if past performance 
information is not available, the offeror will receive a neutral past performance rating; however, an 
offeror without a history of relevant experience may receive a lowered rating for the Experience Factor. 
  
Price: The Government will evaluate price for reasonableness. 
  
Past Performance, Experience, and Price shall not be evaluated on quotations that are 
determined technically unacceptable under the Technical Capability evaluation factor.

1 
 
 
REQUEST FOR INFORMATION 
U.S. Special Operations Command 
AI Based Protections on Commercial Internet  
 
 
27 April 2026 
 
 
 
 
 
 


2 
 
The United States Special Operations Command (USSOCOM), J6 is requesting 
information regarding AI driven cybersecurity solutions for use on its commercial internet 
service that can perform the following capabilities: 
Real-time threat detection, behavioral analytics, automated incident response, and 
continuous learning are necessary to counter increasingly sophisticated threats  to 
enhance the defensive posture of HQs USSOCOM commercial internet.   
This Request for I nformation (RFI) is for planning purposes only and shall not be 
considered as an invitation for bid, request for proposal, or as an obligation on the part of 
the Government to acquire any products or services. Your response to this RFI will be 
treated as i nformation only. No entitlement to payment of direct or indirect costs or 
charges by the Government will arise as a result of contractor submission of responses 
to this announcement of the Government use of such information. Interested parties are 
responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information 
contained in their response. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the 
basis of this RFI or to otherwise pay for the information submitted in response to this RFI. 
There are no guarantees of a follow-on contract for this requirement.   
The intent of the RFI is to: 
1) Identify artificial intelligence (AI) driven cybersecurity solutions that meet the 
minimum technical requirements identified below.  
The minimum technical requirements are as follows:  
• On-prem or hybrid deployment model and integration with existing security 
stacks and tools (e.g. MDE) 
• Protection of Windows, Linux, and Mac operating systems 
• Policy enforcement capabilities (blocking, prompting, step-up verification, session 
restriction) 
• Logging and auditing 
• Enhanced detection for exfiltration attempts, unauthorized access, and 
anomalous file activity 
• Zero Trust cybersecurity principles 
• Real-Time Web Filtering: Ability to analyze and block access to malicious 
websites, including phishing sites, and malware distribution points in real-time.  
• Predictive Threat Intelligence: Identify and block new and emerging (zero-day) 
malicious domains and URLs based on behavioral analysis, rather than relying 
solely on known threat feeds.  
• Encrypted Traffic Analysis: Capability to inspect encrypted traffic (e.g., TLS 1.3) 
for threats without compromising data privacy.  
• Anti-Phishing and Social Engineering Prevention: Advanced detection of 
sophisticated phishing, spear-phishing, and social engineering attempts by 
analyzing content, context, and sender behavior.  

3 
 
• Behavioral Baselining:  Establish and dynamically update a baseline of normal 
behavior for each user and entity (e.g., servers, devices, applications) on the 
network.  
• Anomaly Detection:  Identify and flag statistically significant deviations from 
established baselines that may indicate an insider threat, compromised 
credentials, or account takeover.  This includes detecting unusual login 
times/locations, abnormal data access patterns, and atypical system interactions.  
• Risk Scoring:  Assign risk scores to anomalous activities to help security teams 
prioritize alerts and focus on the most critical threats, reducing alert fatigue and 
false positives.  
• Data Discovery and Classification:  Automatically discover and classify sensitive 
data, such as CUI, across the domain   
• Data Loss Prevention (DLP):  Monitor and prevent the unauthorized exfiltration of 
sensitive data across various channels (e.g., email, web uploads, removable 
media). The system should understand the content and context of data to prevent 
leaks. 
• AI Governance: Provide visibility and control over the use of internal and external 
AI tools by employees to prevent the leakage of sensitive data into generative AI 
platforms. 
Responses to the RFI must include: 
i. Indicate if purchase can be made through NASA SEWP, GSA, FedBizOpps, or on 
some other Government Contract or Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) 
Responses should be no greater than a five page info paper or 15 slide PowerPoint 
presentation. Do not provide price quotes.  
Please provide the name of the firm, address, POC, phone/fax number, and email 
address. 
Responses will be viewed by both Government and non- Government employees.   If a 
Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) is required, submit the NDA with your response.  
E-mail responses only . All communication must be conducted via e- mail to 
Kristen.colyer@socom.mil.

1. Whether this effort is supporting an existing capability or contract, and if so, 
whether there is an incumbent solution currently in place:  This is not to support an 
existing capability 
2. Current cybersecurity tools and platforms in use across endpoint, network, and 
identity layers: Currently MDE, CISCO Firewall, and Active Directory 
3. Approximate scale of users, endpoints, and environments expected to be covered:  
~500 users and 500 endpoints which is a mix of Windows, Mac, and Linux 
operating systems 
4. Expected level of integration with existing systems such as endpoint protection, 
SIEM, and identity services:  Microsoft Defender Endpoint and Active Directory 
5. Desired operational model, including whether this capability is intended to augment 
an existing SOC or be delivered as a managed service: Automated with human 
interaction to ensure  
6. Key outcomes or performance improvements the Government is seeking to achieve 
through this capability: Use AI to protect the command’s commercial internet 
sometimes referred to as “dirty internet”  
7. Are FEDRAMP High SaaS solutions an option?  Yes, that is an option as long as it 
can work on our commercial (aka “dirty internet”) which is the network that the 
solution will be used on.

DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE 
AIR FORCE INSTALLATION CONTRACTING CENTER 
JOINT BASE SAN ANTONIO TEXAS 
 
 
 
REQUEST FOR INFORMATION 
773rd ENTERPRISE SOURCING SQUADRON (ESS) 
 
 
Issue Date:  4 May, 2026 
Response Due Date: 5 May, 2026 
NAICS Code:  541519, Other Computer Related Services 
Subject:  Request for Information (RFI) – AI Installation Lodging Optimization 
 
 
GENERAL INFORMATION 
 
Description: 
 
The 773
rd ESS at JBSA Lackland, Texas, seeks feedback from companies/entities capable of 
providing an AI Installation Lodging Optimization application. 
 
Background: (Per Performance Work Statement) 
 
1.1 Air Force Installation and Mission Support Center (AFIMSC) needs to improve its 
understanding of lodging and housing readiness across its global portfolio of installations. 
Today, the process is manual and relies on fragmented data, creating risks for capacity planning 
and deployment preparedness. 
 
The AI Installation Optimization Application should address this problem. The solution will 
securely integrate authoritative enterprise systems (e.g., ADVANA BLADE, ENVISION) to 
produce accurate pattern-of-life and utilization insights. It will allow planners to use natural-
language querying to assess lodging capacity, building conditions, and other factors. 
Furthermore, it will introduce forward-looking scenario modeling to support budget 
prioritization. This will enable faster assessments, smarter deployment planning, quicker 
decision-making, and better funding alignment with installation requirements and emerging bed 
down needs. 
 
General Information: 
 
THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A SOLICITATION AND IS BEING USED FOR THE 
PURPOSE OF MARKET ANALYSIS ONLY.  
 
Transfer of Undertakings, Protection of Employees (TUPE) may apply to any subsequent 
contract action. This notice is being published in accordance with Federal Acquisition 
Regulations (FAR) Part 5.101 requiring dissemination of information for proposed contract 
actions and FAR 10.001(a)(2)(ii) which requires conducting market research before soliciting 

 
  
 
offers for acquisitions with an estimated value in excess of the simplified acquisition threshold. 
The Government is seeking industry’s input to determine the availability of qualified sources 
with the technical capability to fulfill the AI Installation Lodging Optimization requirement. No 
contract awards will be made from this notice and no solicitation is available on sam.gov or any 
other bulletin board, posting room, or clearinghouse at this time.  
 
In order to develop a sound acquisition strategy, early industry participation is highly 
encouraged; however, participation in this effort is strictly voluntary. All costs associated with 
responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party’s expense. The Government will not 
reimburse costs and will not be liable for any costs associated with responses to this RFI. 
Respondents will not be notified of the responses to this notice. Responses to this notice are not 
considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. 
 
All RFI responses will be used in whole or in part for determining the most effective acquisition 
strategy for similar requirements in the future. Requested information will be used within the 
Department of the Air Force to facilitate decision making and will not be disclosed outside the 
agency. 
 
Response Guidelines: 
 
All responses to this RFI must be provided as an attachment in an e-mail message addressed to 
the Point of Contacts (POCs), below with the subject line “Response to RFI – AI Installation 
Lodging Optimization” no later than 5 May, 2026 at 1400 CST. Only electronic responses will 
be accepted. 
 
Requested Information: 
 
The following is requested from interested companies; 
 
1. Please indicate if your company is willing/ able to provide an AI Installation Lodging 
Optimization application or if there are any reasons that prevent your company from providing a 
quote/proposal should a formal solicitation be issued. 
 
2. Please provide brochures/descriptive liter ature including a capability statement 
commonly provided to the general public, if available. Please provide your CAGE/DUNS for 
SAM information as well. 
 
3. Based upon the above description and the att ached performance work statement, are there 
any aspects that are unclear and/or do not allow a clear understanding of the US Government’s 
requirements? 
 
Please submit a written response via scan/email-attachment on company letter head to the POCs 
listed below.

SECTION 2 
REQUIREMENTS 
2.1 BACKGROUND 
The OSMRE was established in the Department of the Interior by the Surface Mining 
Control and Reclamation Act of 1977 (30 U.S.C. 1211) (SMCRA).  The OSMRE carries 
out the requirements of the SMCRA in cooperation with States and Tribes. The Office 
protects people and the environment from the adverse effects of coal mining.  The 
OSMRE assures that land is restored to beneficial use after mining operations cease, and 
it mitigates the effects of past operations by reclamation of abandoned coal mines. 
The OSMRE mainly oversees State mining regulatory and abandoned-mine reclamation 
programs, assists States in meeting the objectives of surface mining law, and regulates 
mining and reclamation activities on Federal and Indian lands and in those States opting 
not to assume primary responsibility for regulating coal mining and reclamation activities 
within their borders. 
The OSMRE is organized with the Bureau Headquarters located in Washington DC, and 
three Regional Offices:  Appalachian (Pittsburgh, PA); Mid-Continent (Alton, IL); and 
Western (Denver, CO).  
The National Mine Map Repository (NMMR) is an archive of mine map images that serves 
image data to public and private stakeholders under Title II of SMCRA. Originally housed 
in the Bureau of Mines, the NMMR has been archiving mine map images since the 1960s. 
It is located in the OSMRE Appalachian Regional Office.  
Mine maps collected by the NMMR are scheduled as permanent federal records (N1-471-
93-001 & N1- 471-11-001). Performance requirements for digitizing permanent federal 
records were published in 36 CFR 1236 Subpart E in 2023. 
 
The NMMR uses large -format scanners to digitize mine maps. Historic mine maps are 
oversized documents on various physical media that are frequently stiff, damaged or dirty, 
making most unfit for scanning on feed- through or flatbed scanners. These maps must  be 
scanned using table scanners, where the sensor does not make contact with the map 
material, and the maps can be rearranged on the scanning table in cases where the table is 
too small to accommodate the entire map. 
 
2.2 MINIMUM TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS / SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS 
 
2.2.1 Scanner Configuration 
The scanner shall be a high-precision, overhead, non-contact imaging system designed to 
support fragile, oversized documents. 

2.2.1.1 Minimum Table Size 
The scanning table must have a minimum usable area of 78 × 47 inches. 
2.2.1.2 Vacuum Table 
The system must include a vacuum table capable of securing large, brittle materials 
without causing damage. 
2.2.1.3 Non-Contact Capture 
The imaging system must operate without direct physical contact between the sensor and 
the material being scanned. 
2.2.1.4 Critical System Components 
The scanner and its maintenance coverage shall explicitly include the following components: 
• 16K CMOS imaging sensor 
• DC SynchroLight lighting system 
• Motorized holding/scanning table 
 
2.2.1.5 Image Quality Requirements 
The scanner must meet all performance metrics of 36 CFR 1236.50(e)(4) at 400 DPI, 
validated using NARA-approved methods such as FADGI/DICE. 
2.2.1.6 Optical Resolution 
Minimum of 1600 PPI optical resolution, uniformly supported across the entire scanning 
surface. 
2.2.1.7 Tone & Color Accuracy 
• Tone Response (OECF ΔL*): ±5 
• White Balance ΔE(ab): ≤4% 
• Lightness Uniformity: ≤3% 
• Average Color Accuracy (ΔE2000): ≤3.5 
• 90th Percentile Color Accuracy: ≤8.75 
 
2.2.1.8 Geometric & Optical Performance 
• Color Channel Misregistration: <0.5 pixels 
• Sampling Efficiency (SFR10): >80% 
• MTF50: >40% and <75% of half sampling frequency 
• Reproduction Scale Accuracy: ±2% 
• Sharpening Modulation: <1.1 
 
2.2.1.9 Noise 
• Noise Upper Limit (Std. Dev L*): ≤2 
 

    2.3 Software Requirements 
    2.3.1 Core Software 
Vendor shall install all required scanning and control software on a Government-
furnished   workstation. 
   2.3.2 Post-Processing Tools 
The system must include a full software suite providing: 
• Lighting correction 
• Color and geometric normalization 
• Image stitching 
• 3D/relief rendering 
• Artifact correction 
• Metadata embedding 
• Quality assurance tools 
 
  2.3.3 Software & Firmware Support 
Vendor must provide, for the entire performance period: 
• All software updates (e.g., METIS Scan Director, Light Inspector) 
• All firmware updates, patches, and hotfixes 
 
 2.4 Installation & Calibration 
Vendor must provide: 
• Delivery and installation at the NMMR facility 
• Perform OEM-authorized calibration demonstrating compliance with 36 CFR 1236 
performance metrics 
• Validation using GoldenThread targets and OpenDICE (Government furnished) 
• Written documentation of calibration results 
Installation must be performed exclusively by OEM-authorized personnel. 
 2.5 Training Requirements 
Vendor must provide OEM-authorized, on-site training for at least three (3) NMMR 
personnel. 
Training topics shall include: 
• Scanner operation 
• Software workflows 
• Routine maintenance and calibration 
• Troubleshooting procedures 
Training must enable NMMR staff to independently operate and maintain the scanner and 
must be completed within 14 days of installation. 

 2.6 Maintenance and Service Requirements 
The Contractor shall provide comprehensive preventative and corrective maintenance 
services. 
  2.6.1 Preventative Maintenance 
The maintenance agreement must include: 
• 1-2 on-site preventative maintenance visits per year 
• Factory-authorized inspections and calibrations 
• System performance verification 
 
  2.6.1.2 Unscheduled ("Break/Fix") Maintenance 
Vendor must provide: 
• Diagnostics, parts replacement, and repair labor 
• No refurbished, non-OEM, or grey-market parts permitted 
 
  2.6.1.3 Service Level Agreements 
• Telephone support within 4 hours 
• On-site technician response within 24–48 hours 
• Services must occur during federal business hours (8:30 AM–5:00 PM, Monday–
Friday, excluding federal holidays) 
 
  2.7 Technician Qualifications 
All maintenance must be performed by factory-authorized or OEM-certified technicians. 
  2.8 Warranty 
The system must include a minimum three-year extended warranty covering: 
• All hardware components 
• Imaging sensors and lighting systems 
• Software and firmware defects 
• Calibration support 
• Repairs performed exclusively by OEM-certified technicians 
• Only new, OEM-approved replacement parts 
 
 2.9 Compliance 
The scanner must comply with: 
• 36 CFR 1236 Subpart E 
• 36 CFR 1236.46(b)(1) – Acceptable performance-evaluation methods 
• 36 CFR 1236.50(e)(4) – Image-quality performance metrics 
 
 2.10 DELIVERY SCHEDULE 
 

Equipment must be delivered within 60 days after contract award to address:  
Department of the Interior  
Office of Surface Mining and Reclamation (OSMRE) 
National Mine Map Repository (NMMR) 
Appalachian Regional Office

Pittsburgh, PA 15220

1  
Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
Joint Enterprise Tax Calculation Solution (JETCS) 
 
1. PROJECT TITLE 
Joint Enterprise Tax Calculator Solution (JETCS) 
2. BACKGROUND 
In August 2022, Congress enacted the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), which has had 
a significant impact on the Department of Treasury Internal Revenue Service (IRS) 
and its ability to serve the public. This act provides the IRS with a historic opportunity 
to transform the administration of the tax system and improve the services provided 
to taxpayers. The IRA aims to address the tax gap and ensure the fairness of the tax 
system. It provides long-term funding to the IRS allowing for technological upgrades, 
retiring of outdated legacy Information Technology (IT) systems, and investments in 
new technology to enable real-time data and analytics to improve customer 
experience and drive productivity. 
 
Aligned with the published IRS Strategic Operating Plan (IRS SOP), the IRS has 
adopted an IRA Integrated Roadmap that outlines how the IRS will better serve 
taxpayers, tax professionals, and the broader tax ecosystem.”1 The Roadmap 
projects pathways to achieving key outcomes including providing IRS employees 
with the hardware, software, and supplies needed to deliver effective and efficient 
results to taxpayers. To support this outcome which connects to retiring outdated 
technology, the IRS is interested in Commercial Off the Shelf (COTS) tax calculator 
solution due to its potential to replace widespread IRS use of specialized tax 
calculators. 
 
The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) utilizes a diverse array of calculators tailored to 
perform specific tax-related calculations. These tools are essential for audits of tax 
returns, collections of taxes or fees, and allocations of assets across various tax 
categories, such as individual returns, business returns, and estate or gift tax 
returns. The calculators range from Commercial Off-The- Shelf (COTS) software and 
products customized for integration with existing IRS systems, to internally 
developed applications and PDF forms and Excel workbooks for complex 
calculations.  
 
The objective is, a COTS cloud-based, single-tenant Software as a Service (SaaS) tax 
calculation solution that not only aligns with IRS’s stringent security protocols, including 
cybersecurity, Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP), and 
privacy standards but also seamlessly integrates with the IRS systems.  This solution is 
anticipated to support a high-volume, multi-user environment catering to both manual 
and automated IRS workflows. 
 
The tax calculator solution: 
• Must be federally compliant SaaS or deployable on IRS infrastructure.  

2  
• Can be one or more products that is explicitly for the computation of tax, 
interest, and penalties based on data provided. 
• Integrates with an optional vendor middleware.  
• Must be able to map IRS provided dataset to vendor software to perform the 
calculations.  
• Support a high-volume, multi-user environment catering to both manual and 
automated IRS workflows.  
• The solution will support a 10-year rolling tax window including current tax year, 
including single-year, multi-year, and associated multi-form/schedule tax 
computations for correcting tax.  
• Adhering to IRS's performance benchmarks, including peak load expectations 
and 99 percent uptime target and meet a maximum API response time of 10 
seconds.  
• Should have a user interface to view and edit returns.  
  
JETCS objective is to obtain tested, innovative tax calculator solution to integrate 
into IRS workflows and fulfilling complex computational needs. 
3. PURPOSE 
The tax calculation solution will integrate (i.e., interface or exchange information) 
with one or more systems in the IRS IT ecosystem. A primary use case for the tax 
calculator solution involves integration with the cloud-based IRS Enterprise Case 
Management (ECM) solution. The tax calculator solution will provide computations 
to support examiners. The tax calculator solution will receive IRS tax return data 
directly from the middleware to perform automated tax calculations based on tax 
return line-item data. The solution will perform an automated final single-year, multi-
year and associated multi-form/schedule tax computation for the corrected tax, 
penalties, and interest based on adjustments made to the individual or business 
account for a given tax year(s). 
 
IRS seeks a vendor that possesses fully tested, innovative, scalable tax calculator 
service for IRS-wide use with the ability to integrate and perform a full range of tax 
computation requests from single-user workflows to batch calculation requests to 
highly complex tax calculations. Results expected are a fully integrated tax 
calculation solution with IRS workflows that can fulfill IRS examiners’ complex 
computational needs. 
 
Included in scope the IRS expects the tax calculator solution to be maintained by 
the Contractor such that it will be updated in a timely manner and adjusted as 
needed to the evolving needs of the IRS and changes in tax laws. 
 
Furthermore, the IRS seeks to engage a vendor with a strong understanding of 
complex tax rules, regulatory requirements, and their practical application within 
automated calculation environments to ensure accuracy, compliance, and seamless 
system interoperability.  This expertise is vital for adapting the COTS product to 

3  
meet the specific needs of IRS examination workflows and to support future 
expansions, including large batch uploads for processing millions of returns. The 
vendor's responsibilities will extend to maintaining the solution in alignment with 
evolving IRS needs and tax law changes, thereby supporting the IRS Modernization 
objective to eventually consolidate various tax calculators into a single, efficient 
calculator. This initiative not only aims to fulfill immediate operational requirements 
but also positions the IRS to adapt swiftly to future tax calculation needs and 
legislative changes, ensuring sustained compliance and service excellence. 
 
4.  SCOPE OF WORK AND DESCRIPTION OF TASKS  
The scope of this procurement includes the tax calculation capabilities to support 
1040, 1120, 1065 and other priority workflows. The contractor shall maintain the 
1040 Tax Application for a 10-year rolling tax window including current tax year, 
incorporate updates from new tax regulations, and provide enterprise-wide 
application programming interface (API) licensing. The solution must ensure 
continuous vulnerability management and security compliance to obtain and 
maintain Authority to Operate, implement legislative updates as required, meet a 
maximum API response time of 10 seconds. This solution is essential to automating 
and improving the accuracy of IRS tax calculations and enhancing operational 
efficiency.   
Calculations for Forms: The solution will provide calculators for 1040 series, 
including all related forms, schedules, worksheets, and calculations triggered by 
interdependencies among these forms.  In addition, forms deemed priority by the 
business including but not limited to the following workflows: 1040, 1041, 1065, 
1120, 1120-S including associated forms, schedules and worksheets, and 
calculations triggered by interdependencies among these forms will be needed. The 
number of covered forms, schedules, and worksheets will expand as the IRS 
determines additional forms to be migrated into the solution. 
Calculations for Tax Years: The solution will support tax calculations for a 10-year 
rolling tax window through current year, facilitating advanced features and all tax 
years eligible for carryback and carryforward. The number of tax years covered will 
expand as the IRS determines additional forms, schedules, and worksheets to be 
migrated into the solution. The tax calculator solution will provide carryback and 
carry forward between forms/schedules across years without warranting the 
consuming application to provide the data (without multiple passes). For all eligible 
tax years, update and maintain the tax calculator solution to ensure ongoing 
adherence to annually indexed tax parameters as well as the Internal Revenue 

4  
Code, Treasury Regulations, legislative changes, new and/or modified IRS forms, 
schedules, and business needs. 
Seamless Integration: A key requirement is the solution’s capability to integrate 
flawlessly with IRS systems through open, efficient APIs. 
 
4.1 Task 1: Orientation Briefing  
Within two weeks of task order award, the Contractor shall conduct an orientation 
briefing for the Government. The Government does not desire an elaborate orientation 
briefing, nor does it expect the Contractor to expend significant resources in 
preparation for this briefing. Rather, the intent of the briefing is to initiate the 
communication process between the Government and Contractor by introducing key 
task order participants, explaining their roles, reviewing communication ground rules, 
and assuring a common understanding of task order requirements and objectives. 
The orientation briefing shall be held at the Government's facility and both parties 
shall mutually agree upon the date and time. 
The completion of this briefing shall result in the following: 
a) Initiate communications between the Government and Contractor and assure a 
common understanding of task order requirements, objectives, and 
expectations.  Delivery of required Orientation Briefing materials and briefing 
minutes to the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) after the briefing. 
b) The Contractor and Government personnel who will perform work under this 
task order will be introduced. 
c) The Government will show the applicable facilities to the Contractor if the 
Contractor will be performing work on the Government's site. 
d) The Government may provide any Government-Furnished Property (GFP) to 
the Contractor at this time. 
e) Any issues concerning the Contractor clearances for Contractor personnel will 
be discussed. 
f) The Contractor shall demonstrate confirmation of their understanding of the 
work to be accomplished under this Task Order PWS. 
g) The Contractor shall provide the accounting period end dates to be used for the 
term of this task order. 
h) The Contractor shall provide a list of Key Personnel (See C.5.1.1). 
i) The contractor shall take minutes during the orientation meeting and document 
the key points of discussion, action items and who will perform them as well as 
who was in attendance.  
DESIRED OUTCOME: Initiate the communication process between the Government and 
contractor and assure a common understanding of the task order requirements, 

5  
objectives, and expectations; delivery of required Orientation Briefing materials and 
Briefing minutes to the COR after the Briefing 
 
4.2 Task 2: System Integration and Performance  
Integration Support 
The Contractor shall ensure seamless integration of calculation services into JIOS 
workflows and support all required testing and validation activities. 
Accuracy of Calculations 
The Contractor shall ensure that all calculation results transmitted to the calling 
application are accurate and consistent with applicable tax rules and business 
logic. 
Performance Requirements 
When complex calculations are initiated from JIOS as part of customer workflows, 
the Contractor shall ensure: 
• Calculation accuracy meets 100% compliance with approved tax computation logic. 
• Response times meet established performance thresholds (e.g., within 10 seconds 
per transaction, as defined by the Government). 
 
DESIRED OUTCOME: The desired outcome of this effort is the continued availability and 
reliable performance of the COTS Tax Calculator service to support JIOS workflows and 
other IRS systems. The service shall deliver accurate and timely tax calculations, 
seamlessly integrate into customer workflows, and ensure calculation results are transmitted 
correctly to calling applications. The Contractor shall maintain required performance 

6  
standards, accuracy, and system reliability necessary to support the successful closure of 
audits. 
4.3 Task 3: Operational and Maintenance (O&M) Objectives  
• Perform ongoing update and maintenance of the tax calculator solution to ensure it 
remains in line with annually indexed tax parameters, the IRC, Treasury Regulations, 
and specific IRS needs.   
• Promptly incorporate annual and ad-hoc legislative changes and full support for testing 
related to full functionality, data and calculation accuracy, compliance, and performance 
requirements.  
• In the event of an outage, participate in triage and resolution efforts, adhering to the

• Provide plans and timelines for any required updates, whether vendor-led or in 
collaboration with the IRS.  
• Set up and provide tools and processes for continuous monitoring and reporting on

DESIRED OUTCOME: Ensure the COTS Tax Calculator service remains accurate, 
compliant with legislative changes, and fully operational. Required updates shall be 
implemented within established timelines, with continuous monitoring and enhancements to 
maintain performance, reliability, and alignment with IRS operational needs.
