Sources Sought Notice 
Instructions For Use Software 
Title:    Instructions For Use Software  
Agency:  Indian Health Service, Office of Quality 
Issue Date:  Monday, May 4, 2026 
Due Date:  Friday, May 15, 2026 no later than 12:00pm EST 
POCs:  Responses must be submitted via email to Natasha.Bitsoi@ihs.gov. Include “SSN-Instructions For 
Use Software – Your Company Name” in the Subject of the email.   
 
This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is for market research and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a 
solicitation or an obligation or commitment to issue a solicitation by the Indian Health Service  (IHS). This SSN is 
seeking information from  the specific type s of entities  listed below to assess their capabilities in fulfilling the 
requirements set forth in this SSN. The information from this SSN will be used to determine the appropriate set-aside, 
if any, in accordance with the applicable regulations listed. The Government encourages the identified to respond to 
this Notice and will be assessed of their capabilities in the following priority: 
 
1. Indian Small Business Economic Enterprise (ISBEE), 
2. Indian Economic Enterprise’s (IEE) in accordance with HHSAR 326.603-1. 
3. Small business concerns in accordance with FAR Overhaul 19.104. 
 
Responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, 
including whether a ny ISBEE /IEE or small business  set-aside is possible  based on the Contracting Officer’s 
reasonable expectation of obtaining offers from two or more relevant concerns that will be competitive in terms of 
market price, product quality, and delivery capability. An organization that is not considered an ISBEE/IEE firm 
or small business under the applicable NAICS code should NOT submit a response to this notice. The applicable 
primary NAICS code for this requirement is 518210– Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web 
Hosting, and Related Services. Generic capability statements are not sufficient and may not be considered when 
assessing entity capabilities. 
 
Background 
 
The IHS provides comprehensive primary health care and disease prevention services to approximately 2.8 million 
American Indian and Alaska Native (AI/AN) people in 574 federally recognized tribes through a network of more 
than 605 hospitals, clinics, and health stations on or near Indian reservations. IHS facilities are located across 12 Areas 
and serve populations in rural and urban locations in 37 states. IHS healthcare facilities are accredited and Centers for 
Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) certified  to ensure high‑quality, safe, evidence‑based care and to support 
third‑party billing for eligible AI/AN patients. 
Description of Supplies/Services 
 
Background: IHS federal healthcare facilities are required by Joint Commission, Centers for Medicare 
and Medicaid Services (CMS) and other accrediting medical organizations to establish and maintain a safe and 
functional environment for everyone who enters  the organization’s facilities. Manufacturers’ Instructions for Use 
(IFU) and other critical infection control reference documents must be readily available to staff.    
 
The objective of this requirement is to provide a reliable, accessible solution for consistent access to manufacturer 
Instructions for Use and related documentation across all federal Indian Health Service (IHS) facilities. The system 
shall ensure IFUs are readily available and consistently accessible to support patient safety, infection prevention, and 
regulatory compliance.  
 
The Contractor shall provide a commercial off -the-shelf (COTS), automated, web -based Instructions for Use (IFU) 
and Safety Data Sheet (SDS) repository system for use by federal Indian Health Service (IHS) healthcare facilities. 
The software must provide online access to all required Instructions for Use, service manuals, safety data sheets, and 
other manufacturer guidelines, and resources for instruments, equipment, and supplies related to dental, 
medical/surgical and biomedical instruments and equipment, a nd consumables, tissues and implants, and chemicals 
that are in use at each IHS federal facility. 
 
System Requirements:  

  
Sources Sought Notice 
Instructions For Use Software 
The Contractor shall provide a centralized, searchable repository that includes, at a minimum: Instructions for Use 
(IFUs) for medical, surgical, and dental instruments and equipment, IFUs and documentation for implantable and non-
implantable devices, tiss ues, and biologics, Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and archived MSDS documents, Preventive 
maintenance (PM) manuals, service manuals, and technical documentation for biomedical and non -medical 
equipment, Documentation for consumables, including single-use items and chemical products, Facility maintenance 
equipment documentation (e.g., HVAC, fire safety systems), Manufacturer notices, recalls, alerts, and letters of 
obsolescence.  
 
The system shall include search functionality by manufacturer, device name, model number, product type, or keyword.  
 
The Contractor shall provide users with real -time access to current, validated manufacturer documentation.  The 
system shall ensure access to the most current version of all IFUs, manuals, and SDS documents.  
 
The Contractor shall ensure that all documentation supports compliance with applicable regulatory and accreditation 
standards by Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services 
(CMS), Joint Commission (JC), Accreditation Association for Ambulatory Health Care (AAAHC), Association for 
the Advancement of Medical Instrumentation (AAMI), an ANSI-accredited standards development organization,  and 
other applicable federal, state, and local medical regulatory authorities. 
 
System Integration and Interoperability:  
The Contractor shall ensure the system supports interoperability with Government systems and workflows.  The 
system shall support integration with instrument tracking systems, asset management systems, and computerized 
maintenance management systems (CMMS).  
 
User Access Control and Security:  
The Contractor shall provide secure, role-based access controls and user management capabilities.   
The system shall enforce appropriate access restrictions to prevent unauthorized access outside assigned levels while 
allowing higher -level users to maintain oversight.  All access shall comply with applicable federal security 
requirements, including secure authentication and multi-factor authentication (MFA).   
 
Information Technology and Accessibility Requirements  
The system will comply with all applicable federal IT security requirements. The SaaS solution shall comply 
with Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act and WCAG 2.1 Level AA accessibility standards. The Contractor shall 
also comply with applicable federal IT security requirements, including FISMA and NIST SP 800-53.   
 
The system shall meet FedRAMP certification requirements or provide information if your system is hosted on a third-
party non-federal FedRAMP cloud or if the system would require hosting on a federally approved server or cloud. 
 
Capability Statement/Submission Information 
To assist the Government in an expeditious review of your capabilities, the capability statement should be organized 
as follows: 
 
• Cover page 
• Executive Summary 
• Technical Areas in the order listed 
• Past Performance 
• Other Information, as applicable 
 
The tailored capability statement should not exceed 15 pages excluding Past Performance information. Font must not 
be less than 10 point (for readability) and may be submitted in either in either Microsoft Word or Adobe Portable 
Document Format (PDF) but must be a standard 8-1/2 by 11 inch in paper size. All proprietary information should be 
marked as such. 
 
Cover Page 
Please provide a cover page to include: 
 

  
Sources Sought Notice 
Instructions For Use Software 
1. Company Name 
2. Company Designation (ISBEE/IEE/SB)  
3. Type of Business – as applicable (e.g. 8(a), Woman Owned Small Business, HUBZone, etc.)   
4. UEI Number 
5. Point of contact 
6. Primary NAICS Code(s) 
7. Existing federal contracting vehicle(s) numbers, as applicable (e.g. GSA MAS number, NITAAC/CIO SP3, 
etc.) 
8. System for Award Management (SAM) registration status. Note, all respondents must be registered on the 
SAM located at http://www.sam.gov/ prior to any potential award. 
 
Executive Summary 
Provide a high-level overview of your services and include how it will benefit the Indian Health Service. 
 
Technical Areas 
Provide an overview of your IFU software/system for the anticipated requirement to include but not limited to:  
- System capabilities & functionality 
- System workflows & operability 
- System access control 
- System IT certifications i.e. FedRamp certification 
- System reporting and analytics functionality 
- Estimated general pricing of services 
- Experience supporting federal or other healthcare organizations 
- Customer support and technical assistance model 
 
Past Performance 
Please provide any past performance information to support a demonstration of your capabilities in the relevant 
technical areas and magnitude of work. 
 
Other Information (Optional) 
You may include any other information that may be helpful in developing or finalizing the requirements of the 
potential acquisition.  
 
Generic capability statements are not sufficient and will not be considered compliant with the requirements of 
this notice. 
 
Disclaimer and Important Notes  
This notice does not obligate the Government to award  a contract. Any information provided by industry to the 
Government as a result of this SSN is strictly voluntary. Responses will not be returned. No entitlements to payment 
of direct or indirect costs or charges to the Government will arise as a result of contractor submission of responses, or 
the Government's use of such information or otherwise pay for the information provided in response. The Government 
reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally 
appropriate. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its respon se is complete and sufficiently 
detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization’s capabilities to perform the work. Respondents are 
advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide 
feedback to respondents with respect to any  information submitted. After a review of the responses received, a pre -
solicitation synopsis and solicitation may be published on a government GPE. However, responses to this Notice will 
not be considered adequate responses to any resultant solicitation. 
 
Confidentiality. No classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response. The 
Government reserves the right to use any non-proprietary technical information in any resultant solicitation(s).

STATEMENT OF WORK  
 
 
1. Objective/Requirements 
 
This requirement is for the acquisition of the FY26 Total Materia Renewal for NASA 
Headquarters (HQ). The information listed below is required to complete this purchase. 
 
2. Characteristics, Scope, and Specs 
 
QTY DESCRIPTION 
1 Total Materia Basic Package + Extended Range + SmartComp + Material 
Console + Compliance; Corporate License, Annual 
Components: 
Total Materials, DataPLUS, Suppliers, Tracker, Extended Range, 
SmartComp, Material Console, Compliance 
 
The Contractor shall provide access to the Materials Database to the NASA user 
community comprised of NASA personnel and on-site contractors residing at each of the 
15 NASA Facilities, including ancillary facilities, as follows: 
• Location 1: Ames Research Center (ARC). 
• Location 2: Armstrong Flight Research Center (AFRC). 
• Location 3: John H. Glenn Research Center (GRC). 
• Location 4: Robert H. Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC). 
• Location 5: Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL). 
• Location 6: Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center (JSC). 
• Location 7: John F. Kennedy Space Center (KSC). 
• Location 8: Langley Research Center (LaRC). 
• Location 9: George C. Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC). 
• Location 10: NASA Headquarters (HQ). 
• Location 11: John C. Stennis Space Center (SSC). 
• Location 12: Michoud Assembly Facility (MAF). 
• Location 13: White Sands Test Facility (WSTF)/White Sands Complex (WSC). 
• Location 14: Wallops Flight Facility (WFF). 
• Location 15: Independent Verification and Validation (IV&V) (NASA Katherine 
Johnson IV&V Facility” in Fairmont, West Virginia) 
 
The Contractor shall provide direct, seamless, electronic access to the Materials Database 
from NTSS and for transfer of a user’s profile from NTSS to the Materials Database that 
includes the following data, at a minimum: 
• User’s universally unique identifier (UUID) (acquired via the Security Assertion 
Markup Language (SAML) login). 
• User’s first name (acquired via the SAML login). 
• User’s last name (acquired via the SAML login). 
• User’s email (acquired via the SAML login). 

• User’s Center (acquired via the SAML login). 
 
The Contractor shall provide on-demand access via electronic authorization (SAML) to 
users who have been identified and authenticated in the NASA Account Management 
System (NAMS). 
 
The Contractor shall provide a Web-based, user-friendly, robust architecture that is 
seamlessly integrated for effectively accessing materials data. 
 
The Contractor shall provide search capability for users to find and export material 
information quickly and efficiently by: 
• Material designation, searching by the alphanumerical or numerical material 
designation. 
• Property values, mechanical and physical. 
• Standard number. 
 
The Contractor shall provide a one-stop shop for engineering materials information that 
includes built-in tools to help the user choose the most optimal material for the design, 
with sharing capabilities to limit repetition within an organization. 
 
The Contractor shall provide multiple material groups and material properties, including 
metals (ferrous and non-ferrous), non-metals (polymers, ceramics, composites, fibers, 
cement, honeycombs, foams, wood), coatings, lubricants, adhesives, and substances. 
 
The Contractor shall provide general material properties and information as follows: 
• Material description, highlighting its applications, standard, and/or processes. 
• Various temperature values and various conditions for each material designation. 
• Mechanical properties. 
• Physical properties. 
• Chemical composition. 
• Heat treatment diagrams and standard descriptions. 
• Metallography diagrams, including microstructure diagrams in various grain 
sizes. 
• Machinability and manufacturing processes information. 
• Global equivalents list. 
 
The Contractor shall provide advanced material properties for the following: 
• Stress/strain diagrams. 
• Formability data, including high-strain curves, forming limit curves, bendability 
data, and r-factors. 
• Fatigue data, including total, plastic, and elastic curves; experimental points; and 
S-N curves. 
• Fracture mechanics, including KIC values and Paris Law curves. 
• Creep data, including creep rupture strength data tables and Larson-Miller 
parameter estimator. 

The Contractor shall provide the following additional data: 
• Welding, brazing, and adhesion information, including material weld properties, 
consumable property data, weld regime information, and additional joining 
information. 
• Tribology information such as how two surfaces behave in motion. 
• Corrosion information, including, but not limited to, corrosion resistance data, 
pitting resistance equivalent number (PREN), pitting, and chemical resistance. 
• Weatherability information, including property values of materials in various 
environmental conditions. 
• Ageing information, including time/temperature dependency information and 
diagrams and fluid degradation data. 
• Irradiation, including exposure time versus radiation diagrams. 
• Suppliers’ information, including contact information. 
• Compliance information, including compliance regulations for non-metals and 
substances. 
 
The Contractor shall provide the capability to create material lists, bookmarks, and 
material reports with options to save, share information, and download material and 
compliance reports in portable document format (PDF). 
 
The Contractor shall provide the capability to download and export material information 
to computer-aided engineering (CAE)/computer- aided design (CAD) solvers and 
Microsoft Excel. 
 
The Contractor shall provide the following tools: 
• Unknown metals identification tool, an intelligent metal identification system by 
chemical composition obtained from a spectrometer or other analytical sources 
through a patented algorithm. 
• Compliance regulations assessments that instantly assesses materials’ compliance 
using composition data. 
• Data information tracking tool with the ability to monitor monthly updates, 
specifically the changes and additions to each material and standard revisions and 
replacements. 
• Material comparison methods for multiple ways to compare specific material 
properties for several materials at once. 
• Similar materials search engine for finding materials with similar property values 
such as mechanical and physical properties, material group, and chemical 
composition. 
 
The Contractor shall provide the capability to create material lists, bookmarks, and 
material reports with options to save, share information, and download material and 
compliance reports in PDF. 
 
The Contractor shall provide the capability to download and export material information 
to CAD/CAD solvers and Microsoft Excel. 
 

Current database content and addition of new materials and datasets shall be updated at 
least monthly. 
 
The Contractor shall provide a Materials Database via NTSS that complies with Section 
508 of the Rehabilitation Act. 
 
The Contractor shall have detailed quality control procedures in place to ensure 
requirements of the contract are met and the data in the Materials Database are current, 
accurate, and timely. 
 
The Contractor shall provide advance notice to the Government if the Materials Database 
will be temporarily unavailable on the Website and of potential system performance 
impacts in advance of scheduled outages for maintenance. 
 
The Contractor shall schedule planned downtime during off-duty hours if necessary for 
maintenance. 
 
The Contractor shall notify the Government immediately if the Materials Database 
becomes inaccessible and provide reasons for the downtime. 
 
The Contractor shall provide notification to the Government when the Materials Database 
becomes accessible following all downtime. 
 
The Contractor shall provide technical customer support by personnel with detailed 
knowledge of the Materials Database to respond to Government user issues 24 hours a 
day/7 days a week that includes digitizing and curating material information based on 
user requests; programming, testing, and adding additional functionalities and tools to the 
database based on user requests; interpreting user requests; and providing support with 
the most challenging metals identification, properties search, and general standards 
information. 
 
The Contractor shall provide feedback to the Government regarding types of issues 
reported by NASA users. 
 
The Contractor shall provide unlimited Web-based training on use of the Materials 
Database and prior to release of new features and enhancements. 
 
3. Place of Performance 
 
E-delivery to NASA HQ 
ATTN: Tracy Osborne 
 
4. Period of Performance 
 
05/21/26 – 05/31/27 
Need by: 05/20/26

destroy the application. When processing is completed the applicant will appear, in person at Pass

for 1 year, whichever is the shorter period of time. Passes for contractor personnel where the
performance period extends beyond 1 year, or where the contract is extended beyond the original
scheduled completion date, will have to be reissued. Procedures for reissue will be the same for
the original issue.

Statement of Work 

A. Project Title

VISN 23 Zeiss Forum Support Agreement for Surgery ICC

B. Procurement Type

Sole Source

C. Introduction

VA Midwest Healthcare Network (VISN 23) requires a base plus four (4) option year support agreement for the Zeiss FORUM ophthalmic data management platform. The existing warranty period has expired, and continued upgrade vendor-supported maintenance is necessary to ensure all FORUM systems within VISN 23 remain fully operational, secure, and compatible with requirements for the Federal Electronic Health Record (EHR) deployment.

D. Background

Zeiss FORUM is the primary system used within VISN 23 ophthalmology clinics to manage, store, and integrate ophthalmic diagnostic imaging data. The platform interfaces with key ophthalmic modalities and supports clinical workflows that feed into enterprise health record systems. With the expiration of the original warranty, VISN 23 no longer receives software updates, security patches, or technical troubleshooting from the vendor. To maintain compliance with Federal EHR integration requirements and ensure clinical continuity, a formal support contract is needed.

E. Scope

The contractor shall provide comprehensive support services for all FORUM servers, clients, interfaces, and connected modules deployed across VISN 23: Black Hills Ft. Meade and Hot Springs, Central Iowa, Fargo, Iowa City, Minneapolis, Omaha, Grand Island, Lincoln, Sioux Falls, St. Cloud.

F. Place of Performance

The VISN 23 facilities and addresses are outlined in the table below:

G. Period of Performance

The Contractor shall provide Zeiss Forum support for all VISN 23 facilities for a period of one base year plus four (4) option years:

Unless otherwise noted, work shall be performed during normal business days and hours at each VA facility, which is typically comprised of Monday through Friday each week (except federal holidays) between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. local standard time.   Contractor shall confirm each facility normal business days and hours with facility Point of Contacts (POCs).

H. Point of Contacts

The COR shall confirm and provide an updated list of facility Point of Contacts (POCs) to the Contractor after award.  The Contractor shall work with facility POC(s) to get additional facility POC(s) as needed to assist with coordination, planning and implementation of support, testing and maintenance.

The Contractor shall provide the COR and facility POC(s) an Escalation Pathway process and list of Contractor POC(s) with after-hours cell phone numbers and emails for VA to use during urgent/emergent situations that need quick resolution.

I. Out of Scope Services

Contractor shall immediately, but not later than 24 consecutive hours after discovery, notify the CO and COR, (in writing), of the existence of the development of any defects in, or remediation required to, the scheduled solution which the contractor considers they are not responsible for under the terms of the contract. Contactor shall furnish the COR with a written estimate of the cost to make necessary remediation. Any additional charges claimed will be approved by the CO via the COR before service is completed.

J. Work Performance

The Contractor shall provide/comply with the following requirements:

Software updates and upgrades, including all major and minor releases per VHA security protocols, procedures and requirements of the VA’s Office of Information Technology.

Provide all licensing required to support the system.

Virus protection updates, security patches and maintenance required for Federal EHR compatibility.

Technical support via phone, email, or remote access. FORUM Support Line is (844) 352-2965 and email is datamanagment.meditec.us@zeiss.com 

Provide Remote Engineering Technical Support M-F 5am to 5pm PST support to address, escalated issues, questions and problems on an immediate, real-time basis.

Provide diagnosis/root cause analysis.

Provide defined resolution approach: workaround or fix.

Provide operator instruction on actions to be taken on the customer's end to correct the problem.

Provide quality and training initiatives to increase operator knowledge and decrease the number of incoming incidents.

Guidance, troubleshooting and support for system, database, interface, configuration, workflow optimization and issues, and connectivity with ophthalmic devices.

Access to Zeiss FORUM knowledge bases, engineering resources, and system documentation.

Validation assistance and support for updates required for VA/DoD EHR integration.

Provide solutions based on current technology and provide options for enhancements.

Communicate and coordinate in advance to the COR and facility POC(s) any third-party products, software, or services that are needed at each facility, but are not provided by the Contractor, so VA can plan and coordinate to procure any items needed separately.

Perform quality assurance and connectivity testing. Upon completion of service, the Contractor shall test the system to ensure it is fully functional in accordance with the manufacturer specifications and VA standards. Testing shall be coordinated and scheduled with the COR and facility POC(s).

Provide support compatible with Federal EHR and VISTA EMR systems. The current EMR is VISTA and the future EMR is Federal EHR.  The Contractor shall provide implementation, testing and support of all interface requirements between the system and VistA. Contractor shall ensure connectivity and interfacing with EMR is functional.

Coordinate with other Vendors and/or Contractors (e.g., Federal EHR) and/or VA when necessary to maintain system operational uptime.

Provide overnight, next-day delivery of parts when needed to maintain full performance of the system. The Contractor shall provide shipping to return any defective parts from VA Facilities to the Contractor. There shall be no additional cost to the Government for shipping.

K. Conformance Standards

The Contractor shall ensure all products function in conformance with the latest published edition and guidelines of Manufacturer’s Specifications, Association for the Advancement of Medical Instrumentation (AAMI), Joint Commission for the Accreditation of Healthcare Organizations (JCAHO), National Fire Protection Agency 99 (NFPA-99), Center for Device and Radiological Health (CDRH), Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), American Hospital Association (AHA), Institute of Electrical And Electronic Engineers (IEEE), Underwriters Laboratories (UL), Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), College of American Pathologists (CAP), VAHCS standard, and any other Federal, State, and Local regulations pertaining to the products listed for this contract.

L. Network Security

The Contractor shall comply with all VHA security protocols, procedures and requirements of the VA’s Office of Information Technology including filling out and providing all necessary forms upon request within ten (10) days from receipt from the VA:

Any connections to the VA OI&T network shall be compliant with VA Directive 6500 and 6550.  

The Contractor shall complete and return separate 6550 forms with accurate information for the product and software. 

The Contractor shall provide each product’s MDS2, network topology infrastructure.

and a diagram of data flow for each product. 

Any offsite server or network maintenance or support provided by the Contractor can only be done via VPN access after the Contractor has obtained the Site-to-Site (S2S) VPN access from the VA. A Business Associates Agreement (BAA) and Memorandum of Site-to-Site Understanding/Interconnection Security Agreement (MOU/ISA) may be required.  

The Contractor shall complete and return BAA forms for the product. 

The Contractor shall have an active MOU-ISA in place, or the Contractor shall work with VA to get an MOU-ISA in place within 6 months of award if determined beneficial. 

If applicable, the product software shall be approved in the Office of Information Technology’s Technical Resource Manual (TRM) or the Contractor shall be willing to gain approval in TRM. 

The product shall be FIPS 140-2 or FIPS 140-3 compliant or current version. The Contractor will identify the certificate number for FIPS compliance. 

If a cloud service Platform as a Service (PaaS), Cloud Instance or Software as a Service (SaaS) is selected as part of the project to include providing software patches, please review and reference VA Directive 6517 Cloud Computing Services and follow VA Enterprise Cloud Solution Intake processes.

Describe whether the system can integrate with Active Directory or LDAP or Single Sign-on (SSO) with Active Directory.

M. Implementation/Project Management

The Contractor shall provide project management services as needed as part of the support purchase for recalls, PM’s, upgrades, etc, included in the support contract. Project Management Services shall include, but are not limited to: 

A project manager.

A Contractor Project Management Plan (CPMP) that lays out the Contractor’s approach, timeline, and tools to be used in execution of the contract. The CPMP should take the form of both a narrative and graphic format that displays the schedule, milestones, risks, and resource support. The CPMP shall also include how the Contractor shall coordinate and execute planned, routine, and ad hoc data collection reporting requests. The initial baseline CPMP shall be concurred upon and updated with the COR and facility POC(s). The Contractor shall update and maintain the VA PM-approved CPMP throughout the POP.  The CPMP shall include but is not limited to:.

A Gantt Chart (or similar chart) with defined roles and responsibilities (including Contractor provided and VA resources) outlining the detailed support timeline.

Technical support plan to configure, test, and calibrate the products, interfaces, software, etc.

Updates and upgrades plan and checklist outlining any pre-work needed for site readiness.

Training plan to include but not limited to Clinical user and super user training, Biomed technical training, before, during and after updates and upgrades.

VISN 23 has designated technical, clinical and logistics POC(s) for each facility that shall be provided upon award.  The Contractor shall work with the COR and facility POC(s) to coordinate and implement the support, maintenance, updates and upgrades.

Within 2 weeks of the award date, the Contractor shall provide a draft project management plan with milestones, deliverables, and draft schedule/timeline, including the activities required in support of PM’s, updates and upgrades and clearly delineating the party responsible for accomplishing each activity.

Within 3 weeks of the award date, the Contractor shall hold a kickoff meeting with the designated COR and facility technical, clinical and logistics POC(s) to review the project management plan, communications plan, support plan and schedule.

The Contractor project manager shall hold weekly or as needed periodic project meetings (via MS Teams) with the COR and facility POC(s) to report progress, challenges and lessons learned for all facilities.

The Contractor shall provide a meeting agenda prior to all meetings and send meeting minutes including attendance after each meeting to the stakeholders.  If possible, the Contractor shall record all meetings and share the recording with all the VA stakeholders in the meeting minutes.  The recording shall be available to VA upon request and shall not expire.

When the update and upgrade service is complete at each facility, the Contractor shall present an acceptance letter to the facility POC(s) and COR for signature.

Within 3 weeks of updates and upgrades completion, the Contractor shall hold a Lessons Learned meeting with the COR and facility POC(s) to review project input and feedback. The contractor shall include an After-Action Report with the meeting minutes outlining the lessons learned and action items discussed, including but not limited to:

What can be improved and done better next time.

What items that can be fixed.

 Suggest solutions to identified problems.

 If there is no solution yet, provide some options.

What are the successes to maintain those strengths.

N. Manuals, Release Notes and Service Bulletins

VA will not provide service manuals of service diagnostic software to the contractor.  The contractor shall obtain, have on file, and make available to its personnel all operational and technical documentation, (such as:  operational and service manuals, schematics, and parts list), which are necessary to meet the performance requirements of this contract. The location and listing of the service data manuals, by name, and/or the manuals themselves shall be provided to the COR and facility POC(s) upon request.

The Contractor shall provide unlimited electronic copies and ongoing web-based access of the following documentation necessary for the operation and support of the system. These deliverables should be provided to the COR and facility POC(s) at the post award kick off meeting. Any upgrades to these documents shall be provided by the Contractor free of charge.  

User, System Administration, Operating/Maintenance Manuals, Release Notes and Service Bulletins.

Complete technical service manuals including troubleshooting guides, necessary diagnostic software and products, schematic diagrams, and parts lists.

Electronic schematics, troubleshooting guides and parts lists for each proudct purchased.

Manuals shall include all components and subassemblies, including those not manufactured by the Contractor. 

Manuals and documentation shall be identical to the ones supplied to the manufacturer’s service representatives and shall contain the diagnostic codes, commands, and passwords used in maintenance, repair and calibration of the product.

Training videos and materials for future staff.

O. Training

The Contractor providing the support will be responsible for staff/user clinical and Biomed Technician service and support technical training remotely. System training shall be conducted prior to the system updates and upgrades and shall be conducted at various times to meet the needs of multiple VA work shifts.  Training shall include initial user training, super user training and follow-up training.  The Contractor shall coordinate with facility POC(s) and COR to provide staff education at a day/time that works for each VA facility. A System Technology and Services education professional (not sales reps) shall administer the training.  Education curriculum must include the following:

Clinical training:

Clinical applications training.

Training on the user interface, application, and its features.

Super-user and end-user training with the capability of being self-sufficient in operating the system by the end of the training session.

Quick notes or reference guides.

7. Question #7: 
 
“Please confirm whether the requirement for experience supporting earth and 
atmospheric science laboratories is strictly mandatory, or if experience in other scientific 
laboratory environments (e.g., physics, chemistry, or biology labs) demonstrating 
equivalent expertise in instrument integration and scientific software development will be 
considered acceptable. If acceptable, please clarify how equivalency will be evaluated.” 
 
USGS’s Response: Experience supporting earth and atmospheric science 
laboratories is essential to ensure the Contractor is familiar with the type of 
instrumentation and its applications. The U.S. Geological Survey’s Denver Argon 
Geochronology Lab (DAGL) involves highly specialized scientific instruments, 
unique data-acquisition workflows, rigorous environmental controls, and custom 
software ecosystems that are not reasonably comparable to other laboratory 
environments. 
 
8. Question #8: 
 
“Please confirm whether all development activities must be performed onsite at the 
Denver Federal Center, or if a hybrid model (remote development with periodic onsite 
integration/testing) is permissible. If hybrid is allowed, please specify the expected onsite 
frequency and any tasks that must be strictly performed onsite.” 
 
USGS’s Response: The lead developer is expected to be onsite throughout the 
development of the product. The computer system connected to the 
instrumentation is not accessible remotely. 
 
9. Question #9: 
 
“Does the Government have any preferred or existing software architecture frameworks, 
design patterns, or reusable code bases (e.g., from other USGS labs) that the contractor is 
required or encouraged to leverage?” 
 
USGS’s Response: The Contractor will be granted access to a comparable 
LabVIEW package from a similar laboratory for their use.

STATEMENT OF NEED 
55th Operations Support Squadron 
1. This document outlines the requirement for a comprehensive management program for the 55th Operations 
Support Squadron at Offutt AFB. The contractor shall provide a solution that integrates both a flying hours 
management program and a fuel management transaction program, meeting or exceeding the specifications detailed 
below. 
 
2. General Requirements 
The integrated program shall possess the following core attributes: 
• Platform: A secure, web-based application operating within a .MIL cloud environment. 
• Accreditation: The system must have an existing Authority to Operate (ATO), be an Air Force System of 
Record, and a DoD-identified authoritative data source. 
• Personnel: The contractor must provide certified developers and trainers for the system. 
• Updates: The program must have the ability to be updated to align with new and evolving requirements. 
• Training: The contractor will be responsible for the setup, installation, and training of all users by 
certified trainers. 
 
3. Flying Hours Management Program 
This component of the program must provide a suite of tools for the collaboration, forecasting, tracking, and 
management of flying hours, from the command level down to the 55th Wing. Specific features must include: 
• Tracking and Analysis: 
• Actual hours tracked against forecasted hours. 
• Unit hours, funding, distribution, and realignment. 
• Identification and tracking of errors until corrected within the system. 
• Trend analysis capabilities. 
• Mission Codes: Validation and maintenance of mission codes. 
• Reporting: 
• Automated monthly execution reports and data extracts. 
• The ability to produce products suitable for presentation to senior leadership. 
 
4. Fuel Management Transaction Program 
This component of the program will support the WRDCO and the entire 55th Wing fleet of aircraft at Offutt AFB, NE, 
and Davis-Monthan, AZ. The program must provide the following capabilities: 
• Digital Signatures: Allow the WRDCO to digitally CAC sign monthly memos as required by AFI 11-253. 
• Program Overview: A summary grid overview of the entire program for both aircraft accounts. 
• Data Management: 
• Centralized data imports for the validation of all fuel transactions. 
• Weekly import of EEBS data, with the FTPM performing a series of validation tests on the data. 
• Transaction data history must be maintained within the system. 
• Automated Alerts: The system must automatically generate alerts for: 
• Over-fueling. 
• Duplicate transactions. 
• Over-billing. 
• Reconciliation: The ability to reconcile the entire 55th WG fleet of aircraft.

2.  SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION FOR BRAND NAME BASED ON 
CONTRACTOR’S UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OR NATURE OF THE 
ACQUISITION 
 
This procurement of Cisco branded hardware and equipment is necessary to provide a 
critical technology modification of the DDG 1000 LBTE to allow it to maintain 
development and operation of -------- systems. The Land Based Test Environment 
(LBTE) for ------ is a recreation of the Machinery Control System (MCS) and 
Engineering Control System (ECS) network on land. For the LBTE to be able to function 
and continue development, relevant hardware in the LBTE must match what is installed 
shipboard.  
 
The -------- LBTE is required to be compliant with the shipboard Risk Management 
Framework (RMF) package in order to maintain our Authority To Operate (ATO). The 
currently approved RMF package, which is owned by Naval Surface Warfare Center 
Dahlgren Division and shared between test sites including our own, uses Cisco hardware, 
firmware, and configurations which are compliant to Security Technical Implementation 
Guide (STIG) parameters. A deviation from Cisco hardware will result in configurations 
and firmware which are no longer compliant with the ------ Shipboard RMF package and 
potentially uncompliant to STIG parameters, which will result in a loss of the ----- 
LBTE’s ATO. 
 
From a technical perspective, failure to match shipboard hardware may result in the non-
functionality of the -------- LBTE or may otherwise introduce unacceptable risk, as 
software would be developed and deployed to differing hardware. Such risks may include 
costs incurred to redevelop software, material delays to ship updates and installations, 
and, in the worst case, unexpected loss of shipboard functionality to critical systems. 
 
3.   MARKET SURVEY 
 
Market research was conducted on other switch brands, such as Juniper, HPE/Aruba, 
Extreme Networks, Ubiquiti, TP-Link, Netgear, and EnGenius. While these switches 
could reproduce much of the functionality of the Cisco switches, they are unable to run 
the dedicated Cisco firmware and configuration files tailored for our Risk Management 
Framework (RMF) package by NSWC Dahlgren Division. Additionally, during 
discussions on procuring network upgrade material, our Tier 1 integrator, Raytheon, was 
consulted about the potential compliance of other switch brands to the functionality of 
our LBTE. They indicated that the use of other switch brands was not advised and 
introduced unacceptable risk, outside of the fact that it would not be RMF compliant. 
Thus, the brand-name Cisco components are essential to the Government’s requirements. 
 

A market research for providers was performed by searching for parts that were available 
through GSA advantage and the open internet through Google. At time of original 
submission, two companies were shown to be able to provide all necessary parts for 
purchase. They are included in the table below. Pricing at the time of submission and 
price comparisons are contained in the Price_Comparison.xlsx excel file, attached to the 
package submission. Required hardware was also available through several open market

SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS

Notice Type: Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI)

Title: Wing Conference Room Audio/Visual (A/V) Modernization

Location: Will Rogers Air National Guard Base (WRANGB), Oklahoma

Potential NAICS Code(s): i.e., 541512 - Computer Systems Design Services or 334310 - Audio and Video Equipment Manufacturing

1.0 INTRODUCTION AND DISCLAIMER

This is a Sources Sought Synopsis conducted for market research purposes in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations.

The purpose of this notice is to identify potential sources and solutions to include small businesses, capable of providing a comprehensive A/V modernization solution for the Wing Conference Room (WCR) at Will Rogers Air National Guard Base for logical and physical switching between secure and unsecure systems to include respective Video Teleconferencing (VTC) systems. The Government will not reimburse any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information in response to this notice.

2.0 BACKGROUND & STATEMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO)

The Government is seeking a fully integrated, functional, and secure A/V solution that can instantly transition between Classified (RED) and Unclassified (BLACK) VTC and briefing modes.

Potential vendors must be capable of meeting the following Statement of Objectives:

I. Scope: Provide a solution that primarily utilizes existing Government Furnished Equipment (GFE), identifying and proposing any "minimum essential hardware/software upgrades" required.

II. Period and Place of Performance: Base Year plus two (2) Option Years at WRANGB, Oklahoma City, OK.

III. Performance Objectives:

Master Control & Seamless Transition: Centralized master controller allowing seamless transition between "Classified Mode" and "Unclassified Mode" without manual cable swapping for all devices to include VTC systems, all peripherals, and workstations contained in the WCR.

Secure State Transitions (Red/Black Separation): Maintain strict physical/logical separation of data streams per AFSSI 4212 and DISA STIGs. Verifiable disconnection of unclassified components during classified sessions, and vice versa.

Visual Situational Awareness: Automated, unambiguous visual indicators (e.g., signs, GUI banners) displaying the current operating mode (SECRET or UNCLASSIFIED).

System Functionality: Restore all displays, ensure 1-to-1 mapping of physical assets to the UI, and maximize equipment uptime.

Service Level Agreement: Must have ability to provide remote support within 30 minutes and on-site support within 24 hours.

IV. Operating Constraints:

Clearance: On-site personnel will require a minimum SECRET security clearance for classified network integration and Real ID to access WRANGB.

Compliance: All new hardware will be in compliance with DISA STIGs

3.0 REQUESTED INFORMATION (CAPABILITY STATEMENT)

Interested parties are requested to submit a Capability Statement demonstrating their ability to meet the objectives outlined above. Responses should be concise (no more than 5 pages) and include the following:

Required Information	Description

Company Profile- Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, Unique Entity ID (UEI), and Point of Contact (Name, Phone, Email).

Business Size/Status- Specify business size and socio-economic status under the designated NAICS code (e.g., Large, Small, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, HUBZone).

Technical Capability-	A brief narrative demonstrating the vendor's technical approach and capability to achieve the SOO, particularly regarding RED/BLACK separation, DISA STIG compliance, and master control integration.

Past Performance- Examples of up to three (3) similar projects completed within the last five years, ideally within DoD/secure environments.

Contract Vehicles- List of any applicable Government-wide Acquisition Contracts (GWACs) or GSA Schedules the company currently holds.

Feedback on SOO- Any feedback, questions, or recommendations regarding the clarity or feasibility of the stated objectives.

4.0 SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS

All responses must be submitted via email to the Contracting Office points of contact listed below:

Contracting Officer: Ryan Moehle, Maj    ryan.moehle@us.af.mil    405-686-5442

In email messages please use the subject line: "Sources Sought Response - WRANGB A/V Modernization - [Your Company Name]".

I.  Agency and Contracting Activity (RFO 6.104-1(a)(1)):
Agency: AFGSC 
Contracting Activity: 509th Contracting Squadron, 660 Tenth Street Suite 222, Whiteman AFB MO 65305 
 
II.  Nature and/or description of the action being approved (RFO 6.104-1(a)(2)): 
The action to be processed is justification for the use of other than full and open competition due to the availability of only 
one responsible source. In this particular acquisition, HSQ Tech, Inc. is the sole manufacture and proprietor of their software 
and systems. This software and system monitors and controls the Waste Water Treatment Plant, Water Plant, Electrical 
Generators, Transfer Switches, Electrical Systems, and Fire Suppression System to ensure that all of the services are running 
within the correct parameters. In order to solicit this requirement under Full and Open Competition, the entire infrastructure 
in which this system utilizes would need to be reconstructed including the upgrade of 69 remote  
field RTU/PLC panels as well as all existing monitors, laptops, network switches, routers, radio, Oracle Dell Server, UPS's, and 
modems. Doing so would cost up to an estimated $7M.
III.  Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs (RFO 6.104-1(a)(3)): 
This requirement is to provide service and maintenance for the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) System 
which is currently installed at Whiteman AFB in accordance with the Statement of Work. The SCADA system monitors and 
controls the Waste Water Treatment Plant, Water Plant, Electrical Generators, Transfer Switches, Electrical Systems, and Fire 
Suppression System. This is a service for a base year and four (4) option years. 
IV.  Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(4)): 
10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.
V.  Rationale for Use of Authority (RFO 6.104-1(a)(5)): 
This system must be serviced by HSQ Tech, Inc. due to its proprietary nature. HSQ Tech, Inc. is the only company trained to 
service and install their proprietary software and associated hardware. All of the software and a majority of the internal 
hardware for the current SCADA system is created by HSQ Tech, Inc. and can only be maintained by this contractor. HSQ 
Tech, Inc. has been selected for this service for several reasons: Whiteman AFB has a full complement of HSQ Tech, Inc. 
systems and HSQ Tech, Inc. has proprietary rights to all software and associated hardware. Purchasing services through HSQ 
Tech, Inc. will guarantee system performance, reliability, and security. Purchasing this service under Full and Open 
Competition would cause significant hardship to the Government and the internal systems that utilize the current SCADA 
system. 
VI.  Integrated Market Analysis and Efforts to Solicit Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(6), (8), and (10)): 
Our agency contacted HSQ Tech, Inc. to verify if any other entities are certified to work on the company's software. Gus 
Jimenez, Vice President and Chief Operations Officer for HSQ Tech, Inc., responded to our agency on 19 February 2026 by 
stating, "No there is not." See "Email-Proprietary System."  
  
HSQ Tech, Inc. also provided a sole source letter in August 2025 stating that HSQ Tech, Inc. as the manufacturer, is the only 
authorized company that supports the hardware and software for both MISER SCADA System and the RTUs along with MISER 
SCADA Client Software and XView for Windows." See "HSQ_Whiteman AFB Sole Source_082025". 
  

Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition
CUI
March 2026 Page 3 of 3March 2026 Page 3 of 3
A sources sought was posted on System for Award Management (SAM) on 15 August 2025 for an upgrade to the SCADA 
system, resulting in 10 responses. All responses were for a full replacement of the SCADA system or needing to team with 
HSQ Tech, Inc. HSQ Tech, Inc. only allows their trained personnel to utilize the system. No other system or company can 
integrate, modify, change or upgrade software.  
  
CO has concluded that no other vendor will be considered for this procurement. Until the Government changes the entire 
SCADA system, there is no indication that a different vendor can provide this requirement. A synopsis will be posted IAW 
RFO 5.101(c)(4)(vii).
VII.  Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost (RFO 6.104-1(a)(7)): 
The Contracting Officer is responsible for evaluating, determining, and documenting the anticipated contract cost/price is 
fair and reasonable in accordance with RFO Subpart 15.4, Contract Pricing. 
VIII.  Any Other Facts Supporting the Justification (RFO 6.104-1(a)(9)): 
Market research conducted confirmed that no other companies can provide the requested software and maintenance for 
the HSQ Tech, Inc. software and systems. 
IX.  Actions to Overcome Barriers to Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(11): 
HSQ Tech, Inc. is the only vendor that can satisfy the requirement at this time. When and if, HSQ Tech, Inc. decides to release 
proprietary rights for other vendors to maintain their systems then competition barriers will be removed.

Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
Cat6A LAN Drop/Fiber Installation, Bldg. 15177 
 
 
Organization: AFLCMC/EBR 
Address: Bldg. 15177 
Eglin AFB, FL 32542 
 
1. Purpose: 
The contractor shall Engineer, Furnish, Install and Test (EFI&T) the installation of (48) CAT6A network 
drops, and (2) 24-strand Multi-Mode (MM) cables in Bldg. 15177. 
 
2. Speciﬁc Task Objectives: 
2.1.  Cat6A Drop Installation Tasks: 
• In comm room 006, install a new 48-port modular patch panel in Rack C utilizing Rack Units 
(RU) 18/19.  
 
• Install 40-total Plenum UTP Green CAT6A data cables and jacks from comm room 006 to room 
002. Reference drawing T-101. 
 
•  In room 002, install a 48-port modular patch panel on a wall mount bracket as a consolidation 
point using Green CAT6A jacks. 
 
•  Install 8-total Plenum UTP Green CAT6A data cables and jacks from comm room 006 to room 
005. Reference drawing T-101 
 
•  In room 005, install White LD10 Panduit and White deep device boxes for the Green CAT6A 
jacks. Downward sloped 4-port face plates shall be used. 
 
• Contractor shall create a 4.5-inch wall penetration and install a 4-inch sleeve from the hallway 
into comm room 006 above the drop ceiling, and a 4.5-inch wall penetration and 4-inch sleeve 
from the hallway into room 002. Reference drawing T-101.  
 
• Contractor shall create a 2.5-inch wall penetration and install a 2-inch sleeve from the hallway 
into room 005. Reference drawing T-101.  
 
• Install approx. 65-feet of J-hooks with retaining clips as illustrated in drawing T-101. 
 

  
• Sleeves or slots shall not be left open except during cable installation and shall be properly ﬁre 
stopped. All new work area outlets shall have a j-hook placed either above the ceiling or with in 
close proximity to, and a minimum of 12-inches of slack provided on the j-hook. 
 
2.2. Fiber Optic Tasks: 
• In comm room 006, Rack A (FODP 1), install (2) 24-strand MM cables, Aqua color, 1-each 
24MM to comm room 202, and comm room 120. Provide/install LC cassettes and terminate 
the 24MM cables in existing FODP 1.  Reference drawing T-201. 
 
• In comm room 120, utilize existing pathways the Green NIPR cables use from comm room 006. 
Fiber will then be terminated on a NEW wall mounted FODP in the back corner of the room. 
FODP shall be mounted at a height of 6’ from the ﬂoor to the bottom of the mount. 
 
• In comm room 202, utilize the existing pathway that Green NIPR cabling takes from comm 
room 006. The 24-strand ﬁber will terminate into rack O, installing a NEW FODP on RU 1/2.  
 
• Perform 100% veriﬁcation acceptance test and provide a test report for multi-mode optical 
ﬁbers, (all strands) end-to-end and bi-directional attenuation tests IAW OFSTP-14, OFSTP-7, 
TIA-568-C.3 and TIA-526-7. Installer shall use Tier One Testing using an Optical Power Meter 
and Light Source for all Inside Plant (ISP) multi-mode optical ﬁbers.  
 
3.  General Requirements: 
3.1. The contractor shall follow all technical requirements, deliverables, parts and materials, 
speciﬁcations, practices, product speciﬁcations, methods and procedures, and guidance 
contained within the 96
th Communications Squadron Cyber Infrastructure Standards and 
Installation Speciﬁcations (CISIS).  This includes, but is not limited to; 
• Patch Panels: IAW CISIS 2.2.9.1 
• Work Area Outlets (WAO): IAW CISIS 2.2.9.2 
• Horizontal Cable: IAW CISIS 2.2.9.3 
• Fiber Patch Panels: IAW CISIS 2.2.10 
• Grounding/Bonding: IAW CISIS 2.2.11Infrastructure shall be grounded/bonded and labeled 
IAW TIA 607 and the CISIS.  
• Labeling: IAW CISIS 2.2.16 Work Area Outlets (WAO), Racks, Cabinets, Cabling, etc shall be 
labeled IAW TIA-606 and the CISIS. 
• Testing: Cat6A/Fiber cable shall be tested IAW the CISIS Chapter 3. 
• Test Equipment Calibration: Test Equipment and Test Reports shall document a calibrations 
date within 1 year of test date and be IAW the CISIS 3.1.4. 
• Parts and Materials: IAW CISIS Chapter 4 
• Rack Elevations: The contractor shall mount equipment (i.e. Patch Panels) IAW the locations 
speciﬁed in the CISIS Attachment D. 

  
3.2. Product Submittal: The contractor shall provide with their proposal, a complete list of the 
products the contractor will provide to satisfy this PWS, to be reviewed by the government as part 
of the technical evaluation. Provide catalog cuts, illustrations, schedules, diagrams, and/or 
brochures illustrating the manufacturer, part number, size, physical appearance, and other 
characteristics of the materials, systems, or equipment to be installed. This shall include, but not 
be limited to, conduit, duct, innerduct, couplers, handholes, cable, splices, tracers, enclosures, 
cabinets, connectors, patch panels, etc.  Material/Products submitted must be IAW the CISIS 
Chapter 4. 
3.3. The contractor shall provide all tools, installation materials, and test equipment and labor 
required to perform installation as called for by the PWS. 
3.4. Any damage caused by the contractor to existing facilities or equipment during site performance 
of the PWS will be repaired at the expense of the contractor, unless otherwise directed by the 
government. 
3.5. The contractor shall restore the site to the original condition which existed prior to the install, 
unless otherwise directed by the government. 
 
4. Deliverables:  
4.1. The contractor shall provide ISP/OSP copper/ﬁber test report(s) and As-Built drawings prior to 
scheduling a ﬁnal QC inspection IAW CISIS Chapter 3. 
• Test Results: The contractor shall provide test reports IAW the CISIS. 
• As-Built Documentation: The contractor shall provide As-Built documentation IAW the CISIS. 
Provide soft-copy drawings in .PDF format. 
 
5. Acceptance Testing and Veriﬁcation: 
• Witness Test: Following the contractor’s completion of the installation, Test Result and As-
Built review/acceptance by the government, the contractor shall demonstrate acceptable 
performance of the installed infrastructure in the presence of government representatives. The 
government will witness the testing of a government selected sample of ten percent (10%) of 
all installed Cat6A drops and/or ﬁber optic strands to verify compliance with the required 
performance speciﬁcations. In the event that any tested drop or strand fails to meet the 
required performance speciﬁcations during this witness test, the testing event shall 
immediately expand from a 10% random sample to a one hundred percent (100%) test of all 
installed drops and/or strands.  The contractor shall correct all discrepancies found during 
testing. 
• Final QC: The government will conduct a quality control (QC) inspection of the physical 
installation and provide the contractor with a list of any noted discrepancies. The contractor 
shall be responsible for correcting all identiﬁed discrepancies within ﬁve (5) duty days of 
notiﬁcation. A ﬁnal QC inspection will be conducted by the government to verify that all punch 
list items have been successfully resolved prior to ﬁnal acceptance of the work. 
 
6. Applicable Speciﬁcation and Reference Documents: 

  
6.1.   96th Communications Squadron Cyber Infrastructure Standards and Installation Speciﬁcations, 
to include Applicable Publications and Standards referenced within, dated May 2025.

STATEMENT OF WORK 
for 
Online Writing Tool 
 
 
I. INTRODUCTION 
The Indian Health Service (IHS) is responsible for providing federal health services 
to American Indians and Alaska Natives. The provision of health services to 
members of federally recognized tribes grew out of the special government-to-
government relationship between the federal government and Indian tribes. This 
relationship, established in 1787, is based on Article I, Section 8 of the 
Constitution, and has been given form and substance by numerous treaties, laws, 
Supreme Court decisions, and Executive Orders. The IHS is the principal federal 
health care provider and health advocate for Indian people, and its goal is to raise 
their health status to the highest possible level. The IHS provides a comprehensive 
health service  
 
II. SCOPE & PURPOSE 
The Indian Health Service (IHS) Division of Program Management and Budget 
wishes to purchase an online English writing assistance tool for approximately 600 
IHS employees. An online writing assistance software tool will provide 
improvements to articulate in a clear, high-quality, and efficient manner. This tool's 
features allow paragraph rewrites and proofreading to alleviate grammatical errors, 
typos, and incorrect punctuation. An integrated workflow allows us to connect all 
applications and websites on desktops and laptops to assist with narration, improve 
team communication and collaboration with custom styles, support knowledge 
sharing, and define team acronyms. Software also provides security protection for 
data and information when using the tool.  
 
III. TASK OBJECTIVE STATEMENT 
The Indian Health Service (IHS) seeks to procure an online English writing 
assistance software tool to enhance the professional writing capabilities of 
approximately 600 IHS employees. The primary objective of this software is to 
enable users to produce clear, concise, accurate, and high-quality written 
communications. Specifically, the software must include advanced functionalities 
such as paragraph rewriting to improve readability and coherence; comprehensive 
proofreading to identify and correct grammatical errors, typographical mistakes, and 
punctuation inaccuracies; and seamless integration across multiple desktop and 
laptop applications and websites utilized by IHS employees. 
 
Additionally, the software must support enhanced team collaboration and 
communication by enabling customization of writing styles, facilitating consistent 
organizational language, and allowing for knowledge sharing, including the ability to 

 
2 
 
 
define and manage team-specific acronyms and terminology. Given the sensitive 
nature of the information managed by the IHS, the software solution must provide 
robust security features designed to protect user data and maintain confidentiality 
during use. 
 
IV. REQUIREMENTS 
Requirement Description: Brand Name Specific: Grammarly: GRMLYENT-200 
Grammarly Business Enterprise. The Potential Contractor is required to be an 
authorized reseller of the proposed brand name, specifically GRMLYENT-200 
Grammarly Business Enterprise. 
 
The proposed software tool shall provide comprehensive online English language 
writing assistance, inclusive of but not limited to: 
 
• Real-time grammar checking and proofreading to identify grammatical errors, 
spelling mistakes, punctuation inaccuracies, and stylistic inconsistencies. 
 
• Functionality to rewrite paragraphs or sentences to enhance readability, clarity, 
and overall quality of written communication. 
 
• Seamless integration capability with various desktop and laptop-based 
applications (e.g., Microsoft Office Suite, web browsers, email clients) utilized 
by IHS employees. 
 
• Customized style guide functionality that enables defining, sharing, and 
enforcing writing styles, standards, and team-specific terminology, including 
acronyms unique to IHS. 
 
• Advanced collaboration features to facilitate efficient team communication and 
consistency in documentation across teams. 
 
• Robust data security and privacy protections compliant with federal standards 
to secure sensitive IHS information at rest and in transit. 
 
• The solution must be either hosted on-premises or provided as SaaS. If the 
solution is SaaS, it is essential that it complies with FedRAMP at the moderate 
level. 
  

 
3 
 
 
• Security features: 
o SCIM: Automate the provisioning process 
o Managed Mode: Ensure users sign in only from their organizations’ 
email addresses. 
o User Groups: Create separate groups within one subscription to easily 
customize features and manage users.  
o Custom Roles: Manage admin permissions based on the level of access 
needed with flexibility 
o Client Control: Control which apps (e.g., Extension, Desktop app, etc) 
can be used. 
o Confidential Mode: Prevent processing content labeled with 
“Confidential.”  
o Data Loss Prevention: Prevent the intake and transmission of sensitive 
data types.  
o Enterprise Key Management (BYOK): Exercise control over encryption 
key access, rotation, and revocation, and view access logs.  
• Cost center visibility: Gain visibility into license usage across all cost centers.  
• Style guide: create style guides to help write consistently and on brand in real-
time 
• Brand tones: use of brand voice in a tone profile that is adopted or avoid 
specific tones in corresponding 
• Knowledge Share: keep aligned internal information like acronyms, project 
names, term descriptions, and key contracts.  
• Snippets: create and insert reusable phrases, sentences or paragraphs to help 
save time. 
• Analytics dashboard: measures and drives progress with actionable insights.  
• Customer Support: Priority Support: expedited response times from the support 
team 
 
Critical Requirement: For cloud services, the Federal Risk and Authorization 
Management Program (FedRAMP) is a mandatory government-wide program for 
Federal Agency cloud deployments. The FedRAMP program provides a standardized 
approach to security assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring for cloud 
products & services.   
• If the potential contractor is not FedRAMP authorized, NIST SP 800-53 
controls may be considered, but they do not guarantee approval of the proposed 
approach. The Indian Health Service (IHS) is required to maintain a secure 
public health infrastructure, and it is crucial that all applications and services 
comply with federal cybersecurity policies and regulations.   
• Offeror shall acknowledge each bullet below. IHS reserves the right to address 
additional concerns during the review of proposals.  
• The offeror shall demonstrate the services of an “agency-hosted private 
government cloud,” a cloud computing infrastructure dedicated to the Indian 
Health Service. Within this contract, the term “private cloud computing 
infrastructure” refers to computing infrastructure that is provisioned for 
exclusive use by the Indian Health Service and does not have interconnectivity 

 
4 
 
 
to other cloud computing infrastructure.  
• Limit Sensitive Data Input – No Sensitive Data: IHS users shall not enter non-
public or sensitive data into the online writing tool.  
• Data Retrieval and Monitoring: If an IHS user inputs sensitive data by mistake, 
the offeror shall make demonstrative efforts to help IHS retrieve or expunge 
sensitive data from the systems.  
• Privacy Addendum (DPA) and Acceptable Use Policy: How the policy aligns 
with IHS Federal Privacy requirements. Note: Public privacy policies evolve; 
they cannot reduce protections for IHS data. 
• Security Controls and Audits: Offeror shall maintain robust security controls, 
including annual SOC 2 Type II audits and industry-standard practices. A SOC 
2 Type II report evaluates the vendor's controls over security, availability, 
confidentiality, and privacy. Offeror shall list any additional security controls 
IHS needs for compliance with FISMA for this proposal. Security control that 
may not be available at the time of the award but may be available during the 
duration of the contract shall be offered to IHS for consideration. The offeror 
may continue to offer additional security controls once the award has been 
made. IHS recommends that the offeror pursue FedRAMP Moderate 
authorization within 18 months of the award. 
• Data Ownership and Liability: IHS retains sole ownership of its content and 
data; the offeror bears no liability for the content itself. IHS shall remain the 
owner of all text or data entered, and the offeror may not use IHS data for any 
purpose except to provide the service (no secondary use, such as marketing or 
AI model training, unless expressly permitted in writing). No ownership rights 
are conferred to the offeror over any patient information or clinical content 
processed, and such content must be treated as IHS confidential data.  
• No Unilateral Changes to Terms: The offeror shall not change the terms and 
conditions without written authorization from a warranted contracting officer.  
Inquiries regarding the terms and conditions of the contract shall be written and 
sent electronically via email to the contracting officer representative. In the 
subject line, list the award number and the name of the inquiry.  
• Execution of a Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) 
and Business Associate Agreement (BAA) between the contractor and IHS: 
IHS is a covered entity; any vendor handling Protected Health Information 
(PHI) on IHS's behalf should sign a BAA. A BAA contractually obligates the 
vendor to safeguard PHI in accordance with HIPAA's Security Rule. 
• Prohibit PHI Input Without Authorization: IHS users are forbidden from 
inputting PHI unless explicitly allowed. IHS users shall not submit any 
individually identifiable health information into the online writing database 
unless such use is explicitly authorized in writing by IHS's Privacy Office and 
covered by HIPAA BAA. Furthermore, IHS data should not be used as a 
repository of medical records or sensitive patient details in the normal course 
of work. If there are specific use cases where IHS wants to analyze clinical text 
with the contractor, those should be reviewed on a case-by-case basis and 
covered by the BAA and a proper risk assessment. 
• Protecting PII and Privacy: IHS handles various Personally Identifiable 

 
5 
 
 
Information (PII). The contractor shall demonstrate the privacy protection for 
any PII that might be processed.  
• Data Use and Purpose Limitation: IHS data is only to provide writing 
assistance services and for no other purpose. IHS explicitly forbids the offeror 
from using IHS content for product development or marketing without consent, 
ensuring compliance with the Privacy Act and other federal privacy laws.  
• Data Minimization and Retention: Offeror shall store IHS data only transiently 
and delete IHS-specific data after a defined retention period (e.g., after the text 
analysis is returned or within X days). Any logs or stored text containing IHS 
user content must be purged regularly to reduce the risk of long-term exposure. 
If the offeror maintains some user text for audit or troubleshooting, the contract 
should define limits and require secure storage. IHS could negotiate the right to 
request deletion of its content from the offeror's systems at any time. 
• Sub-processor Transparency: The offeror shall notify IHS within five days of 
any sub-processors (third-party services) that might handle IHS data (cloud 
hosting providers) and obtain IHS approval for any new sub-processor.  
• Compliance with Privacy Standards: IHS requires the offeror to maintain 
certifications, ISO 27018, and comply with NIST privacy controls as outlined 
in NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5's Appendix J for privacy. The contractor may 
identify additional privacy standards within their organization that safeguard 
sensitive data and provide strong privacy controls that would benefit IHS data.  
• FISMA Moderate Controls and FedRamp Alignment: As a federal healthcare 
provider, IHS must comply with FISMA, meaning any system or service it 
uses should implement security controls commensurate with the sensitivity of 
the data (often Moderate impact level for PII/PHI). 
• Security Control Baseline: The offeror shall enumerate specific controls or 
families of controls that the offeror will maintain. For example, access controls 
(NIST AC family) to ensure only authorized personnel can access IHS data; 
encryption of data in transit and at rest (NIST SC controls) for any stored 
content; audit logging (AU controls) of administrative access to IHS data; 
incident response processes (IR controls) that align with IHS's requirements for 
reporting and mitigation, etc. Rather than listing all 300+ controls, IHS can 
require that the internal security program meet the general NIST SP 800-53 
Moderate baseline. The DHS clause on additional security measures for 
FISMA is a starting point – IHS should formalize it by requiring annual 
attestation that the offeror meets NIST 800-53 controls for moderate systems. 
If the offeror has a security assessment report mapping its SOC 2 or ISO 
controls to NIST controls, it should be shared with IHS. This ties the vendor's 
obligations directly to federal cybersecurity standards. 
• FedRAMP or Equivalent Assessment: Vendor shall, within 18 months, provide 
the necessary documentation (e.g., security package) to IHS to assess the 
service against FedRAMP Moderate requirements, and shall work in good faith 
toward obtaining a FedRAMP Moderate authorization." IHS requires the 
contractor to submit an annual SOC 2 Type II report and/or an ISO 27001 
certificate to verify controls, as well as the summary results of any penetration 
tests or vulnerability assessments conducted by the contractor. In the interim,

ISO 27001 certificate to verify controls, as well as the summary results of any 
penetration tests or vulnerability assessments conducted by the contractor. 
Regular security check-ins or audits can be written into the oversight plan.  
• Data Breach Notification and Incident Handling: Per OMB and FISMA 
guidelines for federal agencies, IHS must be promptly informed of breaches in 
cloud services. The contractor shall notify the contracting officer representative 
by voice call and via email within 24 hours of discovering any Security

leads to accidental or unlawful access to or loss of customer data. The
