Traffic Records Improvement 
Program Reporting System 
(TRIPRS) 
Statement of Work 
March 2026 
Version 1.0 
 
Prepared by 
The U.S. Department of Transportation 
National Highway Traffic Safety Administration 
Office of National Driver Register and Traffic Records Division 
(NDR&TR) 

Page 2 of 27  
1 INTRODUCTION 
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is an agency of the U.S. 
Department of Transportation (DOT). NHTSA’s mission is to save lives, prevent injuries and 
reduce traffic-related health care and other economic costs. The agency develops, promotes and 
implements effective educational, engineering and enforcement programs with the goal of ending 
preventable tragedies and reducing economic costs associated with vehicle use and highway travel. 
NHTSA accomplishes this in part by awarding State Traffic Safety Information System 
Improvement grants to support State efforts to improve their data systems. NHTSA’s National 
Driver Register and Traffic Records Division (NDR&TR) is tasked with helping states improve 
their traffic safety data collection, management, and analysis capabilities through evaluation, 
training, and technical assistance. The NDR&TR Division is also responsible for the  Model 
Minimum Uniform Crash Criteria  (MMUCC) and helping states align their crash systems and 
documentation to the latest edition of MMUCC. 
2 BACKGROUND 
NHTSA’s NDR&TR support for States centers on six traffic records data systems (Crash, Driver, 
Vehicle, Roadway, Citation/Adjudication, Injury Surveillance). NHTSA commissioned the 
development of the Traffic Records Improvement Program Reporting System (TRIPRS) in 2010 
to monitor and track the advances in the States’ Traffic Safety Information Systems technology 
and practices. TRIPRS allows the collection and organization of data and currently houses State 
documents and information collected in the normal operations of the State Traffic Records 
Assessment Program (STRAP); the Safety Program Assessment (SPA) module that currently 
includes assessments for pedestrian and bicycle safety, impaired driving, and occupant protection 
programs; the Data Mapping module; and the State Electronic Data Collection grant application 
and monitoring module. 
The NHTSA Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) operates and maintains a set of 
virtualized Windows servers that host various Traffic Records data systems. Currently there are 
three pairs of servers that are supporting the TRIPRS application. Each pair is a combination of a 
database/application server and a web server.  One pair is for disaster recovery, one pair is for 
development and testing, and one pair is the production system host. Each pair utilizes the latest 
version of Oracle Enterprise database 19.7.0.0.0 (19c), Oracle Application Express (21.2.0.0.0), 
Oracle ORDS (21.4.0.0.0), Oracle Business Intelligence (BI) Publisher (12.2.1.4.0), Oracle Web 
Logic (12.2.1.4.0) (Web Application Server), and Oracle Web Logic (12.2.1.4.0) (BI Publisher 
Hosting Server). 
3 OBJECTIVES 
The purpose of this project is to support develop, enhance Traffic Records Improvement Program 
Reporting System (TRIPRS) system while sustaining the software in the Production environment. 
The primary goal is to O&M Support, enhance and expand existing features, provide backend 
integration with Oracle cloud Infrastructure (OCI) services and other NHTSA systems. Note that 
this includes non- functional requirements, which include optimizing the development 
environment, cost control, optimization, performance and user experience, all of which must be 
addressed in lockstep with functional requirements. Continuous improvement is a necessity and a 
key common thread across DOT projects. Thus, the architecture and design principles utilized for 

Page 3 of 27  
TRIPRS system, as well as the software development process and associated tooling, must also 
continue to be refined, enhanced and remain extensible to facilitate seamless implementation of 
future requirements. 
Across all programs and projects, using Agile methods and sound software engineering best 
practices, DOT generally seeks to leverage automation to reduce manual efforts, increase 
efficiencies, reduce operational risks, and reduce overall costs by implementing self -service 
features, automating manual tasks and increasingly incorporating new and emerging technologies, 
such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) in addition to existing push for 
serverless and managed cloud services whenever possible. Additionally, as all S93 digital factory 
programs and projects contribute to the same DOT mission, they often operate on closely related 
data. Thus, integration and cross -referencing of information between IT solutions within DOT is 
important. 
The automation goal in particular also includes the software development lifecycle itself. Like 
many projects at DOT, It is the goal of DOT to ensure all stages of the CI/CD pipeline are 
sufficiently automated such that continuous delivery, comprised of any number of small changes, 
are deployed to the Production environment frequently without manual intervention. 
Additionally, in alignment with a key guidance from the S93 Digital factory Chief Technology 
Officer (CTO), all implementations, regardless of which project they original from, must take not 
only a cloud-first but also an enterprise-first approach so that the solutions can be deployed across 
DOT and be readily re-usable by other projects within DOT. 
Using these guiding principles – automation, self -service, enterprise-first, leveraging emerging 
technologies and continuous improvement, the goal of the TRIPRS project to provide users with a 
modern, high-quality software solution, built with highly automated modern techniques, that offers 
exceptional user experience which allows them to carry out their mission activities with ease, 
efficiency and reduced cost. Along the same guiding principles, the Contractor is encouraged to 
be innovative and make recommendations for improvements in processes, techniques, tools and 
new technologies. 
The work performed through this contract will be coordinated with the Traffic Records (TR) 
Project Manager, Contracting Officer Representative (COR) (if different), the DOT OCIO, and 
other contractor staff. Work under this contract will provide TRIPRS application and Oracle 
software support. TRIPRS user support (help desk and training) will be contracted separately from 
this solicitation. 
4 SCOPE OF WORK 
The scope of this statement of work relates Operations and Maintenance (O&M) and Optional 
Development, Modernization and Enhancement (DME) support for the Traffic Records 
Improvement Program Reporting System (TRIPRS) for the DOT’s National Driver Register and 
Traffic Records Division (NDR&TR). TRIPRS is hosted on an Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) 
Platform.

4.1.1 Operations And Maintenance of the TRIPRS Application

support, Database management, documentation, reports, authorization to operate (ATO)) to the 
current TRIPRS application. The TRIPRS application currently includes STRAP, SPA, Data

Sandbox module. All modules are accessible through TRIPRS and several have linked Tableau 
data dashboards.

activities, the TRIPRS system will have an evolving backlog containing various 
requirements and system enhancements. In accordance with the Agile approach, should the 
Government award this optional task, the Contractor shall lead efforts under the direction 
of the COR to groom and refine these Product Backlog items on a biweekly basis, or as 
directed by the COR. As part of the refinement activities, the Contractor shall capture new 
requirements, conduct discovery and elicitation, and track them using NHTSA’s Agile 
project management tools, prioritizing them as directed by the COR. As described in the 
Software Development Process section of this document, each item in the Product Backlog 
must be sufficiently detailed and complete, and the Contractor shall generally maintain a 
clean, accurate, and up -to-date Product Backlog. The Contractor shall lead collaboration 
and coordination efforts with other DOT/NHTSA teams, as appropriate, analyze relevant 
requirements, develop and document detailed requirements, and design, develop, and 
deploy capabilities that meet these requirements. The Contractor shall provide work 
products, milestones, and deliverables for new requirements in accordance with the Agile

1
 Background 
The Government desires a MOC design and implementation approach that will seamlessly 
integrate the entire SDN-B architecture with modularity for future expansion: commercial 
proliferated low Earth orbit (pLEO) providers, government/commercial transport, ground 
elements, and Space Exchange Points (SEPs). The SDN-B MOC will be the centralized hub that 
“brokers” user services, mission plans, and resources. It will deliver enterprise-wide situational 
awareness and a common operational picture of all SDN ground and space assets. 
The MOC requires a hybrid deployment, utilizing both an on-premises and cloud-based 
hardware and software to provision, orchestrate, control, and manage the network transport 
services. It will serve as the primary interface for processing user service requests and ensures 
end-to-end service performance by monitoring the health, status, and performance of all SDN 
network elements. The MOC will operate as a Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated 
(GOCO) facility, designed with a Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) to ensure future 
adaptability and integration. 
1.1 Space Data Network Backbone (SDN-B) Mission Operations Center (MOC) Scope 
The MOC will be an enterprise system responsible for the unified management of the SDN 
Backbone. The MOC scope includes the following: 
• Commercial procurement with modification development for system specific characteristics, 
• lifecycle management, 
• technology refreshes, 
• pLEO provider services management, 
• network performance monitoring, 
• orchestration of space transport network connectivity, 
• user onboarding, 
• information assurance processing, and 
• sustainment and other related tasks. 
1.2 Commercial Viability 
The Government is seeking innovative commercial solutions that may be adapted for 
Government use. This CSO is limited to commercial products or services that are considered 
innovative, defined as: 1) any new technology, process, or method, including research and 
development; or 2) any new application of an existing technology, process, or method.  
This includes, but is not limited to, the application of existing commercial cloud management 
tools for MOC service orchestration, the adaptation of commercial Artificial Intelligence 
(AI)/Machine Learning (ML) analytics for network performance monitoring, or the use of 
commercial data visualization platforms for the common operational picture.  
Proposals for a completely bespoke Government-unique MOC built from the ground up without 
a clear foundation from an existing or emerging commercial capability will be considered out of 
scope. 
 
 

2
 Problem Statement, Operational Challenges, and Desired Outcome 
Problem: Absence of a unified enterprise system for the management, service orchestration, and 
situational awareness of the multi-vendor and multi-band SDN architecture across multiple 
concurrent missions. 
This overarching problem manifests in several critical operational challenges: 
• Systems of Systems Engineering and Integration: Enterprise interoperability and 
operational effectiveness, onboarding/integrating new systems and users, and unified 
technical and architectural governance. 
• Dynamic Management of a Multi-Mission/Vendor Enterprise: Seamlessly orchestrate 
services across the diverse and growing ecosystem of Government systems and commercial 
satellite providers that make up the SDN backbone each with unique management systems. 
• Prioritization: Enforce US Space Force (USSF) mission priorities across the entire 
enterprise in real-time 
• Unified Situational Awareness: Achieve a single, end-to-end operational picture for health, 
status, and performance  
• Manual Operations: Key functions such as service provisioning, network monitoring, and 
fault management are manually intensive.  
• Increased Operator Workload and Decision Latency: The manual correlation of data from 
different systems places a high cognitive load on operators. 
The MOC is being acquired to solve this problem and operational challenges by 1. providing a 
platform for the enterprise management of the SDN Backbone, 2. increasing resilience, 3. 
reducing operator workload, and 4. ensuring data delivery to the warfighter. 
Desired Outcome: Encompasses a solution that can fulfill all requirements and objectives 
presented in the MOC Statement of Work (SOW) and Technical Requirements Document (TRD). 
3 General Information 
3.1 Approach 
Under the CSO, the Space Force may competitively award proposals received in response to a 
general solicitation, like a broad agency announcement (BAA), to acquire innovative commercial 
items, products, technologies, and services, based on a review of proposals by scientific, 
technological, or other subject-matter expert peers within the Space Force. For the SDN-B MOC 
effort, the Government will utilize either Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 
Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 16.5 for Indefinite-Delivery Contracts or 10 US Code (USC) 2371b 
Other Transaction Authority (OTA). Under this CSO, all items, products, technologies, and 
services shall be treated as commercial items and only a single contract award/agreement will be 
made; items, products, technologies and services do not have to be “commercially available” to 
be submitted in response to this solicitation. If the solution meets the requirements of the 
regulation, the solution is treated as commercial whereby the CO will utilize commercial 
procedures to develop and execute the resultant award/agreement. 

T
he Space Force intends to obtain “innovative” solutions or potential new capabilities that fulfill 
requirements, close capability gaps, or provide potential technology advancements. Solutions 
may include existing technologies or procedures that are not currently in use by units at various 
locations that would enhance or streamline their mission capabilities.  
“Innovative” is defined as: (1) Any technology, process, or method, including research and 
development, that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal; or (2) Any application that is 
new as of the date of submission of a proposal of a technology, process, or method existing as of 
such date. 
"Other Transaction for Prototype Projects” refers to this type of OTA. This type of OTA is 
authorized by 10 USC 2371b for prototype projects directly relevant to enhancing the mission 
effectiveness of military personnel and the supporting platforms, systems, components, or 
materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the DOW, or for the improvement of 
platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by the armed forces. This type of OTA is 
treated by DOW as an acquisition instrument, commonly referred to as an "other transaction" for 
a prototype project or a Section 2371b "other transaction". 
“Prototype” can generally be described as a physical or virtual model used to evaluate the 
technical or manufacturing feasibility or military utility. 
“Nontraditional Defense Contractor” means as the term is defined in section 2302(9) of title 10 
USC. With respect to applicable authority, means an entity that is not currently performing and 
has not performed, for at least the one-year period preceding the solicitation of sources by the 
Department of War (DOW) for the procurement or transaction, any contract or subcontract for 
the DOW that is subject to full coverage under the cost accounting standards prescribed pursuant 
to section 1502 of title 41 and the regulations implementing such section. This includes all small 
business concerns under the criteria and size standards in Title 13, Code of Federal Regulations 
(CFR), part 121. 
The Government will utilize a 3-step approach for the SDN-B MOC CSO.  
• Step 1 – Written Solutions Brief (white papers) (open to all that meet security requirements) 
• Step 2 – Oral Presentation / Pitch / Demos (invitation only) 
• Step 3 – Request for Commercial Solution Proposal (CSP) (invitation only) 
Submission and Governmental evaluation of written solution briefs (white papers) is required 
before invited Offerors can proceed to step 2 or 3. The written solution brief phase will be 
utilized to screen the proposed technical approach (in advance of oral presentations and full 
proposal invitations) which helps to streamline the down-select process and strike a fair balance 
between an Offeror’s bid and proposal resources and the Government’s evaluation requirements. 
Offerors submitting written solution briefs (white papers) may be invited to an oral presentation / 
pitch day and subsequently invited to submit a full technical and cost proposal of their solution 
brief submission; however, any such invitation is in no way an obligation on the part of the 
Government to award a contract. Decisions regarding the invitation to submit a full proposal will 
be based on Government evaluation as described in Section 6. The Government reserves the right 
to forgo Step 2 and go directly to Step 3. The Government may decide some Offerors require a 
Step 2 to be considered for Step 3, while other Offerors do not. An Offeror that does NOT 
submit a timely written solution brief is NOT eligible (and thus cannot be invited) to move

C. 1 STATEMENT OF WORK
The scope of work includes A-E services for engineering infrastructure, equipment, and facilities, including 
the following:
Relevant work for the purposes of this solicitation is defined as, specialized experience in engineering 
analysis and design, with major emphasis on ordinary and complex systems and infrastructure including but not 
limited to the following disciplines:
Civil - water distribution, wastewater collection, stormwater management, parking facilities and roadways 
including traffic signals, landfills, dredging for transportation channels and canals, coastal management, 
railroads, demolition, airfields, specialized ground transportation infrastructure (>500,000 pounds carrying 
capacity), security systems and force protection, geotechnical evaluations, and associated infrastructure and 
utilities.
Structural - movable structures and mechanisms; cranes, lifting mechanisms and structures, launch 
structures, towers - guyed and free-standing; large frame structures; port facility structures - wharf and docks; 
structural support components such as foundations, framing - main resisting members, roof, siding; large and 
unique foundations, ground support equipment, and bridges.
Mechanical - mechanical systems and equipment such as Heating, Ventilating, Air Conditioning (HVAC), 
fire protection, process water distribution and collection, pneumatic systems, environmental control systems 
(single pass launch vehicle purge); systems for storage and distribution of cryogens and gases (including high 
pressure gases), and clean rooms (class 100,000 to class 100 per FED-STD-209E and/or ISO 14644-1).
Electrical - low, medium, and high voltage power distribution, emergency power generation, data/control 
centers, renewable energy technologies, lighting systems, surge suppression, lightning protection, fire alarm and 
detection systems, electronic security systems (ESS), electrical control systems, heating ventilation and air 
conditioning (HVAC) controls, and centralized networking and monitoring.
Architecture - minor emphasis; firm must also include experience in multi-discipline facility design 
including architecture, life safety, and sustainable Green design.
Additional Experience - Specialized experience in multiple project phases: Planning and feasibility studies, 
coordination with the appropriate State agencies and NASA Historical Preservation Office for the demolition of 
certain facilities across NASA centers, Preliminary Engineering Reports, Final Design, Environmental 
Permitting, Construction, and Activation/ Commissioning.
The A-E services required for this contract will include, but are not limited to, the following: conducting field 
investigations and surveys, preparing engineering reports with recommended actions, preparing trade studies, 
preparation of designs, specifications, reports and other contract documents suitable for competitive bidding and 
for environmental permitting, and providing construction site inspection and engineering support during 
construction. The A-E firm will perform computer aided design and analysis, specification writing, and detailed 
construction scheduling and cost estimating. The A-E firm's approved designs will typically be utilized for the 
advertising and award of fixed price construction contracts; however, alternative procurement techniques may 
be utilized; such as design-build bridging and performance work statements.
The A-E services will be performed across all project phases including planning and feasibility studies, 
permitting, preliminary engineering reports, final design, engineering services during construction (ESDC), 
activation and commissioning. The engineer of record will have first right of refusal for ESDC task orders if 
original design went through TQN process. Development of detailed construction schedules will be required

during development of studies, preliminary reports and final designs. The A-E services also include design 
services and technical assistance during bidding of construction efforts.
The A-E services also includes engineering services during construction including review of shop drawings, 
requests for information, deviation waivers, resolution of problems, construction inspection services, generation 
of field reports, review of construction record drawings and creation of as-built construction drawings, etc. Cost 
estimating may be required across all project phases. Different types of cost estimating will include, but not be 
limited to, cost-benefit analysis, life cycle cost analysis, parametric cost estimating, detailed cost estimates
/quantity takeoffs, and subsequent estimating performance against bids received. A-E firms may also be 
required to perform studies of alternative solutions, technical requirement development and including final study 
or trade report compilation.
Additionally, the A-E services will provide engineering services as required to perform third party plans 
review of proposed facilities and infrastructure in accordance with applicable building codes and standards as 
required by RFPs NASA will issue. This will typically require plans review conducted by applicable state 
registered building code administrator, plans examiner, and fire protection engineer. This may include plans 
review by additional engineering disciplines as required in specific RFPs. This process will require providing

STATEMENT OF WORK 
SECTION C – DESCRIPTION/SPECIFICATION/WORK STATEMENT 
 
C.1 BACKGROUND 
 
Naval Surface Warfare Center Dahlgren Division Dam Neck Activity (NSWCDD DNA) is 
assigned the duties of systems and software engineering, development, testing, hardware 
engineering, site support, Life-Cycle support inclusive of Integrated Logistics Support (ILS) and 
Configuration Management (CM) activities, fielding and maintenance support, In-Service 
Engineering Agent (ISEA), Cybersecurity (Cyber), C6ISR (Command, Control, 
Communications, Computers, Cyber-Defense and Combat Systems and Intelligence, 
Surveillance and Reconnaissance), Safety, Test and Evaluation (T&E), and Readiness support 
for assigned shore based training systems.  
 
These system assignments include the hardware, software, subsystems, and elements that 
comprise the specific system. These activities are conducted in support of the United States 
(U.S.) Navy, Multi-National and Multi-Agency Naval and Department of Defense (DoD) 
sponsors.  
 
The Integrated Training Systems (ITS) division is the primary support element of program office 
shore-based training objectives within NSWCDD DNA. The ITS division serves as a leader in 
shore-based training research, engineering, development, modernization, sustainment, integration 
and interoperability of Navy, Joint and Coalition surface combat shore-based training systems.  
 
The capabilities it provides encompasses modeling and simulation (M&S), evaluation and testing 
as well as other diverse information technology approaches to include hardware and software 
elements specific to shore-based training and readiness systems. 
 
C.2 SCOPE 
 
The scope of the Task Order is to procure Contractor support services to achieve the acceptable 
levels of requirements analysis; software engineering; hardware engineering; systems 
engineering and technical support; software development and methodologies including 
development, security, and operations (DevSecOps) within an agile framework; software, 
hardware and systems integration; installation;  testing and verification support; Cybersecurity 
and cyber engineering; lab support, outfit and evaluation; ILS and CM support; Life-Cycle 
management; provisioning support; material disposition and inventory management. Such 
support shall include support of the U.S. Navy, Multi-National and Multi-Agency software 
development efforts in the ITS Division for the modernization and sustainment of shore-based 
training systems.

a. The Contractor shall provide all contract administration, contract management, personnel,

b. The Contractor shall provide recommended solutions for technical Information

knowledge, skills, and timeliness required in the SOW. The Contractor shall have the 
capability of developing new technologies and have the technical expertise to transition 
into new operating environments. 
 
 
c. The Contractor shall accomplish the work and provide the deliverables specifically 
described in the SOW. Contract objectives are based on the SOW, which is organized by 
the following disciplines: 
• Software Engineering (C.3.1)

• Training Site Installation (C.3.13) 
• Training Site Accreditation (C.3.14) 
• Training Site Operations (C.3.15) 
 
C.3.1   Software Engineering  
  
The Contractor shall provide software engineering support services to the Government in support 
of shore-based training objectives.   
  
a. The Contractor shall review and analyze current and future requirements to identify 
potential changes, modifications and impacts to existing software product lines, training 
systems and associated systems/subsystems and hardware infrastructures.  
 
b. The Contractor shall identify, assess, and report cost, schedule and technical risks 
associated with all stages of the Software Lifecycle.  
 
c. The Contractor shall conduct research into advanced analytical tools, processes, and 
technologies for future software development and integration. 
 
 
d. The Contractor shall develop software quality assurance plans and procedures to ensure 
that products and services delivered are IAW approved standards and plans. 
 
  
e. The Contractor shall develop white papers, trade studies and decision option papers while 
leveraging industry standards to provide technical recommendations, feedback, and 
coding standards that lead to development of software programs that are scalable, 
portable, and maintainable. 
 
  
f. The Contractor shall provide software code, design, and test cost estimates and schedules 
for Initial Requirement Proposals (IRPs) and Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs).  
 
g. The Contractor shall review and provide analysis of Software Requirement Specifications 
(SRS), associated requirements documentation and system level designs to ensure 
requirements are traceable and align with end user/design specifications. 
 
 
h. The Contractor shall review and provide analysis of Interface Requirement Specifications 
(IRS), Interface Design Documentation (IDD), Weapon Specifications (WS) and other 

Page 6 of 34 
interface control documentation to ensure the compliance of the software with approved 
specifications.  
 
i. The Contractor shall coordinate with stakeholders during software engineering and 
development efforts, including with international military designated contacts and other 
Agency partners. 
 
 
j. The Contractor shall develop software preliminary and detailed designs, including the 
development of Software Design Documents (SDDs) and associated design 
documentation.  
 
k. The Contractor shall develop pseudo code and Unified Modeling Language (UML) 
diagrams to support software design to include use case, class, sequence, and associated 
diagrams using Enterprise Architect (EA) or equivalent. 
 
 
l. The Contractor shall develop and maintain an Open Architecture (OA) design that 
incorporates re-configurability, portability, maintainability, technology insertion, vendor 
independence, reusability, scalability, interoperability, upgradeability, and long-term 
supportability as defined in the Navy Open Architecture (NOA) Contract Guidebook.

The Contractor shall provide software development and testing support services to the 
Government in support of shore-based training objectives.

requirements while maximizing reusability of software. Computer programs will be 
written in one of the following computer programming languages: C, C++, C#, Java, 
Ada, JavaScript, PostgresSQL, and JQuery. 
 
 
b. The Contractor shall develop software that handles input and output in a variety of data 
format.  These formats are flat files, Extensible Markup Language (XML), Experience 
API and JavaScript Object Notation (JSON). 
 
 
c. The Contractor shall develop software using tools in Integrated Development 
Environments (IDE).

Distributed Interactive Protocol (DIS), High Level Architecture (HLA) and Application 
Programming Interfaces (APIs).

I. Introduction. 
This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is for informational gathering, market research and planning 
purposes only. This is NOT  a solicitation announcement and neither constitutes a Request for 
Proposal (RFP), nor does it restrict any future acquisition strategies by the Northeastern Markets 
Contracting Division (NEM-CD). Information contained in the SSN is subject to change and 
nothing contained within is binding or obligates future actions by the Government.  No contract 
will be awarded from this announcement.  No reimbursement will be made for any cost associated 
with providing information in response to this SSN. Any information submitted by respondents is 
strictly voluntary.  Respondents will not be notified of the results of the SSN.    
 
The Government is performing Market Research to identify potential business concerns capable of 
providing the Commercial services/supplies/equipment outlined in this SSN and assist the NEM-
CD in determining the best acquisition strategy for any future requirements Not Suitable for FAR 
Part 13 – Simplified Acquisition Procedures.  Responses to this synopsis may also be used to aid 
in establishing future realistic and achievable small business participation goals. 
 
II. Background. 
 
The National Capital Region (NCR) is one of the most complex and strategically important 
Networks in the Military Health System, delivering care to over 243K enrollers, performing 12% 
of total DHA surgical volume, and overseeing nearly 11% of the DHA workforce.  It serves as 
both an operational hub and a proving ground for enterprise-wide initiatives. With multiple MTFs, 
joint environments, and a diverse beneficiary population, the NCR has demonstrated its ability to 
lead through integration of care, alignm ent of governance structures, and advancement of 
performance management practices. The Network has begun to standardize key processes, 
improve visibility into capability and capacity, and pilot innovative approaches that inform 
broader DHA policy and pract ice—positioning NCR as a learning Network with outsized 
influence on clinical readiness, access, and quality. Additionally, within a resource constrained 
environment and further anticipated reductions, NCR must identify workforce and clinical 
optimization strategies to continue delivering exceptional care with fewer resources.  
 
To continue to evolve as a leading Network and meet its strategic goals around readiness, access, 
quality, and beneficiary experience, the NCR needs dedicated contract support in three high-
impact areas: program management support, business operations support, and health service 
optimization support. These capabilities are not fully available in -house on the scale and 
specialization is required. Additionally, contract support enables uniformed and civilian providers 
to focus on their licenses and roles, whi le still benefiting from disciplined execution, robust 
analytics, and structured implementation that keep initiatives on track and aligned with NCR’s 
strategic priorities.  
 
III. Objective. 
 
The Contractor shall provide Service Optimization Support Services for DHN NCR, in support of 
Defense Health Agency (DHA), to ensure streamline operations & develop efficiencies, for long-
term cost savings and service optimization, for DoD in Healthcare Program Management, Health 
System Optimization, Strategic Business Operations. 

 
An experienced Contractor with an integrated & multidisciplinary team, with scale, infrastructure, 
and proven past performance that can provide the required subject matter experts, spanning project 
and portfolio management, data & analytics, patient safety, governance, organizational design, 
clinical operations, and performance improvements needed to sustain and accelerate current 
efforts. This includes providing experienced senior strategists, program managers, health system 
optimization experts, data scie ntists, human performance specialists, change management and 
communications professionals working as a cohesive unit, with the ability to provide surge or 
pivoted resources as Government priorities evolve.  
 
An experienced Contractor that can bring demonstrated and proven methodologies, mature 
program(s) management, quality assurance frameworks, enterprise -grade analytics, knowledge 
management tools, with reach back to commercial health system expertise, to su pport innovation 
& efficiency that can manage risk, ensure continuity, and provide the breadth and depth of 
expertise required to support NCR’s mission, allowing the Network to move from incremental 
improvements to sustained, enterprise-level transformation.  
 
IV. Relevant Information. 
 
NEM-CD has Identified the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code:  
541611 - Administrative Management and General  Management Consulting Services . 
Information on NAICS codes can be found at www.sba.gov

The contractor shall deliver Service Optimization Support Services to the DHN -NCR Network Operations 
directorate. The Contractor will spearhead strategy development and execution; architect and optimize governance 
processes; design and implement robust performance metrics and executive reporting mechanisms; and drive data-
driven analysis to inform critical strategic decisions. The scope includes leading performance improvement 
initiatives and developing forward-looking strategic plans that proactively incorporate emerging technological, 
medical, and operational advancements to secure future readiness and healthcare excellence.   The contractor will 
provide the following expert personnel:

• Program Manager 
• Project Manager 
• Statistician (Data Scientists) 
• Subject Matter Expert Public Health / Human Performance

• Architect and lead the implementation of an enterprise-wide change management framework to support all 
major transformation initiatives. 
• Lead the design and facilitation of executive succession planning programs to ensure leadership continuity.  
• Develop and implement a comprehensive leadership competency model to guide executive development 
and recruitment.

SURVEY/DESIGN ANALYSES TO REPAIR, UPGRADE, OR REPLACE 
CAS SYSTEM 
 
THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR INFORMATION ONLY. THIS IS NOT A  
REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR QUOTATION OR AN ANNOUNCEMENT OF A  
SOLICITATION. This sources sought request for information is for the purpose of conducting 
market research to provide data for planning purposes. This sources sought synopsis 
announcement does not constitute a formal solicitation and is not a request for proposal, request 
for quote, invitation for bid, does not obligate the government to award a contract, issue a 
solicitation, reimburse respondents for any proposal preparation and/or submittal costs, nor does 
its issuance in any way restrict the Government as to its ultimate acquisition approach. The 
Government will not pay for any materials provided in response to this notice and the submission 
will not be returned to the sender. 
 
The United States Air Force, 7th Contracting Squadron, located on Dyess Air Force Base, in 
Abilene Texas is seeking potential sources capable of providing all personnel, equipment, tools, 
material, supervision, and other items and services to provide a survey/study of the CAS system 
of what it will take to restore, replace, or upgrade the CAS system at Dyess AFB, reducing the 
overall manpower needed to conduct maintenance on the B-1 fleet. 
 
Please refer to the draft SOW for more detailed information. 
 
NAICS 541330 Engineering Services  
Interested firms are invited to submit a Statement of Capability (SOC) showing the company's 
ability to fulfill the requirement above. Offerors are also invited to submit an informal cost estimate 
(solely for market research purposes).  This cost estimate will be used solely to help the Government 
determine the magnitude of this requirement.  This is not a solicitation, nor will a solicitation be 
issued as a result of this announcement, and no award shall be made as a result of this 
announcement. In the event that a solicitation is developed, it will be assigned a formal 
Request for Proposal (RFP) number or Request for Quotation (RFQ), and the 
announcement may be published on SAM.gov.  It is the responsibility of the potential offerors 
to monitor these sites for additional information pertaining to this requirement. 
 
Responses to this notice will assist the government in identifying potential sources and 
determining if a sole source or set-aside of the solicitation is appropriate. Firms responding to this 
announcement should include company name, cage code, point of contact, address, phone 
number. The Government reserves the right to set-aside any subsequent acquisition based upon 
known sources and/or responses to this synopsis. Responses are requested no later than 10:00 
A.M. (Central Standard Time - CST) on 7 May 2026. 
 
Direct responses and/or questions to Taylor Norris at taylor.norris@us.af.mil.  Direct expression 
of interest as well as required documentation should be addressed in a written, electronic format via 
email to individuals identified above, any additional documentation beyond an email should be 
attached in either PDF or Microsoft Word format. All prospective offerors are responsible for 
monitoring this site for the release of all other information pertaining to the synopsis and solicitation. 
 
 

Any information submitted by respondents to this sources sought is voluntary. This sources 
sought notice is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government, nor will the 
Government reimburse any costs associated with the submission of information in response to 
this notice. Respondents will not individually be notified of the results of any government 
assessments. The Government's evaluation of the capability statements received will factor into 
whether any forthcoming solicitation will be conducted as a full and open competition or other 
than full and open. Respondents will receive notice of solicitation once it is posted.

Taylor Norris, CIV, USAF

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
 
SURVEY/DESIGN ANAYLSES TO REPAIR, UPGRADE, OR REPLACE CAS SYSTEM 
 
 
1. GENERAL 
 
The Centralized Aircraft Support System (CAS) at Dyess AFB, Texas is approximately 30 years 
old.  The components and infrastructure of this system have not been inspected or utilized 
since 2013 and their current condition is unknown, thereby making the system 100% non-
operational due to safety and environmental concerns.  As a result of the unknown condition of 
the CASS components and associated infrastructure, Aerospace Ground Equipment (AGE) has 
been the primary means of supporting flight line aircraft maintenance operations.  A 
recommendation of specific requirements, to include materials, equipment, and labor, for 
modernization or replacement of the CAS system will allow the government to make the most 
cost effective decision relative to upgrading or replacing this system at Dyess AFB.  This study 
will provide detailed requirements and justification for project scope.  The study will include a 
survey of content that includes itemized list of work required, equipment/component 
replacement cost estimate, and manufacture/vendor recommendations, with emphasis on a 
long term sustainment program and life cycle management costs.  Replacement of system 
components and/or infrastructure must meet or exceed existing performance specification 
requirements when fully operational. 
 
The CAS system has five remote substations and 21 individual CAS system pit parking spots; 
each individual parking spot contains five CAS system pit access points that house five 
conditioned air system hoses, one electrical system power line, two coolant system 
recirculation lines, two bleed air supply lines, and one fuel servicing line.  The five remote 
substations provide electricity and conditioned air to each CASS pit.  Main power is fed from a 
480V/2500A 60Hz platform via Substation 2. Recent construction has demolished and covered 
9 CAS system parking pits (Positions A 1-5 and B 2-5). Only 3 Loops remain each feeding to 4 
Pits. 
Each of the 12 designated CASS pit locations were designed to provide conditioned air at a 
minimum of 45 degrees Fahrenheit delivered up to 700 lb/min at 42.9 btu/lb at 53 in H2O to 
keep aircraft internal temperatures at 80 degrees or lower during full operation.  Each pit also 
provides three phase 230/400VAC, 400 Hz, 105/115 KVA external electrical power used to 
facilitate scheduled and unscheduled aircraft maintenance.  The coolant system delivers 
pressurized coolant oil to the aircraft liquid cooling system with a cooling capacity maximum of 
200 lb/min providing 37 btu/lb at 158 psig (110 psi minimum) and 80 GPM max (nominal 55 
GPM).  The Dielectric Coolanol Coolant (MIL-C-87252C) is used for advanced operational system 
checks. The coolant oil system is not a mandatory section of the CAS system; however, the 
Government is seeking input from commercial industry on the most cost effective solution to

repair this system; all repair inputs are welcomed. Lastly, each spot is fitted with a bleed air 
source to supplement or replace the Dash 95 air carts required for bleed air trouble shooting 
and additional cooling of the environmental system.  This system is pressured using a turbine 
engine with an output of 147 lb/min at 48 psia, the bleed air system is not a mandatory section 
of the construction/repair of the CAS system; however, the system will need to be removed. 
The fuel servicing line is maintained by the Logistics Readiness Squadron (LRS), and will not be 
addressed in this report. 
 
All recommendations shall include life cycle costs, and an estimate return on investment.  An 
asbestos report shall be included if applicable. 
 
1.1 SCOPE 
 
1.1.1 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS:  The Contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, equipment, 
and transportation required to provide a survey/study of the CAS system of what it will 
take to restore, replace, or upgrade the CAS system at Dyess AFB, reducing the overall 
manpower needed to conduct maintenance on the B-1 fleet.  The Government intends 
to utilize the resulting deliverables from this contract to develop future 
repair/revitalization courses of action.  The 400Hz power and distribution system needs 
to be upgraded.  The 28VDC power that is used for the entire CAS system control circuit 
requires upgrading.  The Polyvinyl Aircraft Coolant (POA) oil system needs to be 
environmentally isolated and deactivated.  The chillers and blowers need to be surveyed 
for expected life cycle replacement.  All pit doors and locking mechanisms need to be 
surveyed for operability.  All pit drainage systems need to be surveyed for effectiveness.  
Work shall be accomplished in accordance with the references listed in Appendix A and 
applicable publications, except as modified elsewhere in this SOW. 
 
1.1.2 400HZ AIRCRAFT POWER: The power and distribution system requires upgrading and/or 
replacement.  This system is 30 years old and replacement parts are unavailable due to 
the technology of the original design being obsolete.  The entire system is inoperable 
and is currently replaced with portable AGE to support flight line aircraft maintenance 
operations.  The Contractor shall provide a detailed analysis of existing components and 
infrastructure, as well as any recommendations for repairs, upgrades, or replacement 
with a new 400Hz power and distribution system which meets or exceeds all codes and 
aircraft requirements.  The contract deliverables for this study is a detailed listing of 
existing and replacement equipment (if recommended), cost estimate (materials & 
labor) for repairs, upgrades, and replacement, and a listing of manufactures/vendors 
that can provide service and parts after contract award, with an emphasis on a long 
term sustainment. 
 
1.1.3 28 VOLT DC (VDC) POWER: The 28VDC power system is used for the entire CAS system 
control circuit (excluding liquid fuel system) and is supplied from the 400Hz power 
distribution center.  Loss of the 400Hz Converter results in loss of the entire CAS system.

The Contractor shall provide operational diagrams and a recommendation for changes 
to the current system configuration which will allow maximum flexibility to accomplish 
separation of the 28VDC control circuit from the 400Hz power system, complete with a 
general statement of work, cost estimate, and list of manufactures/vendors which can 
provide service after contract award, with an emphasis on long term sustainment. 
 
1.1.4 LIGHTNING AND EXPLOSION PROTECTION: Analyze existing lightning protection/surge 
suppression and explosion protection capabilities for current and future system 
requirements.  Provide recommendations for surge protection/suppression and 
explosion protection, as required in an aircraft industrial environment. 
 
1.1.5 AIR COOLING: The Air Conditioning system needs to be looked at in several areas.  
Provide name and location of manufacturer and cost of all upgraded equipment that 
meets or exceeds present performance on equipment specifications, with an emphasis 
on a long term sustainment program.  Provide source and costs for upgrades on current 
electrical relays and subcomponents that are obsolete.  Provide chiller and blower 
replacement specifications, design, and costs, promoting ease of maintenance and 
operation. 
 
1.1.6 PAO COOLING (LIQUID COOLING): The Polyvinyl Aircraft Coolant (PAO) cooling oil 
system will be disabled and will require evaluation to determine if some or all existing 
external components need to be removed and/or replaced.  The government is 
requesting the system be drained and cleaned out so that the imbedded piping may 
then be used to run future conduits for electrical system upgrades. Cost of draining and 
cleaning will be added into the recommendation.  This will assist in transitioning from 
pneumatic to electrical control power of the air delivery system.  If determined not to 
be cost effective, the Contractor will provide various option, the estimated costs, and 
the life cycle cost for system upgrades that meets the same intent.  
 
1.1.7 LINE EQUIPMENT CAVITY UPGRADES: The storage pits imbedded in the parking apron 
are in need of repair, upgrade, or replacement.  The lids and locking mechanisms on all 
of the pits are broken or of poor design as they do not lock, which poses a potential 
driving/tripping hazard while working around CAS pit areas.  The drainage system of the 
individual pits are inadequate and require cleaning or upgrade to allow proper drainage 
of water/fuel away from electrical systems.  The entry/exit ladders of the pits are 
damaged and need to be repaired.  The illumination systems of the pit cavities are 
disabled and request return to service.  The contractor shall provide recommendation 
for upgrading and/or replacing the storage pits to include the estimated costs and the 
life cycle costs to maintain.  If there is other cost effectives ways that meet the intent of 
the line equipment cavity upgrades, the contractor shall make those recommendations 
and the associate life cycle costs.

FOR THE AIR FORCE RESEARCH LABORATORY

ROCKET DIVISION

AEROSPACE SYSTEMS DIRECTORATE

RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT

BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT

BAA-RQR-2019-0001 – Amendment 10

30 Apr 2026

Issuing Office: Air Force Test Center, Directorate of Contracting

Edwards AFB, CA

Distribution Statement A: Approved for public release: distribution unlimited. Public Affairs Clearance Number 19061. 

Other requests for this document shall be referred to AFRL/RQR, 5 Pollux Drive, Edwards AFB, CA 93524-7048.

BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT

BAA-RQR-2019-0001

NAICS CODE: 541715 – Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) with a small business size standard of 1,000 employees.

FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Air Force Research Laboratory, Aerospace Systems Directorate (AFRL/RQ-West).

BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TITLE: Space Propulsion Research and Innovation for Neutralizing Satellite Threats (SPRINT)

BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: This is an Open Broad Agency Announcement (BAA).

BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT NUMBER: BAA-RQR-2019-0001

Solicitation Request: Air Force Research Laboratory, Aerospace Systems Directorate (AFRL/RQ-West) is establishing this open BAA with calls to solicit innovative research proposals of interest to the Space Propulsion Research Branch (AFRL/RQRS) research as described below. The BAA will allow for submission of white papers during the open period of the BAA and will provide for specific proposal preparation times and due dates on individual calls identified during the open period of the BAA. White papers should be addressed to the White Paper Focal Point identified below. This is an unrestricted solicitation. Small businesses are encouraged to propose on all or any part of this solicitation. The NAICS Code for this acquisition is 541715, and the small business size standard is 1,000 employees.  White papers/proposals submitted shall be in accordance with this announcement or with any specific calls issued as a part of this announcement. Offerors should remain vigilant for any specific calls or updates related to this BAA.

White papers shall be submitted to the following email address:

			White Paper Focal Point*:	AFTC.SPRINT.BAA@us.af.mil 

			Please CC the CPOC listed in VII-2 in all submissions.

*DO NOT SUBMIT CLASSIFIED INFORMATION TO THE WHITE PAPER FOCAL POINT UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCE.  IV-1.1.7 lists steps to be taken prior to the submission or handling of classified or ITAR required information.

Open Period: This BAA has an open period of 20 years. For ease of reference, this BAA may be republished at yearly intervals within the open period.


Type of Contract/Instrument: The Air Force reserves the right to award the instrument best suited to the nature of research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract type under the FAR. It is anticipated that awards under this BAA will generally be cost-plus-fixed–fee (CPFF). Cost reimbursement contracts require successful offerors to have an accounting system considered adequate for tracking costs applicable to the contract. Contractors without an adequate accounting system determination will be subject to a pre-award survey of prospective contractor accounting system.


Estimated Program Cost: No Ceiling

Maximum Award Value: ≤$50M

Brief Program Summary: This BAA describes the development of in-space propulsion technologies that broadly apply to improving spacecraft resiliency. Space Propulsion Research and Innovation for Neutralizing Satellite Threats (SPRINT) is an open BAA with calls that enables study efforts on novel concepts, as well as research and development contracts to mature specific technologies to appropriate technology readiness levels (TRL) depending on end use. Specific award details are described below, but the Government anticipates awarding multiple contracts of varying duration and value. This SPRINT BAA allows consideration of white papers as well as calls issued by the Government when specific requirements are identified.

Proposals Due Date and Time: Proposals must be submitted as described below. Multiple awards are anticipated. The amount of resources made available under this BAA will depend on the quality of the proposals received and the availability of funds. White papers may be submitted anytime during the open period. Calls issued by the Government will specify a common due date when proposals specific to each call are due.

I.  PROGRAM DESCRIPTION

I-1.	Statement of Needs

The SPRINT program seeks to improve the utility of spacecraft propulsion technology for resiliency applications. This includes, but is not limited to, a broad range of technologies, different degrees of development efforts, ground and/or space experiments, studies, and modeling and simulation activities. Topic areas of specific interest include:

Chemical monopropellant thrusters, thruster system components, and/or complete propulsion systems and their expected interactions with spacecraft systems

Chemical bipropellant thrusters, thruster system components, and/or complete propulsion systems and their expected interactions with spacecraft systems

Electric propulsion thrusters, thruster system components, and/or complete propulsion systems and their expected interactions with spacecraft systems

Multi-mode thrusters, thruster system components, and/or complete propulsion systems and their expected interactions with spacecraft systems

Plume phenomenology including experimental and/or modelling and simulation (M&S) studies

Mission utility of propulsion research concepts and any associated operational constructs and/or architectures

Some areas, or specific calls, associated with the SPRINT BAA may require access to classified information up to and including Top Secret, Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI). 

I-2.	Deliverable Items 

I-2.1.	Contract Data Requirements List (CDRLs): CDRLs may include but are not limited to Status Reports, Scientific and Technical Reports, Performance and Cost Reports and Presentation Material. At minimum, a final report must be delivered. Specific CDRL requirements will be identified within a letter request for proposal (RFP), specific calls, or contracts issued under this BAA. If less than unlimited data rights is included in any deliveries, it shall be provided in a separate section.

I-2.2.	Scientific and Technical Reports, Final Report: Approval to be based on technical content, including a complete accounting of all activities performed under the technical effort with sufficient detail to allow a follow-on activity to pick up where the technical effort ended and for replication of the results, and format, including compliance with ANSI/NISO Z39.18. The Government will have 30 days to review, edit, and approve/disapprove for technical content and format. The updated final report shall be delivered 30 days after receiving the Government's review. Further guidance on the Test/Inspection Report CDRL is outlined in the associated DD Form 1423.

I-2.3.	Software: Specific software deliverable requirements will be identified within letter RFPs, specific calls, or contracts issued under this BAA.

I-2.4.	Hardware: Specific hardware deliverable requirements will be identified within letter RFPs, specific calls, or contracts issued under this BAA.

1-2.5.	Contractor-Acquired Property (CAP): Property acquired or fabricated under this contract and with contract funds shall be considered Government property IAW FAR 52.245-1 Government Property. Delivery of residual contractor-acquired property is required. Delivery is due thirty days after end of technical effort of each contract if residual hardware is developed. The proposal shall include related costs associated with packaging and shipping CAP to AFRL/RQR in accordance with specific details in individual contracts.

I-2.6.	Other: All other deliverables will be identified within letter RFPs, specific calls, or contracts issued under this BAA. Cost reimbursement type contracts awarded under the BAA will include a Not Separately Priced (NSP) CAP Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) in order to provide for disposition of CAP not anticipated at time of contract award or otherwise not specified for delivery on an existing CLIN. 

I-2.7.	Additional Data: Alternate or additional data items that would streamline or enhance the effectiveness of the effort are solicited. Proposals shall show a list of CDRL items included in the price of the proposal. Electronic submission of data items shall be required on all efforts. 

I-3.	Schedule 

Each award is anticipated to be between 3 to 60 months, however, period of performance will be tailored to each award.

I-4.	Other Information

I-4.1.	Program Security Classification/DD form 254, Operations Security (OPSEC), International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) 22 CFR 120-131, Export Administration Regulations (EAR) 15 CFR 710-774), and specific Base Support (including network access) will be considered for each award on a case-by-case basis.

I-4.2.	Conferences: Offerors should plan for participation in appropriate conferences and workshops in order to present current results. This participation will serve as a mechanism to report current progress to the community.

I-4.3.	Government Furnished Property or Information (GFP or GFI): GFP and/or GFI may be available for any individual contract. All offerors are encouraged to engage with an appropriate Government POC to identify possible ways to leverage GFP or GFI. Specific calls may have specific requirements and/or GFP or GFI available. In accordance with FAR 45.201(b), the contractor is responsible for all costs related to making the property available for use, such as payment of all transportation, installation or rehabilitation costs.

I-4.4.	Data Rights Desired:


(1) Technical Data: Unlimited Rights

(2) Non-Commercial Software (NCS): Unlimited Rights

(3) NCS Documentation: Unlimited Rights

(4) Commercial Computer Software Rights: Customary License

The Air Force Research Laboratory is engaged in the discovery, development, and integration of warfighting technologies for air, space, and cyberspace forces. As such, rights in technical data and NCS developed or delivered under this BAA are of significant concern to the Government. The Government will therefore carefully consider any restrictions on the use of technical data, NCS, and NCS documentation which could result in transition difficulty or less-than full and open competition for subsequent development of this technology.

In exchange for paying for development of the data, the Government expects technical data, NCS, and NCS documentation developed entirely at Government expense to be delivered with Unlimited Rights.

Technical data, NCS, and NCS documentation developed with mixed funding are expected to be delivered with at least Government Purpose Rights. Offers that propose delivery of technical data, NCS, or NCS documentation subject to Government Purpose Rights should fully explain how the data was developed at private expense. Specifically, offers must explain what technical data, NCS, or NCS documentation developed with costs charged to indirect cost pools and/or costs not allocated to a Government contract will be incorporated, how the incorporation will benefit the program, and address whether those portions or processes are segregable.

Offerors that propose delivery of technical data, NCS, or NCS documentation subject to Limited Rights, Restricted Rights, or Specifically Negotiated License Rights will be considered. White papers or proposals submitted in response to individual calls should fully explain what technical data, NCS, or NCS documentation developed with costs charged to indirect cost pools and/or costs not allocated to a Government contract will be incorporated and how the incorporation will benefit the program and whether those portions or processes are segregable.

Offerors responding to the letter RFP within the white paper process or to a specific call shall include the data rights assertions as required by DFARS RFO 252.227-7992, Identification and Assertion of Use, Release, or Disclosure Restrictions. Assertions must be completed with specificity. Each assertion must identify the data and each such item, component, or process listed.

Terms used in this section are defined in the clauses at 252.227-7989, Rights in Technical Data, Computer Software, and Computer Software Documentation—Other Than Commercial Products and Commercial Services, alternate I specifically for commercial software or other than commercial computer software documentation. 

Additional information/instruction regarding data rights may be identified in letter RFPs.

I-4.5.	Model Contract: A model contract may be provided to prospective offerors with letter RFPs or provided as attachments to specific calls. 

II.  AWARD INFORMATION

II-1.	Anticipated Funding

Individual awards are anticipated to be in the range of $100K to $50M per contract; however there is no pre-defined minimum or maximum. Funds are not presently available for this effort. No award will be made under this solicitation until funds are available. The Government reserves the right to cancel this solicitation at any time. The Government has no obligation to reimburse an offeror for any costs.

II-2.	Anticipated Number of Awards

The Air Force anticipates awarding multiple awards over the course of this BAA. Calls issued under this BAA may identify the number of anticipated awards specific to each call. 

II-3.	Anticipated Award Date

Awards made to submitted white papers will depend on full proposal evaluation, successful negotiations, and funds availability. Calls issued under this BAA may include an anticipated award date.

III.  ELIGIBILITY INFORMATION

III-1.	Eligible Offeror/Applicants

This is an unrestricted solicitation. Small businesses are encouraged to propose on all or any part of this solicitation. Foreign persons or foreign-owned firms are precluded from proposing.

III-2.	Military Critical Technical Data Agreement

Contractors proposing for this effort shall register and certify with the Defense Logistics Services Center (DLSC), Federal Center, Battle Creek, MI, 49017-3084 (1-800-352-3572). Contractors that are registered with the DLSC must submit a copy of the approved DD Form 2345, Military Critical Technical Data Agreement, with white paper proposals to the CPOC for verification.

Questions and Answers: Large A&E Services, FA469026RA-E

watching this project since January 9, 2025 and it is still listed as being in the Pre-

Questions and Answers: Large A&E Services, FA469026RA-E 
 
1. There is no explicit mention of having a SECTION H. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION 
within our response, but there are a few other criteria in the RFQ that need to be 
addressed, such as d. Professional capacity for timely accomplishment of the work, and e. 
Volume of work previously awarded by this office and DoD. Could you please clarify 
that a Section H is permitted as part of our response? 
a. Yes, Section H is permitted as part of the response. 
2. Is it allowable for a large firm (ISG) to hold an Ellsworth AFB Large Firm A/E ID/IQ 
when they also hold an Ellsworth AFB Small Firm A/E ID/IQ? 
a. Yes, an awardee can hold both a Small Firm A/E and a Large Firm A/E. 
3. Do you have a requirement for Hazardous Materials Investigation? We do not see it listed 
in the Opportunity description. 
a. Yes, it does refer to ancillary environmental restoration work (Asbestos, lead-
based paint, or other HAZMAT abatement). We also have used our A&E 
contracts in the past to conduct wetland delineation and wetland mitigation plans. 
4. Could you clarify your description of Environmental Engineering?  Is this what you 
might be looking for with regard to my description of Hazardous Materials as mentioned 
in the question above?  If not, we would intend to provide Civil Engineering type 
Environmental Engineering expertise for on-site sanitary waste disposal, industrial waste, 
etc. 
a. Environmental Engineer refers to ancillary environmental restoration work 
(Asbestos, lead-based paint, or other HAZMAT abatement). It also is planned to 
be used for items like wetland delineation and wetland mitigation plans. 
5. Could you clarify Telecommunications Engineering?  We otherwise envision providing 
the following expertise: 
a. Inside of buildings that currently provide Technology Design/Engineering for IT 
data cabling and telephone systems. We also provide design of systems for Door 
Access Control; Security/Surveillance; Intrusion Detection; HVAC Controls; 
Lighting Controls; Audio/Visual Systems Integration, etc. We would anticipate 
that these systems would be frequent within your potential projects. 
i. Yes, they would be frequently used in the projects we use for this contract. 
b. Outside of the buildings, we would consider telecommunications to mean 
telecommunications infrastructure. Will this type of work be within the scope of 
the Large Firm A/E ID/IQ? 
i. Yes. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

2 
6. The Opportunity description includes “Fire Protection”. In our past Small Firm A/E 
ID/IQ projects we have provided stamped/sealed fire protection system 
design/engineering through our Mechanical Engineer (PE). The design of the fire 
protection system typically includes a performance-based specification. Typically, the 
fire protection system (sub) contractor is responsible for the construction of the fire 
protection system including the final hydraulic calculations of the systems. Can we 
assume a similar approach to the Large Firm A/E ID/IQ projects, or would we be 
required to have a Fire Protection Engineer (FPE)? 
a. In most of our larger projects which this contract would be used for mainly you 
would have to have a Fire Protection Engineer (FPE), UFC 3-600-01 requirement.

27 March 2026 
 
Questions and Answers: Large A&E Services, FA469026RA-E 
 
1. Is there a set aside for this SF330 Responses are due on May 4, 2026 at 1:00 PM MT? 
This announcement says UNRESTRICTED FULL AND OPEN but a couple of sentences 
later gives small business guidance on SAM registration. 
a. This SF 330 request is posted via full-and-open competition, with no set-asides 
currently in use. 
2. Do the Architects need to be local to the base and are they full-time positions? It appears 
that this is an “as needed” and an FFP per requirement. 
a. No, the architects do not need to be local so long as they can physically 
communicate with the customer and send deliverables in a timely and proper 
fashion. 
b. This requirement is intended to be awarded as an indefinite delivery-indefinite 
quantity contract that will be exercised via firm-fixed price Task Orders/Delivery 
Orders. Any awarded vendor will be under no obligation to perform, nor will the 
Government be under obligation to request performance beyond the minimum 
stated value of the contract. 
3. Please confirm that the government intends to award 4 contracts for up to 10 years each, 
and that the total capacity of each IDIQ contract is not to exceed $5,000,000. 
a. The Government intends to award up to four contracts for up to ten years each, 
with a total capacity of each IDIQ not to exceed $5,000,000. It is possible that the 
final number of contracts awarded varies from the anticipated number of four. 
4. The announcement does not state the deadline for questions. Is there a deadline for 
(additional) questions? 
a. The deadline for questions is 27 April 2026, 1:00 PM MDT, one week before 
qualification packages are due. 
5. The announcement states “The selected firms must perform the primary Architectural and 
Engineering civil-structural disciplines…” Later the announcement says “A -E’s with 
engineering categories civil and structural will be considered.” Will the government 
please denote the resume requirements of the prime contractor in a proposal versus what 
resumes may be proposed with the prime’s teaming partners (subs)? 
a. We plan on awarding up to two firms whose primary discipline is Architectural 
and up to two firms whose primary discipline is Civil Engineering.

9. The announcement states that “Firms should have the capacity to respond to a very short 
performance timeline for projects which contain specialized discipline requirements and 
keen management/project oversight.” Will the government please define what “Very 
short performance timelines” are? 
a. This would not be our normal way of business. This would have to be an 
emergency or something that would affect the mission directly so that we would 
need to fix something or inspect something quickly to become operational. If 
something like this happened, we would be working with you as to what 
performance timeline would be doable. 
10. For evaluation of Section E and section F (professional qualifications and specialized 
experience), will the government please annotate which subjects will be evaluated more 
favorably? 
a. Both will be evaluated equally. 
11. For part a of the selection criteria and evaluation factors, does the government have a 
required number of projects to be included in section F of the SF 330? 
a. No required number as long as proof of having worked in the area or similar area 
(climate and environmental conditions). 
12. For part a of the selection criteria and evaluation factors, does the government have a 
requirement for Title II projects specifically to be evaluated or can Title I projects that 
include Title II services be used? 
a. SF 330 should clearly demonstrate their ability to perform all requirements und 
this contract. There will not be a separate evaluation for Title I and Title II but 
rather a consolidated evaluation.  
13. For past performance documentation, will the government confirm that PPQs and 
CPARS are both acceptable documentation for past performance evaluation? 
a. CPARS is sufficient past performance documentation. Currently, PPQs are not 
requested. If the contractor does not have CPARS, the contractor may submit past 
performance in a format of their choosing. 
14. Part e of the selection criteria and evaluation factors is Volume of Work. Is there a 
specific timeframe the government is measuring that volume of work? 2 years? 5 years? 
a. “Recent” is defined as a project completed within 5 years of the SF 330 due date. 
15. The announcement requires two copies of the PDF to be emailed to the POCs for 
submission of proposals. Can the government please confirm they desire two copies of 
the same digital file in the same email? 
a. This announcement is for submission of the SF 330 only. One copy should be 
submitted. This is not a request for proposal.

DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE 
 HEADQUARTERS AIR FORCE MATERIEL COMMAND 
WRIGHT-PATTERSON AIR FORCE BASE OHIO 
 
 
 
 
One AFMC…Powering the World’s Greatest Air Force 
 
MEMORANDUM FOR  INDUSTRY PARTNERS 
 
FROM:  AFMC/AFTC/PZIA (Arnold) 
              100 Kindel Drive 
              Arnold AFB, TN 37389-1332 
 
SUBJECT:  AEDC Velocity Alliance – Request for Whitepaper: Question & Answers 
 
1. Would you all have any interest in a company to run the AEDC Velocity Alliance OTA 
Consortium? 
a. The Government will manage the consortium internally. 
 
2. I didn't see that asphalt paving was included in this project. My question is will there be 
any paving included. 
a. A standalone paving project could be competed within the AEDC Velocity 
Alliance by leveraging the existing "General Construction" category. 
 
3. I am writing to clarify the partnership requirements for the RFWP. Specifically, does the 
Alliance Membership require us to identify a Non-Traditional Defense Contractor (NDC) 
or a small business as a partner? Over the last five years, our projects for the Air Force 
and DOE have involved partnerships with five universities and two national laboratories. 
a. The answer is yes, the Alliance Membership requires you to identify a partner that 
meets a specific statutory definition, and your university partners are highly likely 
to satisfy this requirement. 
 
Here is a more detailed explanation to guide your whitepaper submission: 
1. The "Why" Behind the Requirement 
As detailed in "Part 4: Innovation and Partnership Capability" of the RFWP, the 
purpose of this requirement is to satisfy the legal conditions for using this type of 
Other Transaction authority (specifically 10 U.S.C. § 4022(d)(1)(A) or (B)). This 
means th at to join the Alliance, each prospective member must demonstrate an 
established relationship with a partner that falls into one of the following categories: 
• A Non-Traditional Defense Contractor (NDC) 
• A Small Business 
• A Nonprofit Research Institution 
 
2. How Your University and National Laboratory Partners Fit 
This is where your specific experience is highly relevant. 

• University Partners (Excellent Candidates): Your extensive partnerships 
with universities are a perfect fit. Universities typically qualify 
as "nonprofit research institutions" under the statute. Your whitepaper 
should identify one of your university partners by name and CAGE code 
and, as noted in the RFWP (Note 2), be prepared to confirm their 
501(c)(3) or equivalent nonprofit status. By doing this, you would be 
demonstrating your capability to satisfy condition (A) of the requirement. 
• National Laboratories (Potential Candidates): Partnerships with National 
Laboratories are also highly valued. Depending on the specific lab and its 
managing entity, it could potentially qualify as a nonprofit research 
institution. However, the most direct and clearly defined path, based on 
the notes in the RFWP, is to leverage your strong relationships with your 
university partners. 
 
3. Your Path Forward 
For your whitepaper submission, your strongest approach is to: 
1. Select one of your university partners to feature in your "Part 4" response. 
2. Provide the university's or laboratory’s name and CAGE code and provide 
justification on how the university or laboratory meets 10 U.S.C. § 
4022(d)(1)(A) or (B) 
3. Describe your existing relationship and their unique capabilities. 
b. Crucially, link their capabilities directly to the technical project 
you described in your "Part 2" response, explaining how they 
could participate to a "significant extent" in a similar future 
project. 
 
 
 
 
                 GREGGORY C. JONES 
                 Agreements Officer, USAF

a. A standalone paving project could be competed within the AEDC Velocity Alliance by

3. Describe your existing relationship and their unique capabilities.
