Questions and Answers

Solicitation N00244-26-R-3104

Note: All changes to the original solicitation document are reflected in amendments to the solicitation and are highlighted in yellow.

Industry Question: In the solicitation document, Section C, Page 17, Paragraph 8.2.2: “Hours of Operation” states the government is only recognizing 10 out of 11 Federal Holidays. Is Juneteenth included?

Government’s Answer: Yes, Juneteenth is a recognized holiday. This was an oversight, so the solicitation has been amended to reflect this, and the correction is highlighted.

Industry Question: Section L, Page 52 of the solicitation document states: In addition to the Offeror’s Past Performance Data (OPPD), “offerors shall submit Volume II, consisting of a two to five-page past performance narrative.” However, the proposal volume structure identifies Volume II as Technical Narrative and Volume III as the Past Performance. Please confirm that the past performance narrative shall be included in Volume III (Past Performance Narrative) rather than Volume II (Technical Narrative).

Government’s Answer: Correct. The Past Performance narrative shall be included in Volume III – “Past Performance”. The solicitation has been amended to reflect this, and the correction is highlighted.

Industry Question: Section L, Page 53 of the solicitation document states: "Any exception to the terms and conditions of the solicitation shall be explicitly stated in the cost proposal (Volume III)." However, the proposal volume structure identifies Volume III as Past Performance and Volume IV as the Cost Proposal. Please confirm that exceptions, if any, should be stated in Volume IV (the Cost Proposal Narrative) rather than Volume III (Past Performance).  

Government’s Answer: Correct: Any exception to the terms and conditions of the solicitation shall be explicitly stated in the cost proposal (Volume IV). The solicitation has been amended to reflect this, and the correction is highlighted.

Industry Question: Section L, Page 54, under “Experience and Education” states that Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) “are not defined by specific minimum education or experience requirements" and describes SME-III (i.e., Senior SMEs) as "often 15+ years." Please confirm whether proposed personnel meeting all explicit qualification requirements in Section C, paragraph 11.1: “Qualifications” must have at least 15 years of experience to meet SME-III labor category requirements per the SME-III definition in Section L.

Government’s Answer: The 15 years of experience mentioned in Section L under the “SME III (Senior SME)” definition is intended to be descriptive of a typical Senior SME, not a mandatory minimum requirement. The definitive, required qualifications for the Training Instructor positions are detailed in the solicitation document under Section C, Paragraph 11.1: “Qualifications for Instructors”. To be considered compliant, proposed personnel must meet all the explicit requirements listed in that section. While extensive experience is highly valued and will be considered when evaluating proposals, a proposal will not be deemed non-compliant solely for proposing an instructor with fewer than 15 years of experience, provided they meet all the mandatory qualifications outlined in Section C, Paragraph 11.1.

Industry Question: Section L, Page 54, Table L2 of the solicitation document describes Overtime hours as a separate Labor Category than Regular hours, with an estimated 320 annual overtime hours for Commander, Naval Air Force Pacific (CNAP) and an estimated 320 annual overtime hours for Commander, Naval Air Force Atlantic (CNAL). Please confirm the Government's expectation regarding proposed Overtime rates, specifically:

Whether Offerors are expected to propose overtime rates equal to the regular labor category rates, OR whether a premium overtime rate is anticipated;

Whether overtime premium costs (if any) are subject to the ceiling provisions in FAR 52.222-2(a).

Government’s Answer: 

In the cost proposal, you should propose overtime rates that are consistent with your company's established accounting system and compensation policies for calculating overtime pay, as well as the rates established in your base SeaPort IDIQ contract. Then, your Cost Proposal Narrative shall describe the basis of this overtime rate.

Yes. If there are overtime premium costs proposed, the ceiling of this premium cost will be specified in the clause at FAR 52.222-2(a) at the time of task order award. This premium rate must be agreed upon prior to the award of the task order. Then, during contract performance, any request for overtime premiums exceeding this agreed-upon ceiling shall follow the procedures in FAR 52.222-2(b).

Industry Question: Section L, Page 56, under “Labor Escalation” requires the Offeror to describe the development of proposed labor escalation rates without specifying a Government-preferred rate or methodology. Will the Government provide Offerors with an indicative escalation rate range, comparable historical data, or other guidance to ensure consistency in the cost realism analysis across competing proposals?

Government’s Answer: No, per Page 56: “Labor Escalation” of the solicitation, offerors are required to propose their own labor escalation rates and provide a detailed description of how those rates were developed. The solicitation specifically requests that you include your company's historical labor escalation rates for the past three fiscal years to support your proposed rate.

Industry Question: Is the Government requiring the Project Manager-CNAP, whose annual estimated labor hours are 530 hours, to be on site at CNAP while fulfilling their requirements? 

Government’s Answer: No, the Project Manager is not required to be on-site at CNAP.

 Commander, Naval Air Forces (COMNAVAIRFORCES) is responsible to the Chief of Naval OperaSee 1. Introduction: tions (CNO) for explosives 
safety, in accordance with Department of the Navy Explosives Safety Policy Manual (OPNAVINST 8020.14). This responsibility is managed and 
validated through fleet ordnance operation reviews, inspections and implementation of requirements for ordnance handlers to be trained, qualified and 
certified prior to handling live ordnance in training and combat. The Navy's goal of zero explosive mishaps drives readiness, manning, training and 
the material condition of operating areas. COMNAVAIRFORCES accomplishes and verifies this effort through the Weapons Safety and Assistance 
Team (WSAT) and the Mobile Ordnance Training Team (MOTT) under the guidance/task monitoring of the Force Weapons Officer. WSAT 
members are active-duty Naval Officers and Chief Petty Officers. The MOTT is comprised of contractors supporting the Force Weapons Officer.
2. Background: The MOTT effort entails fleet readiness at the intermediate maintenance level as detailed in the Naval Ordnance Maintenance 
Management Program (NOMMP), (OPNAVINST 8000.16). Evaluation of explosives safety, technical data, procedures, life cycle criteria and 
material support evolve through intermediate level maintenance. MOTT's focus is exporting to the user, ordnance(weaponry) support keyed to 
providing initial ordnance training in support of OPNAVINST 8020.14 Series and updates for new equipment procedures and policies. This is a 
continuing task, due to personnel changes, readiness cycles and ordnance evolution and upgrades. The MOTT analyzes the intermediate level 
maintenance process for potential shortfalls in personnel certification, equipment and material, recommending solutions and providing technical 
assistance during readiness reviews.
Each member of the MOTT spends approximately 90 days on travel per year completing the tasking. Travel includes domestic and foreign 
destinations, shipboard underway periods and isolated locations.
3. Scope:  The scope of this PWS is to provide COMNAVAIRFORCES all facets of conventional ordnance intermediate level (I-level) training and 
logistics support for Navy/Marine training and combat operational units to United States Navy (USN) Aircraft Carriers (CVN), Landing Helicopter 
Assault (LHA)s, Landing Helicopter Dock (LHD)s, Amphibious Transport Dock (LPD), Naval Munitions Commands (NMC), United States Marine 
Corps (USMC) Marine Corps Air Stations (MCAS), Marine Air Wings, (MAW), Marine Aviation Logistics Squadrons (MALS), Naval Reserve 
Bases (NRB), Naval Air Facilities (NAF), and Joint Reserve Bases (JRB)s. The contractor will provide comprehensive ordnance training for 
conventional ordnance qualification and certification and provide weapons life cycle management and support. The contractor shall develop and 
maintain program control reporting systems required by Department of War (DAW) regulations.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)
Mist-netting of imperiled bats on Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland
 
1.      INTRODUCTION: Many of the land bases where U.S. Army installations reside are ecologically significant,  
providing refuge for a large number of the nation's threatened and endangered plants and animals. The benefits of 
biodiversity to the public and the environment have long been recognized and the Army's role as land managers 
can influence the floral and faunal diversity both within the installation and on nearby lands. To fulfill long-term 
mission requirements, the military must achieve environmental objectives of sustainability of training lands and full 
compliance with conservation requirements under law. The Army is committed to maintaining its role as a national 
leader in the conservation and management of sensitive natural resources on Army lands.
 
Aberdeen Proving Ground (APG), Maryland, is potentially home to bat species that are federally endangered or 
under review for listing under the Endangered Species Act, and previous surveys have documented species of 
conservation concern. A 2023 acoustic survey of APG resulted in the detection of big brown bat (Eptesicus fuscus
), eastern red bat ( ), hoary bat ( ), silver-haired bat ( ), Lasiurus borealis Lasiurus cinereus Lasionycteris noctivagans
little brown bat ( ), northern long-eared bat ( ), and tricolored bat (Myotis lucifugus Myotis septentrionalis Perimyotis 
). The evening bat ( ) and eastern small-footed bat ( ) potentially could be subflavus Nycticeius humeralis Myotis leibii
present. Periodic surveys are integral for documenting long-term trends in bat occupancy on APG. The 
government requires technical support to live-capture bats via mist-netting and track bat movements via radio 
telemetry.
 
2.      OBJECTIVE: The objective of this effort is to capture bats via mist-netting, affix radio transmitters to capture 
individuals for subsequent tracking by ERDC-CERL personnel, and track bat movements via radio telemetry.
In reference to the clauses at DFARS 252.204-7012 (DFARS CD 2026-O0025) and DFARS 252.240-7997 
(DFARS CD 2026-O0025) there is no Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) or Federal Contract Information 
(FCI) involved in performance of this contractual effort.
W9132T26QA006
Page 4 of 62

3.       MAJOR REQUIREMENTS: To accomplish the above objective, the Contractor shall complete the following 
tasks:
 
a. Task 1. Obtain approval from the Army Animal Research Compliance and Oversight Office (ARCOO). 
The Contractor shall obtain approval from the ARCOO prior to conducting field work. The ARCOO requires a 
protocol approved by an Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) prior to review. The objective 
cannot be accomplished without an approved IACUC protocol.
b. Task 2. Mist-net surveys to capture bats on APG. The Contractor shall conduct mist-netting at a minimum of 
four sites over a four-week period between 1 July and 15 August 2026. Sites will be chosen in coordination with 
ERDC-CERL and APG personnel, based on past survey results and locations of interest. Exact timing will depend 
on site access, weather, and other logistical considerations in coordination with ERDC-CERL and APG staff. At 
each survey site, the Contractor shall set a combination of single-, double-, and/or triple-high mist-nets in potential 
travel corridors and check the nets every 10 minutes for five hours, starting at dusk. The Contractor shall collect 
the following data from each captured bat, at minimum: species, sex, age, reproductive status, mass, forearm 
length, and wing score. The Contractor shall follow all weather, lighting, and other environmental conditions for 
surveys, as well as white-nose syndrome decontamination protocols, according to current USFWS guidelines. 
c. Task 3. Attach radio transmitters to captured bats. In conjunction with Task 1, the Contractor shall attach 
radio transmitters to up to 20 captured bats. The Contractor shall prioritize  spp. and , Myotis Perimyotis subflavus
but other species may be tagged if captures of priority species are insufficient. The Contractor shall include the 
cost of purchasing a total of 20 radio transmitters compatible with tracking bats to day roosts as well as long-
distance tracking using the Motus automated radio telemetry network. The Contractor shall be responsible for 
attaching the transmitters and verifying their functionality.
d. Task 4. Track bat movements via radio telemetry. The Contractor shall locate bats post-capture using radio 
telemetry to determine roost locations on APG. The Contractor shall attempt to locate each bat's diurnal roost 
daily until the radio transmitter fails, falls off, or cannot be located for at least seven days, for a maximum period of 
two weeks. Therefore, the total field work period shall last up to four weeks (mist-netting plus radio telemetry). The 
Contractor shall record coordinates and photographs of each roost found.
e. Task 5. Collect guano samples from captured bats and provide samples to ERDC-CERL. In conjunction 
with Task 1, the Contractor shall collect guano samples from captured bats opportunistically. Guano collection 
shall be limited to those bats that produce a sample in the course of capture, restraint, and handling. Bats shall be 
held only for the time necessary for tasks 2 and 3; they shall not be held for additional time solely for the purpose 
of guano collection. Not every bat is expected to produce a guano sample. Guano samples shall be stored in vials 
or bags and placed on ice in a cooler while in the field. Samples shall be transferred to a freezer in the 
Contractor's place of lodging upon return from the field. All samples and related government-furnished supplies 
shall be delivered to government personnel located on site at the end of the field work period.
W9132T26QA006
Page 5 of 62

4.     GOVERNMENT-FURNISHED SUPPORT/INFORMATION/PROPERTY: The government will provide past 
survey results to inform potential sampling locations, and coordination for access for sampling and radio tracking. The 
government will provide supplies necessary for collecting and storing guano samples in the field, such as vials, bags, 
and cooler with ice. 
5.      CONTRACTING OFFICER'S REPRESENTATIVE (COR): The ERDC CERL COR for this task order will be 
appointed in accordance with DFARS 252.201-7000, and a copy of the designation letter will be provided to the 
Contractor. Although other Government personnel may clarify technical points or supply relevant information to the   
Contractor regarding this task order, only a Contracting Officer has the authority to revise any requirements in these 
specifications, including those resulting from verbal clarification. Only a warranted Contracting Officer (either a 
Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO), or an Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO)), acting within their delegated 
limits, has the authority to issue modifications or otherwise change the terms and conditions of this contract. If an 
individual other than the Contracting Officer attempts to make changes to the terms and conditions of this contract, 
you shall not proceed with the change and shall immediately notify the Contracting Officer.
The Government and the Contractor understand and agree that the services to be delivered under this contract by the 
Contractor to the Government are non-personal services and the parties recognize and agree that no employer-
employee or master-servant relationship exists or will exist under the contract between the Government and the 
Contractor's employees.
6.      MEETINGS AND REVIEWS: The Contractor shall attend the following:
a.      A kickoff meeting, via telephone or video conference, shall be held no later than 10 working days 
after award.
b.      Meetings via telephone or video conference shall be scheduled at the government's discretion 
throughout the contract performance period, to provide progress to date and anticipated problems, 
and to ensure that the Contractor's work is compatible with ERDC-CERL work on other aspects of the 
project.
7.      TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS: The Contractor shall travel as follows:  
a.      One (1) trip to APG, MD, to conduct Tasks 2-5. Field work will be conducted during a mutually 
agreed four-week period between 1 July and 15 August 2026. Mist-netting shall be conducted during 
the first two weeks, and the Contractor shall stay on site up to two weeks after the last night of mist-
netting to complete radio tracking.
W9132T26QA006
Page 6 of 62

 
8.      REPORTS/DELIVERABLES: The Contractor shall submit the following reports/deliverables to the ERDC-CERL 
COR, or to the required reporting system specified, within the time specified:
a.   All bat guano samples collected and frozen during the two-week mist-netting period shall be placed on ice 
and provided to ERDC-CERL personnel located at APG at the end of the field work period, before contracted 
personnel depart the APG area. All guano collection supplies (unused vials, bags, and cooler) shall be 
returned to ERDC-CERL at this time.
b.   A draft report documenting the results of all work performed under this award shall be submitted to the 
COR before the end of the period of service. This report shall contain results obtained, including species 
captured, morphometrics of captured individuals, radio transmitters attached, locations (coordinates) of mist-
 nets deployed, documentation of sampling effort, locations and photographs of roosts, and copies of data
. The government will provide feedback on the report, after which the Contractor shall have 30 days to sheets
revise and resubmit the report. If the revised report sufficiently addresses the requested revisions, the 
government will accept the final report.
c.   DD Form 882: The Contractor shall submit DD Form 882(s) in accordance with Clause No. 252.227-7039, 
"Patents - Reporting of Subject Inventions" of the basic contract. If the period of service of this task order is not 
in excess of eighteen (18) months, an interim DD Form 882 is not required.

Notice of Intent to Sole Source Award 
 
THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR 
COMPETITIVE QUOTES. 
The Billings Area Indian Health Service intends to award a commercial, firm fixed price, sole source 
contract under the authority of Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 6.103-1 to DATIX (USA) Inc., 
311 S Wacker Drive, STE 4900, Chicago Illinois.   
The company shall provide policy management software services to the Blackfeet Service Unit, 
Browning, MT; Fort Belknap Service Unit, Havre, MT; Fort Peck Service Unit, Poplar, MT; Northern 
Cheyenne Service Unit, Lame Deer, MT; and Crow Service Unit, Crow Agency, MT.  
DATIX is the only vendor to be granted exemption by the Chief Information Officer to the FedRAMP 
requirement for the Billings Area. Since DATIX had been providing similar services to the service 
units in the Billings Area before the requirement was established, they have been authorized to 
provide these services without the FedRAMP requirement. The procurement will be conducted 
pursuant to the authority of (RFO) Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial 
Services; 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1), as implemented by RFO 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and 
No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements; and FAR 37.101, Non-Personal 
Services Contract. 
This is not a request for competitive proposal and no solicitation is available. Firms that believe 
they can provide the software are encouraged to identify themselves and give written notification 
within 10 days of the publication date of this notice. A determination by the Government not to 
compete this action is within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be 
considered solely for the purpose of determining to conduct a competitive procurement.

1.   Submission Requirements - "AE firms utilized by the prime AE must also submit complete Architect-
Engineer Qualifications and resumes. Submit one hardcopy of each form plus one CD electronic copy. 
Facsimile and electronic submission of SF330 will not be accepted. SF330 and electronic copy will not be 
returned."  
 
 Typically our subconsultants cover areas outside of our area of expertise (i.e., geotechnical, 
structural, mechanical, electrical, architectural, and survey). We would like to confirm that we 
should only submit resumes for our subconsultants under our SF330 Part 1 Section E resumes. In 
addition, we are required to submit a SF330 Part II for all of our team members. 
 
 Our subconsultant team members are not required to submit a complete SF330 Part 1 package 
individually.

sub-contractor key personnel shall be submitted under SF330, Part I, Section E. Further, only AE firms 
(Prime) desiring to be considered for this acquisition shall submit a completed SF330 package. However, 
SF330 Part II shall be completed for each firm. 
 
2.  Criterion 1 of the solicitation states: "A limit of 24 resumes will be considered to demonstrate 
professional qualifications in each of the areas". Our interpretation of this statement is that our SF330 Part 
1 Section E will be limited to 24 resumes total. The 24 resumes will need to demonstrate proficiency and 
qualification for all the listed key personnel categories. Is this interpretation correct? An alternative way 
to look at this statement is that up to 24 resumes could be submitted in each of the key personnel 
categories. 
 
RESPONSE:  Confirmed, 24 resumes must collectively demonstrate professional qualifications in all of 
the areas. This statement has been revised to state "A limit of 24 resumes will be considered to 
collectively demonstrate all of the professional qualifications."

Performance Work Statement 
Naval Information Warfighting Development Center (NIWDC) 
Information Warfare Subject Matter Expert (SME) Fleet Advanced Tactics Training 
Support 
 
 
1. SCOPE OF WORK: Doctrine, tactics, techniques and procedures (TTP), and Advanced 
Tactics Training.  The Contractor shall provide support for development of doctrine, tactics 
techniques, and procedures and advanced tactics training in the Navy Information Warfare (IW) 
mission areas of Information Operations (IO) and related information related capabilities (IRCs), 
Electronic Warfare (EW), Cryptology, Command & Control (C2) systems, Cyber Operations 
(CO) specifically focused on Defensive Cyber Operations (DCO) and Department of Defense 
Information Network (DODIN) operations, Meteorology & Oceanography (METOC), Space 
Operations, and Intelligence (INTEL). 
 
2. PERIOD AND PLACE OF PERFORMANCE:   
• Base Year - September 28, 2026 to September 27, 2027 
• Option Year 1 - September 28, 2027 to September 27, 2028 
• Option Year 2 - September 28, 2028 to September 27, 2029 
• Option Year 3 - September 28, 2029 to September 27, 2030 
• Option Year 4 - September 28, 2030 to September 27, 2031 
• FAR 52-217-8 - September 28, 2031 to March 27, 2032 
 
All of the following are places where the Contractor may execute functions and tasks for this 
contract in support of NIWDC -   
• Location 1 – NIWDC Headquarters, Joint Reserve Intelligence Center, 7941 Blandy 
Road, BLDG NH-139, Norfolk, VA 23511, or 
• Location 2 - NIWDC component, Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek / Fort Story, 
2555 Amphibious Drive, BLDG 1126, Virginia Beach, VA 23459-3225, or  
• Location 3 – NIWDC Component, Naval Information Forces (NAVIFOR), 115 Lake 
View Pkwy, BLDG 115, Suffolk, VA 23435, or 
• Location 4 - Future site for NIWDC, located in the Hampton Roads area, or   
• Location 5 - Contractor Facilities (unclassified material only) and other 
Government/Contractor sites per temporary duty (TDY)/Travel Requirements.  Travel 
Authorization requests shall be submitted to and/or authorized by the Contracting 
Officer’s Representative (COR). 
• Location 6 - Alternate Location as necessary and determined by NIWDC/Contractor.  
 
3. SECURITY REQUIREMENTS:   
 

 
2 
 
SECURITY: The Contractor shall be responsible for adhering to all Department of Defense 
(DOD), Department of the Navy (DON), and specific Command instructions, guidance, orders, 
directives, and supplements relative to performing tasks set forth in this PWS.  The Contractor 
shall not disclose and must safeguard procurement sensitive information, computer systems and 
data, Privacy Act data, and Government personnel work products that are obtained or generated 
in the performance of this contract. This includes dissemination of protocols and papers not 
generally available through the public literature.  Neither the Contractor nor any of its contract 
service providers shall disclose or cause to disseminate any information concerning operations of 
military activities. Such action(s) could result in violation of the contract and possible legal 
actions.  
 
3.1 The Contractor SHALL NOT:  
3.1.1 Brand (or make any references to award) on their corporate (private or public facing) web 
site(s), any information that references any of the following information: 
• Award of Contract/Task Orders 
• Location(s) of performance 
• Duration of performance 
• Type(s) of work performed 
• Government customer name(s) 
• Contract, or Task Order, Contractor personnel end strength(s) 
3.2 Contractor awarded this effort shall deliver onboarding Contractor information to the COR 
NLT two business days before reporting to place of performance.  The Contractor information 
shall be sent via Signed and Encrypted email, and shall contain the following information on 
each incoming Contractor: 
• Company Name 
• Full Name 
• Date of Birth 
• Position assigned 
• Social Security Number or DOD Identification Number 
• Level of Clearance 
• Email Address 
• Phone Number 
 
3.3 Access will be granted to Government facilities as required in support of the tasking. 
Contractor personnel performing work under this contract shall meet all requirements for gaining 
access to US Government installations. The Contractor shall conform to all DOD, DON, and 
local (base/installation) security instructions (refer to Contractor Unclassified Access to 
Federally Controlled Facilities, Sensitive Information, Information Technology (IT) Systems or 
Protected Health Information (July 2013). 
 

 
3 
 
4. The scope of work requires access to classified information and systems up through TOP 
SECRET/SENSITIVE COMPARTMENTED INFORMATION (TS/SCI).  Contractor 
personnel shall have the appropriate security clearance as of the first day of their support of this 
PWS.  The following shall be considered before assigning any/all proposed Contractor staff as a 
part of any Task Order: 
   
4.1 Personnel who possess TS/SCI clearance SHALL currently be fully adjudicated, and eligible 
for transfer in status, upon report on first day of their support of this PWS.  Interim TS//SCI 
clearances shall not be accepted for any position. 
4.2 The Contractor’s Program Manager(s), and/or Facility Security Officer’s SHALL initiate 
contact to work with the COR, to develop DD-254 forms, NLT two business days before 
Contractor personnel arrive on-site to start work. 
4.3 The Contractor’s Program Manager(s), and/or Facility Security Officer’s SHALL ensure that 
all incoming Contractor personnel have had their Common Access Cards (CACs) from their last 
job revoked, NLT two business days before directing them to contact NAVIFOR Trusted Agents 
for issuance of new CAC credentials. 
4.4 All work is to be performed in accordance with DOD and Navy Operations Security 
(OPSEC) requirements and in accordance with the OPSEC attachment to the DD254.  
 
4.5 All building security identification badges shall be turned into the SSO that issued the 
credential, and all CACs shall be turned into the COR that issued the credential during normal 
working hours. In the event that the Contractor employee checks out at the end of an evening, or 
mid shift, then both the building security badge, and the CAC credential, shall be turned over to 
the Contractor’s Government lead before final departure, as the Contractor shall be required to 
“read out/be debriefed” regarding their clearance, by the servicing SSO, before their final 
departure. If the contractor does not “read out/be debrief before final departure the same day the 
contractor SHALL physically come in during normal working hours on the next SSO work day 
which is Monday through Friday 0730-1600 (7:30 to 4:00). 
 
4.6 The Contractor shall comply with all applicable federal, state and local laws and ensure 
performance is secure while protecting material, equipment, and supplies from damage and loss. 
Government security personnel will have the express right to inspect work spaces, email 
accounts, and operating systems, for security violations at any time during the term of the 
contract.  
 
4.7 The Contractor shall be responsible for safeguarding all government equipment, information 
and property provided for Contractor use. At the close of each work period, Government 
facilities, equipment and materials shall be secured. 
 
4.8 The Government CAC serves as the primary method of identification for the Contractor 
employees, as well as providing the basis of Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) access to the 
Navy/Marine Corps Intranet (NMCI), OCONUS (outside continental United States) Navy 
Enterprise Network (ONE-NET), Consolidated Afloat Networks and Enterprise Services. 
(CANES), and numerous Navy web sites, which may also require PKI access.  The COR will 
assist in providing the Contractor the appropriate documentation for obtaining CACs. The 

 
4 
 
Contractor shall be responsible for obtaining any Government issued identification cards from 
former employees or employees whose access has been terminated off of the Government site 
and to turn those items over to the COR upon termination of employment or access. 
 
4.9 Contract personnel shall wear a badge that clearly identifies them as a Contractor employee. 
The badge will be issued by the COR, via the Special Security Office (SSO), and will contain a 
personal picture, name of employee, and Contractor’s name. While working on the Government 
site, Contractor employee badges shall be worn on the outer garment, above the waist, in full 
view at all times, attached to the outer shirt or jacket pocket by a button or clip or worn around 
the neck secured by an appropriate identification card lanyard.  
 
4.10 Contractor personal shall not, at any time, access or attempt to access the following from 
Government IT assets except when directly supporting this PWS: 
• Corporate Email Accounts 
• Personal Email Accounts 
• Corporate Portals 
• Any Social Networking Site 
• Any Web Based News Site 
• Any Music Streaming Media Site 
• Any Web Based site, that does not directly relate to the assigned job, task, or mission 
 
5. PRIVACY ACT COMPLIANCE:  The Contractor may be in contact with data and 
information subject to the Privacy Act of 1974 (Title 5 of the U.S. Code Section 552a).  The 
Contractor shall ensure that its employees assigned to this effort understand and adhere to the 
requirements of the Privacy Act and to Department of Defense and Department of the Navy 
regulations that implement the Privacy Act.  Department of Navy policy and procedures 
implementing the Privacy Act are detailed in SECNAVINST 5211.5E (Department of the Navy 
Privacy Act (PA) Program).  The Contractor shall identify and safeguard data, information and 
reports accordingly.  In addition, the Contractor shall ensure that Contractor employees assigned 
to the contract are trained on properly identifying and handling data and information subject to 
the Privacy Act prior to commencing work. 
 
6. GOVERNMENT FURNISHED INFORMATION (GFI): GFI will be provided to 
Contractor employees as needed to complete the tasks set forth in this Performance Work 
Statement (PWS). Access to classified information must be granted in accordance with the terms 
and conditions contained in DOD Manual 5220.22-M and DD Form 254 (Contract Security 
Classification Specification). The Contractor shall comply with all current information assurance 
awareness, information security policies, procedures, and statutes applicable to DOD information 
technology; including the July 3, 2007 DOD CIO Policy Memorandum on Encryption of 
Sensitive Unclassified Data at Rest on Mobile Computing Devices and Removable Storage. 
 
7. GENERAL/ADMINISTRATIVE MATTERS: Contractor shall only conduct business with 
designated Government personnel listed as points of contact (POCs). Names of authorized 
personnel shall be provided to the Contractor by the Government COR, in writing and updated as 
necessary throughout the contract period.  

 
5 
 
 
All inquiries, comments or complaints arising from any matter observed, experienced, or learned 
of as a result of or in connection with the performance of this contract, the resolution of which 
may require the dissemination of official information, shall be directed to the COR and the 
Contracting Officer (KO).  
 
7.1 DATA RIGHTS:  It is the Government’s intent to retain unlimited rights to all software, 
documentation, and data first produced in performance of the task. 
 
7.1.1 U.S. Government records, copies of original results and reports, verified original data, 
corrected data, and corrected supporting final reports are maintained by the Contractor, but 
remain the property of the U.S. Government. These files/results must be surrendered to the COR 
immediately upon demand.  
 
7.2 CONTRACTOR QUALITY ASSURANCE: The Contractor shall develop and maintain a 
Quality Assurance Plan (QA Plan) in order to ensure only qualified personnel, as stipulated in 
paragraph 9.1.2, are assigned to fulfill the requirements stated in this PWS.  The Contractor shall 
detail in its quality assurance plan how it intends to maintain personnel qualifications and ensure 
contract employees have up-to-date training and knowledge in their respective areas of endeavor.   
 
7.2.1 This QA Plan shall detail the methodology to be used by the Contractor to monitor and 
grade the performance of its personnel as they carry out the requirements of this PWS.  The QA 
Plan shall address the Contractor’s courses of action to address under-performing employees.  
 
7.3 GOVERNMENT QUALITY ASSURANCE SURVEILLANCE: The Government shall 
evaluate the Contractor’s performance under this contract in accordance with the Quality 
Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP). This plan is primarily focused on what the Government 
must do in order to ensure that the Contractor is performing in accordance with the performance 
standards.  It defines how the performance standards will be applied, the frequency of 
surveillance, and the minimum acceptable defect rate(s).  
 
7.4 COMPLAINTS LOGGED AGAINST CONTRACTOR PERSONNEL: In the event that 
a complaint is made regarding the conduct or ability of Contractor personnel, the individual 
receiving the complaint will contact the COR and the COR will notify the Contractor’s Project 
Manager (PM). The Contractor’s PM and COR will cooperate in investigating complaints made 
against Contractor employees.  If the results of the investigation prove the complaint(s) to be 
valid, the Contractor’s PM shall have a maximum of three (3) working days to propose a 
corrective plan for resolving the matter and preventing future similar occurrences.  This plan 
shall be submitted in writing to the COR.  In the event that the Government deems the corrective 
plan insufficient for resolution of the problem, a written response to the Contractor’s PM will be 
provided within three (3) working days.  
  
7.5 OFFICE SPACE: The Government will provide office space, desk, chair, and common 
office supplies.  In addition to office space, each Contractor employee shall be provided with 
access to government computers and telephones, but not cellular phones, for official use only.  
Under no circumstances will Contractor-provided personal computers, or any personal electronic 

 
6 
 
devices (e.g., cell phones, tablets, Fitbits), be connected to any Government IT system, including 
but not limited to the Navy/Marine Corps Intranet (NMCI).  Contractor personnel shall comply 
with all DOD and Navy IT regulations, policies and procedures including those concerning 
internet usage and cybersecurity. 
 
7.6 STATEMENT OF NON -PERSONAL SERVICE : Contractor employees performing

personnel of the Contractor.  Contractor management shall ensure that employees properly comply

UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION (USDOT) 
NATIONAL HIGHWAY TRAFFIC SAFETY ADMINISTRATION (NHTSA) 
  
Synopsis for Solicitation 693JJ926R000020 
 
Experimental and Mathematical Biomechanics Injury Research (EMBIR) 
 
Synopsis 
This synopsis is issued in accordance with FAR 5.203(a) to provide a minimum 30-day public 
notice prior to issuance of a solicitation. 
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) intends to issue a solicitation for 
a Full and Open Competition in support of the Office of Vehicle Safety Research (NSR-200). 
 
Introduction and Background 
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s (NHTSA) mission is to save lives, 
prevent injuries, and reduce traffic-related health care and economic costs. The agency develops, 
promotes, and implements effective educational, engineering, and enforcement programs aimed 
at reducing vehicle crash-related fatalities and injuries. 
The Office of Vehicle Safety Research conducts research, development, testing, crash 
investigation, and data collection and analysis activities to support the Agency’s safety m
ission and regulatory decision-making. 
 
Contract Type and NAICS 
NHTSA intends to award multiple Indefinite-Delivery Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts. 
Task orders issued under the IDIQ may utilize a variety of contract types, including: 
 Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) 
 Cost-No-Fee (as appropriate) 
 Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) 
 Hybrid contract types, as applicable 
 
The applicable NAICS code is: 
541715 – Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences 
 
 
 
 

2 
 
 
 
 
 
Period of Performance 
The resulting multiple-award IDIQ contracts will include a total period of performance not to 
exceed 60 months from date of award, consisting of: 
 One (1) two-year base period 
 Three (3) one-year option periods 
 One (1) six-month option to extend services 
 
The anticipated effective date of the IDIQ contracts is October 1, 2026. 
 
Solicitation Release 
The solicitation is anticipated to be released on or about May 2026. 
 
Objective / Scope of Work 
The purpose of this effort is to advance the understanding of human injury biomechanics and 
improve vehicle safety through experimental, computational, and analytical research. 
Work under this contract will support: 
 Human injury biomechanics and tolerance research 
 Development and evaluation of anthropomorphic test devices (ATDs) 
 Computational modeling of human and surrogate response 
 Analysis of crash data and injury causation trends 
 Development of injury criteria and performance metrics 
 
Specific tasks may include: 
 Conducting experimental biomechanics testing 
 Supporting ATD design and evaluation 
 Performing computational simulations and modeling 
 Analyzing field and experimental data 
 Supporting development of injury risk functions 
 
Offerors may propose supporting one or more research areas identified in the solicitation and 
shall clearly identify their areas of expertise in their technical proposals. 
 
 
 

3 
 
 
 
System for Award Management (SAM) 
Offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at www.SAM.gov to 
be eligible for award. 
 
Notice 
THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. This synopsis is for informational 
purposes only and does not constitute a commitment by the Government. 
The solicitation will be posted electronically via http://www.sam.gov. No requests for advance 
copies will be honored. 
Interested parties are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for updates, amendments, and 
additional information. 
 
Anticipated Award Timing 
The Government anticipates making award(s) in advance of the October 1, 2026 effective date 
to ensure continuity of research support.

DARPA-SN-26-70 ExPEDitions Proposers Day                                                                                
Special Notice (SN) DARPA-SN-26-70
Expeditionary Power- and Energy-Dense Implementations (ExPEDitions) 
Proposers Day
May 14, 2026
The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Defense Sciences Office (DSO) 
is sponsoring a Proposers Day to provide information to potential proposers on the objectives 
of an anticipated Program Solicitation (PS) for the Expeditionary Power- and Energy-Dense 
Implementations (ExPEDitions) program. The Proposers Day will be held on May 14, 2026, 
from 12:00 p.m. (noon) to 4:00 p.m. (Eastern Time) in Arlington, VA. The event will be 
webcast for those who would like to participate remotely. Advance registration is required for 
attending the Proposers Day in person and viewing the webcast. Note that all times listed in 
this announcement and on the registration website are Eastern Time.
The goals of the ExPEDitions Proposers Day are to: (1) introduce the research community 
(industry, academia, and Government) to the ExPEDitions program vision and goals; (2) 
explain the mechanics of a DARPA program and the milestones of this particular effort; and 
(3) encourage and promote teaming arrangements among potential organizations that have the 
relevant expertise, facilities, and capabilities for executing a research and development 
program responsive to the ExPEDitions program goals.  
DARPA anticipates releasing the ExPEDitions PS in May 2026. If released, the PS will be 
available on https://sam.gov/ Following Proposers Day, DARPA may post the presented 
materials on the DARPA website.  
To maximize the pool of innovative proposal concepts, DARPA strongly encourages 
participation by non‐traditional proposers (including small businesses, academic and research 
institutions, and first‐time Government contractors) in events such as this and any subsequent 
solicitation. 
PROGRAM OBJECTIVE AND DESCRIPTION
DARPA DSO is pursuing foundational technology for electrically rechargeable batteries with 
high energy and power density. While current state-of-the-art batteries enable efficient and 
quiet operations, their low energy density makes them too large and heavy for long-range 
missions or weight-sensitive applications like electric aviation, necessitating the continued use 
of fuel for these missions, which complicates logistics. 
Recent breakthroughs in electrocatalysis, battery design, and materials science may overcome 
long-standing technical hurdles with sluggish reaction kinetics and mass transport 
limitations.1,2,3,4 This new approach will extend the operational range and endurance of 
missions and free portable energy from the constraint of fuel logistics. ExPEDitions 
performers will drive this initiative by designing advanced battery prototypes and integrating 
them into demonstrator devices to prove the technology’s ability to extend mission endurance.   
TEAMING
1 Kondori et al. Science, 2023, 379, 499-505.
2 Zhou et al. Nat. Commun., 2022, 13, 6414.
3 Wang et al. Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. 2025, 122, e2413609122.
4 Anson & Stahl Chem. Rev., 2020, 120, 3749–3786.

DARPA-SN-26-70 ExPEDitions Proposers Day                                                                                
DARPA highly encourages teaming before proposal submission and will facilitate the 
formation of teams with the necessary expertise. Potential proposers may choose to participate 
in either, none, or both of the following options:
1. Attendee List (limited distribution): Participant contact information (name, 
organization, email address) will be distributed to all other ExPEDitions Proposers Day 
attendees. The registration website will ask registrants to indicate whether they 
approve distribution of their contact information.
2. Proposer Profile List (limited distribution): Interested parties will submit a one-page 
profile consisting of their contact information (name, organization, email, telephone 
number, mailing address, and, if applicable, organization website), a brief description 
of their technical competencies, and, if applicable, their desired expertise from other 
teams/organizations. All profiles must be emailed to ExPEDitions@darpa.mil no later 
than 12:00 p.m. (noon) on May 18, 2026. Following the deadline, the consolidated 
teaming profiles will be sent via email to the proposers who submitted a valid profile. 
Specific content, communications, networking, and team formation are the sole 
responsibility of the participants. Neither DARPA nor the Department of War (DoW) 
endorses the information and organizations contained in the consolidated teaming 
profile document, nor does DARPA or DoW exercise any responsibility for improper 
dissemination of the teaming profiles.  
LIGHTNING TALKS
Attendees may be afforded the opportunity to give a Lightning Talk (a brief, 5-minute oral 
presentation) during the webcast outlining their interests and capabilities. The purpose of 
these presentations is to facilitate teaming discussions among the attendees. Upon 
registering, attendees may indicate if they would like to give a Lightning Talk. Due to 
limited availability, DARPA will accept submissions on a first-come, first-served basis and 
does not guarantee that an attendee’s requests to brief will be fulfilled. Submitted briefing 
materials should use the template provided via the registration website and are limited to a 
single, PDF-format slide, which should be appropriate for public release, as they will be 
shared with the session via webcast. The slide must be submitted to ExPEDitions@darpa.mil 
by 12:00 p.m. (noon) on May 12, 2026. DARPA will contact submitters upon receipt of their 
slide with additional guidance for the webcast.
REGISTRATION INFORMATION
The ExPEDitions Proposers Day will be held on May 14, 2026, from 12:00 p.m. (noon) to 
4:00 p.m. in Arlington, VA. There is no registration fee for the Proposers Day meeting or 
webcast.  
Registration opens: As of publication of this announcement. 
Registration website: https://events.sa-meetings.com/ExPEDitionsProposersDay
Registration closes (in person attendance): May 4, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. or when capacity is 
reached, whichever comes first.
Registration closes (webcast): May 4, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. or when capacity is reached, 
whichever comes first.
Advance registration via the above website is required for attending the Proposers Day in 
person and for receiving access to the webcast. The advance registration requirement applies 

DARPA-SN-26-70 ExPEDitions Proposers Day                                                                                
to every individual intending to view the webcast alone or as part of a group. 
Due to the limitations of the conference facility space, in-person attendance is restricted to the 
first 100 registrants with a maximum of five (5) individuals from any one organization and no 
more than two (2) representatives per division/department of that organization. Interested 
parties are encouraged to coordinate attendance internally within their organizations prior to 
registration. 
Registrants in excess of the maximum capacity limitations (100 individuals for in-person 
attendance and 350 individuals for the webcast) may be added to a waitlist. Individuals who 
are unable to register for in-person attendance because capacity has been reached may have 
the option of choosing to be added to the waitlist OR registering for attendance via 
webcast. If slots become available due to cancellations, the slots may be filled on a first-
come, first-served basis from the waitlist.  
ELIGIBILITY
DARPA hosts Proposers Days to: (1) promote teaming arrangements between researchers, (2) 
provide potential proposers with information on whether and how they might respond to the 
Government’s research and development solicitations, and (3) increase efficiency in proposal 
preparation and evaluation. Therefore, Proposers Days are only open to registered potential 
proposers, i.e., the events are closed to the general public and media. For this particular 
program, Proposers Day registration is open to potential proposers who are U.S. citizens, U.S. 
permanent residents, and foreign nationals.  
All registrants who are not U.S. citizens must complete and submit either a DARPA Form 60 
(U.S. Permanent Resident and Foreign National Visit Request – e.g., industry or academia) or 
an Official Visit Request (foreign government personnel, only) through their country’s 
embassy based in Washington, DC, no later than 5:00 p.m. on May 4, 2026. Form 60 
submission instructions are provided on the registration website and in the registration 
confirmation email. Registrants who have submitted a Form 60 that was approved within the 
last six months do not need to re-submit. The Form 60 will remain valid for six months. 
Contact your Embassy staff for assistance in submitting the Official Visit Request. Upon entry 
to the physical meeting, all attendees must present valid, Government-issued photo 
identification.
Q & A
Administrative, technical, and contractual questions about ExPEDitions should be emailed to 
ExPEDitions@darpa.mil. All questions must be in English and must include the name and 
email address of a point of contact. Following Proposers Day, DARPA may post an FAQ list 
on the DARPA website.  
CONTACT INFORMATION
Please refer to ExPEDitions Proposers Day in all correspondence.
Technical Point of Contact:  Keith Whitener, Program Manager, 
ExPEDitions@darpa.mil 
Registration Website: https://events.sa-meetings.com/ExPEDitionsProposersDay
DARPA Opportunities Website: https://www.darpa.mil/research#research-
opportunities 

DARPA-SN-26-70 ExPEDitions Proposers Day                                                                                
DISCLAIMERS AND IMPORTANT NOTES
Attendance at the ExPEDitions Proposers Day or viewing the webcast is voluntary and is not 
required to propose to the anticipated ExPEDitions PS. Interested parties to this notice are 
cautioned that nothing herein obligates the Government to issue a solicitation. The Proposers 
Day does not constitute a formal solicitation for proposals or abstracts. This announcement is 
issued solely for information and program planning purposes and is not a Request for 
Information (RFI). Since this is not an RFI, the Government will not accept submissions 
against this notice, with the exception of the one-page profile referenced in the Teaming 
section above and briefing materials associated with Lightning Talks. No classified, 
International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) controlled, or proprietary information shall 
be presented by the Government at Proposers Day. Inclusion of proprietary information 
during Lightning Talks is at the presenter’s discretion; however, any submitted Lightning 
Talk presentation slides should be appropriate for public release. DARPA will not provide 
reimbursement for costs incurred to participate in this Proposers Day. Recording Proposers 
Day is not permitted.
For those new to DARPA or national security, DARPA makes available a free, comprehensive 
resource via DARPAConnect on how to do business with the agency. In addition to DARPA 
101 materials, relevant preparatory modules include “Making the Most of a Proposers Day” 
and “Understanding DARPA Broad Agency Announcements.” Registration and access are 
free at www.darpaconnect.us.

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
April 27, 2026 
xEMU Liquid Cooling and Ventilation Garment (LCVG) Thermal Control Loop 
Development 
Vendor SOW 
1. Background 
Significant investment by NASA has recently occurred, within the context of the xEMU 
program, to develop the Liquid Cooling and Ventilation Garment, used to control 
crewmember heat storage during extra-vehicular activity, or EVA. This investment 
culminated in the delivery of multiple xEMU LCVG garments to NASA.  The xEMU Liquid 
Cooling and Ventilation Garment Thermal control loop is a very complicated assembly, 
consisting of molded and extruded parts, custom-irradiated to achieve a specific melting 
behavior under increased temperatures, and very specific and directed application of heat 
using custom tooling in order to thermally bond the various parts of the assembly together.  
Development of the materials, tooling and processes for assembly of the LCVG thermal 
control loop required a significant investment by NASA in multiple vendors during the 
xEMU program.  This Statement of Work (SOW) aims to finalize the xEMU LCVG thermal 
control loop tooling design and processes, to enable repair of the existing xEMU LCVG fleet, 
as well as fabrication of additional LCVGs, as needed. 
2. Scope of Work 
The Contractor shall work to mature the xEMU LCVG thermal control loop, including 
manifold-to-manifold, manifold-to-tubing, and tubing co-bonding. This effort includes 
development of the necessary heating elements, heat clamps, and detailed procedure to 
enable NASA to finalize the LCVG thermal control loop fabrication. 
 
All work shall be performed in close coordination with NASA to ensure alignment with 
project objectives and lessons learned from prior development phases. Due to the 
challenges associated with meeting requirements associated with this complicated 
assembly, this contract will be considered a single iteration best-effort, and therefore 
technical requirements are considered “shoulds”; meeting requirements for proof pressure 
and tubing pull-out are not considered a requisite for acceptance.  
3. Period of Performance 
The Period of Performance (POP) for this effort shall be five (5) months following Approved 
to Proceed (ATP). All milestones shall be scheduled relative to ATP. 

4. Milestones and Deliverables Schedule 
Milestone Timing Description Deliverables 
M1 – Kickoff ATP + 2 weeks Project kickoff 
meeting and 
alignment on scope, 
schedule, and 
technical approach. 
Kickoff 
presentation; 
finalized schedule 
M2 – Final Delivery ATP + 5 months Completion of 
optimized thermal 
bonding process 
Delivery of samples, 
applicable drawings 
and testing reports. 
    
5. Technical Goals and Objectives 
The contractor shall design, fabricate, and test xEMU thermal loop assembly components, 
including development of supporting tooling, processes, and documentation to meet NASA 
requirements, which are: 
(1) Proof testing to 52.5 psid for five minutes with no leakage. 
(2) Pull-out testing of all tubing thermal bonds to permanent deformation of 1” length; 
post-prooftesting to 52.5 psid for five minutes with no leakage. 
Below is an itemization of the thermal bonds which need to be developed as part of this 
effort: 
 
Fabrication 
• Primary Thermal Loops: 
• QTY (2) subscale xEMU primary thermal loops, each consisting of: 
• Splitter hose clamp (SDN13103905, QTY 1) thermally bonded to 
Splitter socket (SDN13103906, QTY 1) 
• Splitter socket (SDN13103906, QTY 1) thermally bonded to 
Tubing, paratubing (SDN13103921-002, QTY 4) 
• Tubing, paratubing (SDN13103921-002, QTY 4) thermally 
bonded to Primary manifold tee (SDN13103903, QTY 4) 
• Primary manifold tee (SDN13103903, QTY 4) thermally bonded 
to Tubing, capillary (SDN13103921-001, QTY 24) in deadhead 
configuration 
• Auxiliary Thermal Loops: 
• QTY (4) subscale xEMU auxiliary thermal loops, each consisting of: 
▪ Tubing, auxiliary (SDN13103921-003, QTY 1) thermally bonded 
to Auxiliary manifold tee (SDN13103904, QTY 1) 

▪ Auxiliary manifold tee (SDN13103904, QTY 1) thermally bonded 
to Tubing, capillary (SDN13103921-001, QTY 10) in deadhead 
configuration 
Tooling and Equipment Development 
• Design and fabrication of 6 clamshell molds supporting heating elements and 
thermocouples, unique to each bond area: 
• Splitter hose clamp to splitter socket 
• Splitter socket to paratubing 
• Paratubing to primary and capillary manifold 
• Primary manifold to tubing 
• Capillary manifold to tubing 
• Paratube co-bonding 
• Procurement and wiring of heating drivers, thermocouple data loggers, and 
harnessing for convenient operations 
• Evaluation and iteration of clamshell geometry based on preliminary bond 
evaluations. 
• Any equipment required to test and evaluate against NASA requirements. 
6. Deliverables 
The Contractor shall provide the following deliverables: 
 
-Project kickoff meeting and weekly technical status updates. 
-Drawings and assembly instructions for tooling/custom equipment (thermal bonding rigs) 
-Detailed work instructions for thermal bonding processes, including itemization of 
tools/supplies with supplier sources. 
-Delivery of test results against NASA requirements  
-Updated documentation of production processes and CAD revisions. 
 
7. Assumptions 
1. NASA provides all Elvax parts, drawings, and CAD. 
2. All SDN part numbers provided as GFE by NASA. 
3. No new NASA part numbers issued for thermal loop samples 
4. Best Effort, single iteration tooling and deliverable fabrication; acceptance of 
deliverables not contingent on passing proof pressure leakage tests 
8. Contract Type 
The services described in this Statement of Work shall be provided on a Firm Fixed Price 
(FFP) basis. The Contractor shall perform the services using commercially reasonable best 
efforts and in accordance with the terms and conditions of the governing Agreement. The 
fixed price is not subject to adjustment based on the Contractor’s actual costs incurred in 
performing the services.

APPENDIX A: PROGRAM AND TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION  
   
 
1. BACKGROUND  
The lack of continuous, molecular -level insight into the body — for example real-time 
tracking of hormones, cytokines, and drug levels — leads to preventable disease progression 
and missed chances for early intervention. Wearable technologies could change this by 
providing timely data to inform a speciﬁc course of action or modify behavior in real time . 
Unfortunately, current devices are often cumbersome, inaccurate, or too costly because 
each biosensor is engineered as a bespoke system with expensive, non -reusable 
components.  
Delphi will improve the biosensor development ecosystem , enabling low-cost but high-
performance sensing by shifting to  a chiplet-based architecture. With chiplets, components  
of what would typically be an Application Speciﬁc Integrated Circuit (ASIC) can be reused 
and remixed  into new devices that share the same high performance . Yields and scaling 
tend to be easier, and the approach inherently enables heterogeneous integration , which is 
ideal due to the diverse material set often needed for biosensing. De lphi aims to leverage 
existing advances in chiplets to focus on the components speciﬁc to biosensing. First, " dry," 
hermetically sealed chiplets must provide ultra -low power management, overcoming the 
limitations of  current power-hungry standards and the constraints of low duty cycle 
operation and RF or internal power harvesting.  Additionally, chiplets that ensure secure 
communication  of medical data from these  body-worn devices must be developed.  Second, 
“wet” biosensor chiplets that directly interface with biology are needed . Delphi aims to 
extend the state of art from biophysical measurements  or high-concentration metabolites  to 
the continuous measure ment of low concentration biochemical markers , such as hormones 
and cytokines, over extended periods. Third, these chiplets must be integrated into 
biocompatible packages that are fully encapsulated except at the sensing interface. 
Existing encapsulation methods either lack the selectivity and reliability required at the 
chiplet scale or depend on rigid, complex, non -modular solutions. New packaging strategies 
must protect delicate electronics, preserve sensor surface chemistry, and support durable, 
long-term operation in biological environments.  
By the end, Delphi will quickly and cheaply develop modular wearable or ingestible 
sensors for monitoring a broad range of biological markers.   
2. PROGRAM OVERVIEW  
Today, the lack of deep biological insight — such as continuous monitoring of hormones, 
cytokines, and drug levels — contributes to preventable disease progression, missed 
opportunities for early intervention, and limited personal health agency. Emerging weara ble 
technologies could close this gap by providing real -time physiological data, enabling 
individuals and clinicians to recognize early warning signs, tailor treatments, and adjust 
behaviors in the moment rather than after damage has occurred. Consequently , Delphi seeks 
to empower all Americans to fully understand their bod ies by providing this information. This 
will require a revolution in the cost and performance of biosensors. The program will leverage 
chiplets, a new system architecture in microelectronics, to greatly decrease cost ; reduce size, 

APPENDIX A: PROGRAM AND TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION  
   
 
weight, and power (SWaP) ; and enable all developers to access cutting edge capabilities. By 
the end, Delphi will quickly and cheaply develop modular wearable or ingestible sensors for 
monitoring of a broad range of biological markers. The beneﬁts include early detection to 
prevent disease progression, continuous monitoring for safe home recovery, and precis e, 
closed-loop therapy for superior health outcomes.  
PROGRAM DESCRIPTION   
The Delphi program is soliciting proposals to create an open, extensible platform to support 
wearable and ingestible  biosensors. Current bioelectronic devices are largely built from 
scratch for each application, using discrete components on printed circuit boards and, only 
later, costly custom ASICs. Because each ASIC must integrate multiple functions onto a 
single die, every desi gn becomes its own expensive, time -consuming project, slowing 
progress and limiting performance. Delphi performers will create a standard format of 
packaging and interconnections that will enable integration of chiplets from multiple 
manufacturers. Proposers should identify preferred packaging and interconnect 
solutions; however, a series of meetings in the ﬁrst 2 months of the program will establish 
a consensus packaging approach, thus ensuring interoperability . Given the needs of 
biosensing, ultra -high-density  interconnects are unlikely to be needed. Approaches that 
integrate power, such as a battery or an RF antenna, into the substrate are encouraged.  
Teams will likely need to develop Delphi speciﬁc “dry” chiplets for capabilities unique to 
biosensing (e.g. power management and highly secure communications) but are expected to 
leverage commercially available chiplets or IP for more generic device funct ions, thereby 
leveraging the cost savings due to production scales. While development and testing of 
implantable devices is out scope for the Delphi program, platforms that could ﬁt within the 
size, weight, and power limitations of an implantable device o r serve as wearable or 
ingestible would be viewed favorably.  
Delphi teams will develop “wet” biosensing chiplets capable of real -time measurement of 
deep biological information. Except for continuous glucose monitors, most commercial 
sensors measure only biophysical signals. Routine, continuous detection of low 
concentration biochemical analytes, such as hormones (0.1 — 100 µg/L) and cytokines (≈10 
ng/L), has been demonstrated by only a few groups, and typically for just a few days in 
wearable formats. New sensing modalities demonstrate  the potential for longer term, 
regenerative measurements that could be adapted to hormones, cytokines, or other 
markers. However, each new biomarker currently demands a dedicated discovery and 
optimization process along with device re -engineering, limiting scalability and slowing the 
development of the multiplexed sensor panels needed for comprehensive health proﬁling. 
Delphi is seeking a pproaches that are generalizable to multiple analytes to increase the 
extensibility sensor systems  and platforms. Additionally, the development of surface 
chemistries that prevent sensor fouling is typically arduous. Delphi is open to new concepts 
that can rapidly improve the passivation of sensor surfaces to deliver  methods that are 
compatible with clean rooms. Performing sensor functionalization within the fab , likely in a 
separate post-processing hood,  would minimize  the surface contamination that hinders the 
formation of high -quality passivation. To meet these challenges, teams must develop 
design, optimization, and manufacturing processes that support rapid retargeting of new 

APPENDIX A: PROGRAM AND TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION  
   
 
analytes and scalable production, including chiplet printing and processing, device 
packaging, and sterilization.  
Delphi teams will need to develop robust biocompatible materials and encapsulation 
processes for protecting electronics, while providing biosensors access to their target 
environment. Conventional materials and fabrication methods often fall short when app lied 
to small electronic components. These conventional approaches frequently result in leaks or 
failures, as they are not designed to accommodate the unique challenges posed by 
miniaturized devices. Moreover, there is currently no solution that can simult aneously 
protect delicate electronics, permit selective exposure where needed, and preserve the 
surface chemistry essential for sensor function. Approaches must be made compatible with 
the underlying biochemistry of the biosensor chips while meeting the ex tremely tight 
tolerances and critical materials properties associated with chiplet fabrication to prevent, 
for instance, warping of the small system.  
NATIONAL HEALTH IMPACT 
A national ARPA-H program to enable small, low -cost, high-performance biosensors would 
address key gaps: the lack of scalable platforms for deep molecular monitoring outside 
specialty centers; the need for minimally invasive, high -frequency data on inﬂamm ation and 
metabolic status; and technical barriers in miniaturization, power, and multimodal sensing. 
Emerging technologies — such as self-powered ingestible metabolite sensors, integrated GI 
smart capsules, interstitial ﬂuid -sampling microneedles, and swea t-based biosensors —
demonstrate that battery -free or low-power operation, multi -marker detection, and wireless 
telemetry are feasible in preclinical and early clinical settings. If these platforms can be 
engineered for low -cost, robust manufacturing and des igned for usability and connectivity 
in resource -limited environments, they could expand access to high -frequency molecular 
data beyond infrequent lab testing, enabling earlier detection of disease activity and more 
adaptive management.  
Delphi seeks to lower the cost of all biosensors and is agnostic to the targeted disease. 
However, proposers must identify their targeted disease or health or wellness indications 
and justify their choice, as described below.  Examples of beneﬁts to patients could include 
earlier detection of ﬂares in inﬂammatory bowel disease and rheumatoid arthritis, pre -
symptomatic recognition of sepsis or pulmonary hypertension progression, and dynamic 
monitoring of treatment response, p articularly in rural and low -resource settings. By 
bending the cost curve, Delphi hopes to vastly increase the market for biosensors, enabling 
individuals to better understand and improve their own health , thereby reducing expensive 
and avoidable hospitalizations and emergency department visits.  
PROGRAM SCOPE 
Delphi will unite the scalable production of commercial microelectronics with advances in 
biosensor  detection and biocompatibility coming out of academia and other research 
institutions. Multidisciplinary teams must include at least three key roles: (1) a  “dry” chiplet 
group (interposer/substrate, interconnects, power management, secure communication), (2) 
a “wet” biosensor group for detecting diverse humoral biomarkers, and (3) an encapsulation 
group ensuring hermetic sealing while exposing the biosensing inter face to biological 

APPENDIX A: PROGRAM AND TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION  
   
 
environments. Teams, not ARPA -H, are responsible for full integration. Proposals that do 
not address all TAs and their integration into a functional device will not be considered.  
Proposers should choose one of  two tracks: (1) Minimally invasive devices that either 
penetrate the stratum corneum or are ingested. These devices require FDA oversight and 
will culminate in formal human clinical trials to validate safety and efﬁcacy. (2) Non -invasive 
wearables that do not break the skin’s surface which aim to promote healthy lifestyle 
choices and reduce disease risk. These devices have a lower regulatory barrier and will 
culminate in human factor testing to assess usability and impact. Th is dual-track approach 
supports both advanced medical devices and wellness -focused wearables.  
3. DELPHI  TECHNICAL AREAS  
Delphi will quickly advance the development of modular, chiplet -based wearables and 
ingestibles to monitor a wide range of biological markers. Current bioelectronic devices are 
custom-built for each application, relying on discrete components in relatively  large PCB 
boards or smaller ASICs that integrate multiple functions onto a single die, but that are 
costly to develop and to further reﬁne. A chiplet  architecture enables both smaller and high -
performance systems while lowering the cost of development a nd ongoing edits. Delphi 
aims to leverage existing capabilities in the chiplet space while using the Technical Areas 
(TAs) deﬁned below to focus on the capabilities unique to biosensing.  To this end, Delphi 
comprises four interconnected TAs,  all of which must be addressed:  
TA1 ≡ Dry Chiplets Unique to Biosensing:  Determine a common packaging and 
interconnect strategy. Develop chiplets for ultra -low power management and for secure 
medical data transmission.  
TA2 ≡ Wet Biosensing Chiplet: Develop biology -facing sensors for detection of deep 
biological data that interfaces into the chiplet architecture. This will include not only 
improvements in biological recognition elements but new approaches for surface 
passivation that are compatible with clean room processing. 
 
TA3 ≡ Biocompatible Encapsulation: Develop hermetic encapsulation to seal integrated 
chiplet packages, exposing the “wet” sensing interface to the biological environment while 
preserving the “dry” chiplets from moisture ingress.
 
TA4 ≡ Human Factors Testing or Clinical Trial: Based on the track chosen, assess whether 
the device can be used safely, effectively, and intuitively by intended users under realistic 
conditions, identifying and mitigating any use -related risks.

Figure 1. Summary of Program Technical Areas  
 
TA1: “DRY ” CHIPLETS UNIQUE TO BIOSENSING THAT ARE HERMETIC AND WILL SERVE AS THE 
FOUNDATION FOR THE BIOSENSING CHIPLET COMPONENTS INTEGRATION  
Under TA1, proposals should present a scalable and cost -effective strategy for packaging 
chiplets for biosensing. To ensure interoperability, a consensus approach will be agreed 
upon in the ﬁrst two months of the program, beginning with initial discussion  at the
