REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL No. 74330226R0039 
Fallen Servicemembers Religious Heritage Restoration Program 
 
OVERVIEW 
The American Battle Monuments Commission (ABMC) is soliciting proposals for commercial 
research services to identify American Jewish servicemembers buried under grave markers that 
incorrectly represent religion or heritage, and to identify surviving next o f kin (NOK), as described 
in the attached Statement of Work, Attachment 1. 
 
CONTRACT TYPE 
ABMC anticipates award of a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract. Travel expenses, if required, should 
be proposed as a separate CLIN.  
 
PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 
The period of performance is anticipated for  12 months for the base year , beginning upon contract 
award. 
 
EVALUATION CRITERA 
ABMC intends to award one contract to the vendor whose proposal represents the best value to the 
Government. ABMC will evaluate offerors based on the below factors on a best -value approach, in 
order of importance. Non-price factors, when combined, are more important than price. Price remains 
an important consideration. 
 
Factors 
1. Demonstrated Capability and Expertise: Experience and past performance in work similar to the 
Statement of Work, including research, evidence based documentation, and NOK identification. 
2. Technical Approach: Soundness and feasibility of the proposed methodology, including 
handling of records, case file development, and NOK research. 
3. Management, Schedule, and Deliverables: Ability to manage the work and deliver required 
products in a timely and reliable manner 
4. Quality Control and Data Protection: Adequacy of QC procedures and safeguards for sensitive 
information and PII. 
5. Price: Price will be evaluated for reasonableness and consistency with the proposed approach. 
 
PROPOSAL FORMAT 
Proposals shall be submitted in three volumes in pdf format. 
Volume I – Technical Approach 
Describe how the offeror will perform the Statement of Work, including: 
• Research methodology and source verification 
• Case file development with citations and confidence assessment 

 
• Approach to identifying and documenting NOK 
• Deliverables and schedule 
• Quality control procedures 
• Data protection and privacy safeguards 
• Staffing and key personnel 
 
Volume II – Experience   
Provide evidence of demonstrated capability and expertise, including: 
• Up to three relevant past projects 
• Past performance references (at least two) 
• Experience of key personnel 
 
Volume III – Price   
Provide a Firm -Fixed-Price for the base period and a price breakdown aligned to the Statement of 
Work. Include a brief narrative explaining key pricing assumptions. 
 
QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS 
Questions shall be submitted in writing to the Contracting Officer and Contracting Specialist no later 
than 14 April 2026 at 5PM (Eastern Time). Responses will be issued by written amendment or 
posting. 
 
PROPOSAL SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS 
Proposals shall be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer and Contracting Specialist with the 
subject line “Proposal – 74330226R0039 – Offeror Name” no later than 5PM (Eastern Time) on 
28 April 2026 to the following: 
 
Michael Bachofen     Michael G. Knapp 
Contracting Officer     Contracting Officer’s Representative 
bachofenm@abmc.gov     knappm@abmc.gov   
 
Jessica Young 
Contracting Specialist 
youngj.ctr@abmc.gov    
 
 
ATTACHMENTS: 
1. Statement of Work, dated April 3, 2026 
2. Questions and Answers Template 
 
Solicitation Compliance 
Failure to comply with the material requirements  of this solicitation, including the restriction on 
unauthorized NOK contact, may render a proposal unacceptable.

1 SOW 1,2 Will ABMC provide an initial dataset, candidate list, or prioritized records, or is the 
Contractor expected to independently identify all potential candidate cases across ABMC 
cemeteries?
The contractor is responsible for research to develop and research a list of possible burials 
under the incorrect headstone. ABMC does not have a database of potential cases of mis-
identified individuals.
2 SOW 1,2 Can ABMC clarify the total scope of cemeteries and memorials included in this effort? The scope is within the 26 Overseas military cemeteries administered by the ABMC.
3 SOW 2,4 Does ABMC have an estimated range of anticipated cases (annually or over the base period) 
for planning and pricing services?
There is no specified estimated range for annual identification of cases.
4 SOW 3 Should case identification and screening efforts (research to determine whether a valid case 
exists) be considered part of the core deliverable effort, or is there an expected number of 
completed case files? 
This is part of the core deliverable.
5 SOW 4 Beyond the initial delivery of 3-5 case files by Day 90, is there a target throughput or 
production expectation (e.g. cases per month or quarter)?
There is no specific target but the expectation is that as research identifies potential cases 
the contractor will batch those  for submission to ABMC to keep the process from being 
overwhelmed with a large number of cases at one time. It is up to the contractor to determine 
of a batch is 3 or greater up to five and maintain batch consistency 
6 RFP Instructions Letter 1 Given the FFP structure, can ABMC provide any guidance regarding expected level of 
effort, case volume assumptions, or evaluation approach for price realism?
During both WW1 and WW2 Jewish servicemembers represented about 4% of the total 
among all services. Given this statistic the 4% of the 140,000  buried in ABMC sites is equal 
to about 5600.The expectation for this contract would be closer to 5,000 given that not all 
are buried incorrectly and several dozen have already been corrected.
7 RFP Instructions Letter 1,2 Will price be evaluated based on an assumed workload model (e.g. estimated number of 
cases, or solely on the FFP and supporting narrative? 
Price will be evaluated on FFP and supporting narrative. 
8 RFP Instructions Letter 2 Would ABMC consider or accept pricing submissions that include clearly stated 
assumptions (estimated case volume, identification yield rates), with acknowledgement that 
actual conditions may vary? 
Yes, assumptions shall be clearly stated in submissions with acknowledgement that actual 
conditions may vary.
9 Would ABMC consider an WOSB set-aside for the requirement? Not at this time.

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
 
Fallen Servicemembers Religious Heritage Restoration Program  
 
April 3, 2026 
 
1. Background and Purpose 
 
The American Battle Monuments Commission (ABMC) maintains American military cemeteries and 
memorials around the world and is committed to honoring United States servicemembers with 
accurate commemoration. In support of the Fallen Servicemembers Religious Heritage Restoration 
Program, ABMC seeks contractor support to research and identify American-Jewish servicemembers 
interred in American military cemeteries whose headstones or grave markers incorrectly represent 
their religion and heritage, and to identify surviving next of kin to support potential corrective actions 
and outreach. 
 
2. Scope and Objectives 
 
Scope 
The Contractor shall conduct historical, genealogical, and documentary research to: 
(1) identify American -Jewish servicemembers buried at American military cemeteries with 
grave markers that incorrectly reflect their religion and heritage, and  
(2) identify and locate surviving next of kin for those servicemembers, consistent with 
applicable law, regulation, and ABMC policies. 
 
Important limitations and boundaries (consistent with this SOW): 
 
• The Contractor shall not contact next of kin unless explicitly authorized in writing by the 
Contracting Officer (CO) or Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR). 
• The Contractor’s role is limited to research, documentation, and reporting. Any decisions 
regarding marker corrections and any engagement with families or stakeholders remain with 
ABMC. 
• The Contractor shall not issue public statements, respond to media inquiries, or represent 
ABMC with respect to matters relating to the contract without prior written authorization 
from the CO. 
 

Page 2 of 7 
 
Objectives 
 
• Develop and execute a research methodology to identify likely and confirmed cases of 
misidentified religion/heritage on grave markers. 
• Produce evidence-based case files for each recommended correction, including source 
citations and confidence assessment. 
• Identify, verify, and document surviving next of kin or appropriate family representatives, 
with contact information obtained through lawful means. 
• Provide ABMC with completed case files to support change of headstone suitable for 
ABMC review, decision-making, and potential engagement with families and stakeholders. 
• Ensure sensitive handling of personal data and respectful treatment of the deceased and their 
families. 
 
3. Period of Performance 
 
The contract is anticipated to be a Firm -Fixed-Price (FFP) contract.  The period of performance is 
anticipated to be one (1) base year, with (4) option years (as shown in proposed CLIN structure below) 
that may be exercised at the Government’s discretion and subject to the availability of funds.

4. Definitions and Abbreviations 
• ABMC: American Battle Monuments Commission. 
• American military cemetery: A cemetery administered by ABMC or otherwise identified 
by ABMC in this contract as within scope. 
• Case: A servicemember record for which the Contractor has developed evidence indicating 
the decedent was American-Jewish and the marker religion/heritage is inconsistent with 
available records. 
• Next of kin (NOK): Surviving family member(s) or legally recognized representative(s) as 
defined by ABMC for purposes of outreach and potential marker correction consideration. 
• Source: A primary or secondary document used to support findings (e.g., military personnel 

Page 3 of 7 
 
records, casualty records, burial records, cemetery interment records, vital records, 
synagogue/community records, published rosters, newspaper obituaries, naturalization 
records). 
 
5. Requirements (Tasks) 
5.1 Task 1: Project Initiation and Research Plan 
 
Within 30 calendar days after award, the Contractor shall submit a research plan for ABMC approval 
that describes the methodology, sources, tools, staffing, quality controls, schedule, and risk 
management approach for the work. The plan shall include proposed criteria for identifying likely or 
confirmed American-Jewish servicemembers and for determining that a grave marker is inconsistent 
with the evidence. 
 
5.2 Task 2: Data Collection and Source Research 
 
The Contractor shall collect and analyze relevant source materials to establish identity, service, burial 
location, and religion/heritage indicators. Research may include, as appropriate, Federal records (e.g., 
National Archives holdings), ABMC cemetery/in terment records, Department of Defense casualty 
systems where accessible, state and local vital records, genealogical repositories, community and 
religious archives, and reputable published sources. The Contractor shall maintain full citations and 
copies/record references sufficient for ABMC to independently verify findings. 
 
5.3 Task 3: Case Identification, Analysis, and Evidence Packages 
 
The Contractor shall identify candidate cases and develop an evidence package (“Case File”) for each. 
Each Case File shall, at minimum, include: 
 
• Servicemember identification: full name, service branch, service number (if known), dates 
of birth/death, unit (if known), conflict/era. 
• Burial information: cemetery name, plot/row/grave (or equivalent), current marker 
inscription details relevant to religion/heritage. 
• Summary of evidence supporting American-Jewish identity (primary sources preferred), 
with citations. 
• Summary of evidence supporting that the current marker is inconsistent with the evidence 
(e.g., incorrect religious emblem/wording), with citations. 
• Confidence assessment (e.g., High/Medium/Low) and rationale. 
• Known sensitivities/flags (e.g., conflicting records, ambiguous indicators, name changes), 
and recommended ABMC review steps. 
 
5.4 Task 4: Identification of Surviving Next of Kin 
 
For each Case File, the Contractor shall perform genealogical research to identify surviving next of 
kin and/or legally recognized family representatives and provide ABMC with a documented kinship 

Page 4 of 7 
 
pathway (family tree narrative or equivalent) supported by source citations. The Contractor shall use 
lawful, ethical means for locating contact information. The Contractor shall not contact next of kin 
unless explicitly authorized in writing by the CO or COR. 
 
5.5 Task 5: Coordination, Status Reporting, and Stakeholder Sensitivity 
 
The Contractor shall participate in recurring status meetings (virtual unless otherwise directed) and 
provide updates on progress, issues, and risks. The Contractor shall coordinate with ABMC -
designated points of contact regarding access to ABMC records, cemetery information, and 
prioritization. All work products and communications shall be prepared with appropriate respect and 
sensitivity given the nature of the subject matter.

DESCRIPTION
1. Description 
The Federal Election Commission (FEC) is seeking information from qualified, experienced vendors/contractors about 
securing a commercial vendor to provide access to Amazon Web Services (AWS), through vendor-maintained payer 
accounts. The FEC has several vendor-managed AWS payer accounts with associated subaccounts. The government may 
establish additional payer accounts and/or subaccounts. The cloud is the FEC’s default infrastructure and requires a vendor 
to provide AWS services through a consolidated account and provide detailed billing and usage data.  
 
The government does not need assistance managing the information systems within the accounts. The vendor is 
responsible only for providing access to the FEC’s AWS accounts and providing detailed consolidated billing. The 
requirements of this development effort are described in Attachment 1: Draft Requirements. 
 
1.2 This is a Request for Information (RFI) only 
This RFI is only for the purpose of identifying potential contractors as part of the FEC’s market research. The FEC will not 
reimburse contractors for any expenses associated with their response to this RFI. Responses to this notice are not offers and 
cannot be accepted by the FEC to form a binding contract. Responses to the RFI become FEC property and will not be 
returned. Respondents will not be notified of the result of the review. 
This RFI is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not itself constitute a Request for 
Quotations (RFQ). The FEC does not intend to award Schedule order(s) or BPAs based only on 
responses to this RFI. There is no commitment by the FEC to issue an RFQ, make an award or awards, or 
to be responsible for any monies expended by industry to respond to this RFI. 
 
All information received in response to this RFI marked “Proprietary” will be protected and handled accordingly. 
Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information 
contained in their response. 
 
This RFI will be posted on Contract Opportunities
. No RFQ exists; therefore, do not request a copy of the RFQ. 
The FEC is not required to use Contract Opportunities for any resulting RFQ. 
2.0 Program information 
2.1 Background 
The Federal Election Commission (FEC) is an independent regulatory agency responsible for administering, enforcing, 
defending and interpreting the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971, as amended (FECA or the Act).1 Congress created 
the FEC to administer, enforce and formulate policy with respect to the FECA. The Act reflects a belief that democracy 
works best when voters can make informed decisions in the political process— decisions based in part on knowing the 
 
1 Public Law 92-225, 86 Stat. 3 (1972) (codified at 52 U.S.C. §§ 30101-45). 

Federal Election Commission  
Enterprise Architecture  
Request for Information (RFI)  
Amazon Web Services  
 
Page 3 
sources of financial support for federal candidates, political party committees and other political committees. Public 
confidence in the political process also depends on the knowledge that participants in federal elections follow clear and 
well-defined rules and face consequences for non-compliance. Under the Act, all federal political committees, including the 
committees of presidential, Senate and House candidates, must file reports of receipts and disbursements. The FEC makes 
disclosure reports, and the data contained in them, available to the public through the Commission’s internet-based public 
disclosure system on the Commission’s website, as well as in a public records office at the Commission's Washington, D.C. 
headquarters.  
 
The FEC started its cloud migration journey in 2018 and migrated all internal applications from 
physical data centers to AWS by 2023. In 2024, the services provided by the Electronic Filing Office 
were migrated to AWS, and later that year FECs last physical data center was decommissioned. The 
cloud is now the agency’s default infrastructure. The FEC is working to mature in cloud operations 
by optimizing costs and adopting cloud-native, innovative solutions. 
 
2.2 Anticipated period of performance 
The FEC anticipates the period of performance to be sixty (60) months, including one (1) 12-month base period and four (4) 
12-month option periods.

Notice of Industry Day event for the upcoming Unclassified IT Service Contract 
 
The F-35 Lightning II Joint Program Office (JPO), Arlington, Virginia, will host an industry day May 21, 
2026, to discuss the program’s upcoming requirement for Information Technology (IT) and 
Information Assurance (IA)/Cybersecurity Services (CS).  During this vital forum, the Government 
will share its upcoming procurement needs with our industry partners. This event is intended to be 
a place of transparent communication and collaboration between the public and private sectors; it 
offers a prime opportunity for vendors to understand the Government’s requirements, ask clarifying 
questions, and network with both Government officials and potential partners.  The F-35 JPO will 
use feedback and information about industry capability to refine its requirements. 
 
The F-35 JPO requires comprehensive IT and IA/CS support for its Joint Virtual Enterprise (JVE) 
network and standalone workstations. This support, crucial to the JPO’s mission effectiveness and 
the successful fielding of F-35 mission capabilities, will be provided across all directorates, 
functional areas, and integrated product teams. This includes, but is not limited to, program 
management, enterprise performance management, enterprise architecture, emerging capabilities 
and requirements implementation, life cycle management, operations & maintenance, enterprise 
data management, service desk support, IT training, and CS support. This includes managing the 
JVE network to support both unclassified communications, ensuring seamless connectivity and 
service across the network, and coordinating with contractors responsible for classified systems 
and external trusted networks.  The Contractor shall be responsible for a full range of services as 
outlined in the Draft PWS, Attachment 1. 
 
The Government anticipates the RFP will be released under the North American Industry 
Classification System (NAICS) 541512, Computer System Design Services, with a size standard of 
$34.0 Mil. The resultant contract is expected to be base plus four years. We encourage any and all 
interested parties to attend the industry day to discuss this requirement in further detail. 
 
Please refer to this link for more information and RSVP to the event. Please submit all questions 
through the form on this link: https://www.jsf.mil/industry-day.  
 
Please feel free to reach out to Contract Specialist Sanjana Garg Sanjana.Garg@jsf.mil or 
Contracting Officer, John Meyers at John.Meyers@jsf.mil.

F-35 JOINT PROGRAM OFFICE  
DIRECTORATE OF ENTERPRISE SERVICES ACQUISITION 
 
 
 
 
Unclassified IT Follow-On 
Performance Work Statement  
(PWS) 
 
 
1.0 INTRODUCTION. 
The F-35 Lightning II Joint Program Office (JPO) leads the life-cycle program management of 
the F-35A, F-35B, and F-35C: the fifth-generation joint strike fighter air system of choice for the 
U.S. Air Force, U.S. Navy, U.S. Marine Corps, international partners, and foreign military sales 
customers.  The mandate of the JPO is to deliver a capable, available, and cost-efficient air 
system to the warfighter - outpacing key competitors to win tomorrow's high-end fight as we 
develop, deliver, and sustain war-winning fifth-generation capabilities at high-end fourth-
generation costs. The JPO mission is to ensure the F-35 is: 
• lethal, scalable, and adaptable while safeguarding warfighters and outpacing aggressors. 
• operationally sustainable by delivering parts when needed and leveraging predictive 
maintenance technologies to keep parts on wing longer while enhancing repair velocity. 
• cost efficient for the U.S. services and international partners by optimizing procedures 
across the acquisition life cycle.  
 
Scope. 
The purpose of this effort is to obtain Contractor support to provide Information Technology (IT) 
and Information Assurance (IA)/Cybersecurity Services (CS) to the F-35 Lighting II Joint 
Program Office (F-35 JPO) Virtual Enterprise (JVE) network and standalone workstations as 
well as SSE, cyber systems engineering and risk management (e.g., RMF). The IT Services 
support the F-35 JPO mission and enhance its effectiveness, efficiency, and productivity by 
providing the Government with a full range of IT and CS services.  
The service requirements consist of program management, enterprise performance management, 
enterprise architecture, emerging capabilities and requirements implementation, life cycle 
management, operations & maintenance, enterprise data management and storage, service desk 
support, IT training, end-user capabilities and support, and cybersecurity incident response. 
These services are critical to the successful fielding of F-35 mission capabilities.  


2 
 
The Contractor shall provide resources, materials, and services as necessary to perform the tasks 
defined in this PWS, except as specified in the Government-Furnished Resources and Property 
list. Operating, maintaining, and properly managing the life cycle of hardware, software, and 
services is the crucial, primary service provided by this contract. Auxiliary IT engineer support 
will be provided to the F-35 Autonomic Logistics Information System (ALIS) team, as well as 
CS support to the Air Systems team.  
The F-35’s classified communications also traverse the JVE backbone. The Contractor shall 
provide networking services in support of the classified networks requirements by maintaining 
the JVE network and coordinating connections, changes, outages, etc. with the Contractor 
responsible for the classified systems. The Contractor shall ensure that service is maintained 
across the JVE network up to the switch port feeding the Tactical Local Area Network 
Encryption (TACLANE) or other encryption device where support falls to the Contractor 
responsible for the classified system(s). 
In addition to F-35 JPO-controlled networks, Government and Contractor personnel may require 
access to services provided on other networks. The F-35 JPO has established several trusted 
connections to include:  af.mil, navy.mil, Lockheed Martin (LM) Autonomic Logistics 
Information System (ALIS), and LM Failure Reporting, Analysis and Corrective Action System 
(FRACAS). The Contractor shall maintain the JVE connections to the aforementioned systems 
and will work with those managing those systems to trouble-shoot issues when required.

3.0 TASKS/PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS.  
The Contractor shall provide all services and project supervision, as required in accordance with 
the Performance Work Statement (PWS). 
 
The Contractor’s team shall be responsible for performance of the tasks and activities, as 
specified within this PWS, to support the following: the Government’s day-to-day IT operations 
management processes pertaining to IT service operations; IT engineering activities; continual 
service improvement across the Government’s enterprise; and managing and maintaining CS 
integrity of all servers, devices, storage, or cloud-based computing resources from external and 
internal security threats. 
TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES  
3.1 Operations Management Services  
Operations Management Services is the maintenance and management of IT services to the F-35 
JPO including, but not limited to, telephony services (1,300+ Voice over Internet Protocol 
[VoIP] devices), video audio teleconference services (2,500+ video teleconferences [VTCs] 
annually), Network Operations Security Center (NOSC, 12 critical and 23 less critical service 
checks), network services (355 network devices, at Continental United States (CONUS), Japan, 
and Republic of Korea sites), application services and management (18+ custom applications and 
370+ software titles), and infrastructure management services (338 servers). 
3.2 Telephony Services  
Contractor shall manage Government devices, including but not limited to, laptops, desktops, 
mobile phones, tablets, and mobile hotspot devices. Support covers licensing, throughout the F-
35 JPO community within the confines of DoD and F-35 JPO cybersecurity policies and 
procedures. Contractor shall include the following services: 

4 
 
• Ensure seamless and uninterrupted communication through the implementation and 
continuous support of both voice and data telecommunications infrastructure. 
• Continue to explore innovative ways for improvement in Optimizing the performance, 
reliability, and scalability of telecommunication services, including VoIP, mobile 
communication systems (laptops, mobile phones, iPads, and other like-type devices,) and 
integrated networks. 
• Perform routine audits and troubleshooting to address any service degradation or failures 
within telecommunications systems. 
• Provide recommendations for technology and software refreshes that leverage other DoD 
or commercial technologies that enhance capabilities. 
• Maintain records in accordance with DoD policies, support 100 percent accountability of 
GFD (government furnished devices).  
• Conduct initial user training and assistance for use as necessary to end users upon the 
issuance or assignment of any type of phone.  
 
3.3 Video/Audio Teleconference (VTC) Services  
Contractor shall manage Non-classified Internet Protocol (IP) Router Network (NIPRNet) 
audiovisual (A/V) services for standard conference rooms, VTC rooms, and the Conferencing 
Center in addressing the following requirements: 
• Provide onsite support at the Conference Center as well as onsite support in VTC and 
conference rooms during core hours from 0600-1800 in Arlington, VA. 
• Provide high-quality, secure, and scalable video conferencing services to meet 
organization communication and collaboration needs, supporting both internal and 
external stakeholders. 
• Monitor and maintain the video teleconferencing infrastructure, ensuring seamless 
operation of video, audio, and screen-sharing functionality. 
• Implement and manage regular upgrades and maintenance to ensure compatibility with 
latest software versions, security protocols, and end-user devices. 
• Provide written end-user audiovisual instructions specific to each integrated audiovisual 
conference room configuration. 
• Provide end-user training on the audiovisual and collaboration applications in established 
conference rooms, VTC rooms, and the Conferencing Center upon request.  
• Daily monitoring of equipment for functional and operational readiness . Maintain 
equipment replacements on-hand to quickly repair commonly failed or recommended 
spares by sponsored system agency. 
• Coordinate with internal and external counterparts, to include Government personnel, 
contractors providing services or support for other contracts, or requirements, for 
troubleshooting or implementation of new equipment as necessary, (break/fix or new 
capability).  
• Perform patch and firmware upgrades, break/fix support, daily operations, and 
management support, including onsite assistance for special events.  
3.4 Network Operations Security Center (NOSC) 
Contractor shall manage, monitor, and report on the state of confidentiality, integrity, and 
availability of Joint Virtual Environment (JVE) critical and less critical services, including, but 
not limited to what is contained in Table 1. Critical and Less Critical Services. 

5 
 
 
• Establish a Network Operations Security Center to monitor, detect, and respond to

network performance and security, including detection of intrusion attempts, denial-of-

Instructions to Respondents:
Please provide concise, direct responses to the questions below. Excessive marketing material is not requested. The Government is seeking to understand your company's capabilities and approach to fulfilling the requirements outlined in the Performance Work Statement (PWS).

Part 1: Corporate Information

Company Details: Provide your Company Name, GSA Contract Number (if applicable), UEI Number, CAGE Code, and company website.

Point of Contact: Provide the name, title, email, and phone number for the primary point of contact for this RFI.

Business Size: Provide your business size and all applicable socio-economic categories (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), Woman-Owned, SDVOSB, etc.).

North American Industry Classification System (NAICS)/Product Service Code (PSC) Codes: What NAICS and PSC codes would you recommend for the scope of work described in the PWS?

Part 2: Corporate Experience & Past Performance

Overall Capability: Does your organization possess the capability to perform the services as described in the PWS?

Similar Experience: Please provide an example or examples of a project that your company has supported, that was of similar size, scope, and complexity to the DCPS requirement. For each, specify your organization’s role in supporting large-scale, legacy government financial or payroll systems, particularly those hosted in an IBM Mainframe (z/OS) environment.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

Defense Civilian Pay System

Part 1

General Information

General:

1.1 Introduction. The contractor shall provide all personnel and items necessary to perform the functional and technical support for the Defense Civilian Pay System (DCPS) as defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS) except for those items specified as Government furnished property and services. 

1.2 Background. The primary purpose of this contract is to obtain information and technology (I&T) support for the Defense Civilian Pay System (DCPS) located at the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS), Indianapolis, IN. DCPS was selected as the standard Department of War (DoW) formally Department of Defense (DoD), civilian pay system in 1991. The system maintains pay and leave entitlement records, deductions and withholdings, time and attendance data and other pertinent employee personnel data. Through the use of DCPS, DFAS is standardizing civilian payroll policies, processes, systems and procedures throughout the Department.

Multiple accounting systems interface with DCPS by receiving one or a combination of several standard accounting interface files. These files are created on a daily, weekly or biweekly basis and are electronically transmitted to the appropriate installation level or departmental accounting system. Each disbursing officer that services a DCPS payroll office is responsible for the disbursement of funds, as vouchers and certified by the payroll office. 

The DCPS Automated Information System (AIS) is developed and maintained by a single Central Design Activity (CDA), I&T Payroll Services - Indianapolis. The CDA provides functional requirements analysis; database design and maintenance; identification of system hardware and telecommunications requirements; technical design; programming; documentation; and implementation support and training materials for customers. The CDA also monitors operation of pay processing and receipt of interfacing files between trading partners and resolves problems for customers and payroll offices. Customers of DCPS include the DoW, Health and Human Services, Department of Energy, Veterans Affairs, Executive Office of the President, and the United States Agency for Global Media.

1.3 Objectives. The overall objective of this PWS is to define the tasks necessary to obtain the full software life cycle support in the development and maintenance of DCPS.

1.4 Scope. The contractor shall provide all necessary personnel, management, materials, administrative and technical services required to meet the requirements and/or tasks outlined in this PWS. The software and non-software support services to be acquired fall within the general areas of implementing change requests to the system and performing routine system maintenance. The software and non-software support services to be acquired fall within the general areas of:

	Software Design

	Software Development

	Database Development

	Software Maintenance

	Database Maintenance

	System Change Request Requirements Analysis

Software Testing

	Software Implementation

	Configuration Management

	Release Management

	Systems Interfaces

	Customer Inquiries

	Performance Measurements

	Production Support

	Audit Readiness

	Information Assurance

Appendix A provides a list of the required Systems Skills necessary to perform these support services. 

1.5 Period of Performance (PoP). The period of performance shall be for one (1) Base Period of 12 months and four (4) 12-month option periods.

1.6 Quality Assurance Plan (QAP). The contractor shall develop, maintain, and manage an effective QAP to ensure services are performed in accordance with this Performance Work Statement (PWS) and the performance standards set forth in the Performance Requirements Summary (PRS) at Technical Exhibit 1. The contractor’s QAP is the means by which it assures compliance with the work requirements and shall include procedures to identify, prevent, and ensure the non-recurrence of defective services. The plan should consider the directions provided in Section 7.1 of this PWS and will be used to collect and monitor performance data for reporting to the Contracting Officer Representative (COR). The contractor shall deliver their proposed QAP with their quote. After the initial QAP is accepted, the contractor must receive the Contracting Officer's (CO) acceptance in writing for any proposed changes, and a revised plan must be submitted within 5 business days of any changes. Unless otherwise indicated, the rating period for performance will be quarterly, with formal monthly status reports on progress.

 

1.7 Recognized Holidays. 

New Year’s Day				Labor Day

Martin Luther King Jr.’s Birthday		Columbus Day

President’s Day				Veteran’s Day

Memorial Day					Thanksgiving Day

Juneteenth National Independence Day	Christmas Day

Independence Day				

If the holiday occurs on a Saturday the holiday will be observed on Friday. If the holiday occurs on Sunday the holiday will be observed on Monday.

1.8 Hours of Operation. The contractor shall conduct business between the hours of 6:00am and 6:00pm, Monday - Friday except for federal holidays or when the Government facility is closed due to local or national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar Government directed facility closings. The contractor must at all times maintain an adequate workforce for the uninterrupted performance of all tasks defined within this PWS when the Government facility is not closed for any of the above reasons. Production Support personnel are required 24/7 to perform operations and help desk support.

1.8.1 Extended/Emergency Hours. When mission needs dictate, contractor staff shall be available to support the work described within this PWS outside of standard facility duty hours, including nights and weekends. The Contracting Officer Representative (COR), Contracting Officer (CO), or management will provide reasonable advance notice for such requirements. Except in cases of a bona fide emergency, "reasonable notice" is defined as a minimum of 48 hours. For emergency situations, the COR, CO, or management will provide notice as soon as is practicable, and the contractor shall be required to respond accordingly.

1.9 Place of Performance. The work will be performed at the DFAS Indianapolis Center or at other locations agreed to by the COR or Contracting Officer and the contractor. Travel may be required to CONUS locations to support DCPS customers. CONUS sites are predominantly military bases or other Government installations. See paragraph 1.24 for further travel information.

	1.9.1 Remote Location. The contractor may be authorized to work from a remote location when it’s advantageous to the DFAS mission. This must be coordinated with and approved by the COR.

1.10 Security and Privacy Act. All work performed relative to the requirement identified in the Performance Work Statement is unclassified and requires access to sensitive information, covered by the Privacy Act of 1974 and other DoW/DoD and DFAS regulations.

1.11 Security Requirements.

(a) General Requirements. Contractor personnel must meet the following conditions of employment.

Must be a U.S Citizen or National.

Registered for Selective Service (males born after 12-31-1959). A Status Information Letter is required for any male born after 12-31-1959 that is not registered with Selective Service.

This is a national security position which requires a favorable fitness review and background investigation as a condition of employment. Failure to maintain security eligibility may result in termination.

(b) Personnel Security Investigation (PSI) Requirements. Contractor personnel working on this contract will require a favorably adjudicated Tier 3, or equivalent Noncritical-Sensitive (formerly IT-II) or higher-level Investigation granting National Security eligibility. Contractor personnel must also have current enrollment (within 5 years) in the Continuous Vetting program, in accordance with Trusted Workforce 2.0 standards. No access to classified information is required. In accordance with standard DFAS Personnel Security policy, ALL incoming contractors must submit a new set of fingerprints (taken within the last 30 days) *. 

Contractor personnel must apply for a fingerprint appointment immediately (the next business day) upon award date. 

Contractor personnel shall submit the Contractor Request for Investigation (CRI) (DFAS Form 9035) immediately (the next business day after providing fingerprints) to the Contracting Officer Representative (COR). The information needed in the Declaration for Federal Employment (OF-306) also be submitted to the COR by contractor personnel. 

The COR will submit the OF-306, DFAS Form 9035, and proof of fingerprints to DFAS Personnel Security all at once. Under no circumstances should this documentation be submitted less than fifteen (15) calendar days prior to the intended performance start date. DFAS Personnel Security will review all submitted documentation to validate whether contractor personnel meet personnel security requirements to perform work on the contract or if a new background investigation is required.

Contractors obtaining favorable security evaluations and DoW/DoD CACs for required contractor employees performing on this contract are a prerequisite for contractor performance and invoicing. Also, the failure of a contractor to provide employees who can obtain a favorable security adjudication and a DoW/DoD CAC in a timely manner may be considered negatively when assessing contractor performance, termination, or other.

The Department of Veterans Human Resource Service Delivery (HRSD) Software as a Solution (SaaS)

Introduction

This RFI is for planning purposes only and shall not be considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation or a Request for Proposal.  Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI.  Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to consider.  You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI.  This request does not constitute a solicitation for proposals or the authority to enter into negotiations to award a contract.  No funds have been authorized, appropriated or received for this effort.  Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response.  The Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this RFI.

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 541519.  

Please reference previous RFI 36C10B26Q0193.

2. Submittal Information:

All responsible sources may submit a response in accordance with the below information.  

There is a page limitation for this RFI of 10 pages.  The Government will not review any other information or attachments included in excess of the 10-page limit. NO MARKETING MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED AS PART OF THIS RFI.  Generic capability statements will not be accepted or reviewed.  Your response must include the following:

Name of Company

Address

Point of Contact

Phone Number

Fax Number

Email address

Company Business Size and Status

For VOSB and SDVOSBs, proof of verification in VetCert.	

NAICS code(s)

Socioeconomic data

Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) Number or Unique Entity ID 

Existing Contractual Vehicles (GWAC, FSS, or MAC)

Provide a summary of your capability to meet the requirements and questions described in section c

Your company’s intent and ability to meet the set aside requirement in accordance with VAAR 852.219-73 VA Notice of Total Set-Aside for Verified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses and 13 CFR §125.6, which states the contractor will not pay more than 50 percent of the amount paid by the Government to it to firms that are not SDVOSBs. 

VAAR 852.219-73 VA Notice of Total Set-Aside is being provided in this Request for Information for market research purposes only at this time. This RFI is posted as full and open to allow all industry to respond and help create the acquisition strategy. 

1. COTS SaaS HRSD Solution 

Is your solution a commercially available, out-of-the-box Human Resource Service Delivery Software as a Service (SaaS) platform that is Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP)-certified at a moderate level or above? 

Does your solution require no more than 30% configuration? 

Please provide the name of your solution and confirm that it is a certified SaaS, not merely a PaaS (Platform as a Service). 

Clarify the distinction between configuration and customization in relation to your SaaS offering?

Does your product have its own VA Authority to Operate (ATO)?

2. HR Service Delivery Modules

Does your solution provide talent acquisition, onboarding/offboarding, HR Forms, HR helpdesk and Generative AI enabled & integrated virtual agents for government organizations?

3. Scalability and Performance

Can your solution support scalability and performance for a user base exceeding 400,000 users? 

4. Integration Capabilities

Can your solution integrate seamlessly with multiple interfaces, including VA’s existing core personnel HR Smart system and other necessary systems to ensure interoperability?

5. Low Code Solutions

Does your solution provide VA staff with the ability to develop, manage and deploy low code and AI products?

6. Data Capabilities

Does your solution provide timely (refreshed and available for reporting once every 24 hours) access to large data sets for VA consumption and reports?

7. License Pricing

Provide your pricing model for enterprise solutions with over 400,000 licenses, including any tiered or volume-based pricing options and a rough order of magnitude for the solution and implementation.

Include details on how pricing may scale based on enterprise needs, such as additional users, modules, or features. 

Explain how prices will change if migrated to VA hosted environments.

Please note “HRSD (location of responding (SEWP, GSA, SAMs))” in the subject line of your response.  Mark your response as “Proprietary Information” if the information is considered business sensitive.  The email file size shall not exceed 5 MB.

The Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) invites small businesses 
to submit research proposals under this Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) 
and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) solicitation. All eligible organizations 
with relevant expertise are encouraged to apply (See section 2 for eligibility 
requirements). The topics are described in Section 8 Research Topics, and new topics 
may be added periodically. 
The mission of ARPA-H is to accelerate better health outcomes by supporting the 
development of high-impact solutions to society’s most challenging health problems. 
Innovative small businesses can contribute to this mission through the ARPA-H Small 
Business Program (SBP). ARPA-H holds small business performers to the same 
rigorous technical standards as other ARPA-H performers. Commercialization and 
transition are key elements of the ARPA-H SBP, and ARPA-H provides tailored support 
to help performers overcome a range of challenges. 
This solicitation contains specific topic areas where ARPA-H is seeking proposals from 
small businesses for high-impact solutions. Proposals are expected to use novel 
approaches to achieve revolutionary advances in science, technology, or systems. 
Specifically excluded are proposals for open-ended research projects or that 
represent an incremental advance in the current state of the art. Additionally, 
proposals directed towards policy changes, traditional education and training, or 
construction of physical infrastructure are outside the scope of the ARPA-H mission 
and will not be considered. 
 
 
SHORTCUT TO TECHNICAL TOPICS 
 
  

 
 5 
1.1 Program Phases 
The SBIR/STTR program organizes projects into three phases: 
• Phase I: Feasibility 
• Phase II: Full Research / Research & Development (R&D) Effort 
• Phase III: Commercialization (Not part of this solicitation) 
These phases build on each other, with each subsequent phase the maturity of the 
technology should advance so that the ﬁnal output is ready for commercialization. 
Once a performer has successfully completed a Phase I, ARPA-H (or any other 
agency) can invite them to submit a Phase II proposal to continue development. 
Note: This solicitation does not accept Phase III proposals. 
1.1.1 Phase I: Feasibility 
The objective of Phase I is to determine the scientiﬁc or technical and commercial 
feasibility of the proposed solution. Typically, a Phase I proposer has a solution 
concept but has not yet built a prototype to test technical feasibility.  
This phase is intended to de-risk the effort and is substantially smaller in scope and 
cost than subsequent phases. At ARPA-H, a typical Phase I lasts 6-12 months but may 
last longer in rare circumstances. The result of a Phase I is a proof-of-concept or early-
stage prototype. 
NOTE: Performers with a Phase I award from ARPA-H may submit a Phase II proposal 
to ARPA-H to continue the development of their technology. This usually occurs in the 
last quarter of the period of performance or shortly after contract completion. The 
performer should notify the ARPA-H SBP of their intention to submit a proposal, and 
ARPA-H will provide submission instructions. While all Phase I participants are 
welcome to submit a Phase II proposal, not all will be selected for a Phase II award. 
ARPA-H may also invite performers to submit a Phase II proposal outside of specified 
solicitation timeframes. 
1.1.2 Phase II: Full Research/Research & Development (R&D) Effort 
The objective of Phase II is to further develop a technology or R&D effort initiated in 
Phase I. During Phase II, performers advance from a proof-of-concept into a 
commercially viable prototype. Phase II awards are larger in scope and cost than 
Phase I efforts and typically last 12-24 months, although they can be longer or shorter. 
Individual topics may include estimates regarding the anticipated project duration 
which are meant to guide proposers rather than be hard requirements. 
While the speciﬁc Phase II activities in a project are case-speciﬁc, they usually include 
continued improvement of the technology along with evidence generation. This may 

 
 6 
include completing pre-clinical work, conducting enabling studies for an 
Investigational New Drug (IND), or even ﬁrst-in-human trials. At ARPA-H, it is common 
for a Phase II to conclude with an FDA submission (when applicable). 
Additional emphasis is placed on commercialization during Phase II. Performers must 
submit a detailed Commercialization Plan and provide regular updates. This is a key 
activity of Phase II efforts at ARPA-H and necessary to prepare for a successful 
transition. During Phase II, performers often develop or initiate strategic partnerships, 
manufacturing plans, regulatory engagements, go-to-market strategies, and user-
testing (these examples are meant to be illustrative rather than exhaustive or 
prescriptive).   
A Phase II may be awarded as (a) a follow-on to a Phase I award, (b) a Direct-to-Phase 
II, or (c) integrated into a Fast Track project.

STATEMENT OF WORK/PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT
United States Naval Academy - Information Technology Services Division
1. Background.
The United States Naval Academy (USNA) Information Technology Services Division (ITSD) is responsible for developing, managing and 
integrating information systems and providing information technology products, services and capabilities for approximately 7,000 midshipmen, 
faculty and staff across the academy's 630 acre campus and for the approximately 300 midshipmen candidates, faculty and staff at the Naval Academy 
Preparatory School (NAPS) located in Newport R.I.
The ITSD Finance Department is responsible for all information technology (IT) and other major equipment including integrated planning, 
programming, budgeting, procurement, licensing, receipt, payment, accounting, maintenance, support, and inventory management of all hardware and 
software and associated services in conjunction with other educational support equipment to meet documented organizational needs. It is responsible 
for maintaining liaison with external entities including tenant commands and oversight authorities and
managing special enterprise projects by representing USNA IT interests and coordinating execution across multiple internal and external entities 
including but not limited to GSA/WITS,
NAVSUP/FLC, NAVFAC/PWD, CINC/NSAA, USNA Architect and commercial vendors. The Finance Department also provides general business 
support including travel, training, payroll,
supply, and similar services.
2. Objectives.
The objective of this task is for the USNA to renew the licensing and maintenance for the Momentus venue and event management software (f/k/a 
Ungerboeck) that has been supporting this business process for over 5 years. This system supports the USNA venue managers across the yard that 
maintain the schedules for over 300 spaces available for
being reserved for academic, athletic, religious, or any other type of public or private events. It allows for end-users to request venue reservations 
through a self-service portal, coaches and athletics staff to reserve fields and courts on a recurring basis for team practices, and venue managers to 
coordinate, approve, and deconflict the schedules of the venues that they have under their Management.
3. Scope of Services
The Vendor will provide the following services for the renewal period of Base year PoP is 01 May 2026 - 30 APR 2027
Software Upgrades, Security Patches & Maintenance:
Delivery and implementation of all available software upgrades and security patches throughout the 
renewal period on manual schedule until such time as USNA can align
with wave format of upgrade scheduling.
Ensuring the software remains current and secure against known vulnerabilities.
Notification to the Client of any critical updates or security patches requiring immediate
action.
Software Access:
The software that USNA currently uses has been repackaged into Momentus Enterprise Core Software. USNA must retain all current features as part 
of this new packaging to include:
Continued access to the Momentus platform (110 & OSB) for all authorized users throughout the renewal 
period.
Maintenance of software functionality and availability.

Questions and Answers for Master Breacher Course Support 
Solicitation Number: W9124M26QA006 
Document Page # & Para # Question Gov Response 
Solicitation Pg 57, Para 2.4 (Past 
Performance) 
Please clarify whether Past Performance will be evaluated at the company level, 
individual instructor/personnel level, or a combination of both. If both, what 
weighting or consideration is given to each? 
Past performance will be evaluated at the company level. The 
weight will be seen as either acceptable or unacceptable. 
Company’s with no past performance will not be negatively 
affected and seen as acceptable. 
Solicitation Pg 57, Para 2 (Evaluation 
Factors) 
The solicitation states award will be based on price and other factors; however, it 
also states quotes will be evaluated for technical acceptability and not ranked. 
Please confirm whether this procurement is Lowest Price Technically Acceptable 
(LPTA) or a Best Value Tradeoff. 
Award will be made based on price and other non-price factors. 
Meaning award will be made to the offeror with the lowest price 
who receives an acceptable rating in all other non-price factors. 
Solicitation Pg 57, Para 2 (Evaluation 
Factors) 
Please confirm whether the evaluation factors listed (Technical, Mission Capability,  
Price, Past Performance) are listed in descending order of importance , or if all non -
price factors are evaluated on a pass/fail basis only. 
Pass/Fail 
Solicitation Pg 54, Addendum to 
52.212-1 
The solicitation does not specify proposal format, volumes, or page limitations. 
Please confirm if there are any page limits, formatting requirements, or volume 
structure expectations for submission. 
There are no specified limitations for submissions. 
Solicitation Section B (Pricing) 
Please confirm whether pricing should be structured as cost per course, monthly 
support, or strictly by CLIN as written, and whether offerors may provide supporting 
pricing narratives. 
CLIN as written 
Solicitation General Please provide incumbent contractor name, contract number, and current contract 
value. 
Rampdown Works LLC, one course, $210,000 
Solicitation General Please provide the current number of personnel (manning) supporting this 
requirement, including labor categories and approximate hours. 
Current contractor proprietary information. 
Solicitation General Please confirm whether the Government will provide any historical pricing or IGCE 
range for this requirement. 
$210,000 for one off course 
PWS Para 1.5.7 (Place of 
Performance) 
Please confirm whether all training and support activities are conducted at Fort 
Benning, GA, or if there are any off-site or travel requirements. 
 All training will be completed on ft. Benning but spread across 5 
or more ranges 
PWS Para 1.5.5–1.5.6 
(Operating Hours) 
Please clarify the expected number of courses per year and whether this varies 
annually. 
 3 annual courses with the possibility to conduct a 4th course. The 
4th course POI would differ slightly and an amended PWS would be 
submitted for the 4th course specifically.  
PWS Para 1.5.5–1.5.6 Please provide the annual training schedule (or most recent schedule) including 
number of courses, duration, and typical spacing between courses. 
 Training schedules will not be the same annually and may adjust 
within the government’s Fiscal Year due to other requirements. 
Training calendars are not shareable due to their classification 
levels.  
PWS General Please provide a current course curriculum or syllabus for the Ranger Master 
Breacher Course to better understand scope and level of effort. 
Course material and curriculum are not shareable due to TTPs and 
techniques associated with the sensitivity of the training.   

 
2 
 
 
 
PWS Attachment D (Estimated 
Workload Data) 
The estimated workload data lists labor hours by category. Please confirm if these 
hours represent the annual expected workload and whether they align with the 
anticipated number of courses. 
The estimated workload was part of independent government 
estimate and was used for estimated pricing based on historical data 
only. 
 
PWS 
 
Para 1.10 (Key Personnel) 
Please confirm whether key personnel roles (Contract Manager, Quality Control 
Manager, Systems Administrator) are expected to be full-time, part-time, or 
collateral duties. 
They are expected to meet their expectations, its up to the contactor 
if that requires full time, part time or collateral. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
Document Page # & Para # Question Gov Response 
PWS Para 1.6 (Security 
Requirements) 
Please confirm whether personnel must possess a Secret clearance at time of award, 
or if clearance sponsorship/processing is acceptable post-award. 
 No, secret clearance is not required at the time of award. Secret 
Clearance will only be required if/when the 75RR requests the 
necessity based off future needs of the course or material.  
PWS Para 1.5.1 (Quality 
Control Plan) 
Please confirm that the Quality Control Plan (QCP) is not required at proposal 
submission and is only required after award. 
Required prior to start of work. Not required at time of proposal 
submission. 
 
PWS 
 
General Please clarify what materials and equipment are Government-furnished versus 
contractor-provided (e.g., target materials, tools, vehicles, disposal). 
No Government Furnished equipment  
PWS General Please confirm whether the Government provides storage space, staging areas, or 
facilities for materials and equipment between courses. 
Government will not provide permanent storage.  
PWS General Please clarify expectations for surge or additional courses beyond the baseline (e.g., 
optional courses, funding triggers). 
Yes, there should be an expectation that additional training or 
courses will continue past the RMBC baseline contract.  
Understand a new PWS may need to be created to cover any major 
or minor adjustments.  
Solicitation General Please confirm whether discussions are anticipated, or if award will be made based 
on initial quotes without exchanges. 
No discussions are anticipated. 
Solicitation General Please confirm if multiple awards are anticipated or if this is a single-award contract. Single award.

Heavy wood doors  
Light metal doors  
Heavy Metal doors 
Heavy wood - preferably non press board or particle core, Solid 
wood door 
 
Light metal - Exterior Residential door (preferably nonflammable 
insulation) 
 
Heavy metal - industrial exterior metal doors

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT
1. SPECIFICATION:
1.1. This requirement is in support of the USS BLUE RIDGE (LCC-19), which requires Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM)-authorized 
Technician(s) to provide system programming, testing, and maintenance of the Government furnished and installed King Fisher Temporary Fire 
Detection system. This assistance includes visual and operational inspection of the Government installed Fire Detection Systems. After installation 
Contractor must provide a detailed installation diagram and training on alarm conditions and how to interpret them to U.S. Naval Ship Repair Facility 
and Japan Regional Maintenance Center (SRF-JRMC) Yokosuka Fire Safety Council Representative (FSC) and The Ship Force Watch Standers.
1.2. Technician must be on-site during installation phase and available to provide distance support and occasional "as needed" onsite support during 
normal and evening working hours to facilitate Fire Detection System component monitoring, each modification, and each repair to support work 
upon request from the FSC at SRF-JRMC Yokosuka.
1.3. OEM to provide support from the Japan based technician to accommodate the periodic and sporadic need for Temporary Fire Detection support 
to SRF-JRMC Yokosuka.
2. REFERENCES:
2.1. NAVSEA Technical Manual S0570-AC-CCM-010/8010 Industrial Ship Safety Manual for Fire Prevention and Response
3. ENCLOSURES:
3.1. None.
4. GENERAL SCOPE OF WORK:
4.1. The Contractor will provide OEM-authorized Technical Representative(s) and equipment to provide system programming, testing, maintenance 
of the Government installed King Fisher temporary detection system in accordance with Reference 2.1.
4.1.1. The Contractor must accomplish the requirements of paragraph 4, for up to a total of 335 EA Temporary Fire Detector and associated 
equipment, to include equipment installation and removal assistance "as needed" by SRF-JRMC.
4.1.2. The Contractor must accomplish the requirements of paragraph 4, for up to a total of 35 EA Temporary Flood Sensors and associated 
equipment, to include equipment installation and removal assistance when directed by the SUPERVISOR.
4.1.3. Activation of a temporary detector must be indicated on the centrally manned control panel at Central Control Station (CCS)/Damage Control 
Central (DCC) and the remotely located annunciator panel at either the ship's primary Quarterdeck or the secondary Quarterdeck. An alarm specific 
space location must be provided by the Contractor and available on the control panel and annunciator panel to enable the Ship's watch stander to 
quickly identify which space the alarm was activated in. This will facilitate immediate dispatching of Ship fire response personnel to the affected 
space.
4.1.4. The Contractor must provide an Alarm indicator index or similar to satisfy paragraph 4.1.2. Index must be provided at each control panel and 
annunciator immediately after satisfactory completion of installation programming and testing. Provide electronic copy of the Alarm indicator index 
to the SRF-JRMC FSC. This document must be updated immediately after each new detector is installed under paragraph 4.1.1.
4.2. SYSTEM INSPECTION: The Contractor must inspect each installed system component, including each independent back-up power supply, to 
ensure proper function and operation with SRF-JRMC Yokosuka Shop 99 representatives.
4.2.1. The contractor must provide bi-monthly (two-week interval) inspections of the installed temporary system.
4.2.2. The contractor must verify functionality of each equipment component used to replace each defective equipment component.
4.2.3. The Contractor must repair each nonfunctional part as needed to maintain functionality. The Contractor must notify SRF-JRMC Yokosuka 
Shop 99 of each equipment component requiring replacement. SRF-JRMC Yokosuka Shop 99 will install each replaced equipment component. The 
Contractor must provide a report of each defective equipment component requiring immediate replacement, and each equipment component that may 
require replacement in the future.
4.2.4. The contractor must provide a report of each defective equipment component replaced and/or repaired. This report should include each 
equipment component that may require future replacement and/or repair.
4.2.5. The contractor must provide onsite or remote technical assistance troubleshooting each fire detection system fault within 24 hours from 
notification by the Government. The expected duration of this assistance when exercised is three (3) days. The government may exercise this option 
up to 12 times during the period of performance.
5. ISSUES AND CONDITION REPORTING:
5.1. The Contractor must bring their own tools to support 4.1 and 4.2.

5.2. The Contractor must provide the following training:
5.2.1. Provide One each training session on temporary fire detection system functionality and fault identification for approximately 12 each Ship's 
Force personnel in the following electronic/electrical ratings (GSE/EM, ET/IC). These personnel will be responsible for providing notification to the 
Project Team within 10 minutes on each system fault that cannot be reset during and outside of normal working hours.
5.2.2. Provide One each training session for 9 each SRF-JRMC Fire Safety Officers, 2 each Project Supervisors, and approximately 10 each Zone 
Managers/Work Integration Managers on temporary fire detection system installation and operation.
5.2.3. Provide training session for approximately 90 Ship's Force personnel qualified as Command Duty Officer, Engineering Duty Officer, Officer of 
the Deck, Central Control Station Supervisor, Fire Safety Watch and Sounding & Security on temporary fire detection system functionality and 
operation. Training may be held in between One each and 3 each session depending on mission requirements.
5.2.4. Contractor must provide electronic media of the training material provided to meet paragraph 5.2.1 through 5.2.3 for reference material.

6.4. Option 3 Period of Performance: 03 FEB 2028 - 16 FEB 2028 (14 days)

7.1. The Government will furnish and install each King Fisher Fire Detection System component, and each required replacement component. 
Computer and other computer accessories are not provided under this contract.
8. GOVERNMENT SUPPORT:
8.1. If the Contractor requires additional support, this support must be requested through Project Sup. This request does not constitute approval.
9. CONTRACTOR FURNISHED PROPERTY/MATERIALS:
9.1. Contractor must provide all tools, equipment, and material need to complete the contract requirements of this PWS.
10. ESTIMATED WORK HOURS:
10.1. Normally, all work is performed between the hours of 8:00am and 4:45pm Monday through Saturday.

Spaceport and Launch Assessment Study (SPLAS) 
Statement of Work (SOW)   
Page 1 of 7 
 
DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT C. Distribution authorized to U.S. Government  
agencies and their contractors To protect and limit distribution in accordance with the 
desires of and agreements with the foreign government that furnished the technical 
information. 
 
Assigned pursuant to Chapter 15 of Title 50, U.S.C.(Reference (v)) and Executive Order 
13526 (Reference (w))(date of determination). Other requests for this document shall be 
referred to (USSF , PAW, Space Access).  
 
1. Introduction 
This Statement of Work (SOW) outlines the requirements for a Technical Services Case 
between Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) for Space Access (SA) and a Partner Nation 
(PN) to support the establishment of a PN National Security Space Launch (NSSL) 
capability at a sovereign spaceport, utilizing a Commercial Launch Vehicle (CLV) . This 
SOW is based on the signed Letter of Request (LOR) for Letter of OƯer and Acceptance 
(LOA) between the USG and the PN. 
 
2. Project Objectives 
The objective of this Technical Services Case is to provide the PN with the necessary 
engineering, logistical, and technical assistance to successfully establish an NSSL service 
from a sovereign spaceport utilizing a US commercial launch vehicle (CLV), with a priority 
focus on tailoring USSF best practices for National Security launch operations and mission 
assurance from the spaceport. This includes: 
• Developing a familiarization with the launch vehicle capability and support systems 
• Tailoring US Space Force spaceport development and operations best practices, for 
launch of national payloads from the spaceport to the PN context 
• Identifying potential mission risks and mitigation strategies associated with using the 
CLV for PN NSSL 
• Providing technical documentation and support to enable PN to eƯectively monitor 
and control the CLV launch pad as it relates to PN NSSL service 
• Assessing the requirements and interfaces of the CLV launch system and the 
spaceport 
• Providing launch mission assurance assessment expertise 
 
  

Spaceport and Launch Assessment Study (SPLAS) 
Statement of Work (SOW)   
Page 2 of 7 
 
3. Scope of Work 
3.1  Commercial Launch Service Provider Familiarization: Assess launch vehicle 
capability to meet the mission requirements of PN National Security Space Launch 
using U.S. Space Force evaluation criteria (tailored as needed). This assessment may 
be accomplished through a combination of site and facility visits and document review, 
and shall include: 
o Vehicle capability overview 
o Assessment of the launch service provider’s (LSP) mission execution processes 
and procedures (including but not limited to: manufacturing, vehicle mating, pad 
roll-out, pre-launch, launch,) 
o Ability to accommodate PN national security satellites and meet mass and orbit 
performance requirements 
o Identiﬁcation of technical, cost, and schedule risks 
Deliverable (CDRL A01): General Launch Vehicle familiarization  
3.2  Assessment of Spaceport Operator’s plan to support NSSL: Conduct site surveys at 
spaceport facilities that will support operation of CLV at the spaceport and summarize 
ﬁndings. Assess the spaceport and spaceport operator’s ability to meet the mission 
requirements of the PN National Security Space Launch through use of CLV using U.S. 
Space Force evaluation criteria (tailored as needed). This includes: 
o Ability of payload processing facilities to accommodate PN satellites  
o Identiﬁcation of technical, cost, and schedule risks 
o Assessment of spaceport ability to meet physical and cyber security requirements 
o Identiﬁcation of additional requirements that need to be leveraged on the 
spaceport operator and the CLV launch complex for NSSL that do not apply to 
commercial launch 
The report should include a detailed assessment of the following: 
Launch Site Systems: Assess launch site systems including CLV launch complex sensors, 
interfaces, and infrastructure, spaceport infrastructure, payload processing facilities,  
ground support equipment, sensors, Telemetry, Tracking, and Control (TT&C) systems (this 
may include, but not limited to, launch vehicle telemetry collection, ﬂight safety control (if 
autonomous ﬂight safety is not used), and space vehicle separation (if required)), and 
ground handling processes and procedures to determine whether all equipment meets 
requirements, are capable of being certiﬁed, and have proper interfaces. The assessment 
should also consider launch vehicle and expected space vehicle commodity requirements 
such as liquid nitrogen, hydrazine, kerosene, liquid oxygen, etc. Report will include 

Spaceport and Launch Assessment Study (SPLAS) 
Statement of Work (SOW)   
Page 3 of 7 
 
recommendations of additional sensors or equipment requirements that apply to NSSL 
operations. 
Deliverable:  Spaceport assessment and NSSL requirements documents (CDRL 
A02)   
 
3.3  National Security Launch Requirements:  Work with PN to understand their 
objectives and risk tolerance for National Security Space assets. Based on this 
understanding, and the capability of the launch provider and their launch solution, provide 
general technical assistance and support in deﬁning requirements, and recommend and 
prioritize requirements to ensure the launch solution will meet PN’s mission objectives. 
Recommend a mission assurance approach, such as accepting a launch provider’s 
baseline system and responding to mission unique requirements as needed, or other 
solutions. 
The report should include the following: 
Launch Site Speciﬁcations: requirements based on general CLV launch vehicle 
speciﬁcations to be imposed on the spaceport operator for use of CLV for NSS 
operations. The document shall include NSSL mission assurance requirements for 
the CLV launch complex that may be more stringent than the commercial 
requirements for commercial payload launches. 
Launch Readiness Veriﬁcation (LRV) Process: Develop an LRV process for use 
of CLV , based on USSF mission assurance processes tailored to PN requirements 
to ensure CLV and launch complex systems are capable of achieving PN NSSL 
mission success when operating from the spaceport. 
Test, Evaluation, and System Safety Assessment: Assess spaceport operator’s 
approach to ground and ﬂight safety requirements that meets PN’s launch 
licensing authority requirements and recommend areas for tailoring to reduce 
new/additional qualiﬁcation. This may include identiﬁcation of the U.S. 
Government / U.S. Space Force test, evaluation, and system safety 
documentation that would be applicable to CLV and spaceport operator’s launch 
operations at the spaceport. This may also include recommending tailored 
approaches to said documents. 
Deliverable: National Security Launch Requirements (CDRL A03) 
3.4   Suggested Training: Assess spaceport operator and PN personnel current 
knowledge base and suggest courses for personnel to participate in to gain a better 
understanding space launch operations, safety, mission assurance, regulations, and other 
mission areas as applicable based on their desired level of competence.  This shall be 
assessed through discussions with relevant PN and PAE/SA personnel. 

Spaceport and Launch Assessment Study (SPLAS) 
Statement of Work (SOW)   
Page 4 of 7 
 
Deliverable: List of recommended education & training (CDRL A04) 
 
3.5  Comprehensive Analysis and Recommendations:  At the conclusion of the study 
or period of performance, deliver a consolidated report and brieﬁng with a summary of all 
assessments and recommendations for PN to successfully establish a National Security 
Launch capability using the CLV at the PN spaceport.  This report shall include elements 
of the previously outlined deliverables as well as recommendations for further studies as 
needed to address any identiﬁed gaps in capability. 
Deliverable: Comprehensive National Security Launch Assessment and 
Recommendations Report and Brieﬁng (CDRL A05) 
 
3.6  Technical Interchange Meetings (TIMs): Conduct Technical Interchange Meetings 
(TIMs), planning conferences, review meetings, and other relevant meetings and deliver 
meeting agendas, minutes, and action items for each exchange with the partner, 
spaceport operator, and launch service provider. Target is 12 meetings per year, with 2 in-
person and 10 virtual with PN and spaceport operator.  Additional progress review and 
kickoƯ/closeout meetings with the PAE/SA case team will be required with at least 2 in-
person.  Each virtual engagement will be scheduled not later than 7 calendar days in 
advance, with each engagement not being more than 8 hours in length.  The contractor 
shall provide read ahead materials not less than 24 hours prior to each engagement and 
publish action items not more than 24 hours after each engagement.  In-person 
engagements will be held at a Government or contractor facility most advantageous to the 
study team. OCONUS in-person meetings shall be scheduled not less than 1 calendar 
month in advance to allow suƯicient time for USG personnel to process international 
travel request documentation. 
Deliverable: Meeting Agendas, Meeting invitations, Minutes and Action Items 
(CDRL A06)

Statement of Work (SOW)
