1 
STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
Scientific Evidence Evaluation and Knowledge Integration for 
Translational Toxicology 
 
April 13, 2026 
1 General Information 
1.1 General 
This is a non-personal service(s) contract under which the personnel rendering the service(s) 
are not subject, either by the contract’s terms or by the manner of its administration, to the 
supervision and control usually prevailing in relationships between the Government and its 
employees. The purpose of this contract is to provide all services and supplies necessary to 
conduct scientific evidence evaluation and knowledge integration for translational toxicology in 
support of the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), Division of 
Translational Toxicology (DTT).  
1.2 
Description of Services 
Independently, and not as an agent of the Government, the Contractor shall furnish all the 
necessary services, qualified personnel, procedures, materials, equipment, and facilities not 
otherwise provided by the Government as needed to perform the objectives set forth below. In 
general, activities shall be conducted according to the requirements described in a research 
outline (see Section 3.1), which includes project-specific activities, milestones, and deliverables. 
1.3 Background and Scope 
DTT is an intramural division of NIEHS, National Institutes of Health, that uses traditional and 
cutting-edge research approaches to better understand how factors in our environment may 
impact human health. Such approaches include using scientific expertise to identify, collect, 
analyze, and interpret diverse types of information relevant to the effects of environmental 
exposures on human health. Information from the fields of toxicology, epidemiology, chemistry, 
data science, informatics, pathology, and other disciplines is used in the design of research 
programs; in literature-based health assessments; and in the development of novel tools and 
informatics approaches.  
The objective of this contract is to provide scientific and technical expertise and support for 
scientific evidence evaluation and knowledge integration for translational toxicology related to 
the evaluation and reporting of effects of environmental substances and other issues that may 
impact public health. Nine specific requirement areas under this contract to support DTT within 
NIEHS include: (1) systematic evidence mapping and scoping reviews of environmental health 
literature, (2) systematic review and evidence synthesis, (3) report development and scientific 
writing, (4) document preparation and publication, (5) coordination and management of 
external peer review, (6) logistical management for advisory group meetings and workshops, 
(7) provision of scientific or technical consultants with expertise in relevant scientific disciplines, 
(8) development and implementation of novel tools and informatics approaches, and (9) 

   
 
 2 
program management. These requirement areas are managed by several offices and branches 
within DTT. Additional information about the DTT organizational structure is available on the 
NIEHS website. 
The National Toxicology Program (NTP) is an interagency partnership comprised of NIEHS (part 
of the National Institutes of Health), the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health 
(NIOSH; part of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention), and the U.S. Food and Drug 
Administration (FDA; primarily at the National Center for Toxicological Research). NTP is 
headquartered administratively at NIEHS, and many of the activities performed under this 
contract will support NTP projects and research programs. 
The activities carried out by this contract will address the aforementioned requirements for 
scientific evidence evaluation and knowledge integration for translational toxicology. 
1.4 Overview of Required Capabilities 
The Contractor shall conduct activities supported by the following Capability Areas described in 
more detail in Section 2 – Required Capability Areas:  
• Systematic Evidence Mapping and Scoping Reviews of Environmental Health 
Literature 
• Systematic Review and Evidence Synthesis 
• Report Development and Scientific Writing 
• Document Preparation and Publication 
• Coordination and Management of External Peer Review 
• Logistical Management for Advisory Group Meetings and Workshops 
• Provision of Scientific or Technical Consultants with Expertise in Relevant Scientific 
Disciplines  
• Development and Implementation of Novel Tools and Informatics Approaches 
• Program Management 
1.5 Policies and Procedures 
For scientific evidence evaluation and knowledge integration for translational toxicology, the 
Contractor and applicable subcontractor(s) shall comply with the below guidelines: 
a. Handbook for Conducting Systematic Reviews for Health Effects Evaluations 
• Available at: https://ntp.niehs.nih.gov/go/ohathandbook.  
b. Handbook for Preparing Report on Carcinogens Monographs 
• Available at: https://ntp.niehs.nih.gov/go/rochandbook.  
1.6 Reports and Deliverables 
Information on specific reporting requirements is presented below. All deliverables shall be 
electronic and PC and MAC compatible unless otherwise specified by the Contracting Officer’s 
Representative (COR). Each final document or report shall be submitted electronically in MS 
Word and/or PDF formats to the COR for review. Unless otherwise directed, all submitted final 
electronic deliverables shall be compliant with Section 508 regarding accessibility (see Section 
1.6.4). In some cases, there may be accommodations for which the Government will provide 
information annually. Unless otherwise instructed, all reports submitted under this contract 

   
 
 3 
shall reference the contract number, the title and type of report, and the submission date on 
the first page of the report. 
In addition to the reports mentioned herein, any incidence or unforeseeable occurrence not 
listed here, including personnel changes which may impact activities under the contract, shall 
be immediately reported to the Government. 
DELIVERABLE  REFERENCE  DUE/FREQUENCY  SUBMIT TO  
Quality Management 
Plan Section 1.6.1.1 Revise as needed or when major changes 
occur COR, CO, and CS 
Monthly  
Progress Report  Section 1.6.1.2 Due once per month  COR, CO, and CS 
Monthly Budget 
Summary Report Section 1.6.1.3 Due once per month as an attachment 
with the monthly invoices COR, CO, and CS 
Annual Report Section 1.6.1.4 Due 4 weeks from the last day of each 
contract year COR, CO, and CS 
COR = Contracting Officer’s Representative; CO = Contracting Officer; CS = Contract Specialist. 
 
1.6.1 Periodic Reports 
1.6.1.1 Quality Management Plan 
A Quality Management Plan (QMP) shall be submitted before performance of work under the 
contract and updated versions submitted at regular intervals (e.g., biannually). 
1.6.1.2 Monthly Progress Report 
Once per month, the COR shall receive a summary of the work currently in progress. This report 
shall include details on the status of all active work, current costs for active work, cumulative 
costs for the contract (including direct and administrative costs), any problems encountered, 
and remedial actions taken to resolve those problems. The monthly progress report shall also 
include a summary of the work performed by any subcontractor and/or ad hoc consultant, 
including their deliverables, hours spent, and cost. This summary shall also include a description 
of how the subcontractor/consultant work aided the Contractor in completing or nearing 
completion of a specific project. 
1.6.1.3 Monthly Budget Summary Report 
A summary report shall be submitted monthly that includes budget information for each 
activity separately undertaken and for the contract as a whole. The report must include each 
activity’s budget, total expenditures on the activity for the month, summaries of current 
contract year and cumulative expenditures, and projected expenses to complete each activity. 
Budget summary reports shall be submitted monthly to the COR as MS Excel spreadsheets (or 
in other spreadsheet software by agreement) and shall be sortable as required by the COR. 
Budget summary reports shall be included as an attachment with the monthly invoices. 

   
 
 4 
1.6.1.4 Annual Report 
An annual report shall be submitted within 4 weeks of the last day of each contract year. Each 
annual report shall detail all significant outcomes resulting from the requirements as described 
within the SOW and contract, including a breakdown of costs by research activity incurred to 
date, any problems encountered and remedial actions taken to resolve the problem, and any 
deviations from the SOW and/or contract. 
1.6.2 Research Products 
For each activity performed under the contract, research products shall be generated by the 
Contractor and submitted to the COR according to the milestones and deliverables schedule 
included in the research outline. The type and number of product(s) may vary depending on the 
nature of the activity.  
1.6.3 IT Security Plan and Other IT Deliverables 
Refer to Appendix A for specific requirements related to information technology (IT) security. 
1.6.4 HHS Section 508 and Accessibility Standards 
Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act, as amended by the Workforce Investment Act of 1998 
(P.L. 105-220) requires that when Federal agencies develop, procure, maintain, or use 
information and communication technology (ICT), it shall be accessible to people with 
disabilities. Federal employees and members of the public who have disabilities must have 
access to, and use of, information and data that is comparable to people without disabilities. 
All products, platforms and services delivered as part of this work statement that are ICT, or 
contain ICT, must conform to the Revised 508 Standards, which are located at 36 C.F.R. § 
1194.1 & Apps. A, B, & C, and available at https://www.access-board.gov/ict/. 
All requirements are applicable to support services and documentation deliverables. All 
functional performance criteria apply when using an alternative design or technology that 
achieves substantially equivalent or greater accessibility and usability by individuals with 
disabilities, than would be provided by conformance to one or more of the requirements in 
Chapters 4-6 of the Revised 508 Standards, or when Chapters 4-6 do not address one or more 
functions of ICT. 
For each proposed product or platform, a fully completed Accessibility Conformance Report 
(ACR) using the Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT) 
(https://www.itic.org/policy/accessibility/vpat) or HHS conformance checklist(s) 
(https://www.hhs.gov/web/section-508/accessibility-checklists/index.html) must be 
submitted. 
Prior to acceptance of deliverables, the offeror must demonstrate conformance to the HHS 
Section 508 requirements via HHS Section 508 checklist(s) (https://www.hhs.gov/web/section-
508/accessibility-checklists/index.html). The Government reserves the right to perform testing 
on required ICT items to validate the offeror’s Section 508 conformance claims. If the 
Government determines that Section 508 conformance does not meet the HHS Section 508 
requirements, the Government shall, at its option, require the offeror to remediate the item, at 
no additional cost to the Government, to align with the HHS Section 508 conformance 
requirements prior to acceptance. 

   
 
 5 
References: 
• Section 508 Standards: https://www.access-board.gov/ict/ 
• HHS Policy on Section 508 Compliance and Accessibility of Information and 
Communications Technology (ICT): https://www.hhs.gov/web/governance/digital-
strategy/it-policy-archive/hhs-policy-section-508-compliance-accessibility-information-
communications-technology.html 
• HHS Accessibility and Section 508 Conformance Checklists: 
https://www.hhs.gov/web/section-508/accessibility-checklists/index.html  
1.7 Post Award Conference/Periodic Progress Meetings 
The Contractor shall attend any post award conferences convened by the contracting activity or 
contract administration office in accordance with FAR Subpart 42.5. The Contracting Officer 
(CO), COR, and other Government personnel, as appropriate, may meet periodically with the 
Contractor to review the Contractor's performance. At these meetings the CO will apprise the 
Contractor of how the Government views the Contractor's performance and the Contractor 
shall apprise the Government of problems, if any, being experienced. Appropriate action shall 
be taken to resolve outstanding issues. These meetings shall be at no additional cost to the 
Government. 
1.7.1 Progress Meetings 
The Contractor shall attend, participate in, and furnish input to scheduled and unscheduled 
meetings, conferences, and briefings that relate to the functions and services herein as 
required by the Government to provide effective communication and impart necessary 
information. The Principal Investigator (PI), Program Manager (PM), and/or designated 
representative shall attend meetings as requested by the Government. Meeting attendees shall 
at times include Contractor managerial, supervisory, and other personnel knowledgeable of the 
subject matter. Meetings may start or end outside of regular duty hours.  
1.8 Contracting Officer’s Representative 
As determined by the CO, a COR will be appointed and identified by letter of designation, a 
copy of which will be provided to the Contractor by the CO. The designation letter states the 
responsibilities and limitations of the COR. The COR has the responsibility and authority to 
monitor all aspects of the day-to-day administration of the contract. Responsibilities include 
ensuring the timeliness and delivery of quality products and services to meet the requirements 
of the contract. 
1.9 Personnel 
This contract requires a high degree of collaboration among (or by) Contractor staff. Each 
requirement described in this SOW shall be performed by an appropriate mix of professional 
and technical staff. The Contractor shall employ and/or have access to staff with broad 
professional and technical expertise in environmental health sciences necessary to conduct 
evaluations of complex scientific literature and fulfill the activities of the SOW. Contract 
personnel shall have the expertise to contribute to problem formulation and research design as 
required. Contractor staff may need to be available after normal working hours and on 
weekends. 

   
 
 6 
Personnel assigned to this contract, including subcontractors and/or consultants, shall 
demonstrate to the COR that there are no conflicts of interest relative to the work to be 
conducted prior to performing work under the contract. Personnel assigned to this contract 
with access to federal IT resources may be required to pass a security investigation (see 
Section 4).

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
                          SAFEGUARDS IT COMPUTER SECURITY SUPPORT 
 
 1 
 
1.0 OVERVIEW 
 
1.1   INTRODUCTION AND BACKGROUND 
 
The Office of Safeguards (Safeguards) within Governmental Liaison, Disclosure and Safeguards 
(GLDS) function of Privacy, Governmental Liaison and Disclosure (PGLD) is responsible for 
ensuring that Federal Tax Information (FTI) provided outside of the IRS is secured and used 
appropriately. Safeguards assess approximately 300 federal, state and local agencies, as well as 
their authorized contractors receiving FTI under various sub-sections of Internal Revenue Code 
(IRC) §6103 and other IRC provisions. Agencies must implement appropriate safeguards to 
protect confidentiality and prevent unauthorized access or use of FTI. Safeguards works in 
partnership with the recipient agencies to identify and mitigate risks to FTI. The specific 
safeguard requirements are outlined in IRC §6103(p)(4) and detailed in Publication 1075, Tax 
Information Security Guidelines for Federal, State, and Local Agencies. 
 
Publication 1075 is primarily based upon National Institute of Standards & Technology (NIST) 
Special Publication (SP) 800-53, Assessing Security and Privacy Controls for Information 
Systems and Organizations for moderate risk systems, IRC §6103 statutory requirements and IRS 
policy and procedure. All automated information systems and networks which receive, process, 
store, transmit, or protect FTI must meet these information protection requirements. 
 
Current Contract Number 2032H5-23-F-00312  
Incumbent:  Sky Solutions, LLC. 
Approximate contract value:  $15,864,000.00 
 
2.0 OBJECTIVE  
 
The objective of this requirement is to increase security of FTI and to ensure consistent 
application of information security standards across all partner agency information systems. 
 
3.0   REQUIREMENT TASKS 
 
The mission of Safeguards is to promote taxpayer confidence in the integrity of the tax system by 
ensuring the confidentiality of IRS information provided to federal, state, and local agencies.  
Safeguards verifies compliance with IRC §6103(p)(4) safeguard requirements through the 
identification and mitigation of any risk of loss, breach, or misuse of FTI held by external 
government agencies. 
 
The Contractor shall provide cybersecurity and information technology (IT) expertise. The 
Contractor shall optimize its processes, to reduce costs and minimize risk to FTI in possession of 
agency partners, while continuing to meet all regulatory and agency documented standards and 
guidance; and obtain information technology expertise and ancillary support to enable Safeguards 
to meet on-going and new regulatory objectives having an impact on the Safeguards Program. 
 
The Contractor shall collaborate with IRS leadership, staff, and other contractors in support of 
agency computer security reviews. Support shall include the following: conducting preparatory 
agency outreach; conducting pre-review research and analysis to determine scope and potential 
areas of concern; executing automated and manual computer security compliance scans of partner 
agency systems during the review; preparing reports, documenting scan results and other 

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
                          SAFEGUARDS IT COMPUTER SECURITY SUPPORT 
 
 2 
computer security findings; and analyzing and responding to various partner agency computer 
security information submissions. Other computer security review-related support includes 
stakeholder outreach, risk-based modeling for agency review selection, computer security review 
methodology updates, and general IT expertise. The Contractor shall provide ad hoc support for 
the assessment of other projects, pilots, and new legislation that include provisions falling within 
the purview of Safeguards. 
 
In accordance with Executive Order (EO) 14179, the contractor is permitted to use Artificial 
Intelligence (AI) to assist in this task.  
 
The Contractor shall adhere to IRS Publication 1075 (Tax Information Security Guidelines for 
Federal, State, and Local Agencies), Federal Security Modernization Act (FISMA), Privacy Act 
of 1974, Internal Revenue Code  §6103, NIST Risk Management Framework and IRS Safeguards 
Program requirements when utilizing artificial intelligence tools to enhance technical support 
capabilities assisting in the management and updates of Safeguards Computer Security 
Evaluation Matrices (SCSEM’s) and associated automated evaluation files.  
 
Contractors shall not process, store, or have access to FTI, PII, SSI, Classified or controlled 
unclassified information and any agency specific confidential data.  
 
The Contractor shall utilize only publicly available information from approved sources including 
IRS Publication 1075, NIST Special Publications and Standards, IRS Safeguard Program public 
website materials, Federal regulations and guidance documents and publicly available industry 
best practice standards to include Center for Internet Security (CIS) Benchmarks and Defense 
Information Systems Agency (DISA) Secure Technical Implementation Guides (STIG). All 
queries submitted must contain no FTI or PII; referenced only publicly available information, 
comply with informational handling classifications and be reviewed for compliance prior to 
submission. 
 
3.1   TASK 1- ORIENTATION BRIEFING  
 
The contractor shall facilitate an orientation briefing via a video conference call (Microsoft (MS) 
Teams, Zoom, etc.) with its representatives, ensuring all parties have a common understanding of 
the task order tasks and requirements. The contractor shall bring, at a minimum, its key personnel 
to this meeting. 
 
3.2   TASK 2, RAMP-UP KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER/TRANSITION-IN  
  
3.2.1 RAMP-UP KNOWLEDGE 
 
Ramp-Up Knowledge Transfer is defined as the contractor acquiring and understanding the 
necessary documentation, information, and processes related to any work in progress. The 
Government anticipates this task will be performed in conjunction with the Transition-In 
activities after the award of this task order.  
 
The contractor shall appoint a knowledge transfer manager serving as key personnel to oversee all 
areas of information that are accounted for and all knowledge of information is transferred from 
the current incumbent. This can be the Project Manager (PM) or other approved key personnel. 

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
                          SAFEGUARDS IT COMPUTER SECURITY SUPPORT 
 
 3 
Prior to the transfer of knowledge, the contractor shall develop a final Knowledge Transfer Plan 
(KTP). The final KTP shall identify the contractor resources and roles involved in the transfer 
process, provide a list of risks and mitigation strategies for the transfer, and contain a detailed 
resource balanced project schedule developed with Microsoft Project or compatible equivalent. 
The project schedule shall identify tasks, dependencies, deliverables, and milestones. The project 
schedule shall be at a sufficient level of detail to track progress on a bi-weekly basis. 
 
 
The contractor shall meet with the IRS bi-weekly (twice a month) to discuss the progress of the 
knowledge transfer. The contractor shall show an updated MS Project Schedule or compatible 
equivalent and discuss any risks or concerns at this time. 
 
In addition to the Ramp-Up activities in the approved KTP, the contractor shall perform the 
following activities during the Ramp Up: 
 
• Assign personnel and submit security background packages within 10 calendar 
days to ensure background investigations are completed efficiently and gain 
access to IRS’s network.  
• Create a project schedule at a sufficient level of detail to track progress on a 
weekly basis. 
• Request access within 2 business days to tools and documentation (based on 
                          successful adjudication of background clearance of contractor personnel) 
• Review and understand all the technical and process documentation.  
• Review and understand the case management system. 
•           Knowledge Transfer/Transition-In Status Reports, for the duration of  
                   the transition-in period only, shall detail status of activities identified  
                   in the final KTP. 
 
Note: Completed background requests shall be sent to IRS COR/Alternate COR via encrypted 
electronic file. Any incomplete packages will be rejected for re-submission within 2 workdays. 
 
The contractor shall provide a KTP and a MS project or compatible equivalent schedule that is 
accepted by the Government and successfully completes knowledge transfer in accordance with 
the plan with a total transition-in project schedule not to exceed one hundred twenty (120) 
calendar days after Government acceptance of the KTP.  In addition, the Contractor shall provide 
complete and accurate status reports for the KTP. 
 
3.2.2 TRANSITION- IN  
 
The Transition-In task permits an effective transition from the incumbent Contractor to the new 
Contractor. The Government estimates this task will take approximately 120 calendar days to 
complete from date of award of the task order. Successful transition can be defined by its capacity 
to maintain full continuity of operations. To ensure a successful, low-risk transition, the 
contractor shall follow the approved Transition-In Plan and keep the government fully informed 
of status throughout the transition-in period. During the transition-in period, the incumbent is 
responsible for performance. This Task would be worked concurrently with Task 2, Ramp-Up 
Knowledge Transfer.  
 

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
                          SAFEGUARDS IT COMPUTER SECURITY SUPPORT 
 
 4 
In addition to the transition activities in the approved KTP, the contractor shall ensure the 
following activities have been successfully completed within 75 days of the transition-in period to 
ensure timely commencement of services after the 120-Day Transition-In period: 
 
1. Obtain final access to tools and documentation 
2. Comprehend and successfully perform all the technical and process documentation. 
3. Comprehend and successfully apply the existing data and system security policies in 
place. 
 
The Transition-in Checklist provides a vehicle to verify completion of the necessary transition-in 
activities. The Transition-in Checklist shall be developed by the Contractor and shall include all 
necessary activities to ensure an effective transition from the incumbent Contractor to a new 
Contractor that were performed. The Transition-in Checklist shall be signed by both, the 
Contractor and the COR after completion of the task. 
 
3.3   TASK 3, TASK MANAGEMENT  
 
3.3.1 General Requirements 
The Contractor shall provide personnel, including an equivalent contractor Subject Matter Expert 
(SME), to perform the requirements set forth herein. 
3.3.2 Monthly Status Report (MSR) Call 
The Contractor shall facilitate a Monthly Status Report (MSR) Call that includes presentation 
materials, such as a slide deck and supporting documentation, outlining expenditures, billings, 
progress, status, and any problems or issues encountered during task performance. The MSR shall 
include financial projections and an overview of support provided during the previous invoice 
period, including a list of all deliverables accepted and those in progress. All MSR materials and 
activities are subject to review and acceptance by the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) 
and the Technical Point of Contact (TPOC). 
3.3.3 Task Order Program Management Plan (PMP) 
The Contractor shall develop, implement, and maintain a Task Order Program Management Plan 
(PMP), subject to Government review and approval, manage, track, and evaluate performance 
throughout the period of performance. The PMP shall include control policies and procedures 
consistent with standard industry practices for project administration, execution, and tracking. 
The PMP may consist of multiple components, including, a project plan and performance status 
dashboards. The PMP shall include a consolidated roll-up of performance data for all active 
subtasks and shall be structured to support reuse for MSR Calls and other reporting requirements. 
The Contractor shall maintain the PMP in accordance with agreed-upon project management best 
practices. The PMP is subject to review and acceptance by the COR and TPOC. 
 
3.3.4 Administrative Touchpoint 
The Contractor shall attend and facilitate a weekly Administrative Touchpoint meeting, not to 
exceed one (1) hour in duration, as scheduled by the COR. The purpose of this meeting shall be to 
address onboarding activities, Government Furnished Equipment (GFE), and other administrative 

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
                          SAFEGUARDS IT COMPUTER SECURITY SUPPORT 
 
 5 
matters. The Contractor shall prepare, update, and present a performance status dashboard that 
identifies completed deliverables, timeliness of performance, and any deliverables returned due to 
deficient quality. These meetings and associated materials are subject to review by the COR and 
TPOC. 
 
3.3.5 Annual Planning Meeting 
The Contractor shall schedule, coordinate, and facilitate an Annual Planning Meeting with the 
COR, and the TPOC to discuss planned activities for the upcoming option year. The Contractor 
shall prepare and submit meeting materials to the COR for review and approval in advance of the 
meeting.  
 
3.4   TASK 4, COMPUTER SECURITY REVIEWS  
 
The Contractor shall work with external partner agency stakeholders to execute system 
configuration checks, interview system users (e.g., administrators), and to examine system 
artifacts (including policies and procedures) against management, operational and technical 
requirements, Center for Internet Security (CIS )Benchmarks, NIST requirements, and current 
IRS standards (e.g., IRS Publication 1075, IRC §6103). The scope of the assessment (“review”) 
will include all hardware and software associated with the processing, storing, or exchange of FTI 
including mainframes, operating system, telecom devices, applications, multi-function devices, 
firewalls, servers, cloud infrastructure, and databases. The contractor shall use the Safeguards 
Computer Security Evaluation Matrices (SCSEMs) and automated evaluation files as a guide to 
perform Computer Security Reviews on local, state or federal agencies, and their authorized 
contractors, that receive FTI under IRC §6103.  
Completion of computer security reviews resulted in the Safeguard review report (SRR) being 
issued to the external partner agency. The SRR consists of Sections A through H. Sections A 
through G are completed by the IRS staff and Section H dealing with information technology is 
completed by the contractor.  The SRR serves to identify an agency’s compliance with their

General Information
1. Master Contract Task Order Solicitation Notice: This solicitation is a Request for Quotations (RFQ). To the 
extent that the terms, RFP, Offer, Proposal, and Offeror appear in the solicitation and any attachments or

2. NAICS/PSC Code: The services in this solicitation are best represented by NAICS 541330 and PSC Code 
R408.
3. Extent of Competition: This solicitation is issued under the authority of FAR 16.5 as a 100% small business 
set-aside under the Seaport PSMAC. All terms and conditions of the Seaport PSMAC apply to this solicitation 
and resultant task order. 
4. Provisions and Clauses: All applicable and required provisions/clauses set forth in Seaport PSMAC 
automatically flow down to all Task Orders. 
5. Incumbent: This is a follow-on requirement to Task Order N00189-26-F-W061 awarded to Capstone 
Corporation under the CNIC PSMAC. 
6. Quote Preparation: The quote submission shall clearly state and acknowledge every amendment number

Request for CollaboraƟon (RFC) 
 
2028 Dress Rehearsal and 2030 Census 
Decennial as a Service (D-X) 
April 14, 2026 
 
 
(REVISED – APRIL 21, 2026*) 
 
This revised RFC removes all Help Desk related scope and terminology. References to incidents, 
Ɵckets, case management, HR or Safety, and other ITSM concepts have been eliminated to align 
its D-X requirement with its intended logisƟcs and XaaS-domain focus. These removals are 
reﬂected in the updated document. 
 
*All changes are made using Track Changes. 
 
 
 
 
Version 2.0 
 

 
2 
 
Purpose of This Follow-up Request for CollaboraƟon 
The U.S. Census Bureau (USCB) is issuing this Request for CollaboraƟon (RFC) to follow on the 
insights gained from the iniƟal Decennial-as-a-Service (D-X) Request for InformaƟon (RFI)  SAM 
noƟce #13PDRD25Q00000007 on 8/14/25, to gather addiƟonal industry input on areas not fully 
addressed in the original RFI responses. As we conƟnue reﬁning our acquisiƟon strategy, the 
USCB remains commiƩed to transparency, open communicaƟon, and meaningful collaboraƟon 
with industry partners. Accordingly, this RFC is designed to: 
 Address capability areas not fully addressed in the original RFI 
 Validate assumpƟons and operaƟonal models held by the government 
 Encourage industry to share best pracƟces, risks, and integraƟon strategies 
 Strengthen alignment between government expectaƟons and commercial capabiliƟes 
 Support a more informed, evidence-based acquisiƟon approach 
The detailed scope and operaƟonal descripƟons provided in the iniƟal D-X RFI conƟnue to serve as the baseline for 
this RFC. Please consider that informaƟon when assessing capability gaps or dependencies. 
The Census Bureau values industry experƟse and seeks to ensure that the D-X soluƟon is shaped 
through open dialogue, shared understanding, and collaboraƟve problem-solving. 
This RFC seeks industry partners capable of delivering a single fully integrated, naƟonwide 
equipment and endpoint lifecycle management ecosystem, operaƟng under a single-integrator 
model, to support logisƟcs, equipment handling, cellular services, site deployments, and 
operaƟonal support funcƟons necessary for the 2028 Dress Rehearsal and 2030 Decennial 
Census operaƟonal readiness across all states and U.S. territories. 
BACKGROUND  
The objecƟve of the D-X program is to deliver a complete, as-a-service soluƟon for centralized 
management of standard equipment and mobile devices that ensures cybersecurity 
compliance, operaƟonal eﬃciency, cost transparency, and end-to-end lifecycle accountability, 
while meeƟng all schedule milestones for the 2028 Dress Rehearsal and 2030 Decennial Census, 
including site deployment and teardown Ɵmelines, mobile device deployment cycles, ATO 
approvals, and system go-live dates.  The D-X soluƟon must be a turnkey, FedRAMP-authorized, 
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5-compliant, ATO-authorized, as-a-service operaƟonal ecosystem, 
coordinated under a single-integrator model, and including but not limited to the following 
capabiliƟes: 
 
 Devices, equipment and asset management services 

 
3 
 
o End-to-end management of all standard equipment and devices provided as-a-
service, including but not limited to mobile devices, peripherals, networking gear, 
printers/MFPs, and paper data capture equipment 
o Mobile device provisioning, conﬁguraƟon, and deployment 
o Equipment maintenance, repair, replacement and compliant disposiƟon 
o Inventory accuracy, chain-of-custody tracking, and real-Ɵme asset visibility 
 LogisƟcs, Warehousing, and Deployment OperaƟons 
o Warehousing (secure and nonsecure), kiƫ ng, staging, and order fulﬁllment for 
mobile devices and other equipment, with support for ﬂexible delivery opƟons 
such as informed delivery to individual residences, delivery rerouƟng, and a 
range of alternaƟve delivery methods proposed by industry to meet large-scale, 
distributed Census operaƟonal needs. 
o Shipping, returns, and reverse-logisƟcs workﬂows that incorporate ﬂexible 
delivery and return capabiliƟes, including informed delivery noƟﬁcaƟons, 
delivery rerouƟng, scheduled pickup windows, carrier-agnosƟc drop-oﬀ opƟons, 
and other alternaƟve delivery/return methods appropriate for naƟonwide and 
U.S. territory based ﬁeld operaƟons, supporƟng deliveries to and from ﬁeld 
oﬃces, regional census oﬃces, satellite operaƟonal sites, and individual 
employees’ residences across all states and U.S. territories. 
o Support for site deployments across all states and U.S. territories, including 
remote and island locaƟons, including installaƟon of vendor supplied equipment, 
peripherals, and other site-based infrastructure required to establish fully 
operaƟonal ﬁeld oﬃces. 
 Mobility, Uniﬁed Endpoint Management (UEM), and Cellular Services 
o UEM for device conﬁguraƟon, compliance, patching, and security baselines, and 
cross-plaƞorm governance to ensure that all mobile devices, regardless of 
operaƟng system or management plaƞorm, follow the same security baselines, 
conﬁguraƟon standards, compliance requirements, and lifecycle controls. 
 Mobile Device Management (MDM) for device enrollment, policy 
enforcement, compliance monitoring, and lifecycle controls 
o CoordinaƟon of mobile device provisioning throughout deployment cycles, 
including device setup, and readiness checks to ensure assets are fully 
operaƟonal. 
o Cellular service acƟvaƟon, eSIM management, coverage opƟmizaƟon, and surge 
capacity 
o IntegraƟon of mobility, idenƟty, and security baselines across all devices 
 
 Security, Compliance, and ConƟnuous Monitoring 

 
4 
 
o FedRAMP-authorized, NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5-compliant hosƟng and security 
controls, with conƟnuous monitoring and reporƟng aligned to federal 
requirements 
o ConƟnuous monitoring, vulnerability management, and incident response 
coordinaƟon 
o IntegraƟon of mobility, idenƟty, and endpoint security baselines across all 
devices and plaƞorms 
o Incident detecƟon, escalaƟon, and Tier 3 security response coordinated with 
Census security operaƟons 
o Secure data handling, media saniƟzaƟon, and compliant disposiƟon processes 
 OperaƟonal Support, Maintenance, and ITSM IntegraƟon 
o Tier 3 technical support and engineering-level issue resoluƟon integrated with 
the Government’s ITSM plaƞorm 
o Incident, request, and change management workﬂows aligned to Census 
processes and cross-vendor escalaƟon paths 
o Performance monitoring, SLA tracking, and escalaƟon governance across all XaaS 
service areas 
 ReporƟng, AnalyƟcs, and AutomaƟon 
o Real-Ɵme dashboards for inventory, logisƟcs, deployments, cellular usage, and 
support performance 
o PredicƟve analyƟcs for demand planning, device health, and operaƟonal 
readiness 
o AutomaƟon to streamline provisioning, updates, and service workﬂows 
 Program, Vendor, and Contract Management 
o Centralized coordinaƟon under a single-integrator model 
o Governance model that oversees and coordinates all Everything-as-a-Service 
providers and government systems 
o Risk management, performance oversight, and conƟnuous improvement 
Transparency and CollaboraƟon 
 This noƟce is part of our broader eﬀort to build a collaboraƟve, transparent, and 
industry-informed acquisiƟon environment for D-X. The Census Bureau may work to 
support a fair, informed, and well-aligned acquisiƟon process through the following: 
Publishing relevant operaƟonal plans, schedules, milestones, and mission constraints, as 
available, to help industry tailor responses to the realiƟes of Census ﬁeld operaƟons on 
the 2030 Decennial Census Website (hƩps://www.census.gov/programs-
surveys/decennial-census/decade/2030/2030-census-main.html). 

 
5 
 
 Engaging in two-way, iteraƟve communicaƟon, including follow-up quesƟons, reverse 
vendor days, and other collaboraƟve forums, to explore ideas, clarify concepts, and 
reﬁne approaches with industry when possible. 
 InviƟng industry feedback on feasibility, risks, and alternaƟves, and ensuring vendors 
have equal access to the informaƟon needed to develop well-informed responses. 
AddiƟonal InformaƟon for Industry 
The following areas were not fully addressed in the original RFI and require input to support 
planning, integraƟon, and acquisiƟon strategy development. 
For the purposes of this RFC, “Everything-as-a-Service (XaaS)” refers to a fully managed, subscripƟon-based service 
model in which vendors deliver the tools, technology, processes, people, and outcomes required to support Census 
operaƟons. This includes OEM-agnosƟc soluƟons, integrated service delivery, predictable pricing, and end-to-end 
lifecycle management across mulƟple service domains. The Census Bureau uses XaaS to describe a uniﬁed 
ecosystem of managed services that collecƟvely supports the 2028 Dress Rehearsal and 2030 Census. 
Managed Service Integrator (MSI) Model 
The USCB is considering a single-integrator model in which one Managed Service Integrator 
(MSI) provides end-to-end orchestraƟon across all D-X service domains. This MSI would 
coordinate mulƟple XaaS providers and ensure uniﬁed governance, interoperability, and 
accountability across logisƟcs, mobility, devices, warehousing, asset management, cellular 
services, site deployments, and support operaƟons. The USCB is seeking industry insight into 
MSI models, governance structures, and best pracƟces for managing a large, mulƟ-vendor 
ecosystem under a single-integrator construct. 
AssumpƟons: 
 Demonstrated experience coordinaƟng many diﬀerent operaƟonal areas, such as 
logisƟcs, devices, mobility, cellular services, site deployments, and support, so they 
funcƟon as one integrated service. 
 Proven tools and processes to keep all systems and vendors aligned, sharing accurate 
data, and working together smoothly across the enƟre operaƟon. 
 Can manage and support Decennial Census operaƟons across all states and U.S. 
territories, including remote and island locaƟons, making sure equipment, deployments, 
logisƟcs, cellular services, and support all work together smoothly at naƟonwide scale. 
 Takes responsibility for delivering consistent, end-to-end service outcomes across all 
operaƟonal areas, not just managing individual vendors 

 
6 
 
Command Center AssumpƟons 
The D-X vision includes a Command Center that provides a real-Ɵme operaƟonal cross-domain 
layer that provides conƟnuous visibility, coordinated response, and cross-domain decision 
support across the D-X ecosystem. It uniﬁes data from logisƟcs, asset management, endpoint 
management, cellular services, and help desk other XaaS-domain workﬂows into a single 
operaƟonal view, enabling leadership and operaƟons teams to monitor service health, track 
incidents and requests across departments track cross-domain condiƟons and workﬂow acƟvity, 
and take acƟon without switching between systems. 
AssumpƟons: 
 Provides a uniﬁed operaƟonal picture that enables real-Ɵme monitoring of service 
health, incident trendsservice-tower condiƟons, and cross-domain workﬂow status 
across all D-X service areas XaaS domains. 
 Enables proacƟve operaƟonsmanagement, including endpoint health monitoring, 
vulnerability tracking, and ﬁeld service coordinaƟon, by leveraging integrated data and 
automated alerƟng across all Ɵers XaaS towers. 
 Supports coordinated incident response and case rouƟng acrossresponse and workﬂow 
rouƟng across IT, HR, Safety, LogisƟcs, and ﬁeld operaƟonsother D-X service domains, 
ensuring that leadership and operaƟonal teams can track progress and take acƟon from 
a single environment. 
 Operates on a common data foundaƟon that may support AI-driven automaƟon, 
allowing the system to autonomously resolve requests, execute mulƟ-step workﬂows, 
and complete end-to-end acƟons within established policies. 
Data Interoperability and IntegraƟon 
D-X will rely on a combinaƟon of mulƟple commercial and government systems working 
together seamlessly. To achieve this, the USCB must understand how vendors approach data 
integraƟon, API frameworks, synchronizaƟon, and real-Ɵme visibility across disparate plaƞorms, 
including those operated by federal partners. We are seeking industry insight into best 
pracƟces, integraƟon paƩerns, and potenƟal challenges associated with building a uniﬁed 
operaƟonal ecosystem that spans both commercial and government environments. 
AssumpƟons: 
 Integrates commercial and government systems into a uniﬁed operaƟonal ecosystem 
that supports seamless data exchange and coordinated service delivery. 
 Applies federal and commercial best pracƟces to ensure data quality, synchronizaƟon, 
and real-Ɵme visibility across diverse plaƞorms and partner environments. 
 Provides end-to-end integraƟon across logisƟcs, UEM, cellular, and asset management 
systems to enable consistent, mission-ready operaƟons. 

 
7 
 
OEM-AgnosƟc Device and Equipment As-a-Service Models 
The USCB is evaluaƟng OEM-agnosƟc as-a-service models for mobile devices (smartphones, 
tablets, laptops), oﬃce equipment (printers, mulƟfuncƟon devices), paper data-capture 
equipment (scanners, leƩer openers, guilloƟnes), and oﬃce networking equipment (access 
points, servers, and related infrastructure). These models may include brand-speciﬁc or 
equivalent conﬁguraƟons where required. The USCB seeks industry input on how such 
as-a-service oﬀerings are typically structured commercially, including provisioning approaches, 
service levels, lifecycle services, refresh strategies, and performance management. The USCB 
also requests informaƟon on risks, dependencies, and constraints that should be considered 
when implemenƟng an enterprise-scale, mulƟ-vendor as-a-service model. 
AssumpƟons: 
 Bundles diverse equipment categories, including mobile devices, oﬃce and paper data 
capture equipment, scanners, and networking hardware, into a uniﬁed, scalable, 
OEM-agnosƟc program that delivers provisioning, kiƫ ng, and lifecycle services. 
 Predictable pricing, refresh cycles, and service-level commitments that are in alignment 
with other large-scale as-a-service programs, including break/ﬁx services, rapid 
replacement SLAs, inventory pooling, buﬀer stock strategies, and secure end-of-life 
disposiƟon. 
 Supports enterprise-scale device volumes, including approximately 360,000 
smartphones, 20,000 tablets, and 20,000 laptops, with the ability to surge or de-surge 
inventory and services based on operaƟonal tempo and ﬁeld deployment needs. 
 Provide cellular service for all mobile devices naƟonwide across all states and U.S. 
territories by leveraging the best-performing local carriers in each area, supported by 
performance monitoring, availability metrics, and rapid carrier remediaƟon path

Engineering services, with a size standard of $16.5M.  Magnitude of construction project 
estimate is between $25,000.00 and $100,000.  It is anticipated that one contract will be 
awarded from this announcement by May 2026.  
(a) Contract Award Procedure: Before a small business is proposed as a potential 
contractor, they must be certified by VETbiz and registered in the System for Award 
Management (SAM) database. Register via the SAM internet site at http://www.sam.gov. 
Failure of a proposed SDVOSB to be certified by the CVE at the time the SF-330 is 
submitted will result in their elimination as a proposed contractor. The proposed services 
will be obtained by a Negotiated Firm-Fixed Price Contract. 
(b) Nature of Work: Corporal Michael J Crecenz VA Medical Center (CMCVAMC) in 
Philadelphia, PA, is seeking Architect-Engineering (A/E) services to develop working 
drawings, phasing plans, infection control plans, contract specifications, and cost 
estimates for full and complete construction of Project No. 642-25-125, A/E – Remove 
and Replace Building 2 Grease Trap.  
II.  PROJECT INFORMATION (Scope of Work):
A/E – Remove and Replace Building 2 Grease Trap:
The A/E shall provide design and engineering services for this design project, including all 
applicable site visits, laser and video scanning, field investigation, studies, and user interviews 
to prepare construction drawings, specifications, narratives, cost estimates and schedules 
associated with the following work:
(a) Perform field investigative services, including underground and video scanning, of all 
surrounding utility lines and piping associated with the grease trap, including inlet piping 
from kitchen to outlet piping to sanitary system. Determine integrity of piping, whether 
complete removal and replacement of existing piping is required or an alternate solution 
such as pipe jetting and lining. Complete removal and replacement of piping shall 
require additional engineering services, such as civil and structural engineering.
(b) Design a new grease entrapment system for the Building 2 kitchen. Entrapment system 
shall provide similar or increased grease capacity.
(c) Design phasing. Temporary grease entrapment system for the duration of the 
construction project. A Traffic control plan. Demolition and construction plan, including 
removal of manhole and associated concrete, trenching and shoring work.

Presolicitation Notice
Presolicitation Notice
Page 4 of 7
All work shall have a minimal impact on CMCVAMC facilities, including kitchen operations. The 
above paragraphs constitute a basic outline (objectives) of the work to be accomplished and in 
no way comprise all the details for design of this project. The A/E shall initiate detailed 
inspection of the project site to determine the needs and conditions for the design of this project. 
Copies of VA Medical Center Philadelphia, PA existing if available record drawings will be made 
available to the highest rated A/E firm; the A/E will verify the validity of the record drawings prior 
to the start of design work and conduct site investigations as necessary throughout the design. 
A/E is solely responsible for the management, including all associated labor, equipment, 
materials, mailing costs, and inspection, to meet the requirements of the design project. The A/E 
shall further provide meeting minutes for all meetings held under this design project. The A/E 
firms’ representatives performing site investigations on VA Medical Center Philadelphia campus 
must have the following additional requirements before starting site investigations on campus:
a) A/E PIV badge must be always worn by A/E or representative while on campus.
b) At least five (5) business day notice to VA prior to arrival.
If at any time an employee of the A/E firm becomes ill, they should not remain or report to work 
at VA Medical Center Philadelphia.

descending order of importance.

DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A. Approved for public released; distribution unlimited 
 
Approved for Public Release 
26-MDA-12338 
REQUEST FOR INFORMATION  
 
Missile Defense System - Next (MDS-Next) 
 Capability Solutions for Strategic Architecture Thrust Areas  
 
Notice Number: 26-MDA-12338 
 
NAICS Code: 541715 - Research and development in the physical, engineering, and life 
sciences, except nanotechnology and biotechnology 
 
 
1.0 BACKGROUND 
 
The Missile Defense Agency (MDA) is executing a strategic planning effort to inform future 
capability development and investment opportunities in response to the 2035+ projected threat 
environment. As part of this effort, the Agency has identified Strategic Architecture Thrust 
Areas representing priority focus areas for advancing missile defense capabilities in the 2035+ 
timeframe. These thrust areas reflect where the Agency is seeking new or alternative 
approaches to address future mission challenges and achieve improved mission outcomes. 
 
This RFI represents the transition from identifying and prioritizing strategic focus areas to 
evaluating solution approaches that can advance those areas. Responses will inform 
prioritization of capability areas and potential POM investment decisions.  
 
Detailed descriptions of the Strategic Architecture Thrust Areas will be available to 
respondents with the appropriate clearance level. Additional context on future capability 
attributes is provided in the MDS-Next Characteristics briefing that will be available to 
respondents at the Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) level. See Section 9.0 for 
instructions on requesting access to these resources.   
 
2.0 OBJECTIVE 
 
The objective of this RFI is to obtain solution-oriented information describing specific capability 
approaches and architectural concepts that advance one or more of the identified Strategic 
Architecture Thrust Areas. Responses should clearly describe what capability is being proposed, 
how it addresses the thrust area, and how it improves mission outcomes. 
Information received will be used to: 
• Identify solution approaches that measurably address validated Strategic Architecture 
Thrust Areas 
• Assess the technical feasibility, maturity, and integration considerations of proposed 
approaches 
• Enable focused technical dialogue and evaluation at the 1:1 technical exchange  
• Inform prioritization of potential capability areas and support POM-28 investment 
decisions 
 
This effort is intended to produce decision-relevant insights to further long-range planning 
efforts. 
 
3.0 STRATEGIC FRAMING 

 
DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A. Approved for public released; distribution unlimited 
 
Approved for Public Release 
26-MDA-12338 
 
The Agency is not solely seeking incremental improvements to existing systems or approaches. 
Respondents are encouraged to consider whether fundamentally different capability constructs, 
architectures, or operational concepts are required to advance the identified Strategic 
Architecture Thrust Areas. 
 
In particular, respondents should consider: 
• Whether current approaches represent the most effective and efficient path forward, or if 
alternative paradigms may provide greater mission advantage 
• What new capabilities or concepts, including those developed outside traditional missile 
defense applications, could be adapted to significantly improve outcomes 
• Preference will be given emerging technologies, cross-domain solutions, or non-
traditional approaches that could change how the mission is executed or approached 
 
The intent is to identify both evolutionary improvements and non-traditional or disruptive 
approaches that provide meaningful operational advantage. 
 
4.0 SCOPE 
 
Responses should focus on capability-level approaches and architectural concepts that: 
• Directly align to one or more Strategic Architecture Thrust Areas  
• Address challenges posed by the 2035+ projected threat environment 
• Demonstrate the potential to improve operational effectiveness at the system or mission 
level 
 
Respondents should consider: 
• How the proposed approach changes outcomes relative to the identified Strategic 
Architecture Thrust(s), and if applicable, the Key Area(s) where the architecture would 
particularly benefit from additional science and technology (S&T)  
• Applicability across multiple mission areas or threat sets, where relevant 
• Integration with existing and planned missile defense architectures 
 
5.0 SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS 
 
Respondents shall use the Strategic Architecture Thrust Areas to ensure clear alignment of 
proposed solutions. The MDS-Next Characteristics briefing is provided as additional context to 
inform how proposed approaches align to desired future mission attributes. The characteristics 
briefing is not an exhaustive list and is provided as reference. Characteristics provided in the 
briefing should not be interpreted as limiting or constraining potential solutions.   
 
Submissions must clearly align to one or more Strategic Architecture Thrust Areas. Responses 
should be specific, structured, and focused on capability outcomes. Respondents should avoid 
general descriptions, marketing material, or platform-centric responses. Responses that do not 
demonstrate clear alignment or sufficient detail may be assessed as less relevant. 
 
Responses shall be submitted as concise pitch papers and must address the following elements: 
 
• Strategic Architecture Thrust Area Alignment 

 
DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A. Approved for public released; distribution unlimited 
 
Approved for Public Release 
26-MDA-12338 
o Identify the specific Strategic Architecture Thrust(s) and Key Area(s) addressed 
and describe how the proposed approach advances that intent  
o Maintain clear traceability to the Strategic Architecture Thrust(s) and Key Area(s) 
throughout the response 
 
• Capability Approach 
o Provide a clear description of the proposed capability or architectural concept 
o Describe: 
 The function of the capability 
 How it operates within the broader system 
o Responses should address: 
 Whether the approach represents a new or alternative way to achieve the 
mission outcome 
 How it differs from or improves upon current or planned capabilities 
 Estimated timeline to achieve initial operational fielding of the proposed 
capability, including key milestones for development, prototyping, testing, 
and deployment 
o Where applicable, identify: 
 Approaches derived from other domains, missions, or industries 
 Capabilities not traditionally associated with missile defense that could be 
adapted to this mission 
 
• Operational Impact 
o Describe how the approach improves mission outcomes in relation to the thrust 
area 
o Address: 
 What operational limitations are mitigated or eliminated 
 Whether the approach enables new operational concepts or reduces 
reliance on existing constructs 
o Clearly articulate whether the approach: 
 Enhances current capabilities, or 
 Fundamentally changes how the mission is performed 
 
• Technical Feasibility and Maturity 
o Describe the current level of maturity (concept, prototype, demonstration, etc.) 
o Technology Readiness Level  
o Identify key technical challenges, risks, or dependencies 
 
• Cost Considerations 
o Provide the estimated Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost for the proposed 
solution, including development, prototyping, integration, production, and 
fielding, as applicable 
o Identify: 
 Major cost drivers and underlying assumptions 
 Any dependencies on Government-furnished resources, infrastructure, or 
enabling capabilities 
 Areas of cost uncertainty or variables that could materially affect the 
estimate 
 

 
DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A. Approved for public released; distribution unlimited 
 
Approved for Public Release 
26-MDA-12338 
• Integration Considerations 
o Describe how the approach would integrate with: 
 Existing systems 
 Planned architectures 
o Identify required interfaces, dependencies, and enabling capabilities 
 
• Small Business Considerations 
o The Government is seeking to understand the capability of small businesses to 
contribute to the Strategic Architecture Thrust Areas and to inform potential 
future acquisition strategies. 
o Small business respondents are requested to address the following: 
 Describe relevant capabilities, technologies, or solution approaches the 
small business can provide that align to the Strategic Architecture Thrust 
Areas 
 Identify any unique or innovative contributions the small business brings, 
including capabilities derived from non-traditional or commercial 
applications 
o If proposing a teaming arrangement, describe: 
 The role of the small business in the overall solution 
 Any teaming partners or subcontractors, as applicable 
 How the small business contributes to the overall capability approach 
 
• Additional Considerations 
o Respondents are strongly encouraged to identify solutions that: 
 Leverage capabilities from other Services, Agencies, or Departments 
 Adapt technologies or concepts from the commercial sector or other 
mission areas 
 Reduce costs per missile defense kill or sustainment costs of fielded 
system 
 Represent cross-domain or non-traditional applications relevant to missile 
defense 
 
6.0 USE OF SUBMISSIONS  
 
Responses will be reviewed by the Agency to identify Technology Areas for further examination 
and will inform prioritization of capability areas and potential POM investment decisions. The 
submissions will be discussed as part of the respondent’s requested 1:1 technical exchange. 
Submission does not constitute a commitment by the Agency to pursue any specific approach or 
activity. 
 
Provided responses will not be returned and respondents are advised that MDA is under no 
obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received except as required to confirm 
receipt of classified materials, or to request clarification with respect to any information that is 
submitted in accordance with the instructions contained in this RFI. MDA makes no commitment 
regarding the use of a submission; nor is any acquisition expected from this RFI or the 
submissions that may be made hereunder. 
 
7.0 MARKING 
 

 
DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A. Approved for public released; distribution unlimited 
 
Approved for Public Release 
26-MDA-12338 
Respondents are encouraged to respond with the submission of information that is not 
constrained by proprietary information rights. If proprietary information is included in a 
respondent’s submission, the respondent is responsible for ensuring its submission contains 
appropriate and adequate markings of said proprietary information. Further, any proprietary 
information MUST be marked as such on a page-by-page basis. 
 
The Government intends to use third party, non-Government (i.e. contractor, Federally Funded 
Research, and Development Center personnel) support personnel as subject matter experts in the 
review of responses received, including the review of any marked or unmarked proprietary 
information provided.  MDA utilizes subject matter experts at Federally Funded Research 
Laboratories and other support contractors to meet our mission objectives.  The Agency 
maintains non-disclosure agreements on file with these organizations and companies to allow 
them access to proprietary information for the purpose of evaluations and recommendations.  
Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI) and Personal Conflict of Interest (PCI) clauses are 
incorporated within each of these contracts.  Submission of a response to this RFI constitutes the 
participant's acknowledgement and agreement that the information provided in the response, 
including any marked or unmarked proprietary or source selection information, may be disclosed 
to these non-Government support personnel. Respondents with questions or objections could 
contact the following unclassified email mda.mbx.sppa@mail.mil. 
 
Respondents are further notified the Government may use Artificial Intelligence (AI) 
mechanisms to review and assess responses.  
 
8.0 COMPENSATION 
 
This RFI only supports MDA planning activities. Submission of information by a respondent 
hereunder is entirely voluntary. The Government does not intend to award a contract based 
on this request or reimburse any costs for the information requested as a result of any 
company, organization, or individual providing a response to the RFI. MDA reserves the 
right to use information that has been voluntarily provided by respondents without 
compensation as part of MDA’s ongoing efforts to refine the Missile Defense System 
Strategic Investment Plan and Technology Roadmap. 
 
9.0 RFI RESOURCES 
 
The following resources are available to assist respondents in replying to this RFI: 
• Strategic Architecture Thrust Areas briefing (SECRET level) 
• MDS-Next Characteristics briefing (CUI level) 
• 1:1 technical exchange with subject matter experts from MDA 
 
To request access to these resources, send an unclassified email to mda.mbx.sppa@mail.mil 
with the information in a. – d. listed below. Complete requests must be received by MDA 
no later than (NLT) 1200 Central Standard Time (CST) on 1 May 2026. 
 
a. General Information 
• Organization Name and CAGE Code 
• Facility Clearance Level (FCL) 
• Facility Security Officer (FSO) name and contact information

Approved for Public Release 
26-MDA-12338 
• Primary point of contact name, contact information, and clearance level 
 
b. Strategic Architecture Thrust Areas briefing (SECRET level) 
• Indicate capability to receive this over SIPR (Yes/No) 
• If not capable of receiving via SIPR, the briefing will be held for those respondents with 
the appropriate clearance level in conjunction with the 1:1 technical exchange 
 
c. MDS-Next Characteristics briefing (CUI level) 
• Confirm primary point of contract name and email address to receive briefing via DoD 
SAFE 
 
d. 1:1 technical exchange with subject matter experts from MDA (anticipated the week of 27 
April 2026 – 15 May 2026) 
• Indicate preference for in-person or virtual exchange. In-person exchanges will be held in 
Huntsville, AL and are available at the unclassified level and higher. Virtual exchanges 
are limited to unclassified, CUI, and Secret (with SIPR capability) levels.  
• Indicate desired classification level 
• Identify all attendee names, contact information, and clearance level 
 
Upon receipt, the Government will verify clearance information, coordinate access to the 
briefings, and schedule the 1:1 technical exchange.  
 
10.0 WHITE PAPER SUBMISSION 
 
White papers must be received via secured electronic submission by MDA NLT 1200 CST 
on 11 May 2026 at the following addresses:

Solicitation Information/Instructions:

This solicitation is to procure Project Facilitator services under an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) type contract in accordance with the IDIQ PWS.  The scope of this IDIQ will be for Project Facilitator work at any VHA facility. This will be a multiple-award IDIQ contract set-aside for Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB).   See Section E for specific proposal instructions as well as response dates and evaluation criteria.  This IDIQ contract will have an ordering period of five (5) years from award and is available for use by any VA Contracting Officer in coordination with Program Contracting Activity Central. 

SECTION B - CONTINUATION OF SF 1449 BLOCKS

	

B.1  CONTRACT ADMINISTRATION DATA

  1.  Contract Administration:  All contract administration matters will be handled by the following individuals:

    a.  CONTRACTOR:  

    b.  GOVERNMENT:  Contracting Officer 36C776 

Department of Veterans Affairs

6100 Oak Tree Blvd, Suite 490

Independence OH 44131

  4.  GOVERNMENT INVOICE ADDRESS:  All Invoices from the contractor shall be submitted electronically in accordance with VAAR Clause 852.232-72 Electronic Submission of Payment Requests.

  ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF AMENDMENTS:  The offeror acknowledges receipt of amendments to the Solicitation numbered and dated as follows:

B.2  ORDER LIMITATIONS, CONTRACT CEILING, AND ORDERING PROCEDURES

This Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract has a base ordering period of sixty (60) months from the date of award. The effective period of the contract shall include this ordering period and shall continue until completion of the final Task Order (TO) issued under the contract. The period of performance of any TO is independent of the base ordering period, and TO performance may extend beyond the expiration of the ordering period, provided the TO was issued prior to the end of the ordering period. The Government is under no obligation to issue any TOs against this contract beyond satisfaction of the minimum ordering guarantee. TOs may be issued at any time during the base ordering period. Any duly warranted Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Contracting Officer is authorized to place orders under this IDIQ contract.

The TOTAL MAXIMUM CONTRACT VALUE, defined as the cumulative sum of all contractor payment obligations associated with all TOs issued under this IDIQ contract, shall not exceed $6,400,176. The MINIMUM GUARANTEE ORDER(S) VALUE for this IDIQ contract award is $2,000.00, provided that the Contractor demonstrates it has exercised due diligence and made its best efforts to secure one or more TOs under this contract.

Ordering under this IDIQ contract will be conducted in accordance with applicable laws and regulations governing placement of orders under multiple award IDIQ contracts. The Government reserves the right to use written or oral communications, including but not limited to written proposals, oral presentations, or a combination thereof, as appropriate to the nature and complexity of each requirement. For new projects (i.e., requirements that are not follow on or continuation efforts where an incumbent on this IDIQ is the primary facilitator (PF)), the Government will provide fair opportunity to all eligible IDIQ awardees in accordance with applicable regulation. Selection criteria for new project TO awards may include any combination of the following factors, listed in no particular order of importance unless otherwise specified in the TO request: technical approach and capability, price/cost, and past performance. PTAG

Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office 
Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market 
information gathering which the USPTO will use to determine which contractor(s) is/are the most 
likely to successfully meet the agency’s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative 
competition. As a result of this market research, the solicitation will only be issued to those qualified

below.

Purpose of this Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI)

educate USPTO about the capabilities and offerings of commercial sources to offer: 
• A team of Emergency Management Specialists/Continuity of Operations (COOP) Subject 
Matter Experts and 1 Project Manager that will update USPTO's COOP Plan and Program from 
its current state to where it adheres to all aspects of the recently updated Federal Continuity 
Directives that were released in 2024, bringing USPTO into compliance.

thorough market research, identify suitable providers, and make informed decisions.

Introduction and Background 
The United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) is the federal agency for granting U.S. 
patents and registering trademarks. The strength and vitality of the U.S. economy depends 
directly on effective mechanisms that protect new ideas and investments in innovation and 
creativity. The continued demand for patents and trademarks underscores the ingenuity of 
American inventors and entrepreneurs.  
The Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (OCAO), Office of Administrative Services, 
Security and Emergency Management Division oversees implementation and compliance with 
all federal laws and regulations pertaining to COOP and OEP programs including developing 
plans, procedures, training materials and educational programs for designated COOP; Pandemic, 
Emergency Communications, and OEP (such as printed material, articles, Power Point, 
classroom and computer-based training). 
The Office of Procurement (OP) within OCFO awards and administers a wide variety of 
contracts and simplified purchases for the acquisition of goods and services in support of the 
agency’s mission. It seeks to obtain immediate program support to help perform day-to-day 
activities as the office continues to grow and expand to meet demand. 
 
Purpose and Scope 
 
Purpose  
The purpose of the COR contract is to acquire support services by securing a company that will 
provide four Emergency Management Specialists and one supervisor to assist the Security and 
Emergency Management Division with assessing USPTO’s COOP program and revising the 
COOP plan to adhere to the recently updated Federal Continuity Directives (FCD). Focus areas 
include; gap analysis; Mission Essential Function (MEF) Validation; Business Process Analysis 
(requirement) / Business Impact Analysis (BIA); COOP Plan update and documentation; and 
developing a Training, Testing, and Exercise (TT&E) Program. All work must conform with 
applicable federal government regulations and policies, as well as other agency supplemental 
regulations and policies as appropriate.

contract.

interviews, analyze operations and needs to develop a gap analysis based on current 
Continuity Directives.

validation report. 
• Objective 3 - Conduct a full Business Process Analysis / Business Process Analysis 
through workshops and interviews with Business Units.

updated Federal Continuity Directives, to include Primary, Alternate, Contingency,

Requirement Description/ Draft Scope 

The Naval Surface Warfare Center, Philadelphia Division is hereby issuing a Request for Information (RFI) from all potential sources to provide information regarding a commercial, modified commercial, or non-commercial product/service solution(s) to the below specifications:

1.0 INTRODUCTION

1.0.1  The Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD) is a Department of Defense entity responsible for research and development, test and evaluation, engineering and fleet support organization for the Navy’s ships, submarines, military watercraft and unmanned vehicles. This requirement is for NSWCPD Code 426, which has responsibility for Lifecycle Management (LCM) and In-Service Engineering (ISE) for US Navy Main Reduction Gears (MRG). The LCM and ISE mission involves maintaining adequate and effective operational readiness, safety and mission effectiveness of US Navy MRGs and their associated auxiliary systems. In support of this mission, NSWCPD provides engineered solutions to fleet MRG problems.

MRG Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) design, construct, install, service, support and provide repair and replacement parts for the gearboxes under their purview. They possess certain unique knowledge, experience and expertise, and access to technical information that is not available elsewhere. 

In support of its MRG LCM and ISEA mission, NSWCPD intends to leverage off the contractor’s unique knowledge, experience and expertise, and access to technical information related to the RENK BUSL 261, RENK ASL 2/160, RENK BOS 156, and RENK ASL 95 reduction gear models, for the purpose of improving in-service and lifecycle support initiatives. The contractor will assist NSWCPD in developing, delivering and executing engineered solutions to fleet MRG problems.

1.0.2  This contract is for non-personal services.  It does not create employment rights with the U.S. Government whether actual, inherent, or implied

1.0.3  Government/Contractor Relationship

1.0.3.1  The services to be delivered under this Contract are non-personal services and the parties recognize and agree that no employer-employee relationship exists or will exist under the Contract between the Government and the Contractor's personnel.  Therefore, it is in the best interest of the Government to provide both parties a full understanding of their respective obligations. 

1.0.3.2  The Contractor employees shall identify themselves as Contractor personnel by introducing themselves or being introduced as Contractor personnel and displaying distinguishable badges or other visible identification for meetings with Government personnel. In addition, Contractor personnel shall appropriately identify themselves as Contractor employees in telephone conversations and in formal and informal written correspondence.

1.0.3.3   Contractor personnel under this Contract shall not engage in any of the inherently Governmental functions listed at FAR Subpart 7.5 or DFARS Subpart 207.5. 

1.0.4  Employee Relationship: 

1.0.4.1  The services to be performed under this Contract do not require the Contractor or its personnel to exercise personal judgment and discretion on behalf of the Government.  Rather the Contractor's personnel will act and exercise personal judgment and discretion on behalf of the Contractor.  

1.0.4.2  Rules, regulations, directives, and requirements that are issued by the U. S. Navy and NSWCPD under its responsibility for good order, administration, and security are applicable to all personnel who enter a Government installation or who travel on Government transportation.  This is not to be construed or interpreted to establish any degree of Government control that is inconsistent with a non-personal services contract. 

1.0.4.3  Inapplicability of Employee Benefits: This Contract does not create an employer-employee relationship.  Accordingly, entitlements and benefits applicable to such relationships do not apply.   

1.0.4.4  It is the Contractor's, as well as the Government's, responsibility to monitor Contract activities and notify the Contracting Officer if the Contractor believes that the intent of this Section has been or may be violated.  

1.0.4.4.1  The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer in writing via letter or email within three (3) calendar days from the date of any incident that the Contractor considers to constitute a violation of this Section.  The notice should include the date, nature, and circumstances of the conduct; the name, function, and activity of each Government employee or Contractor official or employee involved or knowledgeable about such conduct; identify any documents or substance of any oral communication involved in the conduct; and the Contractor's estimated date when, absent a response, cost, schedule or performance will be impacted.

1.0.4.4.2  The Contracting Officer will, within five (5) calendar days after receipt of notice, respond to the notice in writing.  In responding, the Contracting Officer will either:

(i)	Confirm the conduct is in violation and when necessary direct the mode of further performance,

(ii)	Countermand any communication regarded as a violation,

(iii)	Deny that the conduct constitutes a violation and when necessary direct the mode of further performance, or

(iv)	In the event the notice is inadequate to make a decision, advise the Contractor what additional information is required, and establish the date by which it should be furnished by the Contractor.  

BACKGROUND 

Virtually all mechanical equipment needs continuing engineering support to solve operational problems. Military systems require a higher level of engineering support than commercial equivalent systems. The military systems normally push the leading edge of technology and are subjected to ever-changing and demanding environments and mission cycles. New problems are continually experienced after approval for operational use. The new problems are a result of greater exposure, changes in mission, changes in system weight or configuration, variations in manufacture or repair, aging of the hardware, maintenance concept changes, critical materials availability, and changing component coating and fuel compounds. (i.e.: Bio-Fuel technologies and similar advances). These changes in engine usage can be dramatic and can have a dramatic impact on safety, readiness, and mission effectiveness. Therefore, a direct contract relationship with MRG OEMs is essential to maintain these systems at full operational capability.

SCOPE OF WORK 

This Statement of Work (SOW) describes services to be applied via Task Orders (TOs) detailing specific support requirements within the scope of this contract SOW. The overall scope of this SOW is to provide lifecycle, modernization and in-service support for the RENK BUSL 261, ASL 2/160, BOS 156, and ASL 95 reduction gear models and their related shipboard auxiliary systems. The support required will involve technical, logistics, training, administrative and program management efforts related to reduction gear lifecycle and in-service concerns.

2.2	NAVSEA S9241-DC-MMC-020, Technical Manual for MAIN REDUCTION GEAR ASL 2/160 / BUSL 261; Operation and Maintenance Manual; Volume 2; LCS 1 Variant, LCS 5AF.

2.3	NAVSEA S9241-DC-MMC-030, Technical Manual for MAIN REDUCTION GEAR ASL 2/160 / BUSL 261; Depot Level Maintenance Manual; Volume 1; LCS 1 Variant, LCS 5AF.

2.4	NAVSEA S9241-CY-MMC-A10, Technical Manual for Reduction Gear, Gas Turbine, RENK Model BOS-156; LCS-6 AND FOLLOW ON.

2.5 	NAVSEA S9241-C9-MMC-A10, Technical Manual for Reduction Gear, Diesel Engine, RENK Model ASL-95; LCS-6 AND FOLLOW ON.
