•	technical issue resolution

•	owners group meetings

•	engineering investigations

•	failure analysis, root cause determination and associated light repairs

•	product improvements (design, development, testing & evaluation, and deployment), 

•	new technology development and integration

•	technical documentation product development, revision and update

•	land-based and shipboard testing and evaluation. 

•	field technical service support, in conjunction with engineering efforts and tasking

3.2 Engineering investigations - The contractor shall conduct engineering investigations, using contractor personnel, material, and facilities; unless specific material is provided by the Government. The investigations shall relate to the RENK products and new RENK MRG equipment including, but not limited to: failure analysis, root cause determination and associated light repairs, technical issue resolution, software changes and upgrades, installation, operation, maintenance, operations limits, training requirements, and documentation. A report of the results of each investigation, including conclusions and recommendations shall be prepared. 

3.3	Logistics Support Services - The contractor shall provide necessary product line expertise and information necessary to support the development, updating and revision of various Navy logistics products, including: 

 

•	Equipment configuration management and associated Allowance Parts Lists (APLs)

•	parts and sub-assembly provisioning

•	planned maintenance system (PMS) procedures

•	maintenance standards

•	parts stocking and availability

3.4 Product improvements (design, development, testing & evaluation, and deployment) - The contractor shall provide materials, engineering personnel, and the manufacturing and testing facilities to design parts, components, or systems to meet the program objectives and support new technology development and integration. The contractor shall validate the designs by bench tests, MRG system tests, and support of fleet evaluations. Engineering Change Proposals (ECP) and associated technical data shall be developed and submitted. Section 1: Purpose 
The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to gather market research information for 
understanding the Government’s options regarding Nuclear Surety Cross Check Analysis 
(NSCCA)/ Nuclear Safety Analysis and Technical Evaluation (NSATE)/ Independent 
Verification/Validation (IV&V) for the Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) hardware/
software integration for the Sentinel Weapon System. NSCCA/NSATE is defined in AFMAN 
91-119/ AFMAN 91-118; test, simulations, and other evaluation techniques must be used to 
prove the safety and surety of the weapon system. The Government is evaluating Independent 
Verification/Validation options for Nuclear Surety for FPGA hardware/software integration for 
the Sentinel Weapon System.
THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ONLY 
This RFI is issued solely for information/planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for 
Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the 
Government to contract for any supply or service. Further, the Government is not seeking 
proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised the 
Government will not pay for any information or costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs 
associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party’s expense. Not 
responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued.  
Section 2: RFI Questions 
1. Demonstrate your ability to test, simulate, and evaluate FPGA's in accordance with 
AFMAN 91-119/AFMAN 91-118. Define the tools, modeling capabilities, and simulations 
environments you use to assess potential failure modes, unauthorized access pathways, and 
inadvertent launch scenarios. Responses should speak to the process for tracing and 
verifying surety requirements from top-level system specifications to component-level and 
software-level implementation.
2. Demonstrate your capability to provide a comprehensive security infrastructure for 
performing analysis for Special Access Programs (SAP). Your response must detail your 
methodology for complying with DoDM 5205.07 (SAP Security Manual) and DoDI 8510.01 
(Risk Management Framework). This must include the qualifications and number of 
personnel holding active Top Secret clearances with nuclear enterprise experience, the 
accreditation status of your facilities for processing Top Secret/Restricted Data, and your 
documented processes for managing CUI, NATO, and CNWDI material.
3. Describe in detail the steps you would take to perform a Nuclear Surety Cross Check 
Analysis on a system undergoing modernization with new components or hardware. 
Responses should speak to the technical approach to verifying the modified system remains 
compliant with AFMAN 91-119/AFMAN 91-118. This response must include analyzing 
emergent vulnerabilities introduced at the hardware, software, and network interface levels 
and assessing electromagnetic interference and other environmental factors to prevent 
impacts on safety-critical components.

PRE-SOLICITATION NON-COMPETITIVE –  
Notice of Intent to Sole Source 
1. SOLICITATION NUMBER: 75N98026Q00234 
 
2. TITLE: External Institutional Review Board (IRB) Services for Multi-Site 
Studies 
3. RESPONSE DATE: May 5, 2026, at 9:00 am EDT.  
 
4. PRIMARY POINT OF CONTACT: 
Nicholas Capobianco 
nicholas.capobianco@nih.gov  
 
I. INTRODUCTION: 
THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NON-COMPETITIVE (NOTICE OF INTENT) 
SYNOPSIS TO AWARD A CONTRACT WITHOUT PROVIDING FOR FULL OR 
OPEN COMPETITION (INCLUDING BRAND-NAME).  
 
The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), Division of Intramural 
Research (DIR), requires continued Institutional Review Board (IRB) services to 
support ongoing multi-site clinical research studies conducted under Investigational 
Device Exemption (IDE) and Investigational New Drug (IND) protocols. These studies 
involve multiple participating sites and require centralized IRB oversight in accordance 
with NIH policy. 
The NIH Intramural IRB is currently unable to serve as the IRB of record for certain 
NHLBI multi-site studies, including those with existing reliance on a commercial IRB 
and those requiring continuity through study closeout. As a result, NHLBI requires the 
services of an external IRB to ensure uninterrupted regulatory oversight, subject safety, 
and data integrity. 
 
 
II. NORTH AMERICAN INDUSTRY CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM (NAICS) 
CODE and SET ASIDE STATUS 
NAICS Code: 541990 – All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services 
Size Standard: $19.5 million 
This acquisition is not set aside for small business. 
 
 
III. REGULATORY AUTHORITY  
The resultant contract will include all applicable provisions and clauses in effect through 
the Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2024-07 dated 08-29-2024. 

This acquisition is conducted under the procedures as prescribed in FAR Part 12—
Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services and FAR Part 13—
Simplified Acquisition Procedures. 
 
IV. STATUTORY AUTHORITY 
This acquisition is for a commercial service and is conducted under the authority of FAR 
13.106-1(b)(1)—Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will 
Satisfy Agency Requirements. 
 
V. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT: 
Purchase Description: 
The Contractor shall provide IRB services on an as-needed basis, including but not 
limited to: 
• Initial and continuing review of multi-site study protocols 
• Review of investigators and sub-investigators 
• Review of informed consent forms (ICFs), including site-specific language 
• Review of recruitment materials and subject-facing documents 
• Review of protocol amendments and modifications 
• Review of reportable events requiring full board review 
• Site closeout activities 
• Administrative reviews and changes 
• Emergency use reviews, as required 
Salient Characteristics: 
The required services must meet the following minimum characteristics: 
• Ability to serve as the IRB of record for ongoing multi-site FDA-regulated 
clinical studies (IDE/IND) 
• Capability to maintain continuity of IRB oversight for active protocols without 
disruption 
• Existing infrastructure to support reliance agreements across multiple study sites 
• Compliance with all applicable federal regulations, including 45 CFR 46 and 21 
CFR 56 
• Ability to support ongoing reporting, amendments, and closeout activities for 
studies currently under review 
• Secure handling of sensitive human subjects research information 
 
PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: 
June 1, 2026 – May 31, 2027 
 
PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: 
Services will be performed remotely via electronic communication between the 
Contractor and NHLBI personnel. 

VI. CONTRACTING WITHOUT PROVIDING FOR FULL OR OPEN 
COMPETITION (INCLUDING BRAND-NAME) DETERMINATION 
The Government intends to award a sole source contract to: 
Advarra, Inc. 
6100 Merriweather Drive, Suite 600 
Columbia, Maryland 21044 
This determination is based on the need for continuity of IRB oversight for ongoing 
multi-site clinical studies currently under review by Advarra. Transitioning to a different 
IRB provider at this stage would introduce unacceptable risks, including disruption to 
regulatory oversight, potential impacts to subject safety, and compromise of data 
integrity. 
Existing reliance agreements and the history of oversight associated with these studies 
further necessitate continued use of the current IRB of record through study completion. 
 
VII. CLOSING STATEMENT 
THIS SYNOPSIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. However, 
interested parties may identify their interest and capability to respond to this notice. 
A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon 
responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responsible 
sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation which shall be 
considered by the agency. 
Responses must include sufficient detail to demonstrate the capability to meet the 
requirement and must include pricing information, delivery timelines, business size 
status, and proof of active SAM registration. 
All responses must be received by the closing date and time of this announcement and 
must reference the solicitation number, 75N98026Q00234. Responses must be submitted 
electronically to Nicholas Capobianco, Contract Specialist at 
nicholas.capobianco@nih.gov.

Introduction: 
Mobile Command and Control Systems (MC2S) Branch has the responsibility of acquiring 
and sustaining mobile C2 systems in support of the U.S. Air Force and Department of 
Defense. The MC2S Branch is conducting market research through this Sources Sought 
Request for Information (RFI) for the intended competition of the MC2S requirement. A 
Classiﬁed Industry Day to include one-on-one sessions is notionally planned for the mid-
July timeframe, but subject to change.  Conﬁrmation of dates and attendance instructions 
for Industry Day will be determined and announced separately after responses to this RFI 
are reviewed.  
This is a request for information only and does not constitute a request for quote (RFQ) or 
request for proposal (RFP), or a promise to issue an RFQ or RFP in the future.  
General Information: 
Please provide the following information in response to this RFI: 
- Company Name 
- Company Address 
- Company Point of Contact (POC) 
- CAGE Code 
- NAICS Code(s) 
- Company Status as Large or Small Business 
- Company Facility Clearance Level 
To the maximum extent possible, please submit non-proprietary information. Any 
proprietary information submitted shall be identiﬁed as such and handled/protected in 
accordance with applicable Government regulations. The Government requests responses 
to the questions below. Respondents are welcome to provide additional information not 
speciﬁcally requested below. 
The Government will accept unclassiﬁed and classiﬁed responses. The Government will 
provide email addresses where classiﬁed information can be sent upon request.  Please do 
not submit responses greater than 20 pages of original text responses, and no more than 
20 pages of general organizational description materials (brochures or other marketing 
materials). 
Request for Information: 
1. Please provide responses to the following questions that summarize your 
organization’s ability to meet mission-speciﬁc capabilities, ability to sustain 
capabilities, facility capabilities and your ability to meet security requirements. 

2. Mission-speciﬁc capability questions: 
a. What is your organization’s ability to design, integrate, produce, and sustain 
mobile command and control systems-of-systems?  Please provide 
examples of experience in this mission area. 
b. Please provide additional details and experience in the following areas: 
i. System engineering of mobile C2 systems, in particular experience 
with system-of-systems integration.  
ii. Integrating, testing, managing, and sustaining classiﬁed systems.  
iii. Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP). Please detail experience hardening and 
testing systems (IT/comm systems, power systems, HVAC systems, 
etc.), vehicles/transportation capabilities IAW MIL-STD-188-125. 
iv. Mobile, transportable, or ﬁxed power generation systems. 
v. HVAC systems, in particular designing mobile or transportable HVAC 
systems with sizing and space limitations 
vi. Water puriﬁcation systems 
vii. Satellite communications systems, both commercial and military 
viii. Radio systems (RF/HF/UHF etc.), both commercial and military 
ix. Other secure communications capabilities. 
c. Please detail experience partnering, coordinating, and/or working with other 
capability providers (companies or other organizations) to integrate 
capabilities into system-of-system platforms.  
3. System Sustainment questions: 
a. What is your organization’s ability and experience to provide on-going 
sustainment of the systems described in the mission-speciﬁc questions?  
i. Experience conducting periodic depot maintenance (PDM), depot 
level repairs, ﬁeld level repairs (both emergency and routine), or 
equivalent actions.  
ii. Experience developing and/or providing training for delivered systems.  
b. Experience with documentation. Detail experience developing technical 
manuals, network interface documentation, system speciﬁcation 
documentation, engineering drawings, engineering models (MBSE), or other 
relevant data. 
4. Facility and Security questions: 
a. Does the company have cleared facilities? If so, to what level(s) is the facility 
cleared? What networks and/or secure communications capabilities are in 
the facility? Does the company have cleared production and/or maintenance 
spaces within the facility? 

b. Does the company have experience with Government Owned Contractor 
Operated (GOCO) facilities? If so, please provide details on management of a 
GOCO facility. 
c. Please provide examples of current or recent performance of classiﬁed 
requirements or contracts to the best of your ability while providing this 
information at the unclassiﬁed level.  
5. Industry Day attendance: 
a. Please provide whether your company plans to attend the MC2S Industry 
Day. 
b. Please provide whether your company requests a one-on-one session with 
the MC2S Branch for questions.  
i. Industry Day location and dates will be determined after responses to 
this RFI have been reviewed. Details will be provided in a separate 
announcement to industry. For planning purposes, the notional 
Industry Day timeframe is mid-July at Hanscom AFB, Bedford, MA.

Consolidated Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
PROJECT TITLE: Application Arsenal (AA) Enterprise Engineering and Lifecycle Support 
1.0 TASK ORDER PURPOSE 
The purpose of this Task Order is to procure engineering, software development, technical 
services, and program management for the continued design, implementation, security, 
and sustainment of the Application Arsenal (AA) enterprise service. The primary objective is 
to deliver comprehensive lifecycle support to ensure the system operates securely and 
effectively, meeting the evolving needs of the warfighter and government personnel. 
2.0 SCOPE 
The scope of this effort includes the full lifecycle of systems engineering and software 
sustainment for the AA platform. The contractor shall provide all necessary personnel, 
materials, and services to perform the tasks outlined in this PWS. The primary technical 
environment for this effort is the Overmatch Software Armory (OSA); however, work may be 
directed to other government-mandated DevSecOps pipelines (e.g., ORION) as required. 
This contract is intended to be the primary support vehicle for the Application Arsenal 
platform. The performance requirements described below may be initiated and funded by 
diverse DoD Components. The contractor shall support all tasks as directed by the 
Contracting Officer's Representative (COR), provided the work is within the scope of this 
PWS. 
3.0 BACKGROUND 
The Naval Information Warfare Center Pacific (NIWC-PAC) established the Application 
Arsenal (AA) to provide critical software delivery capabilities to the fleet. 
Application Arsenal (AA) is the enterprise distribution, update, and installation service for 
software at the tactical edge. It enables software developed in a software factory to be sent 
Over-The-Air (OTA) to the edge across many different environments. AA currently deploys 
software to Agile Core Services (ACS), the USMC Common Hosting Environment (CHE), the 
Overmatch Production Environment (OPE), Five Eyes (FVEY) partners, and autonomous 
vehicles, with more systems projected to come online. 
This PWS defines the requirements for contractor-provided services essential to enable the 
design, implementation, and sustainment of the AA enterprise service for a diverse set of 
DoD-wide stakeholders, including the Rapid Capabilities Office (RCO), the Portfolio 
Acquisition Executive for Robotic and Autonomous Systems (PAE RAS), the Portfolio 
Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS), the U.S. Marine Corps (USMC), and Naval 
Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA). 

4.0 APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS 
The contractor shall comply with all documents referenced in the performance 
requirements that the contractor will have to use or comply with in performance of this 
PWS tasking. This list is not exhaustive, and other documents may be specified in 
individual Task Orders. 
• NIST SP 800-53, "Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and 
Organizations" 
• Applicable Department of Defense (DoD) and Department of the Navy (DoN) 
regulations, directives, and instructions. 
5.0 PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS 
5.1 Engineering & Integration Requirements 
• 5.1.1 AA Development: The contractor shall provide the planning, development, 
testing, and integration required for all new AA releases and enhancements. 
o 5.1.1.1 Capability Development: Efforts shall include modernizing existing 
deployment architectures by leveraging and integrating with the Overmatch 
Software Armory (OSA) DevSecOps pipeline, deploying with Agile Core 
Services (ACS), and ensuring alignment with the Common Hosting 
Environment (CHE) and other shared government platforms. The contractor 
shall design and implement scalable, secure integration pathways for Navy 
programs of strategic importance, ensuring compliance with mandated 
DevSecOps tooling, security guardrails, and enterprise release practices, 
including interoperability with Five Eyes (FVEY) partners. 
o 5.1.1.2 Cybersecurity Engineering: The contractor shall engineer and 
integrate required cybersecurity controls into new AA releases in alignment 
with Risk Management Framework (RMF) standards. Deliverables shall 
include Security Control Traceability Matrices (SCTMs), Plans of Action and 
Milestones (POAMs), and other documentation required for the Authority to 
Operate (ATO). 
o 5.1.1.3 Fielding: The contractor shall perform the installation, configuration, 
and testing necessary to field new releases across all authorized operational 
environments for CONUS and OCONUS locations, ashore and afloat. This 
effort shall include robust system validation through Factory Acceptance 
Testing (FAT), Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), and System Operational 
Verification Testing (SOVT). 

• 5.1.2 Software Delivery Pipeline Integration and Replication 
o 5.1.2.1 DevSecOps Engineering Services: The contractor shall provide 
engineering services to design, implement, and integrate secure DevSecOps 
pipeline capabilities within the Government-designated DevSecOps 
environment (e.g., OSA, ACS). 
o 5.1.2.2 Secure Software Distribution: The contractor shall develop and 
validate secure methods for efficient transfer and replication of software 
artifacts to remote and distributed environments, including ashore, afloat, 
autonomous, and cloud-hosted domains. 
• 5.1.3 Infrastructure, Command and Control (C2), Autonomous Systems, and 
Cross-Domain Solution (CDS) Integration 
o 5.1.3.1 CDS Engineering and Integration: The contractor shall integrate with 
existing infrastructure and established Cross-Domain Solutions (CDS) to 
provide the secure, bi-directional data transfer capabilities necessary to 
support distributed autonomous operations across disparate security 
domains. 
o 5.1.3.2 Integration Support for Autonomous Systems: The contractor shall 
support the integration of edge servers, autonomous vehicle platforms, and 
related mission systems with currently fielded and emerging technologies. 
This includes the integration of payloads and sensors common to unmanned 
and autonomous systems. 
o 5.1.3.3 Support for Autonomous Operations and Data Exchange: The 
contractor shall leverage and enhance existing infrastructure to support 
Command and Control (C2) data exchange for real-time operational 
scenarios, exercises, and mission requirements. This includes data to and 
from autonomous systems, such as mission tasking, telemetry, and sensor 
data. 
 
• 5.1.4 Rapid Agile Development & Integration Support (RADIS) (RDT&E): The 
contractor shall provide a rapid technical response to issues employing engineering 
techniques to solve problems using an agile software approach to develop, test, and 
integrate new C4I capabilities to meet identified Science & Technology (S&T) gaps 
for the warfighter. 
5.2 Support Requirements 
• 5.2.1 Application Arsenal (AA) Sustainment: The contractor shall provide 
comprehensive support to sustain the functionality, security, and operational 
availability of all fielded AA releases. 

o 5.2.1.1 Operations & Maintenance (O&M): The contractor shall operate, 
maintain, and sustain all fielded releases, including proactive monitoring, 
repairs, and routine updates. 
o 5.2.1.2 System Administration: CSWF-qualified personnel shall perform 
routine system administration on Linux and Windows servers. 
o 5.2.1.3 Cyber & Information Assurance (IA): The contractor shall provide 
operational IA support, including managing security patches, conducting 
vulnerability scanning and remediation, and preparing all required artifacts 
for cybersecurity compliance. The contractor is not responsible for managing 
the eMASS ATO record. 
o 5.2.1.4 Help Desk: The contractor shall provide help desk support, including 
remote and on-site assistance. 
• 5.2.2 Sustainment of Fielded Capabilities: The contractor shall provide 
engineering and technical support for the sustainment of previously fielded 
software, infrastructure, and cross-domain capabilities, including support for 
exercises and operational events. 
• 5.2.3 RADIS (O&M): The contractor shall provide a rapid technical response to 
enhance, upgrade, test, and integrate C4I capabilities to meet identified S&T gaps 
for the warfighter, developing user stories in OSA or other Government-mandated 
environments. 
• 5.2.4 Training and Logistics Support: 
o 5.2.4.1 Training Support: The contractor shall provide user and 
administrator training for sustained systems. 
o 5.2.4.2 Logistics Support: The contractor shall provide logistics support to 
maintain operational readiness, including tracking software licenses and 
managing version releases. 
• 5.2.5 Technical Data and Reporting: The contractor shall generate, update, and 
maintain a complete and accurate Technical Data Package (TDP) for all supported 
systems and report regularly to government stakeholders. 
6.0 TRAVEL 
No travel is anticipated on this Task Order. Should travel be required, it will be authorized 
separately by the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR). The following long distance 
travel is estimated: 

The Contractor shall attend support meetings, conferences, workshops, and fieldings at 
CONUS and OCONUS locations in support of the SOW requirements. Travel to locations 
within United States Africa Command (USAFRICOM), United States Central Command 
(USCENTCOM), United States European Command (USEUCOM), United States Indo-
Pacific Command (USINDOPACOM), United States Northern Command (USNORTHCOM), 
United States Southern Command (USSOUTHCOM) may be required. All travel 
requirements (including plans, agenda, itinerary, or dates) shall be pre-approved by the 
Government, and is on a strictly cost reimbursable basis. All travel is expected to originate 
from San Diego, CA. 
Contractor personnel must adhere to all current DoD, SECNAV , OPNAV , and NIWC Pacific 
instructions related to foreign travel. 
7.0 PROPERTY REQUIREMENTS 
No Government Furnished Property (GFP) is anticipated for this Task Order. 
8.0 SECURITY 
The work performed under this effort is anticipated to be up to the SECRET level, with 
potential for personnel to provide services within laboratories and vessels classified up to 
TOP SECRET. The contractor personnel will require access to classified data, information, 
meetings, and spaces. The contractor shall adhere to all security requirements outlined in 
the DD Form 254, Contract Security Classification Specification. 
9.0 DELIVERABLES 
The contractor shall provide the data deliverables specified in the Contract Data 
Requirements List (CDRL), DD Form 1423, attached to the Task Order. This includes, but is 
not limited to, a Software Development Plan (SDP), Monthly Status Reports, and Technical 
Data Packages (TDP). 
10.0 PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS SUMMARY

SUPPORT SERVICES FOR HEWLETT PACKARD ENTERPRISE HIGH PERFORMANCE COMPUTE NODE 
 
PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
 
FOR 
 
SUPPORT SERVICES FOR HEWLETT PACKARD ENTERPRISE HIGH PERFORMANCE COMPUTE NODE 
 
 
PART 1 
GENERAL INFORMATION 
 
 
1.1
 General: This is a non-personnel services contract to provide on-site Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) High-
Performance Compute (HPC) system administration support services to be provided to the Naval Oceanographic Office 
(NAVOCEANO or NAVO) for a period of one year and is similar to the system administration support services provided 
on contract N0018925P0496. The Government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service 
providers performing the services herein  
 
 
1.2 Background 
1.2.1 The Naval Oceanographic Office (NAVOCEANO) collects, processes, and disseminates complex oceanographic 
data, forecasts, and products to Fleet users using HPC technologies including Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine 
Learning (ML) algorithms.  NAVOCEANO requires specialized services for the system administration, operational 
support, and cybersecurity compliance of a new Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) High-Performance Compute (HPC) 
cluster. This system is a strategic asset designed to run advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) 
algorithms. The architecture consists of cutting-edge technologies, including GPU-accelerated compute nodes, an HPE 
Slingshot high-speed interconnect, a Lustre-based parallel file system, and an image-based operating system deployment 
infrastructure. Due to the new technology and complexity of these components, expert contractor support is necessary to 
ensure the system's stability, security, and optimal performance to meet mission-critical objectives 
 
 
1.3 Description of Requirement 
The contractor shall provide specialized support services for system administration,
 operational support, and cybersecurity 
compliance of the HPE HPC system.  The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, 
and other items necessary to perform the services. 
 
 
1.4 Period of Performance, Place of Performance and Hours of Operation  
 
1.4.1 The period of performance shall be 12 months after award.  
1.4.2 The contractor shall perform services at NAVOCEANO. NAVOCEANO is located at Stennis Space Center, 
Mississippi. 
1.4.3 Recognized Holidays/Government Closure:  Federal law (5 U.S.C. 6103) establishes the public holidays for 
Federal employees.  Any other day designated by federal statute, executive order, presidential proclamation and/or local 
determinations relating to adverse weather conditions, national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar 
Government directed facility closings may require office closure.  During such periods of closure, contractor employees 
will not be allowed to work, nor will the contractor be compensated, however, offsite work is allowed, with Contracting

employee’s effort through the company’s internal management system; this management system shall provide project

Special Notice
Information Innovation Office
Future Program: Decentralized Artificial Intelligence 
through Controlled Emergence (DICE)
DARPA-SN-26-65
April 21, 2026

DARPA-SN-26-65
PROGRAM ANNOUNCEMENT
The purpose of this Special Notice is to provide public notification of additional research areas of 
interest to the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Information Innovation 
Office (I2O), specifically for the forthcoming Decentralized Artificial Intelligence through 
Controlled Emergence (DICE) program by I2O Program Manager, Susmit Jha. 
If released, the solicitation will be made available at https://SAM.gov. 
PROGRAM BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES
Future conflicts will unfold at machine speed in highly dynamic and contested environments. This 
will require autonomous, multi-agent artificial intelligence (AI) systems to create an asymmetric 
battlespace advantage and reduce risk to warfighters.
The DICE program seeks to develop the theory and algorithms for decentralized coordination and 
local inference control to enable a scalable, adaptive, and resilient collective of heterogeneous AI 
agents that can autonomously execute sustained long-time-horizon missions in contested 
environments while remaining under our control. In contrast to small-scale, rigid, and fragile 
centralized orchestration or the high-risk unpredictable nature of ad hoc compositions of AI agents, 
DICE aims to harness the scalability and adaptability of self-organizing systems while minimizing 
risks and ensuring that the collective behavior remains predictable and aligned with intended 
outcomes. This approach mirrors the principles of decentralized self-organization that underpin 
the internet's own scalability and resilience, where robust global behavior emerges from simple, 
local rules.
DICE aims to develop a decentralized AI architecture suitable for rapidly evolving, unpredictable, 
and contested environments. With this architecture, AI agents can dynamically form teams using 
peer-to-peer coordination to execute complex missions. This coordination will be robust to failure 
or compromise of individual agents, as well as to “rogue” AI agents that might develop misaligned 
instrumental goals. The local inference control on each AI agent will ensure role coherence of 
individual agents and constrain the emergent behavior of the collective to maintain alignment with 
commander’s intent over the long term, even across multiple inference steps. DICE will seek to 
expand and leverage the theory of self-organizing systems and distributed consensus algorithms, 
together with recent breakthroughs in controlling the internal reasoning and inference of AI 
foundation models at inference-time. 
DICE aims to advance AI beyond individual agent capabilities by fostering system-level capability 
that emerges from the interactions between agents. This controlled emergence ensures DICE AI 
agents remain on mission, maintain doctrine, suppress misbehaviors, and remain resilient to agent 
loss or compromise. The program’s scope does not include the development and deployment of 
autonomous systems in the real world. The program will use simulation environments to 
demonstrate DICE architectures in Department of War-relevant use-cases, targeting measurable 
gains in scalability, adaptability, and resilience against both benign failures and adversarial attacks.

A. Introduction:  

The US Geological Survey (USGS), Denver Argon Geochronology Lab (DAGL), Denver, CO has a requirement for the automated operation of mass spectrometers and peripheral hardware (e.g. valves, lasers). The DAGL aims to achieve this by developing new, customized automation software modules built using a commercially available programming environment designed to enable construction of applications with graphical user interfaces for hardware automation, such as LabVIEW or an equivalent environment. This effort requires support for developing the overall application architecture, programming the custom automation software, and training laboratory staff in its construction, use, and maintenance.

B. Background: 

	

The US Geological Survey’s (USGS) Denver Argon Geochronology Lab (DAGL), located at the Geology, Geophysics, and Geochemistry Science Center (GGGSC), produces 40Ar/39Ar geochronology data for multiple USGS Programs, including the Mineral Resources Program and National Cooperative Geologic Mapping Program, among others. These data benefit a variety of stakeholders, from federal and state government agencies, to industry and academia.

The DAGL historically used a Macintosh-based, closed-source software application called Mass Spec for operating analytical instruments and associated peripheral hardware. Changes in USGS information technology (IT) regulations forced the DAGL to move away from Macintosh systems in the lab in 2022, and the developer of Mass Spec is nearing retirement and has indicated support will terminate. In response, the DAGL purchased a new open-source software application called Pychron that was being embraced by the 40Ar/39Ar community at that time. Although Pychron has allowed for intermittent operation of the lab, it has proven to not be sufficient for our needs. The Pychron developer is not regularly available for required bug fixes (which are abundant, especially following regular mandatory IT patching), and while the code is open-source, we have found the documentation is not sufficient for us to contribute meaningfully to code maintenance, and the lack of transparency of calculations has introduced significant issues for data management and quality.

The pivot to develop a customized LabVIEW (or equivalent)-based software application has the benefit of direct involvement by laboratory staff, enabling ongoing updates and improvements to be made after they are fully trained in the application. We aim to utilize an environment that represents a major software development environment and framework that is successfully deployed as customized applications in similar USGS labs (e.g. Denver Noble Gas lab, Moffett Argon Lab). We intend to build on the shoulders of these existing customized LabVIEW (or equivalent) applications to create new software specific to our analytical systems, but we do not currently have the expertise to do this.

C. Definitions:

40Ar/39Ar geochronology – an analytical method that involves the measurement of isotopes of argon in a material to determine a geologic age.

LabVIEW– a graphical programming environment and software framework provided for purchase by National Instruments that allows users to create custom applications (including graphical user interfaces) for hardware automation/control, and data collection.

D. Scope:

The USGS DAGL requires a complete LabVIEW (or equivalent)-based, custom software solution for acquiring data on the Thermo Scientific Argus VI mass spectrometers located within the DAGL. While developing the software, the Contractor shall actively involve laboratory personnel in the design and implementation of the new application(s) and simultaneously train them in the programming environment with a focus on components that will aid them in the long-term operation and maintenance of the software application(s). In addition to communicating with and operating the Argus mass spectrometers, the software application(s) will communicate with and/or control a variety of hardware peripherals, including Photon Machines lasers (and motorized sample stages), pressure gauges, ion pumps, Agilent DAQs, and thermocouples. The software application(s) will appropriately store analytical data and instrument metadata in files or a database, as needed by lab personnel. The software will integrate instrument/hardware communications and analytical data storage with required sample metadata for 40Ar/39Ar geochronology into an appropriate graphical user interface. 

E.  Technical Requirements.

The Contractor shall provide the following:

Basic Training. Train lab personnel in basic programming environment concepts and design patterns, with a focus on software components relevant to instrument control and data acquisition and storage.

Create modules in programming environment for communications with and control of:

Thermo Scientific Argus VI Mass Spectrometers

Pressure gauges

Ion pumps

Agilent DAQs for control of valves and readback of thermocouples

Photon Machines CO2 and UV laser systems

Create graphical user interface for sample metadata entry

Create module for data acquisition, to include:

Graphical user interface for building and executing run sequences 

Live instrument feedback (e.g., visuals of valve states and plots of data as they are acquired)

Create module for data storage to files and/or database

Create complete solution (including graphical user interface) for integrating the above modules

Lab personnel will be proficient in programming environment such that they can maintain and modify the resulting software application(s).

Modules will be accepted when they are able to control each piece of hardware.

User interface sufficiently captures sample metadata and stores in appropriate locations.

Data can be accurately and reliably acquired in an automated run sequence.

Data are accurately and reliably stored in appropriate file formats and/or database.

The complete solution is user-friendly and accessible to lab personnel. Source code will be version controlled and stored in one or more USGS DAGL GitLab repositories.

Executive Summary 
This is the third appendix to NASA SBIR/STTR Program FY2026-2027 Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) and 
solicits proposals for the Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) Phase I funding opportunity.   
Chapter 6 of this appendix contains the proposal submission instructions and Chapter 9 contains the technical 
research topics. Instructions for how to prepare your proposal can be found in the BAA 
(https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/bf991b7587b1438ca7930a9b840635dc/view ).  The chapter numbers align 
to the chapters in the BAA and can be used to locate additional information within the BAA. In any instance where 
specific requirements in this appendix conflict with requirements in the BAA, the specific requirements in th is 
appendix take precedence for this opportunity. 
Important Dates 
Proposals Due: May 21, 2026 by 5:00 PM ET 
Note that the submission open period is shorter than prior years. 
Deadline for guaranteed response from the Help Desk: May 20, 2026 by 5:00 PM ET 
Multiple Submissions 
NASA will not accept more than two (2) proposal packages from any one offeror for this funding opportunity. See 
sections 3.2 in this appendix and section 4 in the BAA.

3. Proposal Preparation Instructions and Requirements 
3.2 Multiple Proposal Submissions 
Each proposal must be based on a unique innovation, limited in scope to just one subtopic, and submitted only under 
that one subtopic. You may not submit more than two (2) proposals to the funding opportunity in this 
appendix. You may submit more than one unique proposal to the same subtopic; however, you must not submit the 
same (or substantially equivalent) proposal to more than one subtopic. If you submit substantially equivalent 
proposals to several subtopics, NASA may decline all such proposals.  
4. Method of Selection and Evaluation Criteria 
The rubric containing all evaluation criteria is available in attachment 26 B.1 STTR. 
5. Considerations for Contracting and Additional Information 
No additional content, requirements, or exceptions beyond information in BAA.  
6. Submission of Proposals  
6.1 How to Submit your Proposal Package 
NASA uses electronically supported business processes for the SBIR/STTR program. You must have internet access 
and an email address. NASA will not accept paper submissions.  NASA’s electronic systems for submission and 
contract management are not document repositories.  NASA follows federal regulations for records management and 
disposal (NPR 1441.1E). 
6.1.1 Electronic Submission of Proposals 
NASA will be using ProSAMS for the submission of these proposal packages. ProSAMS requires firm registration 
and login. To access ProSAMS, go to https://prosams.nasa.gov/. To submit proposals to this appendix, select “STTR 
2026B-I” from the solicitation type dropdown as you start a new proposal.  
 
NASA recommends that an authorized small business representative be the person to register the firm and complete 
the required firm level forms. They will be the only person allowed to edit the firm level forms.   
 
For successful submission of a complete proposal package, you must complete all required and applicable forms and 
upload the required documents per the submission requirements indicated in ProSAMS.

6.1.2 Deadline for Proposal Package Submission 
NASA must receive your proposal package for STTR Phase I no later than 5:00 p.m. ET on Thursday, May 
21, 2026, via ProSAMS.  
 
You are responsible for ensuring that all files constituting the proposal package are uploaded and endorsed prior to 
the deadline. If a proposal package is not received by the 5:00 p.m. ET deadline, NASA will determine the 
proposal package to be incomplete and will not evaluate it. Start the submission process early to allow sufficient 
time to upload the complete proposal package.  
 
If you wait to submit a proposal package near the deadline, you are at risk of not completing the required 
uploads and endorsements by the required deadline, and NASA may decline the proposal package.   
6.1.3 Proposal Package Submission 
Upload all components of a proposal package using the Proposal Submissions module in ProSAMS. The designated 
business representative and principal investigator must endorse the proposal package.  All transactions via ProSAMS 
are encrypted for security purposes.  
 
If your proposal contains ITAR/EAR information, it may be submitted via ProSAMS. 
Do not submit security/password-protected PDF files, as reviewers may not be able to open and read these 
files. NASA will decline proposal packages containing security/password-protected PDF files and they will not 
be evaluated. 
 
You are responsible for virus checking all files prior to submission. NASA may decline any proposal package that 
contains a file with a detected virus.

designated Business Official’s email address as provided on the proposal package cover sheet. If you do not receive 
a proposal package acknowledgment after submission, immediately contact the NASA SBIR/STTR Help 
Desk at agency-sbir@mail.nasa.gov.  
6.1.5 Withdrawal of Proposal Packages 
Prior to the close of submissions, you may withdraw proposal packages. To withdraw a proposal package after the 
deadline, the designated small business representative must send written notification via email to agency-
sbir@mail.nasa.gov. 
6.1.6 Service of Protests 
Protests, as defined in section FAR 33.101 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation, that are filed directly with an 
agency, and copies of any protests that are filed with the Government Accountability Office (GAO), must be served 
on the Contracting Officer (addressed as follows) by obtaining written and dated acknowledgment of receipt from: 
 
  

NASA SBIR/STTR Program 
FY26-27 BAA Appendix 26A-I SBIR 
4 
 
Kenneth Albright  
 NASA Shared Services Center 
 Building 1111, Jerry Hlass Road 
 Stennis Space Center, MS 39529 
Agency-SBIR-STTRSolicitation@mail.nasa.gov 
 
The copy of any protest must be received in the office designated above within one day of filing a protest with the 
GAO. 
6.2 Phase II Information 
If you are awarded a Phase I contract, you will be eligible to submit a proposal for an SBIR/STTR Phase II follow -
on contract. NASA will send instructions directly to you with information on how to submit your Phase II 
proposal(s). You will receive details on the due date, content, and submission requirements for Phase II proposals. 
The Phase II proposal submission will open approximately 60 days prior to the proposal due date stated in your 
contract.  
 
If you submit your Phase II proposal outside of the timeframe specified by NASA, your proposal will be declined 
without evaluation. Additional guidance can be found in your Phase I contract (Request for Proposal for Phase II 
Follow-on Contract). 
7. Proposal, Scientific and Technical Information Sources  
No additional content, requirements, or exceptions beyond information in BAA.  

NASA SBIR/STTR Program 
FY26-27 BAA Appendix 26A-I SBIR 
5 
 
8. Submissions Checklist 
For assistance in completing your Phase I proposal package, use the following checklist:  
□ The technical proposal and innovation are submitted for one subtopic only.  
□ The entire proposal package is submitted consistent with the requirements outlined in BAA chapter 3. 
□ Proposal Contact Information 
□ Proposal Certifications

consultants (if applicable)

□ The technical proposal does not exceed a total of 15 standard 8.5- by 11-inch pages with one-inch margins 
and follows the format requirements (BAA section 3.1.4).  
□ All required letters/documentation are included. 
□ A letter of commitment from the appropriate government official if the research effort requires use 
of government resources (BAA sections 3.1.5.4 and 5.13).  
□ A letter from the Small Business Official explaining why the SBIR research project requires the 
use of government resources, if the effort requires government resources (BAA sections 3.1.5.4 
and 5.13)

□ Total proposed funding for the effort does not exceed $225,000 (BAA section 1.3), and if requesting

1.0 INTRODUCTION  
 
1.1 The Air Combat Command Head quarters (ACC HQ)  is the primary force provider of 
combat airpower to America's warfighting commands. To support the global implementation of 
national security strategy, ACC operates fighter, reconnaissance, battle- management, and 
electronic-combat aircraft. It also provide s command, control, communications, and intelligence 
systems, and conducts global information operations.  
 
1.2 As a force provider, ACC organizes, trains, equips, and maintains combat-ready forces for 
rapid deployment and employment while ensuring strategic air defense forces are ready to meet 
the challenges of peacetime air sovereignty and wartime air defense. Additionally, ACC develops 
strategy, doctrine, concept s, tactics, and procedures for air and space- power employment. The 
command provides conventional and information warfare forces to all unified commands to ensure 
air, space and information superiority for warfighters and national decision-makers. The command 
can also be called upon to assist national agencies with intelligence, surveillance,  and crisis 
response capabilities. 
 
2.0 CSO BACKGROUND AND APPROACH 
 
2.1 This Commercial Solutions Openings (CSOs), issued in accordance with DFARS 212.70, 
is a competitive solicitation seeking proposals for innovative, commercial technologies and 
services that accelerate attainment of capabilities detailed in Attachment 7 to meet ACC’s mission. 
 
2.2 ACC HQ intends to obtain innovative  solutions or potential new capabilities that fulfill 
requirements, close capability gaps, or provide potential technology advancements. Solutions may 
include existing technologies or procedures, not currently in use by the United States Air Force 
(USAF), that would enhance or streamline USAF mission capabilities. "Innovative", as defined in 
DFARS 212.70, means any technology, process, application, or method, including research and 
development, which is new as of the date of proposal submission. 
 
2.3 This CSO seeks the best commercial approaches to meet various technology objectives of 
ACC. All items, technologies, and services acquired using this CSO will be treated as commercial 
items. The Government encourages white-paper proposals that span a wide spectrum of possible 
technical and business solutions in response to the specific technology topics listed in Attachment 
7. The Government reserves the right to award to any combination of proposals which offer the 
best overall value to the Government, and to oversee all processes and approaches once initiated. 
Awards of efforts as a result of this announcement will be in the form of FAR Part 12 contracts or 
other transactions (OT) as codified in 10 U.S.C. § 4022. 
 
3.0 GENERAL INFORMATION 
 
3.1 Funding is not currently available for the topics provided in Attachment 7. Industry 
responses will be carefully reviewed and prioritized, with funding sought by ACC HQ to pursue 
innovative and optimal solutions. The price and affordability of proposed technologies will 
contribute to ACC’s interest in pursuing proposed solutions. Any awards resulting from this CSO 
will be made based on the evaluation results of a two-phased proposal process described in Section 

Page | 2 
4.0. The Government reserves the right to fund all, some, one, or none of the proposals submitted; 
may elect to fund only part of a submitted proposal; and may incrementally fund any or all awards 
under this CSO. All awards are subject to the availability of funds. 
 
3.2 All coordination and communication between Offerors and the Government will be 
conducted using www.sam.gov
 and the points of contact associated with this CSO, as specified 
below: 
 
POINTS OF CONTACT: Questions regarding the administrative or technical content of this CSO 
and any white paper submissions (reference Para 4.2.1 below) must be forwarded via email to  
ACCAMIC.MFT.CSO@us.af.mil. 
 
4.0 SUBMISSION INFORMATION 
 
4.1 SUBMISSION OVERVIEW. This CSO is open for a period of one calendar year as of the 
posted date on www.sam.gov. Phase I submissions will be accepted at any point during this period. 
Offerors are encouraged to monitor www.sam.gov for any specific calls or amendments to the 
CSO that may have updated information. This CSO will be conducted in two phases.  
 
4.2 TWO-PHASED SUBMISSION. 
 
4.2.1 Phase I. Interested offerors must submit Quad Charts and White Papers prepared following 
the formats at Attachments 1 and 2 respectively  and to the email address noted in Paragraph 3.2 
above. Phase I submissions will be evaluated against criteria as described in Attachment 6 of this 
CSO. All submissions must be unclassified. Phase I submission shall be sent to the POCs listed in 
Section 3.2. 
 
4.2.1.1 Notification of Selection. All offerors providing Phase I submissions will be contacted 
by the Government, either with an email informing them that the effort proposed is not of 
interest to the Government at this time or with a request for a formal price and technical 
proposal (Phase II) by a specific date. 
 
4.2.2 Phase II. Phase II proposals will only be accepted from Offerors who are invited by the 
Contracting Officer to submit a full proposal. In order to be considered for award under Phase II, 
offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at 
www.sam.gov, be 
considered responsible within the meaning of FAR Part 9.1, Responsible Prospective Contractors, 
have a satisfactory performance record, and otherwise be eligible for award based on federal law 
and regulation. 
 
4.2.2.1 Proposal Submission. Upon notification for a proposal by the Contracting Officer, 
offerors have 30 calendar days to prepare and submit a proposal in accordance with the format 
and instructions at Attachments 3-5. 
 
4.2.2.2 Proposal Review, Evaluation and Selection Process . Each proposal will be evaluated 
by the Government and the proposal must stand on its own technical merit. Proposals will be 
evaluated in accordance with the evaluation criteria and process specified in Attachment 6.  

Page | 3 
The primary basis for selecting proposals for acceptance shall be technical, importance to 
agency programs, and funds availability. In order to provide the desired evaluation, qualified 
Government personnel will conduct reviews and (if necessary) convene panels of experts in 
the appropriate areas. IAW DFARS 212.7004 price shall be considered to the extent 
appropriate, but at a minimum, to determine that the price is fair and reasonable. Proposals 
need not be evaluated against each other since they are not submitted in response to a common 
performance work statement or statement of work.

ATTACHMENT 2: WHITE PAPER FORMAT 
 
The White Paper narrative expands on the Quad Chart presentation and must be 8.5 x 11 inches 
with one-inch margins, no longer than five pages, single-spaced, with text in Times New Roman, 
no smaller than 12-point font. All white papers must specify a project title, the Offeror’s 
organization, and the specific topic number associated with the proposal (see Attachment 7). 
Pages exceeding the page limitation will not be read or evaluated. White Papers must not exceed 
a file size of 25 MB. 
 
The White Paper must be limited only to further explanation of the information conveyed in the 
Quad Chart, as deemed necessary by the Offeror. The information should provide sufficient 
information on the research being proposed (e.g. the hypothesis, theories, concept, approaches, 
data measurements, and analysis, etc.) to allow for an assessment by a technical expert. Expand 
as deemed necessary on the following sections of the Quad Chart: Objective; Description of the 
Effort; Benefits of the Proposed Technology; Technical Challenges; Major Goals/Milestones by 
Government fiscal year. Do not include corporate or personnel qualification, past experience, or 
any supplemental information not requested in the Quad Chart. 
 
Offerors shall mark each page of its white paper that contains proprietary information. It is the 
Government’s intention to acquire any data rights necessary to satisfy agency needs; however, this 
will be negotiated on a case -by-case basis with applicable data rights clauses included in any 
resultant contracts.  An offeror may provide with its white paper assertions to restrict, use, release 
or disclosure of data and/or computer software and computer software documentation that will be 
provided in the course of contract performance. Rules governing these assertions are prescribed in 
DFARS clauses 252.227-7013 through 7017 and may be accessed at www.acquisition.gov

III. CREDENTIALS. [Describe the Offeror’s qualifications to perform the proposed work.

ATTACHMENT 4: PRICE PROPOSAL FORMAT 
 
The price proposal must include pricing information sufficiently detailed for meaningful 
evaluation of the proposal. Since the CSO is limited to commercial solutions, detailed costs will 
not be required. For pricing purposes, Offerors should assume a contract or agreement start date 
of approximately 90 days after submission of the proposal. 
 
Since all proposals must offer commercial items, technologies, or services, the requirements of the 
Truthful Cost or Pricing Data Act  are not applicable. However, if the Contracting Officer 
determines necessary to support a determination of a fair and reasonable price, other than certified 
cost and pricing data may be requested. 
 
The responsibility for providing adequate supporting data and attachments lies solely with the 
Offeror. Further, the Offeror must also bear the burden of proof in establishing reasonableness of 
proposed prices; therefore, it is in the Offeror’s best interest to submit a fully supportable and well-
prepared price proposal. 
 
The Offeror shall prepare the Price Proposal (with the exception of the narrative information

AI Effects at the Edge
(AI Capabilities for Modular Mission Payload) 
Assessment Event 

09 JUN 2026 - 11 JUN 2026

Submit NLT 27 APR 2026 
at or before 11:59 PM ET
for consideration
 

U.S. Citizens Only

Purpose
The Cyber Fusion Innovation Center (CFIC), in collaboration with Army Cyber Command (ARCYBER) Technology and Innovation Center (ArCTIC) is in search of industry expertise for the development of an Artificial Intelligence (AI) / Machine Learning (ML) model embedded on a commercial platform. This platform will enable advanced capabilities for modular mission payload (MMP) development and seamless integration with connected sensors. This release documents ArCTIC’s methodology for pursuing, selecting, and assessing such solutions. 

Background/Synopsis
In Fiscal Year 2025, Army Cyber Command (ARCYBER) identified a critical need to collaborate with qualified industry partners to develop and deliver an advanced AI-driven capabilities tool. Current systems are unable to autonomously create and deploy Modular Mission Payloads (MMPs) using AI/ML models, relying instead on manual processes that are both time-consuming and inefficient. This limitation has created operational challenges in integrating mission payloads with connected sensors and achieving real-time adaptability in dynamic environments.

ARCYBER envisions a commercial platform embedded with an AI/ML model that will transform the way mission payloads are developed and deployed. The platform must be capable of pulling techniques from supported data repositories to enhance payload development while also pushing data to repositories to ensure seamless integration and operational readiness. Additionally, the solution must autonomously develop low-sophistication MMPs, reducing the need for manual intervention and accelerating deployment timelines. Finally, the platform must enable the porting of AI-developed payloads to connected sensors, ensuring operational forces can leverage these capabilities effectively.

Requirements and Focus Areas

Functional Requirements

Data Repository Integration: The platform must support pulling and pushing data to/from supported repositories

Modular Mission Payload Development: AI/ML model must autonomously develop low-sophistication MMPs

Sensor Integration: The platform must port AI-developed MMPs to connected sensors

Technical Requirements

AI/ML Model: Embedded AI/ML model capable of autonomous payload development

Platform Compatibility: Commercial platform must support integration with connected sensors

Scalability: Platform must scale to support enterprise-wide operations

Initial Focus Areas

Phase 1 (Prototype) - Demonstrate AI/ML model capabilities for pulling/pushing data and developing MMPs

Phase 2 (Expansion) - Expand platform capabilities to integrate with a broader range of sensors

Technical Approach and Architecture

Proposed Architecture (Offeror Shall Address)

Offerors shall propose a technical architecture that addresses:

AI/ML Model Design: Methodology for embedding AI/ML models on the platform

Data Repository Integration: Approach for pulling/pushing data to/from repositories

MMP Development: Algorithms for autonomous payload development

Sensor Integration: Mechanisms for porting MMPs to connected sensors

DevSecOps & ATO Compliance

Offerors shall demonstrate how their solution will:

Comply with ARCYBER's DevSecOps standards

Achieve Authority to Operate (ATO) through automated security scanning and compliance validation

Implement Containerized Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) for reproducible deployments

Deliverables

Phase 1: Solution Development

Platform: Commercial platform embedded with AI/ML model

Documentation: Architecture, design, and operational guides

Demonstration Environment: Functional prototype showcasing MMP development and sensor integration

Phase 2: Expansion - Enhanced Capabilities: Expanded platform capabilities for broader sensor integration

Why Should You Participate?
ARCYBER seeks to enter into non-FAR-based agreements with Industry, Academic, and National Lab partners whose solutions are favorably evaluated by ARCYBER Subject Matter Experts. As such, these events are considered competitive in the same manner as a Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) or Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO), and solutions will be evaluated independently of one another primarily for technical merit.

What happens after whitepaper submissions? 

(About grading and downselection for a Virtual Demonstration Assessment Event)

The Stakeholder will assign Assessors to an Assessment Team to review, grade, and potentially provide anonymous constructive feedback on whitepapers received by the deadline noted above. This Assessment Team will suggest subsequent down select companies whose white paper solutions have the highest value and feasibility. Then, those companies will be invited to present and/or demonstrate their capability in a private, virtual pitch / demo session hosted through an online platform with Stakeholders and Assessors on a specific date.

Thereafter, prospective solutions will be evaluated through a multi-phased process with the intent to competitively award one or multiple contracts through: CFIC’s B2B Contracting Mechanism through its Partnership Intermediary Agreement (PIA) with the Government, Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs), or other non-Far based agreements for prototype projects in accordance with 10 U.S. Code §2371b, if deemed appropriate and in the Government’s best interest.

Timeline
Phase I: 06 APR 2026 - 27 APR 2026 – Submission Window
Industry, academia, and government partners MUST submit a 6-page submission response whitepaper document through this link – CLICK HERE. Submissions will not be accepted via email. Submit NLT (No Later Than) 11:59 p.m. Eastern on Wednesday, 27 APR 2026.


For more details on submissions, please review the information (including whitepaper submission instructions and template) under the paragraph below titled “How You Can Participate”.

Phase II: 29 APR 2026 - 13 MAY 2026 – Submissions Reviewed for Downselect
Submitted documents will be placed in review based on rubric parameters identified through the requirements and criteria included in this document. Submissions will be reviewed by the Assessment Team and subsequently graded for potential down selection. The Assessment Team will conduct internal meetings to review graded whitepaper documents for down-selects of those respondents / submissions they feel have the highest potential to satisfy their needs. Favorably evaluated submissions will receive an invitation on or about 19 MAY 2026 to virtually present a demonstration of their solution during Phase III.

Phase III: 09 JUN 2026 - 11 JUN 2026 – Virtual Demonstration Assessment Event
Virtual Demonstration presentations will be held virtually through MS Teams. During the 1-hour time allotted, each presenting entity will demo their solution and capabilities that should satisfy, to the best of their ability, the requirements and criteria noted in this release. 


Each group will be notified of their presentation date and time by CFIC staff. 


For additional information on the process after the presentations, please see the paragraph below titled
“What happens after whitepaper submissions?”.


Phase IV: Follow-On
The Government has several acquisition/contract vehicles (i.e., various IDIQ contracts, purchase orders, etc.) to potentially purchase the final solution if operationally viable. The Government may elect to award to all, some, and/or none of the solutions from Phase II. It is anticipated that notification of final selection will be sent out via email from CFIC on or about 15 JUN 2026.

How You Can Participate
Companies seeking to submit a whitepaper must have an account in Vulcan that is finalized for use NLT 48 hours prior to the submission deadline. 

For technical issues with the Vulcan platform, email support@vulcan-sof.com. 
Unless Vulcan has a significant and unavoidable outage on the submission deadline date, there will not be any deadline extensions provided.

Submissions will only be accepted through the Vulcan platform – CLICK HERE TO SUBMIT.

Use the whitepaper submission instruction sheet and template – CLICK HERE TO LEARN MORE & DOWNLOAD.

Vulcan submission instruction sheet – DOWNLOAD THE PDF.

To learn more about how to use Vulcan, please refer to this information on the CFIC website - https://www.cyberfic.org/joinvulcan.

Questions?  
For submission-related questions, please contact Brandon Sizemore at bsizemore@cyberfic.org and Amanda Green at agreen@cyberfic.org. 

DISCLAIMERS:
An award resulting from this Assessment Event may result in the award of follow-on contracts, transactions, or agreements, subject to the availability of funds. Upon determination that the competitively awarded prototype project(s) has been successfully completed, and subject to the availability of funds, the prototype project(s) may result in the award of a follow-on production contract or transaction without the use of competitive procedures.  Such awards may include multiple phases. 

Non‐Government advisors may be used in the evaluation of submissions and will have signed Non‐Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) with the Government. The Government understands the information provided in this announcement is presented in confidence and may contain trade secret or commercial or financial information and agrees to protect such information from unauthorized disclosure to the maximum extent permitted and as required by law. An organization's participation in any part of the selection process under this announcement indicates concurrence with the aforementioned use of contractor support personnel.
